nativeBearer.description: The native field app's one-hour access token (POST /api/{tenant}/auth/token), bound to ONE tenant and one handset: presented on another tenant's path it is refused 404. Accepted on /api/{tenant}/work/mobile/* only.

partnerKey.description: A key we issued to this partner, presented as `Authorization: Bearer sbh_live_…`. It is the ONLY credential this surface accepts: there is no session, no cookie and no utility in any path — the key names its own connection, which names the utility, and every read is scoped by it. A request with no key, an unknown key, a revoked or expired key, a key presented from an address the connection does not allow, a key whose scope does not name the operation, and a disabled connector are all refused with the SAME 404 and the same body, in the same time (BR-INT-044): the refusal is deliberately not a diagnosis.

passwordHeader.description: A key we issued, presented exactly as issued in the `password` header (no `Bearer`). The key names its utility; there is no utility in any path. A missing, unknown, revoked or expired key, an address the connection does not allow and a disabled connector all get the same refusal, in the same time.
passwordHeader.name: password

sessionCookie.description: Server-side session (identity `sessions` table), set httpOnly by POST /api/{tenant}/auth/session and bound to that ONE tenant (BR-IDN-006): presented on another tenant's path it is refused 404. The browser sends it automatically; no client code reads it.
sessionCookie.name: sbh_session

post.description:
`POST /api/auth/activation/lookup` — `{code}` → `{tenant, utility_name}`
(`DEF-FLD-10580`, PO 2026-10-24: *"the code from the office sets the
utility"*). NO utility in the path: the phone is one build for every
utility and knows only the code. Public, throttled per address AND per
device, one refusal for every way a code can be wrong
(`native.lookup_activation_code`).

POST /exports — 202 + job_id for ANY list that registered itself.

Route registered in config/urls.py, not in this module's urlpatterns: like
`/jobs/{id}`, `/exports` is a PLATFORM resource served by the module that
hosts the jobs table, not a tenancy feature path. Nesting it under
tenancy's settings routes would misname it.

The body mirrors the list's OWN request state (BR-SHL-011's grammar):

    {"resource": "premises", "filters": {...}, "sort": "...",
     "dir": "asc|desc", "q": "..."}

Filters may also arrive as `f.<name>` query params — the same URL state the
screen already carries — so a client can post the very query string it is
displaying; the body wins where both name the same filter. Anything outside
the resource's declared vocabulary is IGNORED, never a 4xx (BR-SHL-011).

`resource` is required and must be registered: an unknown one is a plain
404 (HR-1 / 11b G4), never a guessed queryset. Over 50,000 rows the service
refuses 422 BIZ-CAP with the real count, and no job and no file exist.

get.description:
Hand over the file a finished export job produced (BR-REP-018 / IS-11).

A PLATFORM path beside `/jobs/{id}` and `/exports`, for the same reason
those two are: the exportable lists live in many modules, so the download
belongs to none of them — it belongs to whoever hosts the `jobs` table.

**One 404 for every different no** (HR-1 / 11b G4). An unknown id, another
tenant's id, a job that is not an export, a job that has not SUCCEEDED, a
job with no stored file and a file past the utility's retention all produce
the byte-identical refusal (`exports.resolve_artifact`). Distinguishing them
would leak which job ids exist, and a 403 would leak it loudest.

**A 302 to a signed S3 link, never the bytes** (PO 2026-10-02: *"the system
checks the record and hands over a link to the file that lasts 4 hours"*).
The link names the file (`Content-Disposition` is signed into it) and lives
the 2026-08-30 ruling's four hours. The bytes do not pass through this
process: a sync web worker is killed at 60 s, and a print set is 100 MB+.
The frontend's plain `<a href download>` follows the redirect unchanged.

Roles: any signed-in member of the tenant, the same gate the export's own
accept applies (services.request_list_export records why A4 has no
per-list export cell). The narrowing to "the user who started the job" is
the same owed refinement job_status records — the BE-07 record has no
actor column, and inventing one here would be inventing schema.

get.description:
The ONE resource every 202 in this API promises (B12 r1 / 11b §2.17).

Route registered in config/urls.py, not in this module's urlpatterns: the
path is `/jobs/{id}`, a PLATFORM resource that happens to be served by the
module hosting the `jobs` table — nesting it under tenancy's settings
routes would misname it.

Roles: any signed-in member of the tenant (AnyTenantRole). The ratified
contract says a caller may poll a job THEY started, but the BE-07 record
(core/jobs.py, `jobs` table) has NO actor column — inventing one here
would be inventing schema, so the scope enforced is the TENANT's, and the
narrowing to the starting user is REPORTED as an owed refinement (it needs
a `started_by` column + a B2 addendum). Nothing sensitive rides in the
payload this serves: id, kind, status, progress, checkpoint, result_link,
error — and, for the sample-data plant only, `steps`.

⚠ `checkpoint` WAS MISSING FROM THAT LIST AND FROM THE PAYLOAD UNTIL
DEF-3280 (2026-09-02). The plant job has recorded the label of the block it
just finished since 2026-08-19 and no client could read it, so this
endpoint could answer *"11 of 17"* and never *"Meter reads"*.

⚠ `steps` IS THE SAMPLE-DATA PLANT'S AND NO OTHER KIND'S — CR-064 (PO
2026-09-02, *"list down all 17 steps and show 1 by 1 when they finish"*).
All twenty-eight, always, in creation order, each carrying what the run
recorded for it or `not_started` when it has not been reached. The key is
ABSENT for every other kind rather than empty, because a job with no blocks
has no steps and an empty list would read as an answer.

Absent, malformed, or another tenant's job id → the same plain 404 (HR-1 /
11b G4: existence must not leak, and a 403 would confirm it).

get.description:
`GET /api/partner/v1/bill-download/?bill_id=…` — one bill, as the page
we print.

⚠ **200 IS PDF BYTES AND EVERY OTHER CODE IS A JSON SENTENCE
(`BR-INT-044`).** You cannot put a refusal inside a PDF — a partner's
reader would open it and show a human a document that says nothing useful,
or fail to open it at all — and the refusal has to be the same bytes every
time. So this route answers exactly one content type on success and
`_refused()`'s single body on failure, which is the same object every other
address on this surface returns and takes no argument by design.

⚠⚠ **A BILL THAT IS NOT THIS UTILITY'S ANSWERS THE SAME SENTENCE AS A
REFUSED KEY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE SECURITY ARGUMENT OF THIS ROUTE.** *No
such bill* and *not yours* must be one answer, because a partner that could
tell them apart could walk our invoice numbers and learn which ones exist —
an enumeration oracle on a money document. **It is not a comparison we make
and then hide; it is structural**: the lookup goes through
`billing_seam.collectable()`, which filters on `tenant_id` AND on the
collectable statuses, so an unknown number, another utility's bill and a
draft all return `None` from the same `.first()` and leave through the same
line. There is no branch here that knows which of the three it was.

⚠ **THE PDF IS THE ONE WE ALREADY RENDER — `documents.render_invoice` and
`frozen_bill.reproduce`, which is what `GET /invoices/{id}/document.pdf`
serves to our own screens.** A second renderer would be a second bill: the
same run, the same account, two documents, and the customer's copy and the
partner's copy disagreeing about a total is the kind of thing that is found
by a customer. `X-Document-Provenance` travels too, for `BR-NOT-027`'s
reason — a PDF has nowhere to carry a caption, so a re-rendered bill says
so in a header rather than pretending to be the kept original.

⚠ **THE FILENAME IS THE INVOICE NUMBER**, and `inline` rather than
`attachment`: a partner showing a bill to a customer in a browser wants the
page, and their own client decides whether to save it.

⚠ **NO `format=csv` HERE.** A CSV of one PDF is not a thing, and a
`format` parameter that is silently ignored on one route of a surface where
it works on three others is `DEF-014`'s cousin — so it is not accepted and
not mentioned; the route serves one representation.

`GET /api/partner/v1/bills` — wave 3, the NESTED bill.

`company_id` (verified, never used to select) · `since` · `until` · `page` ·
`page_size`. One record per bill, one row per LINE, each line carrying the
GL account it posted to — PO 2026-09-16, verbatim: *"we save bills as a
multiple line items with gl code map so for bill we will need nasted json
with multiple records with gl code mapped"*.

⚠ **THE WINDOW IS OPTIONAL HERE AND REQUIRED ON PAYMENTS**, because the
supplied specification writes it that way. A bills pull with no window is a
partner's FIRST pull — every bill the utility has ever issued, which is what
a new integration actually wants — and the envelope's `total_records` is how
they know they got all of it.

`GET /api/partner/v1/consumer-info` — the customer record, by number.

**ONE IMPLEMENTATION, TWO ADDRESSES.** This is `_serve_accounts` with a
selector in front of it: the same door (`_admit`), the same seam, the same
composer, the same shape and the same envelope. ⚠ **AND SINCE
`DEF-INT-5622` IT IS ITS OWN OPERATION — `serve_consumer_info` — SO THE
DOOR AND THE RATE WINDOW ARE ITS OWN AND NOT THE LIST'S.** That is what
gives it a row on the connector screen, which is the whole defect: it was
built, routed, tested and INVISIBLE. ⚠ **A second
implementation is the thing this route most invites and is exactly what it
must not be** — the day a field was added to one and not the other, a
partner reading a customer at two addresses would get two different answers
from one utility and nothing on either side could see it.

⚠ **`remote_plan_id` IS SERVED HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE**, by PO ruling
2026-09-17. Asked what it should carry: *"this rate plan ID for that
account"*; asked in which APIs it is required, the answer is this one — it
appears in no other payload of their document. `seams/customers.as_record`
takes `with_detail`, so they are declared fields on one composer rather than a
second record type.

⚠ **`additional_data.payment_received` IS NOT SERVED AND IS NOT GUESSED**
(`OQ-INT-12399`, OPEN). Their document carries it on this payload and what
it MEANS was put to the PO and is the one question of the six they did not
answer. It is a money field: the candidate readings — the last payment's
amount, the total ever received, what was received this cycle — are three
different numbers, and a finance system reconciling against the wrong one
balances to nothing. **The key is absent rather than null**, for
`_echoed_utility_id`'s reason: an absent key is the absence of an answer and
a null is an answer.

`GET /api/partner/v1/customers` — RETIRED, see `/partner/v1/accounts`.

⚠ **IT IS REGISTERED IN `PARTNER_ROUTES` LIKE EVERY OTHER PARTNER ADDRESS
AND NOT BESIDE THE LOOP**, so `_with_utility_from_key` opens the utility
from the key before this runs. A retirement notice still has to
authenticate — see `_serve_retired` — and authenticating means reading a
tenant table, which without that first arrow returns zero rows for a VALID
key and would refuse every caller while looking exactly like a bad key.

⚠ **THE SCOPE IT CHECKS IS `serve_customer`, WHICH IS WHAT THE KEY THAT
USED THIS ADDRESS WAS GRANTED.** A key that never could call it still
cannot, and learns nothing new.

`GET /api/partner/v1/ledger` — a page of the books.

Wave 5 of `CR-110-BRC04` phase 2. The nine checks are `_admit`'s and are
shared with the other four addresses; everything below is check 9 — select,
order, page — which is the only one that differs per route.

⚠ **`start_date` AND `end_date` ARE REQUIRED HERE AND OPTIONAL ON THE
OTHERS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE.** The ledger is the largest set
this product can hand over — every bill line and every payment writes
journal lines, so a month at the top of T5 is around 200,000 rows. An
unbounded pull is the paging trap with nothing to bound it: the table moves
under the walk, page numbers skip, and **a missed journal entry is a missed
posting** that neither side can see. A caller that forgets the window is
told so in six words rather than served a walk that quietly loses rows.

⚠ **THE ENVELOPE CARRIES TWO TOTALS BECAUSE TWO THINGS ARE BEING COUNTED
(`CR-110-BRC04` phase 2 wave 5).** `total_records` counts what `records`
holds — partner ROWS — on this route exactly as on the other four, so a
partner's job can add up what it received and compare. `total_entries` is
the paged unit, and `total_pages` is derived from IT, because **the page is
a page of ENTRIES**: pairing a debit with its credit reads a whole entry,
so a page boundary may never fall inside one. `seams/ledger.collectable`
carries the argument.

post.description:
`POST /api/partner/v1/make-payment/` — Invoice Cloud posts us a payment.

**Confirmed with the Product Owner before a line was written** — decision
log 2026-09-24, *"THE INVOICE CLOUD *MAKE PAYMENT* API, CONFIRMED BEFORE A
LINE IS WRITTEN"*, which is this endpoint's specification and names the
eight authorisation checks, the date mapping, the status correction, the
till-and-batch answer, the audit actor and five mismatches between the
partner's document and this product.

⚠ **THIS VIEW IS THIN AND MUST STAY THIN (B8/LAW 0).** It runs the door,
reads the payload, hands over, writes the run row and answers. Every rule
it obeys belongs to somebody else: checks 1–8 to `_admit`, steps 9–19 to
`invoice_cloud_payment`, and the payment itself to
`payments.services.record_payment`, which is the only thing in this product
that may write a payment row, an allocation or a journal line (hard rules
4, 5 and 7).

⚠ **THE REVERSAL THIS BUILDS, STATED AND NOT ASSUMED.** `BR-INT-071` is
CONFIRMED and says in as many words *"`POST /api/partner/v1/make-payment/`
IS NOT BUILT"* and *"A PARTNER DOES NOT POST A PAYMENT TO US"* (PO
2026-09-17). **It was reversed by the PO on 2026-09-18 in four words —
*"they post to us daily"* — and the whole design was then walked with them
and confirmed on 2026-09-24.** The supersession chain is written into
`BR-INT-071`'s own row and into `BR-INT-083`, which is the rule this
address implements. A lane that meets the old sentence first must read the
dated clause under it.

⚠ **THE SCOPE IS THE SECURITY PROPERTY AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE.** A key
may call this only if its own `scope` names `record_payment`, which only
`pay_invoicecloud_partner` declares. A key without it is refused by
`_admit`'s check 5 — the SAME bytes, the SAME `404` and the SAME padded
floor an unknown key gets — so a read-only key cannot create money and
cannot learn that a write door exists.

⚠ **`_admit` FIRST, BEFORE THE BODY IS TOUCHED.** `BR-INT-021`, and
`_admit_then`'s own docstring records the case that caught it once
already: a `400` about a field name handed to an unauthenticated caller
tells them the address is real and what its parameters are called. Every
payload refusal below is reachable only past all eight checks, which is
what makes it safe for them to be specific.

⚠ **`JSONRenderer` ALONE, NOT `PARTNER_RENDERERS`.** A CSV of one payment
receipt is not a thing, and a `format=csv` that is silently ignored here
while it works on three sibling routes is `DEF-014`'s cousin. One
representation, and it is the one their document posts and parses.

that may write a payment row, an allocation or a journal line (hard rules
4, 5 and 7).

⚠ **THE REVERSAL THIS BUILDS, STATED AND NOT ASSUMED.** `BR-INT-071` is
CONFIRMED and says in as many words *"`POST /api/partner/v1/make-payment/`
IS NOT BUILT"* and *"A PARTNER DOES NOT POST A PAYMENT TO US"* (PO
2026-09-17). **It was reversed by the PO on 2026-09-18 in four words —
*"they post to us daily"* — and the whole design was then walked with them
and confirmed on 2026-09-24.** The supersession chain is written into
`BR-INT-071`'s own row and into `BR-INT-083`, which is the rule this
address implements. A lane that meets the old sentence first must read the
dated clause under it.

⚠ **THE SCOPE IS THE SECURITY PROPERTY AND IT IS NOT IN THIS FILE.** A key
may call this only if its own `scope` names `record_payment`, which only
`pay_invoicecloud_partner` declares. A key without it is refused by
`_admit`'s check 5 — the SAME bytes, the SAME `404` and the SAME padded
floor an unknown key gets — so a read-only key cannot create money and
cannot learn that a write door exists.

⚠ **`_admit` FIRST, BEFORE THE BODY IS TOUCHED.** `BR-INT-021`, and
`_admit_then`'s own docstring records the case that caught it once
already: a `400` about a field name handed to an unauthenticated caller
tells them the address is real and what its parameters are called. Every
payload refusal below is reachable only past all eight checks, which is
what makes it safe for them to be specific.

⚠ **`JSONRenderer` ALONE, NOT `PARTNER_RENDERERS`.** A CSV of one payment
receipt is not a thing, and a `format=csv` that is silently ignored here
while it works on three sibling routes is `DEF-014`'s cousin. One
representation, and it is the one their document posts and parses.

get.description:
`GET /api/partner/v1/payments` — wave 4.

`company_id` · **`start_date` and `end_date`, both REQUIRED** · `page` ·
`page_size`. The four coded fields ship as `{code, label}` in OUR
vocabulary; the partner maps at THEIR end from the reference endpoint, which
is the PO's ruling that struck the clerk mapping screen — *"this will not be
required in case of they read cases - we just need to actiavte connectors
and issue a key thats all"*.

⚠ **BOTH DATES ARE REQUIRED AND AN UNBOUNDED PULL IS REFUSED, NOT SERVED
EMPTY.** The supplied specification declares them required; a partner that
omitted one and got every payment the utility has ever taken would page
through a set that is still moving underneath it, which is the trap above.

`GET /api/partner/v1/receipts` — our payments as New World Receipts.

⚠ **`authentication_classes = []` IS THE DOOR BEING THE DOOR, AND IT IS
NAMED IN `tests/test_be_default_authentication.py` RATHER THAN THE
ASSERTION BEING WIDENED.** Every partner route opts out explicitly and
presents a key at `serve.resolve_caller` before it does anything at all; a
caller who could already authenticate would not be one. That test asserts
the opt-out list EXACTLY, so it goes red the day this address lands and the
address is added deliberately — which is what `DEF-INT-4256` records
happening the one time it was not.

⚠ **NO `PARTNER_RENDERERS` ON THIS ONE, DELIBERATELY.** The other routes
negotiate JSON and CSV; this address serves exactly one media type and
returns a plain `HttpResponse`, so there is nothing for DRF to negotiate
over. Registering `JSONRenderer` here would make `?format=json` answer a
shape their importer has never seen, from an address whose whole purpose is
one vendor's file.

THE THREE SELECTORS, AND WHY THE ORIGIN IS NOT ONE OF THEM
-----------------------------------------------------------
`start_date` and `end_date` are REQUIRED, as on the ledger and for the same
reason: an unbounded pull walks a table that is moving underneath it and
**a missed receipt is a missed posting** neither side can see. `page` and
`page_size` are the surface's own.

**The origin is NOT a parameter.** The feed is `webhook` only — PO ruling
2026-09-22, and it is New World's own requirement rather than our narrowing
— so it is a property of this address, not a choice a caller makes. A
partner that could ask for `origin=entry` could quietly double-count every
counter receipt their cashier system already posted.

⚠ **THE ENVELOPE OF EXCEPTIONS IS IN THE HEADERS, NOT THE BODY.**
The body is their XML and must stay exactly what their importer parses, so
what went wrong on our side travels as response headers and on the run row:
how many receipts did not balance, by how much, how many distributions
carried no GL account, and which tenders went out unmapped. **That is the
half that makes *send it even if it is not balance* safe** — an unbalanced
receipt nobody counted is the silent failure the ruling was protecting
against, one step further along.

`GET /api/partner/v1/reference?company_id=…` — every code
this product can put on a partner payload, with its meaning.

PO 2026-09-16, verbatim: *"you ahve to extend the defination of codes so
that partner can resolve all codes at there end otherwise they will ahve an
issues"*. A partner pulls it once, caches it, and never meets an unknown
value.

⚠ **NO SCOPE TICK — ANY VALID KEY MAY READ IT** (`operation=None`). The
scope guard still bites: `scope_permits` answers `False` for a key with
NOTHING granted, so a key that may call none of the four may not read the
description of what it may call either. What it may not do is single out
one of the four ticks, because a partner that may read bills needs the bill
vocabulary and a partner that may read the ledger needs most of the same
one — a per-tick reference would be four documents that overlap, and the
first code a partner met outside its own slice would be the failure this
endpoint exists to prevent.

⚠ **IT CARRIES NO UTILITY RECORDS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT AN OPERATION.**
Four of the seven lists are closed vocabularies of the product; three are
the tenant's own LOOKUPS — the services they sell, the tenders they take,
the account statuses they use — which is configuration a clerk edits on
Settings, not a customer, a bill or a payment. So it is metered
(`REFERENCE_WINDOW`) and recorded like every other partner read, and it
adds no row to the connection screen.

post.description:
S114 "Create utility & go live": one transactional commit, idempotent on
the subdomain natural key (BR-TEN-010) — replay returns 200 + the existing
tenant; first commit returns 201 + Location.

**The owner is signed in at commit** (PO ruling 2026-08-10, supersedes
BR-TEN-045). Signup and the new tenant now share one origin, so the session
opened inside the provisioning transaction rides back as the ordinary
httpOnly `sbh_session` cookie and the SPA can go straight to
`/{subdomain}` → S62. `signed_in` says whether it did; the session id
itself is never in the body (it is the credential — cookie only).

A REPLAY is answered 200 with `signed_in: false`: BR-TEN-010 matches on
subdomain + owner email and checks no password, so that path may not mint a
login (see services.provision_tenant).

get.description:
`GET /accounts/deposit-standard?unit_id=&account_type=` — the deposit
the unit's plan asks of this category (`BR-RAT-020/023`, `DEF-CUS-6369`).

What the Deposit step on S18 (step 4) and S19 (step 5) SHOWS, read before
the account exists: `{asks, amount, currency}`. It is the SAME walk the
commit takes (`deposit.standard_for_unit` → `seams.deposit_rule_for_account`
→ `rating.deposit_rule_for`), so the figure on screen is the figure the
server takes. `asks: false` means *this plan asks no deposit of this
category* — the step then offers nothing to type (`OQ-CUS-12620` (a)).
`account_type` is the category CODE the Customer step holds. Where the
plan prices the deposit by meter size and no meter is fitted, the answer
offers the plan's sizes (`pick_size`, `sizes`) and `size_class=` prices
the one the clerk picked (`DEF-CUS-9521`).

⚠ **REGISTERED ABOVE `accounts/<str:account_id>` ON PURPOSE** — below it,
`deposit-standard` would be read as an account id and answer 404.

post.description:
`POST /accounts/imports` — stage. BR-CUS-051: nothing is written to
`accounts` or `customers` until the commit below.

Answers 201 synchronously rather than 11b's 202 + job, for the reason the
assets import packet already recorded: `core.jobs` has no registered store
on this deployment, and a 202 pointing at a job that will never be polled
is a worse promise than a synchronous answer. REPORTED, not invented.

get.description:
`accounts_template.csv` — the PUBLISHED template (BR-CUS-046).

A real downloadable artifact, not a README sentence: the file an operator
opens in a spreadsheet, fills in and uploads, carrying the column set the
PO's AC-1 enumerates and a comment block stating the import ORDER
(BR-CUS-047) so the rule arrives with the file rather than after the first
failed run.

One template, no per-tenant variant — the same standard S28 reads follows
(BR-MET-032: mapping is re-detected on every upload, never remembered).

⛔ **CLOSED 2026-09-01 — `BR-CUS-1043` / `DEF-2592`.** This file publishes
the column set of a door that no longer accepts uploads, and a template
whose columns no live loader reads is the same *"promised and honoured by
nothing"* fault as the `Customer #` cell one file along (`DEF-2593`). The
live import hands out its own template, derived from the columns it actually
reads. Kept and unreachable, like the two write doors.

post.description:
`POST /accounts/imports/{id}/commit`.

Refuses 409 BIZ-IDEMPOTENT when this batch — or the same FILE under the
same batch tags — has already been committed (CLAUDE.md rule 6 / DB-12).
Otherwise always answers the BR-CUS-051 summary: "N created · N failed",
with the per-row error report beside it.

`POST /accounts/master` — BR-CUS-068 (PO ruling 2026-08-22, OQ-314's
second half): create the premises' MASTER account — one ordinary `accounts`
row, `kind='master'`, payer = the owner/manager, attached to every
common-area unit (or the `unit_ids` subset) through the same
service-agreement linkage every account uses.

Refuses 409 BIZ-STATE naming the unit for anything that is not one of this
premises' common areas, for a unit already occupied, and for one already
covered by another master; 422 when a common area has no plan (BR-MET-040)
or the premises names no owner/manager and the payload no contact.

There is deliberately NO separate list/detail route: a master account is an
ordinary row, so `GET /accounts?f.kind=master` and `GET /accounts/{id}`
serve it — that inheritance is the whole point of the ruled design.

get.description:
`GET /accounts/subcategories` (`DEF-CUS-6426`) — the ACTIVE sub-categories
a clerk picks under a category on New account and Move-in.

⚠ **A CUSTOMERS READ, NOT THE SETTINGS LOOKUP.** The same rows are served by
`GET /lookups/account_subtypes`, a Settings door
(`SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin`, A4 `settings_lookups`) that answers a
Billing Clerk 403 — measured 2026-09-23 as the seeded clerk — so the two
screens a clerk opens accounts on showed no sub-category at all. That door
is left exactly as signed; this serves only what a picker needs (active
rows, code, name, the category they hang under), with the posture of
`GET /service-requests/categories`, which serves the categories themselves.
The PO's ruling of 2026-09-23 (`OQ-CUS-12618`) names the source: Settings →
Reference data → account categories and sub-categories.

BR-CUS-018's other half: the saved draft becomes the unit's occupant.
Refuses 409 BIZ-STATE when the unit already has one (BR-CUS-017).

get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/build` — the build this account owns, or `null`.

Two readings in order: the build whose `owner_account_id` names this account
— the direct fact, **live since `OQ-373` closed on 2026-08-25 → `BR-MET-116`;
this line said *"starts being true when `OQ-373` is ruled"* until 2026-09-12
(`DEF-MET-5081`)** — then the build at the account's own address. The second
reading is not a stand-in for an unbuilt first one: a build whose owner was
never named has no `owner_account_id` to match, and its address still does.

`GET /accounts/{id}/close-impact` — B19 §15.9's step 3, serialized.

ONE subtraction and five landings: everything outstanding (the prior
balance from the LEDGER plus the final bill net of BR-MET-107's export
credit) less what is applied against it (the deposit, its BR-CUS-057
interest, this account's own credit). `?final_bill=` states the drafted
total as TEXT.

**A GAP IS SERVED, NEVER PAPERED OVER.** When a term cannot be read the
payload carries `landing: null`, the `gaps[]` codes and an `unavailable[]`
entry naming the rule that leaves each open — `deposit_interest_not_accrued`
(BR-CUS-057's engine is not built), `open_disputes_not_readable`
(only when a PUBLISHED dispute store cannot answer — BR-CUS-096 is
SUSPENDED by PO ruling 2026-10-11, so no store at all reads as no dispute),
`export_credit_exceeds_final_bill` (BR-MET-107's open half, deliberately
not floored at zero), `sibling_credit_rule_unsigned` (OQ-362) and
`held_excess_has_no_release_path`. This view returns those verbatim: a
settlement decides where a departing customer's money goes, so a gap must
reach the screen as a gap.

A READ — no `audit_log` row, because nothing moved. The three decisions
below each write their own, inside the service (hard rule 7).

GET/POST /accounts/{id}/close-out (DEF-724 · BR-CUS-430 · BR-CUS-431).

GET answers `eligible` with the blocking rule's own words when it is False,
the cut date that WILL become `closed_at`, the balance read from AR (never
the `accounts.balance` cache — BR-CUS-015), what BR-CUS-082 will do with it,
and the four stated absences a screen may not paper over.

POST performs the act. No `preview` route is mounted beside it: the GET IS
the preview, and a second one would be two answers to one question.

second person on the account (name, email, phone), shown on the account

ONE account's dunning position — the pause, the plan, the tier, the trail.

The S21 header's answer to *"why is this customer being chased, or not?"*,
and the record a utility shows a regulator when a customer says they were
never told. Sends AND skips: an account excluded for a medical hold and one
nobody ever chased must never read the same.

`GET|POST /accounts/{id}/communication` — the dialog, and its one commit.

**GET** answers everything the compose view needs and nothing it does not:
who the message would go to per channel, whether that channel actually
delivers on this deployment, and which kinds may be composed here at all.

**POST** queues it. The response says `queued`, never `sent` — there is no
word in this module's vocabulary for a thing that left the building, because
nothing does.

patch.description:
`PATCH /accounts/{id}/contact` — correct the account's primary contact.

**`BR-CUS-045`'s PII columns, keyed to the ACCOUNT — a different table from
`PATCH /customers/{id}`**, which writes the `customers` row reached through
`customer_accounts`. The Overview's CUSTOMER group renders this one, and
until 2026-09-13 nothing in the product could write it: the wizards CREATE a
contact and the portal's self-service door writes the customer. The Product
Owner found it by driving the screen — *"I cannot edit Customer details"*.

The guard is on the service as well (`BR-SHL-025`: the server-side guard is
THE guard), so the write refuses twice.

get.description:
POST /accounts/{id}/correct-unit — `BR-CUS-1047` (PO ruling 2026-09-12).

Re-points an account at another unit AS A CORRECTION: a `reason_code` from a
fixed list of three, approved by the supervisor making the call, effective
TODAY (an `effective_on` in the body is refused BY NAME), and **every issued
bill left exactly as it is** (hard rule 4).

⚠ **A MOVE IS NOT A CORRECTION.** A customer who has actually moved still
leaves by `POST /accounts/{id}/move-out` and arrives by
`POST /accounts/{id}/move-in` — the bills, meters and reads belong to the
unit and must not follow a person. This door serves a RECORD that named the
wrong unit, and every reason it accepts says so.

Refuses 403 AUTH-002 for a Billing Clerk, 409 BIZ-STATE for a master
account, for an account with no unit, for the unit it is already on and for
a unit another account occupies (`BR-CUS-017`'s surviving half), and 422 for
an unknown reason or a missing one.

GET serves this account's corrections, newest first — the Overview's
history, and the answer to *"why is this account on Suite 2 when five bills
say Suite 1?"*

get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/credit-notes` — S21's Credits tab (CS-37 · P13).

Every credit note on one account, newest first, each carrying its number,
date, amount, reason and the bill it was raised against.

**An account with none answers 200 with an empty list, never 404.** "This
customer has never been given a credit" is a true and useful answer; a 404
would say the account does not exist, which is a different fact and one the
screen would have to draw as an error. A cross-tenant or unknown id reaches
the same empty list under HR-1 — RLS plus the explicit tenant filter mean it
resolves to no rows rather than to somebody else's (hard rule 1).

`GET /accounts/{id}/credit-path` — *"can I give them a credit instead?"*

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  PO, 2026-09-22: "we can not have two path for 1 capabilities wew     ║
║  will confuse user." SO THIS MINTS NO WRITE VERB AT ALL.              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
A clerk closing an account in credit has two ways out — a cheque or a
credit note — and **only one of them is visible from where the choice is
made.** `POST /accounts/{id}/refunds` is one click away on this tab; the
credit path lives in billing and a payments screen has no way to find it.

**THIS IS A SIGNPOST, NOT A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION.** It answers *is the
credit path available on this account, and against which bill*, and hands
back the addresses of **billing's own mounted routes** so the browser calls
billing directly. The write stays exactly where it has always been:
`corrections.execute_credit_only`, reached through `POST /corrections`,
`…/approve` and `…/execute`. Nothing is proxied and nothing is re-derived.

⚠ **THE FACT A PAYMENTS SCREEN CANNOT KNOW BY ITSELF IS THAT A CREDIT IS
RAISED AGAINST A BILL AND A REFUND AGAINST AN ACCOUNT.** So *"credit them
instead"* is not symmetrical with *"refund them"*: the clerk must name a
bill, and this serves the ones they may name.

**`available: false` MEANS THIS ACCOUNT HAS NOTHING TO CREDIT TODAY** — not
that the feature is unbuilt. The reason travels on `problems` so the screen
prints a sentence rather than greying a control and leaving the clerk with
*"why not?"* (`BR-SHL-025`).

A READ. No clock, no money arithmetic, no write, no audit row.

`GET /accounts/{id}/credit-sources` — CR-059 CS-7's evidence half (S58).

CS-7's acceptance line is *"a credit built from two overpayments can be
refunded, **listing the payments behind it**"*, and this is the second
clause. A GET: it writes nothing and may be taken twice with no consequence.

Answers what the account holds on account, and which payments built it —
each with the part of itself that no bill absorbed, because a $350.00 cheque
that left $57.13 behind CONTRIBUTED $57.13 and a screen listing $350.00
would offer a clerk money that is not there.

⚠ **THE ROWS AND THE REFUNDABLE FIGURE DIVERGE AFTER THE FIRST REFUND, ON
PURPOSE.** Nothing records which payments a past refund drew on — the PO's
ruling of 2026-09-01 is that a refund names the ACCOUNT and not a payment —
so `refundable` is the position and the rows are evidence. `problems[]` says
so on every response rather than leaving a screen to add them up and be
refused by the refund path.

`AdminOrClerk`, matching `POST /accounts/{id}/refunds`: this is what a clerk
reads immediately before raising the refund, and a role that may raise one
must be able to see what it is drawing on.

post.description:
`POST /accounts/{id}/deposit-carry-forward` — CS-22 (S19 step 4 · S21).

`{id}` is the CLOSED account holding the deposit; the body names the new one:

    to_account_id     the account moving in — REQUIRED
    moved_on          the caller's business day — REQUIRED, never a clock
    reason            REQUIRED free text; the audit row is the only durable
                      record of why a customer's security moved
    expected_amount   OPTIONAL confirmation of the PRINCIPAL. When the offer
                      screen shows `carried $153.50` and posts that back,
                      the service REFUSES with both figures named rather
                      than silently moving $150.00 — see the writer.
    memo              optional, written on both legs
    idempotency_key   the wizard's submit token — REQUIRED

**201 on a new carry, 200 on a replay.** A move-in wizard whose step 4 is
submitted twice must carry the deposit ONCE; the second submit answers with
the first movement and `created: false`.

**`AdminOrClerk`, matching the credit transfer above.** Nothing leaves the
utility, no bill is re-opened and no customer is charged: the same money
stays held for the same person against a different account of theirs. A
move-in is clerk work by definition — a door narrower than the transfer
would mean no clerk could complete the wizard they are given.

⚠ **THE OFFER IS CUSTOMERS' DOOR AND THIS IS PAYMENTS'.** BR-CUS-089 gates
the offer on a stored `strong` identity match and
`GET /customers/{id}/deposit-carry-forward` is where that gate lives. This
door proves the two accounts share a HOLDER and moves the money. A screen
calls the offer first; that ordering is stated in the writer's docstring and
in this lane's decision-log row rather than enforced here, because payments
may not re-implement a customers judgment about a person.

get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/deposit-carry-preview?to=` — what would move.

A GET, writing nothing: what the closed account HOLDS, what the new one
holds already, and the receipt date that travels with the money.

⚠ **NO `amount` PARAMETER, AND THAT IS THE CONTRACT.** The whole principal
moves (PO 2026-09-01: the clerk ACCEPTS the offer, they do not size it), so
a screen has nothing to choose and no figure to post back except the
confirmation the write door takes.

`GET /accounts/{id}/disconnect-bills` — *"the bills behind that figure"*.

Blueprint p136 draws the unpaid bills that add up to the balance a cut is
justified by, directly under that balance, with the caption *"Three unpaid
bills reconcile to the balance exactly."* **Nothing called anything for this
before `CR-125-BRC07`.** A clerk was shown a figure and no way to see what
it was made of, on the step that decides whether to cut somebody off.

⚠ **SERVER-PAGED (`NFR-3`) AND UNCAPPED (`NFR-5`).** `?page=` and `?per=`
are BR-SHL-011's own grammar and clamp rather than error. The nearest
existing route — payments' `GET /accounts/{id}/open-bills` — serves no page,
no due date and no state; it is untouched and this does not replace it.

⚠ **THE SUM IS STATED ONLY WHEN THE PAGE HOLDS EVERY ROW.** The drawn
caption is a reconciliation CLAIM, and a total over one page of several is
not one. `bills_behind_the_balance` carries the whole reasoning.

Read-only: no clock (`as_of` is a parameter, `BR-TEN-043`), no write, and
every amount is the owning module's own.

post.description:
`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case` — start a case at TIER 1.

Idempotent on the OPEN CASE rather than on a key — `open_case` returns the
one already open — because `uq_one_open_disconnect_case_per_account` already
makes a second impossible and a second call is an ordinary double-click.
200 rather than 201 for that reason: this door cannot promise it created
anything.

`sequence` is `BR-CUS-082`'s closed pair — a SERVICE sequence that can end in
a cut, and a COLLECTIONS sequence that cannot — and an unknown one is refused
by the service with both names.

`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/advance` — move up one rung.

⚠ **A PERSON CLICKS THIS. NOTHING ADVANCES ITSELF** (`DEF-320`,
`NO_SCHEDULER` on every ladder payload). That absence is the reason this
route has to exist at all: a ladder nothing walks and nobody can walk is a
ladder that never moves.

The service refuses on a protection in force, on a payment that cleared the
arrear, and on a plan pause — each by name, and each of those refusals
reaches the clerk as a sentence through `_as_catalog_refusal`.

`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/cut` — the crew attended; supply is off.

The act itself, on the day, and the money rules `BR-CUS-103/104/105` land
here — all three inside `commit_cut`, none of them re-implemented in this
layer.

⚠ **`final_reads` GOES TO THE METERING EVENT DOOR, event `disconnect`** —
carried through, never written here, exactly as the transfer's shared
reading is.

✅ **`OQ-383` IS CLOSED AND THERE IS A VOCABULARY NOW (2026-09-20).** This
paragraph read *"there is no vocabulary for a crew that attended and did NOT
cut … this route does not invent that vocabulary; it carries the absence"* —
correct on the day it was written and false since the PO named four
outcomes: **locked gate, access refused, paid at the door, disputed**. Their
door is `POST .../disconnect-case/visit` below, and `BR-CUS-1083` is the
rule. This route is still the one that records a cut that HAPPENED, and
`CREW_OUTCOME_UNRECORDABLE` still rides its payload — amended, pointing at
the other door rather than saying there is none.

`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/finish` — the held bill, now raisable.

**`DEF-CUS-6063`.** A cut whose final bill billing refused leaves the supply
off and the account on its OLD status, and until this route existed nothing
in the product could ever finish it: `commit_cut` refuses `already_cut` by
name and BR-CUS-107's status is written from `commit_cut` and from nowhere
else. This is the door the clerk who fixed the data presses.

⚠ **IT TAKES ONE FLAG AND NO DATES, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT.**
This paragraph read *"IT TAKES NO BODY, ON PURPOSE"* until 2026-09-21, and
the reason it gave still holds for every DATE and every FIGURE: the window
comes from the case's own `cut_on`, the money comes from the engine, the
status comes from BR-CUS-107, and a parameter for any of those would be a
clerk choosing how many days a customer pays for. **`without_bill` is not
one of those.** PO ruling 2026-09-21: *"in single bill we have final bill
workflow - so if clark want to complete the bill he can do it from there -
we will need to allow clark to complete the cut request later without
bill."* It names WHICH OF TWO ACTS the clerk is performing, and only the
clerk knows that.

It is read STRICTLY as the boolean `true`. A missing, null or any other
value is the ordinary path — the safe one, the one that asks billing first
— because hard-won law 3 says the unsafe option is the one you type.

⚠ **A STILL-REFUSED BILL IS A 200 WITH `finished: false`, NOT AN ERROR** —
`raise_and_issue_cut_bill`'s own posture, for its own reason: the refusal is
a configuration problem a human fixes and the engine's sentence is the
useful part of the answer. The `_laddered` error shape is kept for the three
cases where the ACT itself is refused (no case, no cut, already finished).

`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/notices` — the notice went out.

`tier` and `on_date` are both required. **The date is the caller's**: a
notice dated by the server is a statutory clock started on a day nobody can
evidence, and `BR-CUS-039`'s waiting periods are counted from it.

⚠ **`DELIVERY_UNAVAILABLE` rides every case this module writes** (`DEF-692`):
recording that a notice was SENT is not the same as the product having sent
it, and nothing here claims delivery.

`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/reconnecting` — they paid; a crew is on the way.

`BR-PAY-036`, and the gate here reads AR. ⚠ **`DEF-708`: the reconnection fee
reaches AR through nothing today**, so this gate lets a customer through
short by exactly the `CC-RECON` amount — which is absent on every tenant in
this tree anyway (`DEF-700`). Both are stated on `reconnection-terms` above
and neither is papered over here.

`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/restore` — supply is back on.

The last rung, and the one that closes the `service_off_windows` interval
the cut opened. `on_date` is required for the same reason every other date
here is: a billing consequence is counted from it.

`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/stop` — a human stops the ladder.

`on_date` and `reason` are both required and neither is defaulted. This is
the manual override on a process that ends in a household losing supply, so
the record of who stopped it, when, and why is the whole point of the act
(hard rule 7).

⚠ **`note` IS THE DRAWING'S `What happened` AND IT JOINED THIS DOOR ON
2026-09-20 (`CR-125-BRC07`).** Blueprint p137 draws a free-text line under
the three reason radios, captioned *"Recorded with the act and with who did
it"*, and **there was no parameter and no column for it** — so the wizard
asked for a sentence and dropped it, which is worse than not asking.
`disconnects.DisconnectCase.stopped_note` carries the decision to give it a
column, including the two cheaper options that were refused.

⚠ **OPTIONAL, LIKE THE SERVICE IT CALLS.** A required note would refuse a
stop, and a refused stop means a disconnection carries on because a clerk
had nothing to type.

`POST /accounts/{id}/disconnect-case/visit` — the crew attended and did not cut.

**`BR-CUS-1083`, PO ruling 2026-09-20**, verbatim: *"The register reflects
reality. Today a failed visit is invisible and the case looks untouched."*
The four outcomes are the PO's own words and the set is closed;
`apps/customers/disconnect_visits.py` holds every rule, including WHERE each
outcome sends the case and why three of them share a destination.

`on_date` and `outcome` are both required and neither is defaulted. A date
defaulted to today would put a crew at a meter on a day nobody was there —
a failed visit is usually recorded the next morning — and an outcome
defaulted to anything is this route choosing what happened at somebody's
house.

⚠ **`note` IS OPTIONAL, LIKE `stop_by_hand`'s.** A required note would
refuse the recording, and a refused recording leaves the case advertising a
cut date that has passed, which is the whole defect this door closes.

get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/disconnect-notices` — `DSC-02.3`'s own notice table.

`DEF-CUS-5169`. Step 3 of the disconnect wizard draws **What has gone out
already** over this account's letters and then attests to one of them, and
neither half was reachable: the only notice read in this file is the
TENANT-WIDE `awaiting-proof` queue, whose rows named no account, and the
proof door is keyed by a notice id that nothing on any screen showed a
clerk. So a step that said *"Record it first"* had nothing behind it and
**no cut could be scheduled from that screen on any account here.**

⚠ **IT IS A READ AND IT DECIDES NOTHING.** `service_proof_for` still owns
the answer that governs a cut and `assert_service_proved` still refuses
without it; this route only lets a screen show the rows the table already
holds. Nothing about what a lawful cut requires moves.

⚠ **NO DELIVERY CLAIM RIDES ON IT.** `proof_payload` carries the PROOF
columns and never `delivery_state`, which stays NULL with
`DELIVERY_UNAVAILABLE` beside it (`DEF-692`) — the drawn `DELIVERED?`
column really is unknowable today, and the screen says so in its own words.

`GET /accounts/{id}/disconnect-panel` — step 1's customer and money panels.

Blueprint p135–p136 put **fifteen** customer facts and **six** money facts
in front of a clerk before they cut anybody off; the shipped screen showed
six of the fifteen. Measured 2026-09-20, thirteen of the fifteen were
already on `GET /accounts/{id}` and simply not rendered — so this route
carries **only the six that were genuinely missing** and repeats none of the
others. A second copy of a fact is a fact that can disagree with itself.

⚠ **IT IS ADDITIVE TO THE ACCOUNT PAYLOAD AND NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR IT.**
The wizard fetches the account as it always did and this alongside; the
alternative was widening `account_detail_dict`, which is another lane's
file and is read by S17, S21 and eleven other surfaces that do not want a
payments plan lookup on every render.

Read-only.

`GET /accounts/{id}/disconnect-review` — step 5's review, in ONE call.

Blueprint p140–p141. The shipped review drew six of fourteen rows and
omitted **eight notice-and-proof facts that the wizard had already fetched
on step 3** — at the moment a person presses a danger-tier button.

⚠ **IT RE-READS RATHER THAN REMEMBERS, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THE ROUTE.**
The alternative is the front end carrying a legal fact forward across four
steps. This calls `service_proof_for` — the SAME function
`assert_service_proved` uses to decide whether a cut may be scheduled at
all — so the summary a clerk confirms and the guard that lets them confirm
it cannot drift apart.

⚠ **IT DECIDES NOTHING.** No write, no state change, no gate. `POST
/disconnects/schedule` is still the one commit (`BR-SHL-019`) and still
re-checks everything itself.

Read-only.

post.description:
`POST /accounts/{id}/discounts` — record an assistance claim (task 5.4).

Writes an enrolment through rating's own service, so there is ONE grant
table and the bill run reads the table it already reads. The status is
rating's to decide (`pending` vs `not_required`, per BR-RAT-076) and a
caller-supplied one is refused.

⚠ **A CLERK WAS REFUSED HERE BY ANOTHER MODULE'S RBAC UNTIL 2026-10-05.**
Rating's `enrol_account` was `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)` (reported by the
R2 lane, 2026-08-25). The PO ruled (b) on 2026-10-05 — *"Let billing clerks
record it themselves"* — and rating now admits a Billing Clerk, so this door
enrols for the clerk. Any refusal rating still raises passes through
UNCHANGED.

⚠ **`DEF-RAT-9297` — THIS PASSED THE WHOLE BODY AS THE PROGRAMME ID AND
ANSWERED 500 EVERY TIME** (`CR-166-BRC10` r2 t3). `claim_assistance(actor,
account_id, programme_id)` takes an id; the view handed it
`{"programme_id": …}`, so `_discount_or_404` raised Django's own *"… is not
a valid UUID"*. Tests called the service directly and no test posted to the
URL, so the view's argument was never exercised. The body is read FIELD BY
FIELD now — `programme_id` required, `household_size` passed through so the
service can refuse it by name as before.

get.description:
`GET|POST /accounts/{id}/documents` — the Documents tab and its upload.

⚠ **PAGED IN SQL, NOT IN PYTHON (`NFR-3`).** `CLAUDE.md` counts four live
breaches that all named the old 3,000-connection ceiling as their excuse
(`DEF-PAY-4221`); this is a new list and it is not the fifth. A landlord's
four hundred filings are counted with `COUNT(*)` and drawn ten at a time.

⚠ **`POST` IS `AdminOrClerk`, NOT `AnyTenantRole`** — `BR-SHL-031`, verbatim:
*"v1 uploads staff-mediated, consumer portal v2"*. An Executive may read the
tab and may not file into it, which is the same split `account_notes` makes
one tab across.

Multipart because the bytes come through the application: `file` is the
part, everything else is a form field.

⚠ **413 AND 415 ARE CAUGHT HERE AND NOT RAISED AS CATALOG REFUSALS.**
`HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE` maps a B12 §3 code to a status and neither transport
row has one, so a `ValidationError` would answer 422 to a file over the cap
(B12 r1's HTTP-series rows; 11b G11). The body is the SHARED envelope
`core.errors.http_series_refusal_body`, which is the kernel follow-up
`apps/tenancy/api.py` reported in 2026-08-09 and which this wave built
rather than copying.

delete.description:
`GET|DELETE /accounts/{id}/documents/{docId}` — a link that dies, and the
filing that can be taken back.

Four hours, and it is a bearer token: `document_store.download_url` mints it
at `document_storage.url_ttl_seconds()`, capped by the PO ruling of
2026-08-30. The row is resolved under THIS tenant first and the URL is
minted second, so a link is never issued for a document the caller could not
have found — another utility gets a 404, the same answer as for one that
never existed (`BR-TEN-003`, HR-1).

⚠ **THERE IS A `DELETE` NOW, AND WHAT IT DELETES IS THE FILING.** This
docstring read *"There is no DELETE … so no removal route is invented"*
until 2026-09-13, when the PO ruled on wave I's own report that *"a clerk who
files the wrong scan cannot take it back"* — verbatim, *"We should have this
functionality"* (`BR-CUS-1052`). **The two rules that sentence cited are not
reversed:** `BR-CUS-036` still audit-locks system and contract documents, so
a `DELETE` of either answers **409 `BIZ-LOCKED`** with its reason rather
than removing anything; and `NFR-35` still makes the bytes write-once for
seven years, so **no byte is erased** — the stored object stays and only
the account's filing of it goes away. (⚠ It is no longer under an object
LOCK: `CR-160-BRC10`, 2026-10-02, suspended the lock for every file; nothing
in the product deletes the object either way.)

⚠ **`DELETE` IS `AdminOrClerk`, NOT `AnyTenantRole`** — the same split
`POST` makes one route up, and for the same reason (`BR-SHL-031`, *"v1
uploads staff-mediated"*). An Executive reads the tab and may not take a
document off it. The permission class on the view is the READ's, so the
narrower gate is checked in the branch, exactly as `account_notes` and
`account_documents_list` already do.

**204 and no body.** Nothing survives the call that a caller could want: the
filing is gone from every read, and the audit row it wrote is not this
endpoint's to serve.

`GET /accounts/{id}/documents/{docId}/content?as=view|download` — the
file itself, for a clerk to open or save (`DEF-CUS-9147`).

The service request's content route (`CR-158-BRC10`) for an account, with
its headers taken from that view rather than restated: `inline` only for a
PDF, PNG or JPEG asked for with `as=view`, `nosniff`, a policy under which
no script runs inside a served file, and `private, no-store`.

`AnyTenantRole` — a READ, like the link one route up. Resolved under this
tenant first; another utility gets 404. Audited, one row per open or save.

`GET /accounts/{id}/eligibility` — move-in step 4's panel (task 5.4).

**Eligibility NEVER blocks service; it only changes what is charged**
(B18 §5.3.4, BR-RAT-043, BR-RAT-112). `blocks_service` is a CONSTANT on the
payload, not a computed field, so no input can make it true.

Whether an unproven claim reduces the bill straight away is **per
programme**, not a global answer: BR-RAT-076's stored
`proof_before_first_reduction`. A READ — no audit row.

`GET|POST /accounts/{id}/final-bill-preview` — S20 step 3's FIGURE.

**PO ruling 2026-09-19 on step 3 of the move-out wizard, verbatim:** *"we
need to do it"*. This is the keystone that ruling names: steps 3, 4 and 5
were one blocked chain because `close-impact` takes a final-bill figure the
caller states and **nothing in the product ever stated one**, so `landing`
was `null` on every account and step 4's four shortfall radios rendered
enabled over a `POST` that refused with `no_shortfall` every single time.

**IT PRICES AND POSTS NOTHING.** The Billing blueprint settles it itself on
p112, in a dashed panel: *"NO BILL IS ISSUED BY THIS SCREEN. Billing raises
the final bill; this wizard prices what it will contain and posts nothing.
The figures above are a settlement position, not an invoice, and the
account closes owing what the invoice will say."* No invoice, no invoice
line, no journal line, no payment, no ledger entry and **no bill number** —
stage 6 is where a draft is written and where `core.numbering` spends a
number (BR-BIL-063), and it is not on this path. That is what makes the
figure safe inside a wizard a clerk may abandon halfway.

**`?moved_out_on=` IS REQUIRED AND IS NEVER A CLOCK** (BR-TEN-043, gate
G6): it is the move-out day the clerk stated at step 2, it is the day the
bill runs THROUGH (BR-CUS-056 — the outgoing account pays the move day),
and it is the day BR-CUS-057's deposit interest accrues to. A settlement
re-opened next month recomputes to the same figure because the date is a
stored business fact. `?period_start=` is OPTIONAL and re-prices a window a
clerk corrected; absent, billing derives the first unbilled day itself and
**refuses** an account it cannot derive one for rather than guessing.

**WHAT TO DO WITH THE ANSWER:** pass `total` — the CHARGES — straight to
`GET /accounts/{id}/close-impact?final_bill=`. It is deliberately NOT net
of BR-MET-107's export credit and NOT net of the deposit: `close-impact`
applies both and serves `export_credit`, `final_bill_net` and the five
landings. Subtracting either here would double-count it.

⚠ **`POST` PRICES THE READS THE CLERK KEYED AND WRITES NOTHING EITHER** —
PO ruling 2026-09-20, verbatim *"option b is correct"* (`DEF-CUS-5931`).
Step 2 asks for the closing register and step 6 writes it with the close, so
at step 3 the closing read does not exist and every move-out refused on a
missing meter factor. The body carries `final_reads` in the SAME shape the
move-out door takes at step 6 — `[{"meter_no": "M-4021", "value": "52410"}]`
— and it is read, never stored. `GET` is unchanged and prices from committed
reads alone; both methods answer the identical payload, and the one on the
wire that says which is `priced_from_uncommitted_reads`.

⚠ **A POST THAT WRITES NOTHING IS THIS PRODUCT'S OWN SHAPE FOR A PRICED
PREVIEW**, not an exception invented here: `POST /billing/one-time/preview`
is phase 1 of the one-time bill and its comment says *"writes NOTHING"*. The
method is the body's, not the side effect's — a capture of eleven registers
does not belong in a query string, and a re-read with a corrected reading
must not be cached by anything between the clerk and the engine.

A READ — no `audit_log` row, because nothing moved. `account_close_impact`
directly below states the same for the same screen.

PO ruling 2026-09-20, verbatim *"option b is correct"* (`DEF-CUS-5931`).
Step 2 asks for the closing register and step 6 writes it with the close, so
at step 3 the closing read does not exist and every move-out refused on a
missing meter factor. The body carries `final_reads` in the SAME shape the
move-out door takes at step 6 — `[{"meter_no": "M-4021", "value": "52410"}]`
— and it is read, never stored. `GET` is unchanged and prices from committed
reads alone; both methods answer the identical payload, and the one on the
wire that says which is `priced_from_uncommitted_reads`.

⚠ **A POST THAT WRITES NOTHING IS THIS PRODUCT'S OWN SHAPE FOR A PRICED
PREVIEW**, not an exception invented here: `POST /billing/one-time/preview`
is phase 1 of the one-time bill and its comment says *"writes NOTHING"*. The
method is the body's, not the side effect's — a capture of eleven registers
does not belong in a query string, and a re-read with a corrected reading
must not be cached by anything between the clerk and the engine.

A READ — no `audit_log` row, because nothing moved. `account_close_impact`
directly below states the same for the same screen.

`POST /accounts/{id}/hold-excess` — BR-CUS-096, *"hold until dispute close"*.

ADDED for the same reason as `/refund` above, and REPORTED the same way.

The `refused_excess` landing: the deposit is worth more than everything
owed AND part of what is owed is disputed, so the excess is HELD — because
the amount owed can still move. Refused by name on every other landing.

⚠ The response states, on every call, that **nothing chases the hold**:
BR-CUS-096 does not say who releases it or on what clock, and there is no
release path, no timer and no queue in this repository. That sentence
(`held_excess_has_no_release_path`) is the deliverable; inventing a release
clock here would be answering a question the PO has not been asked.

get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/ladder` — `DSC-02.3`'s ladder panel plus the open case.

Two facts on one payload because the screen shows them together: where the
ladder says this account stands, and the case row (if any) that records it.

⚠ **`scheduler` RIDES EVERY ANSWER AND IT SAYS NOTHING ADVANCES ITSELF**
(`disconnects.NO_SCHEDULER`, `DEF-320`): nothing in this product reads a date
and acts on it. A screen that hid that would imply a case walks its own
ladder, and it does not — `advance` below is a person clicking.

⚠ **`tier` IS NULLABLE AND `TIER_UNMAPPED` IS A REAL VALUE.** Payments'
`second_5_day` rung has no chip in B18 and `tier_for_rung` refuses to invent
one: mapping it onto a tier would tell a regulator a certified letter went
out.

⚠ **`cut_floor` JOINED THIS PAYLOAD ON 2026-09-12 — `OQ-CUS-1810` CLOSED.**
The earliest date a cut may lawfully happen: the FINAL notice's SERVED date
plus the tenant's own period from `BR-PAY-017` (`final_notice_hours`),
counted in **business days** and rolled past that tenant's own
`holiday_calendars` rows. It rides HERE rather than on a new route for two
reasons: the ladder is the resource that owns notices, and step 3 of the
wizard needs the tier, the served dates and the floor together — one call
or three sentences saying *not served to this screen*.

⚠ **IT IS A WARNING AND NOT A GUARD, AND THE PAYLOAD SAYS SO.** PO,
verbatim: *"(b) Floor it at the notice date itself now… - give a message but
allow it"*. `enforced: False` travels with it, no validator reads it, and
the date field gets NO `min` — a `min` would silently stop a clerk typing
the date at all, which is the opposite of what was ruled.

⚠ **NO SERVED NOTICE MEANS NO FLOOR, STATED AS AN ABSENCE.** A notice is
ISSUED by the ladder and SERVED by a person outside the product;
`served_on` is null until somebody records the proof. A floor counted from
an ISSUE date would be a legal claim about a letter nobody has confirmed
arrived, so it answers `null` with a reason code and the screen says the
period cannot be counted yet.

patch.description:
`PATCH /accounts/{id}/mailing-address` — where the BILL goes.

Hard rule 8's first named exception (`customers.addresses kind='mailing'`),
which had a CREATE path and no correction path at all. `kind` is not read
from the body: this route writes `mailing` and nothing else, so the retired
`kind='service'` cannot arrive through it (`BR-MET-1161`). An empty `line1`
removes the row, which is how the account says *the bill goes to the service
address* — the sentence the screen already draws.

post.description:
POST /accounts/{id}/move-in (11b §S19 · US-CUS-004) — {id} is the
OUTGOING account; the new occupant takes ITS unit.

201 with a Location header, because this creates a NEW account with its own
number (T4-06 step 5: reopening does not exist). Refuses 409 BIZ-STATE with
BR-CUS-017 while the unit is still occupied, and with BR-CUS-056 when the
start date lands on the outgoing account's move day.

⚠ **`services` — `BR-CUS-1101`, PO ruling 2026-09-25. OPTIONAL, and
ABSENT MEANS ALL OF THEM.** A list of service codes saying which of the
unit's services this account takes: *the unit has six, the account takes
three*. A code the unit has no service point for is refused 422
VAL-UNKNOWN-LOOKUP **naming it**, with the unit's own offer beside it —
a clerk cannot buy a connection that does not exist. An EMPTY list is
refused too (`final_reads`' reason): a screen that sent the key sent it
because a clerk ticked boxes. Nothing is stored beyond the
`service_agreements` rows themselves, so an absent agreement and a
deliberate untick are the same fact, which the PO was shown and accepted.

POST /accounts/{id}/move-out (11b §S20 · US-CUS-005 · BR-CUS-030).

The occupant leaves and the unit derives Vacant again (BR-MET-036). The
response carries the BR-CUS-031 `final_bill_handoff` this module can
assemble and a `warnings` list naming every downstream that does not exist
— no final bill, no deposit settlement, no dunning stop.

11b also lists `POST /accounts/{id}/move-out/preview`. It is NOT mounted:
the preview is B4.3 final-bill math over invoices billing does not have, and
a route that answers 501 is a promise (see the module docstring).

get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/move-out-estimate?meter_no=&moved_out_on=` —
`DEF-BIL-10052` task 5: the estimate step 2 shows when *Estimate* is ticked,
computed by billing's own draft-bill path so step 2 and step 3 agree.
A READ: nothing is written.

`GET|POST /accounts/{id}/notes` — the Notes tab and the S22 modal.

NOT paginated, deliberately, and it is the one list in this module that is
not: 11b G5's rule is about LIST SCREENS, and the capability matrix types
this as a CARD LIST scoped to one account, ordered pinned-first. A page
boundary through a pinned-first order would hide exactly the note somebody
pinned so it would not be missed.

post.description:
`GET|POST /accounts/{id}/notes` — the Notes tab and the S22 modal.

NOT paginated, deliberately, and it is the one list in this module that is
not: 11b G5's rule is about LIST SCREENS, and the capability matrix types
this as a CARD LIST scoped to one account, ordered pinned-first. A page
boundary through a pinned-first order would hide exactly the note somebody
pinned so it would not be missed.

patch.description:
`PATCH /accounts/{id}/notes/{noteId}` — pin, unpin, correct.

There is no DELETE. IS-1's pattern for an audited annotation is supersede or
edit, never remove, and no rule rules on deleting a note — so no route is
minted for one (a route that answers 501 is a promise).

get.description:
WHAT EACH OF THIS ACCOUNT'S BILLS STILL OWES — CR-059 CS-4, closing OQ-154.

The list the S22/S35 Record modal aims money at when a clerk picks *"A
specific bill"* or *"Split across bills"*, and the figures S21's Bills tab
shows beside the issued total.

**THE POINT IS THAT IT IS THE OPEN BALANCE AND NOT THE ISSUED TOTAL.** Both
controls have been CONFIRMED law and executed by the allocator since
2026-08-11 and have rendered DISABLED on both screens, because
`GET /invoices?f.account_id=` serves what a bill was ISSUED for and that is a
different number the moment anything has been paid: `BL-2608-018410` was
issued at **247.87**, a 200.00 payment left **47.87** open, and a picker
built on the bill list would have offered the clerk 247.87 to aim at.

Each row carries the bill's number, its issue date, its total, what has been
allocated to it, what it still owes and its CHAR(3) currency; the position
carries the account's own currency, the number of open bills and their sum —
P1's *"owes 341.10 across 2 bills"* header, summed over exactly the rows
below it. A settled bill is ABSENT rather than listed at 0.00.

Read-only, by every rule in the module: no clock, no money arithmetic, no
write. It reshapes `billing_seam.open_invoices_for_account`, which already
did the subtraction, and **the allocator is untouched**.

A cross-tenant or unknown account id refuses by the same sentence and the
same rule id `POST /accounts/{id}/payments` refuses by — the picker and the
record call must agree on what an account is.

`GET|POST /accounts/{id}/payment-plans` — one path, two verbs.

The same shape `accounts` above takes: DRF routes a path to one view, and
splitting the read onto a second URL would give the S24 history and the S24
send two different resources for one thing.

post.description:
`GET|POST /accounts/{id}/payment-plans` — one path, two verbs.

The same shape `accounts` above takes: DRF routes a path to one view, and
splitting the read onto a second URL would give the S24 history and the S24
send two different resources for one thing.

`POST /accounts/{id}/payment-plans/preview` — step 1 → step 2.

**WRITES NOTHING**, and the response says so on the wire (`writes: []`), the
same contract §S23's preview carries. ❄️ GT-47 is what it computes: 267.30
less a 50.00 down payment over six instalments is 5 × 36.22 and a FINAL
36.20 — the remainder lands on the last row and nowhere else (BR-CUS-043),
which is what makes Σ equal the total to the cent.

Step 2's per-row edits come back through this same route with `edits`, so
the arithmetic that re-sums them is the server's (B4.4) and a clerk cannot
send an agreement whose own numbers disagree.

Record ONE payment against one account (11b §1 regenerated · US-PAY-001).

The body is BR-PAY-022's field set: *"account → amount, method,
posting+clearing dates, reference, allocation choice"*, plus BR-PAY-012's
purpose and r14 #4's memo.

    amount           decimal STRING, > 0
    posted_at        the USER's posting date — required (BR-PAY-033)
    cleared_at       the clearing date, or absent = still processing
    method           a tenant method CODE (BR-PAY-026) — optional
    confirmation     check / confirmation number — optional
    memo             optional
    purpose          bill | deposit | plan_down | prepay (default bill)
    apply_to         oldest_first | newest_first | carry_credit |
                     specific | split (BR-PAY-001; default oldest_first)
    targets[]        {invoice_number, amount?} for specific / split
    idempotency_key  the form's client token — REQUIRED (see below)
    currency         optional; must equal the account's (BR-TEN-042)
    type             payment | credit | adjustment (default payment)
    reason           a tenant reason code — REQUIRED for the latter two

**`idempotency_key` IS REQUIRED, and refusing without it is the point.**
`record_payment` stores no key when the caller names none, and a double
submit then records two payments — its docstring says so and says the API
layer will pass one. Generating one HERE would produce a different string on
the second submit and dedupe nothing while looking as though it had, so the
only honest options are "require it" and "take the money twice".

A REPLAY ANSWERS 200 WITH THE ORIGINAL PAYMENT and `created: false`, not
409. 11b §3 G7 makes a duplicate a 409 for the four operations it
enumerates — bill runs, read/payment IMPORTS, webhooks, tenant provisioning
— and a staff double-click is none of them: BR-PAY-028's field-map row reads
*"duplicate submit → single row"*, US-PAY-001 TC-6's expected outcome is
"One row only", and G7's own list already contains the same shape
(`POST /tenants`, *"repeat returns existing tenant"*). A 409 toast for a
button that worked is a wrong answer a clerk would act on.

201 on a new payment, with the allocation inline: a clerk who has just taken
$292.87 has to be shown what it paid, and the allocator worked that out in
the same transaction.

`POST /accounts/{id}/plan-changes` — step 3's confirm.

201 because a NEW effective-dated assignment row is created. The response
carries `problems[]`: the deposit-differential instruction US-CUS-017 §1 (c)
asks for is NOT registered (OQ-168 — BR-CUS-042 and BR-CUS-062 disagree),
and a caller must read that rather than infer it from silence.

get.description:
Step 1's picker: the PUBLISHED, service-compatible plans (BR-RAT-030),
the current plan for contrast, and each row's service-drop note.

A read, so any tenant role may see it — an Executive reviewing what a clerk
is about to do is A4's whole View posture.

post.description:
`POST /accounts/{id}/plan-changes/preview` — step 2's figures.

POST for a read, exactly as 11b §2.6 contracts it: the preview takes a
BODY (target plan, effective option or date) and a GET with that body in
the query string would be a cacheable URL carrying a customer's pending
plan change. It writes nothing — asserted in US-CUS-016 TC-1 — and the
response's `writes: []` says so on the wire.

Every figure in it comes from the rating engine or from the tenant's own
stored base charges; this layer computes no money at all (B8/LAW 0).

CS-27 — a MASTER account pays its TENANTS' bills with one cheque.

Same body as `POST /customers/{id}/payments`; the payer is the account in
the path and every part must name a unit account on that master's premises,
or the master's own account for money deliberately left as its credit.

⚠ **A PART THAT WOULD LEAVE MONEY AS A TENANT'S CREDIT IS REFUSED, WHOLE**
(BR-PAY-1130): the landlord's money must never sit on a different person's
account, where it would auto-apply to that person's next bill. Reduce the
row to what the unit owes and put the remainder on the master, which is the
only lawful home for a leftover.

**The master gets the TENDER and no payment entry**, except that leftover —
three signed rules force it and `premises_position.py`'s docstring carries
all three, because the next lane will otherwise "simplify" the payment onto
the master and credit a debt the master never had while four bills stay open.

get.description:
CS-27 — the building this master may pay for, unit by unit.

Read-only. `may_pay` rides on every row because CS-27's S22/S35 draws that
column by name and BR-SHL-025 forbids a control that cannot say why.

`GET` the protection panel · `POST` a new hold. Two verbs, one resource.

ONE view rather than two, on the `payments/api.write_offs` precedent, and
for a reason worth writing down: **two `path()` entries on one pattern is a
route the router can never reach.** Django resolves the FIRST match and
stops, so a second view mounted at `accounts/<id>/protections` would be dead
code that every test passes over — hard-won law 2 wearing a URL. This lane
wrote exactly that bug and `G52` caught it, which is the check working.

── GET — `DSC-02.2`'s protection panel ──

⚠ **`all_clear` IS COMPUTED OVER THE THREE PROTECTIONS THAT EXIST**, not
over `DSC-02.2`'s ten: six of the ten are unbuilt (`DEF-691` / `BR-CUS-101`).
It is served under its own name and a screen must NOT render it as the drawn
`All clear` chip — a green summary over six unasked questions is a fabricated
clearance on the screen that authorises a cut. The three-valued `outcome`
(`pass` · `fail` · **`unavailable`**) is what carries that honestly, and
`unavailable` is NOT `pass`.

── POST — record a medical or weather hold (`BR-CUS-039`) ──

**This is the act that stops a cut**, so its dates are the caller's and
never the server's: `effective_from` is required, and `expires_on` is
optional because a protection with no stated end is a real thing — the
check payload's `lifetime` field is what says which.

ONE view rather than two, on the `payments/api.write_offs` precedent, and
