get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/reconnection-terms` — `DSC-02.4`'s quote.

⛔ **`fee` IS NULLABLE AND NOTHING HERE SUBSTITUTES A NUMBER FOR IT.**
`BR-BIL-007`: the amount is the tenant's own charge code, and
`reconnection_terms` answers `None` with a reason when that code is not
configured or is not a flat amount. ⚠ **THIS READ *"`DEF-700` IS THE STATE
OF THIS TREE — no seed creates `CC-RECON`"* UNTIL 2026-09-21, AND BOTH
HALVES ARE NOW FALSE.** The PO ruled that day — *"reconnection fee is $75 -
fix the code and seed"* — and the code is spelled **`RECON`**, seeded at
**$75.00**, on every provisioned tenant. A tenant that deletes its row is
still a real state, which is why the absence stays; it is no longer the
DEFAULT one, and a literal here would still be quoting a price the product
cannot charge.

⚠ **`timing` IS `BR-CUS-104` AND IT IS NOT DECORATION:** the fee becomes owed
AT THE CUT, so what a customer must clear to be reconnected is their arrears
PLUS the fee. ⚠ **AND THIS PARAGRAPH SAID `posting` REPORTS THAT THE FEE
*"reaches AR through nothing today"* AND THAT THE GATE *"lets a customer
through short by exactly the fee"* — BOTH WERE CLOSED ON 2026-08-27 AND THE
SENTENCE OUTLIVED THEM BY THREE WEEKS (`DEF-CUS-6071`).** `DEF-708` is
fixed: `commit_cut` raises and ISSUES the fee, so it is in AR from the
moment of the cut and the gate that reads AR requires it.

⛔ **WHICH IS WHY `to_clear` IS NOT AN ADDITION ON A CUT ACCOUNT —
`DEF-CUS-6050`.** Once the fee is issued the position ALREADY holds it, so
`to_clear.total` is that position read ONCE and the fee is not added to it;
before the cut it is still arrears + fee. `to_clear.basis.fee_in_arrears`
says which of the two this answer is, and any caller building its own figure
out of a balance and this fee must read it. Worked on `A-11340`:
**$8,315.00** either side of the cut, never $8,390.00 and never $8,240.00.

post.description:
`POST /accounts/{id}/refund` — BR-CUS-081's settle-and-refund.

ADDED: no document or screen names this path (B18 §6.2's move-out row is
the two above), so it is REPORTED as an addition. It exists because
`refund_disposition` is a published callable of the settlement module and
hard-won law 2 is what happens to one nothing can reach.

*"settle the $142.30 from the $153.50 deposit and refund $11.20; the
account closes at zero and the bill does NOT stand."* BOTH movements come
back on one response, because a payload carrying only the refund reads as
"the whole deposit went back" — the reading the PO rejected.

Reachable ONLY on `refund_due`. `refused_excess` is refused by name and
belongs to `hold-excess` below (BR-CUS-096). **The amount is the
settlement's own and is never a caller input**, so a clerk cannot refund a
figure they typed; `method` is the closed vocabulary ACH · mailed cheque ·
carry to new account, and the forwarding street is required for the CHEQUE
alone.

It does not PAY. Payments owns `refunds`, whose `payment_id` is NOT NULL
with no account column (OQ-195), so a deposit excess has no row to become —
the response says so in `execution_unavailable[]` and this layer does not
soften it.

`POST /accounts/{id}/refunds` — RAISE one. J15 step 1 (CR-059 CS-6).

The body is S58's Record-refund form:

    payment_id       the overpayment this draws back — REQUIRED (see below)
    amount           decimal STRING, > 0
    method           `check` or `ach`; `card` is refused with its rails note
    requested_at     the clerk's business moment — REQUIRED, never a clock
    reference        the cheque number — the service REQUIRES it for cheques
    reason           optional
    memo             optional
    idempotency_key  the form's submit token — REQUIRED

**NO MONEY MOVES HERE** (`BR-PAY-014`). The row exists so J15 step 2's
approval queue has something to show and so `BR-PAY-037`'s *"both acts
recorded distinctly"* has somewhere to record the first one. 201 on a new
request, **200 on a replay** with the original — the `account_payments`
argument, applied to the same clerk and the same double click.

⚠ **`payment_id` IS NOW OPTIONAL — CS-7 LANDED 2026-09-03, AND THIS
PARAGRAPH USED TO SAY THE OPPOSITE.** It read: *"`payment_id` … REQUIRED"*,
and that a refund could name only one payment because `refunds.payment_id`
was `NOT NULL` with no `account_id` beside it. **Both halves are now
false.** `payments/0018` carries the PO's ruling of 2026-09-01 (`OQ-195`,
option (a)): the column is nullable and `refunds.account_id` is NOT NULL.
Corrected in place rather than deleted, because hard-won law 1 is what a
stale guarantee in a docstring costs.

**So the ACCOUNT in the path is the address, and it always was** — this
route was built for this ruling on 2026-09-01, before the schema could hold
it. What changed is only that the body field is now genuinely optional:

  * **`payment_id` given** — the credit came from ONE overpayment and the
    refund says so. PE-9's **$350.00 → $57.13** is unchanged.
  * **`payment_id` omitted** — **the case CS-7 exists for.** The credit was
    built from several payments; the refund is against the account's credit
    balance and names none of them. The PO's own worked figure: **$40.00 in
    June plus $17.13 in July refunded as one $57.13 cheque.**
    `GET /accounts/{id}/credit-sources` is what lists the payments behind
    it, because listing them is evidence and not a link.

**SO THE PATH SEGMENT IS ENFORCED RATHER THAN DECORATIVE.** A `payment_id`
naming another account's payment is refused here, by name. Without that
check the account in the URL would be a label — a clerk on account A's
screen could raise a refund funded by account B's overpayment, and every
downstream figure (the credit test, the offset, the ledger) would be
account B's while the screen said A.

⚠ **`cross_account_check` IS ALWAYS TRUE AND IS NOT A CLIENT CHOICE.**
*"Offset first"* is CONFIRMED law (PO 2026-08-12, `OQ-135` CLOSED): a
customer holding a credit on one account and an arrear on another has the
credit applied to the debt before any refund is paid. Letting the form send
`false` would let a screen switch a ruling off. On the repo fixture the
refusal is **$57.13** of credit against **$948.20** overdue on a sibling
account with a final notice already sent — the refund does not go out, and
the clerk is told which account and roughly how much.

**What that refusal is NOT is the offset being APPLIED.** Moving the credit
is a balance TRANSFER between two financial records with one reviewed writer
(CS-8, task 31), and `offset_before_refund` computes both figures and moves
nothing. Until CS-8 lands, a customer owing elsewhere cannot be refunded
here at all — which is the ruled behaviour, and is stated so the screen lane
renders the refusal rather than a spinner.

`POST /accounts/{id}/settle-shortfall` — S20 step 4 (B18 §6.2).

*"Step 4 decides where the remaining balance goes. It cannot be skipped."*
Reachable ONLY on the `short` landing; every other landing is refused by
name (`customers.move_out.no_shortfall`) rather than recording a decision
about nothing. `path` is one of three — collect · payment_plan · transfer — and an
unknown one is refused with the closed set. ⚠ `write_off` is refused BY
NAME (`customers.move_out.write_off_not_at_move_out`, PO 2026-10-12,
*"MOVE-OUT DOES NOT WRITE OFF"*): the balance stays outstanding and is
chased (BR-CUS-082); Finance or a System Admin writes it off later in
Payments (BR-PAY-020).

**The transfer TARGET is resolved from the data and is never a caller
argument** (BR-CUS-097: *"a transfer cannot be built against an ambiguous
target"*), which is what makes US-BIL-011 TC-6's forged transfer
unrepresentable rather than merely rejected. No account id in this body is
read as a destination.

200: the decision is RECORDED — an `audit_log` row written by the service,
`persisted: false` on the wire. ⚠ On `transfer` the books MOVE since
2026-10-14 (`OQ-1250` → a, `CR-185-BRC10`): one AR→AR entry, owner account
DR / this account CR, reported as `posting.posted: true`; on collect and
payment plan no money moves.

`POST /accounts/{id}/statement` — queue this account's statement.

Body: `{"from": "2026-07-01", "to": "2026-07-31", "copy_no": 0}`.

`copy_no` is the one deliberate door through hard rule 6's key and it is
the human's: asking again for the SAME period returns the same rows with
`created: false`, and a clerk who genuinely wants a second copy passes
`copy_no: 1`. That is the same posture a bill reprint takes (US-BIL-024
TC-4), and it is why a double-clicked button cannot queue two statements.

Hard rule 7's audit row is written by the queue's owner for the queue
write, naming the actor handed down here. This view writes none of its own:
a second row would be two records of one event, and a statement moves no
money to audit separately.

get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/transfer-preview?to=&amount=` — BR-PAY-866's *before*.

A GET, because it writes nothing and changes nothing: the same read may be
taken twice, by two clerks, with no consequence.

Answers what the money will MEET on the destination — bill by bill, in that
tenant's own order — what will carry as credit, and what the source will hold
afterwards. CS-31's own note is why it is a server read rather than a screen
sum: *"It must be computed by the service, not assembled on the screen, or
the warning and the outcome can disagree."*

post.description:
`POST /accounts/{id}/transfers` — CS-8, the keystone (S21 · S58).

The body is the Transfer modal:

    to_account_id    the sibling account — REQUIRED
    amount           a decimal STRING; a float is refused (rule 2)
    moved_on         the caller's business day — REQUIRED, never a clock
    reason           REQUIRED free text; the audit row is the only durable
                     record of why a customer's money moved
    memo             optional, written on both legs
    idempotency_key  the modal's submit token — REQUIRED

**201 on a new transfer, 200 on a replay**, both carrying both legs and
`created`.

⚠ **THIS DOOR DOES NOT OFFSET A REFUND AUTOMATICALLY, and that is the lane
judgment recorded on 2026-09-03 rather than an omission.** `refunds.
request_refund` still REFUSES when the customer owes elsewhere and names the
arrear; a person then opens this door and presses Transfer. Making the
refund path call this one would move a joint holder's money with nobody
looking, which is the risk OQ-135's own option (b) was written against.

get.description:
`GET /accounts/{id}/units` — **every unit at a master account's address,
its live occupancy, and who its bill goes to** (`BR-CUS-1094`).

PO 2026-09-23, verbatim: *"show all units with its status what wil be billed
to master account - can we do that?"*

⚠ **IT WRITES NOTHING AND IT STORES NOTHING**, which is not tidiness here
but the rule itself: `BR-CUS-1094` is a prohibition as well as a ruling —
*"No column may cache which units a master account pays for, because a
cached answer is wrong the first time a tenant moves in and nothing would
go red."* Every answer on this payload is derived at read time from the two
seam reads `apps/billing/gather` uses, so what this screen shows is what a
bill run starting NOW would decide.

**404 for an account that is not a master**, through the 404-never-403
refusal every other read in this module uses: an ordinary account has no
building to answer for, and saying *"this account is not a master"* to
somebody who may not be allowed to know the account exists is the leak that
refusal shape exists to prevent.

A READ — no audit row (`CLAUDE.md` hard rule 7 is about money ACTIONS).

`GET /accounts/{id}/usage` — the ACC-01 Usage tab's chart and KPI strip.

⚠ **MOUNTED FROM `metering`, NOT FROM `customers`, AND THE PATH IS STILL
`/accounts/…`.** `meter_read_monthly_usage` is metering's table (BR-MET-106
is a metering rule and the figure is Σ over `meter_reads`), so the module
that owns the data serves it; the URL names the RESOURCE a clerk is looking
at, which is an account. `apps/customers/api.py` lists the
`/accounts/{id}/…` subpaths it deliberately does not serve and `usage` is
not among them, so nothing is being taken from another module.

NO 11b ROW TO FOLLOW — the usage surface has no contract entry, like the
eleven `/reads` routes and the nine `/imports` routes before it. House
grammar (resource, then subpath); REPORTED for the A11 addendum with them.

`?months=` accepts r10's own filter vocabulary (12 or 24) and FALLS BACK to
24 for anything else rather than 4xx-ing (BR-SHL-011).

**It does not recompute.** A GET that writes is a GET that surprises
somebody; `monthly_usage_service.recompute_account` is the writer and is
called by the lane that changes reads. An account whose months have never
been computed therefore serves an empty `series` and every month ABSENT,
which is the truthful answer to *"what has been stated about this
account?"* — see the frontend's own stated absence.

`GET /accounts/{id}/work-orders` — the jobs on this account and at its address.

⚠ **THE ADDRESS IS THE PREMISES', REACHED BY WALKING** (`BR-MET-1161`, PO
2026-09-04). An account declares no address column and must not grow one, so
the premises is found account → unit → premises and the orders are gathered
from there. An account naming no unit gets its own orders and nothing else —
a true, smaller list rather than a guessed larger one.

Each row carries `stands_on`, so the screen can say whether a job stands on
this account or on the address it shares (`US-WRK-004`).

CR-028 AST-W5 T3 (§10-D6 RULED): every non-retired asset standing on a
geocoded premises — the AST-03 map's markers, popup facts and filter
vocabularies. No work-order fact (§10-D7).

CR-028 AST-W5 T2 (§10-D3 RULED): the Lifecycle tab's three lists +
the Asset value panel, ONE call (B16 §4.8's contract). NO GL sentence,
no depreciation posting — the panel is BR-AST-047 arithmetic only.

`GET /assets/metered-services` — BR-TEN-162 / DEF-901.

Which utility services this tenant ACTUALLY METERS, read from its own
asset register. The S64 read-validation page asks it before drawing a
threshold form, because thresholds judge READINGS and a service with no
meter produces none: the PO asked *"are these settings applicable to
sewer"* of a page offering fourteen tunable inputs for a service priced as
a percentage of water (BR-RAT-015).

⚠ **IT IS A READ OF THE ESTATE, NOT A LIST OF "UNMETERED SERVICES".** A
utility that genuinely meters sewer gets `sewer` in this list and gets the
form, with nothing to configure anywhere. See
`selectors.metered_service_codes` for what counts as a meter and why
lifecycle stage is deliberately not a predicate.

`AnyTenantRole` on purpose: it is the same fact `GET /assets` already
serves any tenant role, aggregated — no cost, no money, no identity — and
the settings page that consumes it is behind its own A4 gate already.

CR-028 AST-W4 (AST-05 step 1): the series suggestion + the UNIQUE
availability probe. A READ on tenancy's preview contract — nothing
allocates, nothing advances (`selectors.asset_no_preview`); `available`
is null when no number was asked about, never a guess.

`GET /assets/size-banded-services` — `DEF-AST-7660`.

Which of this tenant's ENABLED services price by SIZE BAND, which do not,
and which nobody has ruled. An assign form reads it to know whether the
connection size is REQUIRED before the clerk presses `Assign ✓`, instead
of finding out inside a bill run months later.

⚠ **IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE BROWSER MUST NOT INFER THIS.** See
`selectors.size_banded_services` — the obvious client-side substitute is
`DEF-3098`'s retired proxy and would refuse a solar install for a size
that service does not have.

⚠ **THREE LISTS AND NOT A BOOLEAN PER SERVICE.** `not_ruled` is a real
answer and collapsing it into `not_banded` would silently tell a screen
that a blank size is lawful on a service nobody has been asked about —
the prime directive resolved by a default. **It is EMPTY on every tenant
today** (measured 2026-09-28): the one unruled thing is the DIMENSION
`thermal_heat_steam`, and a dimension is not a service code. The list
exists for the twelfth service, not for a case running now.

`AnyTenantRole`: no money, no cost, no identity — it is a projection of
ratified law plus the tenant's own enabled-service list, and every screen
that consumes it is behind its own gate already, exactly like
`GET /assets/metered-services` above.

CR-028 AST-W5 T1 (§10-D5 RULED: counts & costs ONLY): the Inventory
tab's aggregate — uninstalled (behavior class `available`) grouped by
type, with the honest-null costs. No reorder, no van, no stock table.

`GET /assets/{id}/assignments?page=&per=` — US-AST-006's Assignment
history, SERVER-PAGED (`AST-B-24` · `DEF-MET-4995` · `NFR-3`).

The envelope is `{count, next, previous, results}` — the same four names
`GET /assets` and `GET /assets/{id}/work-orders` already answer with, so an
asset detail screen reads ONE convention across all four of its lists
instead of three different ones. `07-frontend/src/api/paginated.ts` is that
convention's single declaration on the client side.

CR-028 AST-W2 (DEF-475 closed): US-AST-005's Reads tab, SERVED — the
asset's committed heads with BR-AST-029's typed pair folded per date.
Quantities with explicit units only; no money (BR-AST-016/025).

`GET /assets/{id}/usage` — the trailing-12-month strip, PER REGISTER.

PO verbatim, 2026-08-26: *"We ahve to calcualet last 12 month consumption
from these readings and display it on account and meters"*. The account
half is `/accounts/{id}/usage` above; this is the meter half CR-038's
ADDITION section measured as the gap.

⚠ **THE TWO ENDPOINTS ARE NOT THE SAME QUERY WITH A DIFFERENT KEY, AND THE
PAYLOAD SAYS SO.** The account one reads the STORED `monthly_usage` rows;
that table is keyed (account, service, month) and has no asset or channel
grain, so it cannot answer for one meter — let alone for one register of a
TOU meter, whose windows BR-MET-135/BR-RAT-014 forbid blending. This one
computes from the meter's own committed reads through the SAME
`monthly_usage` rules module, and publishes `source:
"computed_from_reads"` plus `stored_source_absent` naming **OQ-421** so a
reader comparing two figures knows which is which. See
`apps/metering/asset_usage.py` for the whole disposition.

`?months=` takes 12 or 24 and FALLS BACK to 12 rather than 4xx-ing
(BR-SHL-011) — 12 because that is the PO's own word for this task.

Mounted from `metering` on an `/assets/…` path for the same reason
`/accounts/{id}/usage` is: the module that owns `meter_reads` owns the
figure, and the URL names the resource the clerk is looking at. No 11b row
to follow; REPORTED for the A11 addendum with the others.

`GET /assets/{id}/work-order-templates?page=&per=` — what may be raised
HERE: the asset's TYPE (a template naming no type is unrestricted, not
inapplicable) and its SERVICE (`CR-168-BRC10` P2.21), paged in SQL. The
envelope, plus `asset`. (SRV-2's one-round `rows` twin was retired by lane
SRV-3 once lane RAISE read only `results`, 2.501.0.)

`GET /assets/{id}/work-orders` — every job raised against this asset.

Serves the Maintenance history's Work-order column (`BR-WRK-056`: *no column
is added to `AssetMaintenance`*) and `Work-028`'s own list. A cross-tenant
id yields an empty page rather than a 404 — the same sentence as *nothing
has been raised for this asset* (hard rule 1).
GET /audit-log — S61's list. No other verb is defined here (BR-AUD-002).

post.description: POST /audit-log/export — 202 + job_id (B12 r1 async contract).

get.description:
GET /audit-log/{id} — the US-AUD-005 drawer payload (who/what/when/
entity/before/after). Read-only: no other verb is defined (BR-AUD-002).

GET /audit-log/{id}/diagnostic — **the reproduction record, System Admin only.**

CR-067 task B2's missing half (`DEF-3321`). `error_diagnostics` has been
written, referenced and swept since the A-tasks landed, and **nothing read it
back**: this module defined three routes, none of them touched that table,
and `apps/audit/diagnostic_models.py`'s own trailer said so —
`D=deferred(no endpoint of its own)`. So the six lines CR-067 §5 measures the
whole change against — the exception, where in the code, which job step,
which release, the settings in force, the request's field names — could not
reach any screen in this product. Hard-won law 2 one layer lower than usual:
not a component nothing passes a prop to, a TABLE nothing serves.

⚠ **`SystemAdminOnly` HERE IS THE BOUNDARY, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE
ENDPOINT AS MUCH AS THE DATA IS.** Every other route in this module is
`AdminOrExecutive` (BR-AUD-009 — *"read-only; System Admin + Executive"*),
and the S61 drawer's own role check is `BR-SHL-025` CONVENIENCE: both halves
of that drawer come out of the ONE payload `GET /audit-log/{id}` already
serves, so `useTenantRole` decides what is DRAWN and an Executive holds the
bytes either way. **A separate read is what turns that into a real gate:**
the technical record now arrives on its own request, and an Executive asking
for it is refused 403 AUTH-002 by the server with the BR-AUD-018 attempt row
written, whatever the browser thinks. `DEF-3321`'s own prevention column asks
for exactly this.

⚠ **WHY A NARROWER GATE THAN THE SCREEN IT SITS ON IS NOT A CONTRADICTION.**
BR-AUD-009 says who may read the TRAIL — what was attempted, by whom, when,
and the plain-words reason. This serves something else: frames, a release, a
deployment's configuration. CR-067 §3's approved table already says *"a second
section in the same row's drawer, **System Admin only**"*, so the narrowing is
the change request's own, ratified with it, and not a choice made here.
Reported for the BR-AUD-009 amendment alongside `f.outcome`.

**Read-only by construction**, like every other row resource here: `get` is
the only handler, so POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE answer 405 from DRF's own dispatch
(BR-AUD-002 / HR-4). There is no write path to a diagnostic at all — the
kernel's sink is the only writer, and the sweep is the only remover.

**NO `audit_log` ROW IS WRITTEN FOR A SUCCESSFUL READ**, which is hard rule 7
read as it is written: the trail attaches to a MONEY action, and no read on
this screen — including `GET /audit-log/{id}` itself — writes one. A REFUSED
read is audited already, by the BE-02 handler's BR-AUD-018 attempt row, which
is the half that matters for a System-Admin-only door.

post.description:
`POST auth/activation/check` — FF-56: `{code, identifier}` (a work email
or phone number; `email` still accepted) → who the account
is for, the utility, its password rules, and a ticket for FF-57.

`POST auth/activation/complete` — FF-57: own password + device name →
signed in (the same answer as `POST auth/token`).

`POST auth/password-link/check` — `{token}` → who it is for, the utility
and its password rules. Public and throttled; one refusal for every way a
link can be dead (BR-IDN-002). POST, so the token never sits in a log.

`POST auth/password-link/complete` — the person's own password. Spends
the link, activates an invited membership, ends every session; the person
then signs in (BR-IDN-022 as amended 2026-10-05).

delete.description:
Sign-in is UNAUTHENTICATED but never tenant-less (BR-IDN-001).

Since the PO's 2026-08-10 ruling the tenant comes from the path, so the
route is `/api/{tenant}/auth/session`: require_tenant() resolves it FIRST
and answers a plain 404 when the slug names no tenant — the same body a
foreign-session request gets, so neither reveals which tenants exist.

post.description:
Sign-in is UNAUTHENTICATED but never tenant-less (BR-IDN-001).

Since the PO's 2026-08-10 ruling the tenant comes from the path, so the
route is `/api/{tenant}/auth/session`: require_tenant() resolves it FIRST
and answers a plain 404 when the slug names no tenant — the same body a
foreign-session request gets, so neither reveals which tenants exist.

get.description:
`GET auth/sign-in-options` — is *"Keep me signed in"* offered here?

⚠ **IT IS PUBLIC BECAUSE THE SCREEN THAT ASKS IT IS.** The sign-in form is
rendered before anybody has a session, so a signed-in read cannot answer
it. Without this, a utility that switches the tick box off would still see
it drawn, and the person ticking it would be refused at sign-in with no
idea why — hard-won law 2's mirror, a live control over a dead setting.

⚠ **IT RETURNS ONE BOOLEAN AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE READ.** Not the
policy, not the limits, not the timeouts, not the lockout numbers. Those
are an attacker's reconnaissance — *"this utility locks after three
attempts for five minutes"* tells a password sprayer exactly how to pace
itself — and none of them changes what the sign-in FORM looks like. The
serialiser here is a literal dict rather than the policy payload with
fields removed, because a filter is one edit away from leaking and a
literal is not.

⚠ **AND IT DISCLOSES NO TENANT.** An unknown utility gets the DEFAULT
answer (`True`), never a 404 — a 404 here would turn this into a free
"does this utility exist" oracle for anyone who can spell a subdomain,
which is the same enumeration `BR-IDN-002` forbids one door along.
`require_tenant` has already refused a slug that resolves to nothing, so
what is left is the ordinary case of a tenant with no policy row.

Throttled exactly as the other public reads are (11b G12):
`PublicOnboardingThrottle`, 60/min.

delete.description:
`POST auth/token` — sign in on the native app → bearer tokens.
`DELETE auth/token` — sign out THIS sign-in (the bearer in the header).

Public for the same reason `auth/session` is: a caller who could already
authenticate would not be signing in. DELETE authenticates by hand, as the
cookie's sign-out does, so the POST half can stay public.

post.description:
`POST auth/token` — sign in on the native app → bearer tokens.
`DELETE auth/token` — sign out THIS sign-in (the bearer in the header).

Public for the same reason `auth/session` is: a caller who could already
authenticate would not be signing in. DELETE authenticates by hand, as the
cookie's sign-out does, so the POST half can stay public.

`POST auth/token/refresh` — `{refresh_token, device_id?}` → a new pair.
Single use; a spent token presented again ends the sign-in for both.

get.description:
The S32 chip's and S33 column's rows (US-PAY-024).

There is no POST and no action route here, and that is BR-PAY-015 rather
than an omission: an intent is recorded by BILL ISSUE and nothing in v1 may
charge anybody. A retry endpoint would be a charging path with a name.

`GET /bad-debt?f.start=&f.end=` — CS-26's report (S36 Revenue & AR).

Bad debt by reason and by month over the window, netted for CS-25 reversals,
with the ledger's own write-off total computed independently and served
beside it. Money at four decimals, shares at six, both beside a CHAR(3) code.

`f.reason` narrows the ACCOUNT list (`/bad-debt/accounts`), not this — the
totals are the whole point of the report and a filtered total that still
called itself the total would be the defect this exists to avoid.

`GET /bad-debt/accounts?f.start=&f.end=&f.reason=` — the rows behind a bar.

Same window and same statuses as the report, one row per write-off, so a
reviewer clicking *"uncollectible, 2,840.00"* sees exactly the rows that
figure is made of and the two reads can never disagree about what is in it.
S38 step 1's picker — the tenant's LIVE bank accounts (B2 r14 #1).

post.description: Explain a fee line → Bank fees (6800) against cash; or link a Reverse's fee.

get.description: Bank fees already posted on a Reverse that this fee line could be.

post.description:
Match a returned line to its payment — reversing it once if nobody has.

Posts the returned amount holding → cash (PO 2026-10-30, G3 = A). A second
submit of the same pair answers 200 with the row that exists.

CS-16 — explain a bank line that is not a deposit of ours. S40, from a line.

*"Every bank line ends the period either matched or explained, with a reason
and a GL. Silence is not a state."* `reason_code` must be one of this
utility's own reconciliation difference reasons once it has any (CS-18), and
`gl_account_id` must be a live account of its own chart.

**NOTHING IS POSTED.** Creating a journal entry from an unmatched bank line
is batch decision G3 and the PO has not ruled on it, so the explanation is
recorded, the books are untouched, and `unavailable[]` says so on every
response. A second submit of the SAME explanation answers 200 with the row
that exists; a DIFFERENT one is refused, quoting what the line already says.

get.description: The payments a RETURNED line could be — by amount, cheque number and date.

CS-18 — differences grouped by reason AND GL account, over a period.

*How much was processor fees this quarter, how much was error.* `from` and
`to` are required business dates: a report whose period defaulted to
"everything" would answer a question nobody asked and would keep answering
it as the register grows.

Each row is counted under the MONEY's own date — a batch explanation under
its banking day, a line explanation under the bank's posted day — never
under the day somebody typed it.

post.description:
CS-17 — tie MANY bank lines to one batch, or one line to many batches.

The PO's own case (2026-08-12, OQ-161): a $2,840.00 cheque batch and a
$14,280.00 ACH batch banked the same afternoon, posted by the bank as ONE
credit of $17,120.00. Before this route neither batch could ever reconcile.

`bank_line_ids[]` and `batch_ids[]` are both required and the set's two
sides must foot EXACTLY — a set that does not tie is refused with both sums
named, because nothing rules how to apportion a difference across members.
A double submit of the same membership answers **200** with the set that
exists and `created:false`, never a red 409 (hard rule 6).

S38 steps 1–2 — persist the statement, then auto-match the unambiguous.

The file arrives as `file_base64` because this API is JSON end to end and a
multipart branch here would be a second request shape for one operation.
The bytes are decoded and handed to the engine unchanged — nothing in this
layer parses a bank file, and `lockbox.py` is the only parser.

Idempotent on **file + tags** (BR-PAY-028 🔒): re-importing the same bytes
for the same account and period is REFUSED naming who imported them first,
when, and the import's id. That refusal is a 422 carrying the sentence, not
a silent second copy of every line.

get.description:
S38 step 2, re-openable — every line's CURRENT state, not a replay.

Recomputed from the persisted link rather than by re-running the matcher, so
a pairing a human named an hour ago is still there when they come back.

CS-14 — the reconciliation STATEMENT for one imported bank statement.

**IT STATES TWO FACTS AND EXPLAINS THE GAP; IT ADJUSTS NEITHER SIDE.** PO
ruling 2026-09-02 (`OQ-1310` CLOSED), verbatim: *"we need to go on factual
basis, if bank as report we count if bank did not report we dont count, and
if clark wants to balance the book they can always make journal entries on
their own - that is allowed"*. So the body carries the bank's own closing
figure, the books' cash, and the difference between them —
`difference_bank_less_books`, named so a screen cannot render it the wrong
way round — with the reconciling items listed beside it, AGED, as the
explanation. **No adjusted balance and no sign on any item**, which is what
supersedes CS-14's stated arithmetic. Every figure is assembled from rows
that already exist, so this can never disagree with S37 beside it.

**Absences are served as `null` and never as `0.00`**, each with its reason
in `unavailable[]`: a statement imported before the balances existed, or a
chart with no designated cash account, makes the difference UNKNOWN — which
is a different answer from "the two agree" and only one of them is good news.
S8's Bill layout tab — what we print on, and what else we could print on.

post.description:
Choose the tenant's bill layout. **Future bills only** (BR-BIL-026).

`SystemAdminOnly` at the decorator AND `publish`'s own role check behind it,
and the doubling is deliberate: BR-BIL-027's TC-2 asks for *"absent/disabled-
with-reason **and** server-rejected"*, and the service check is what holds
when the next caller is a script rather than this screen.

A repeat of the live choice answers 200 with `changed: false` rather than
minting an identical version — see `choose_layout`. It is not an error: a
clerk clicking the layout they are already on has asked for the state they
already have.

get.description:
A layout, drawn on this tenant's most recent bill, as `application/pdf`.

INLINE, because the whole point is to look at it: the frame on S8 shows the
page and the browser's own viewer carries print and save, which is the same
posture `invoice_document_pdf` takes for a real bill.

⚠ **IT WRITES NOTHING.** No version, no pin, no stored document, no audit
row — CLAUDE.md rule 7 asks for an audit row on every MONEY ACTION and this
moves no money and changes no record. Choosing a layout is the money-shaped
act and `choose_bill_layout` audits it.

post.description:
S30 One-time tab step 3 — the run row and ONE draft bill (BR-BIL-020).

201, with the draft's own figures inline. A draft is not money (BR-BIL-004),
so this is safe to serve as a plain create; what it is NOT is an issue, and
the response says so by carrying `unavailable` — the tab renders it, so a
clerk learns the bill cannot be sent yet from the screen rather than from a
later refusal they cannot explain.

A repeat is 409 BIZ-IDEMPOTENT with who/when/link (BR-BIL-005). That matters
more here than on a cycle run: a double-clicked *Create bill* on a move-out
would otherwise produce TWO final bills for one tenancy, and a final bill is
the one nobody looks at again.

get.description:
S30 One-time bill step 1 — the account card, from the ACCOUNT (`DEF-BIL-8281`).

Read the moment an account is chosen, independent of the preview: the
preview refuses while a required step-1 field is empty, and the card's
Plan, Cycle, Last bill and the Days-to-pay default are facts about the
account, not about a bill. Writes nothing; another tenant's id is a 404
through customers' own tenant-scoped read (hard rule 1).

post.description:
S30 One-time bill step 1 — `DEF-BIL-10068` / `DEF-BIL-10069`.

The same body as the preview; answers `{duplicate, closed_month}` the
moment the period is picked, without pricing anything and without
writing. A POST for the preview's reason: the body is a request, and a
cached answer would hide a draft discarded a second ago. The rules and the
PO's words are `one_time_answer.period_check`'s docstring.

S30 One-time tab step 2 (US-BIL-010..014) — *"See what they'd owe"*.

A POST that writes nothing, and the verb is the honest one: the body carries
a period, a kind and (for a catch-up) a list of sub-periods, which is more
than a query string should hold, and re-previewing must not be cached by an
intermediary — a clerk who fixes a plan and previews again must see the fix.

Every refusal a preview can produce is a REFUSAL rather than an empty
result. Single-account mode has one account and one waiting clerk, so
`prepare_run`'s both-halves shape (which exists to stop one bad account
hiding 493 others) has nothing to protect here.

Contract §5 — *Send*: authorise and issue this run's ONE draft (US-BIL-033).

🔒 HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING — the door into financial immutability for every
one-time bill; the money half is `one_time_send.send`, whose docstring is
the long form. Row in 12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md.

Refused, before anything is read, unless all FIVE release confirmations
arrive as literal `true` — compliance, email, text, autopay and final (PO
ruling 2026-09-30, option B; each untaken one named on
`confirmations.<name>`, `billing.oneTime.err.confirmRequired`); the run
stays a draft and no number is spent. The single *"I checked the amounts"*
tick this used to take is retired. `delivery` is one of three words and
`sent_at` is the clerk's instant with its offset (BR-TEN-043 — never a
clock). **Idempotent:** a second call answers `200` with the SAME bill.
A cycle run's id answers 404 here: this door is for one-time runs only, and
a cycle run is released through S31's own gate.

get.description:
The Pending-billing QUEUE (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-006) — S30's chip and list.

*"Hold ≠ forget."* This is the door back for every account a run did not
bill: the row, its age, whether it has escalated, and WHICH DOOR it came
through (a phase-1 hold — never calculated — or a phase-3 mark-for-later,
which was calculated and broke at a named stage).

`as_of` is a REQUIRED query parameter and is not defaulted to a server
clock. Aging is measured against the TENANT's today (BR-TEN-043, gate G6),
and a queue re-opened from another timezone must not silently age its own
rows by a day. The refusal names the parameter rather than guessing.

`escalation_days` is accepted for the same reason it is an argument in the
service: the tenant setting BR-BIL-021 requires does not exist yet, so the
story's fixture value is the DEFAULT and a caller that knows the tenant's
number passes it. Reported in the body's `unavailable`, never implied.

`GET` — what a set would contain. `POST` — produce it.

⚠ **THE POST TAKES THE CALLER'S INSTANT AND READS NO CLOCK** (`BR-TEN-043`,
gate G6 — there is no `timezone.now()` anywhere under `apps/billing/`). The
archive's filename says when it was made, and a worker that picked the job
up an hour later must not name the file with its own queue latency. The
client sends `new Date().toISOString()`, exactly as the release gate does.

get.description:
`GET /billing/print-sets/bills` — the bills in this period, one page.

⚠ **THE SCREEN HAD THE FORM, THE COUNTS AND THE BUTTON AND NO LIST**
(`DEF-BIL-5354`). The blueprint's note names what that costs: *"A clerk's
commonest question here is not how many — it is IS THIS CUSTOMER'S BILL IN
THE SET, usually because that customer has rung. Without a searchable table
the answer is generate it and look in the zip."*

**ONE TABLE FOR THE WHOLE POPULATION, NOT TWO.** Every bill the selection
holds is listed, each carrying whether it will print and, when it will not,
the reason — because *"two tables would make a clerk searching for one bill
look twice, and the counts would stop reconciling the moment a filter was
applied."*

**PAGED IN THE DATABASE, AND THE TOTAL COMES FROM IT** (`NFR-3`/`NFR-5`).
At the top of the ICP a print set is tens of thousands of bills; the page is
taken by `StandardPagination` and only the rows on screen are serialised or
judged. The verdict costs ONE extra statement for the whole page —
`forecast_rows` composes the address seam as a single `id__in` rather than
asking it a row at a time.

`status` IS NOT ACCEPTED HERE EITHER, for `print_set_selection`'s reason:
the selection is issued and paid bills always, so a status control would
offer a narrowing the server is about to override.

post.description:
`POST /billing/remittance/parse` — what the scanner just typed, taken apart.

    line   REQUIRED — the characters the wedge sent, guards included

Answers the three fields and the amount as a DECIMAL STRING beside the
minor units it was read from. The string is what the form fills (hard rule
2: money never travels as a JSON number), and the minor units travel too so
a caller can show the clerk exactly what the barcode said.

get.description:
Screen 16's `DEFAULTS` group — WHAT TO OFFER AND WHAT IT OPENS ON. READ ONLY.

The blueprint calls this group *"the single biggest error-reducer in this
redraw"* (p047): three decisions a clerk makes ONCE instead of hundreds of
times per account. To draw it a screen needs three things it cannot know —
which cases carry a standing answer, which choices each offers, and what the
tenant's own setting opens each control on.

⚠ **IT EXISTS SO THAT NO LIST IS TYPED INTO A SCREEN.** The PO's instruction
of 2026-09-14 is *"no hardcoding"*, and `resolve_case_defaults` obeys it by
spelling no literal at all — it validates against `decisions.CHOICES_BY_CASE`
and fills from `settings_seam.run_case_defaults()`. A browser that carried
its own copy of those words would drift off them the day either changed, and
the failure mode is a control that submits a choice the server then refuses.
`decisions.CHOICES_BY_CASE` says exactly this in its own docstring about
S31.3, and this is the same argument one screen earlier.

⚠ **`holds` IS SERVED PER CHOICE BECAUSE THE DRAWING REQUIRES IT**: *"every
option states whether it bills or holds"* (p032, p036 — *"Two of them hold
and produce no bill, and a clerk cannot be expected to know which"*). It is
read from `decisions.HOLDING_CHOICES`, the same set `_is_held` reads, so the
word on the option and the behaviour at prepare time cannot disagree.

⚠ **NO WORDS FOR A CLERK ARE SERVED HERE, DELIBERATELY.** The codes are the
contract; the catalogues render them. A sentence composed in this module
would be a twelfth locale nobody translates (G15/G18), and the two absences
this product distinguishes — *no such choice* and *no catalogue entry* —
would collapse into one.

⚠ **THE THREE CASES COME FROM `RUN_CASE_DEFAULT_KEYS`, NOT FROM THIS FILE.**
That mapping is the one place a settings key is spelled, which is why
`runs.py` never spells one; naming the three here would be the second copy
the whole arrangement exists to avoid.

Screen 16's `SCOPE` group and its `WHAT THIS COVERS` card. READ ONLY.

**EVERY FIGURE IS A COUNT — no money and no forecast**, which is the
drawing's own note and a cost rule before it is a taste rule: resolving a
scope FOR REAL costs the measured 137 ms per account, so a card that showed
what a scope was worth would pay for the whole run to draw its header.

⚠ **IT RESOLVES A SCOPE; IT DOES NOT SCOPE A RUN, AND IT SAYS SO.** A run's
idempotency key is cycle + period and carries no scope, so a narrowed run
consumes the key for the whole period and everything it left out is refused
as a duplicate — with no exclusion row written, so those accounts never
reach the held queue and nothing ever bills them. `committable` is therefore
FALSE for every narrowed scope, with the limit stated in the clerk's own
words. A scope chooser shipped over that key is a revenue hole with a
dropdown on it; this is the half of it that can ship today.

Parameters: `cycle_id` (required), `scope` (one of the drawn kinds,
defaulting to the whole cycle), `scope_id` (repeatable) and `f.service`
(repeatable — the services a run would be narrowed to).

`GET` — SET-07D's **Runs** tab (CR-029 RC-W4b, B17 §4). `POST` — S31
step 1's exit (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-001): ONE `bill_runs` row in draft.

── THE GET ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
**THE BLUEPRINT'S SCREEN 27, §07 Past billing runs (p145–p146).** Seven
drawn columns — RUN · CYCLE · PERIOD · BILLS · VALUE · RUN BY · STATUS —
newest first, with four tiles above them and a real pager below. The cycle
detail's own Runs tab reads the same route with `f.cycle_id`.

**PARAMS:** BR-SHL-011's grammar. `q` searches run number, cycle and person
(the placeholder's own three things); `f.cycle_id`, `f.status` and `f.year`
are the three chips the toolbar draws; `page` and `per` page it, `per`
clamping to 50/100/200/500/1000. There is NO `sort`: p146 draws no sort
affordance on any heading, and a control nobody drew is a control invented
(B14 rule 37 — build the shape, not the figures).

⚠ **IT USED TO TAKE A CLAMPED `limit` WITH NO TOTAL AND THE REASON GIVEN
HAS EXPIRED (amended 2026-09-15).** The old note argued *"a run history grows
at the TOP, so page 2 of it is not a stable read … there is no pager on the
Runs tab to drive one either"*. The second half was true of the CYCLE tab
and is untrue of this screen, which draws *"Showing 1–34 of 34"* with a
rows-per-page control; the first half is answered by a TOTAL order rather
than waved away. **`NFR-3` is why it matters and `NFR-5` is why a ceiling of
200 could not stay**: correct at a 3,000-connection utility, silently
truncating at a 40,000-account one.

**THE ENVELOPE IS `{count, next, previous, results}` PLUS `tiles`.** That is
the four names `07-frontend/src/api/paginated.ts` declares, and the extra key
is spread back in by hand because `_page_envelope` returns a fresh dict.
⚠ **IT ANSWERED `{"runs": [...]}` UNTIL 2026-09-15** — one caller,
`getBillRuns` in `endpoints.ts`, and it moved in the same commit.

⚠ **TWO THINGS THIS DOCSTRING TOLD SESSIONS WERE IMPOSSIBLE, AND BOTH WERE
FALSE WHEN THEY WERE READ (`DEF-BIL-5353`, the corrections are below in the
lifecycle block with their dates):** `run_no` is populated and real runs
carry `RUN-0001` upward, and the rule that kept MONEY off this row is about
another module's creation screens. The VALUE column is served: Σ of the run's
locked bills as the stored decimal string beside its `CHAR(3)` currency.

⚠ **AND `status` NOW MOVES** (`BR-BIL-1045`, `DEF-BIL-5352`). It read
`"draft"` on every finished run this product had ever made — including one
that had issued 1,251 bills — because both its writers wrote at creation.
`runs.record_run_outcome` is the one writer now; `selectors.bill_runs_page`
and `runs.py`'s status block carry the whole argument.

This endpoint was skipped by RC-W3b on purpose — `apps/billing/api.py` was
a live sibling lane's file at the time (hard-won law 11) — and the cycle
detail shipped a stated absence naming it, which is the only reason a
missing endpoint stayed visible for a day instead of for a release.

── THE POST ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

⚠ **AMENDED 2026-09-30 (bulk bill run redesign, plan A1/B1/B3/B4).** The
POST is now `run_scope_api.create`: every Scope refusal and warning at once
(`field_errors` + `params.warnings`), run name and template REQUIRED, and
`scope_services` no longer read — the PO removed the services filter. The
paragraphs below about `bill_date` and `due_days` still hold.

201 with the id inline. 11b marks this row STALE against B12 r1's
`202 + job_id` law — that law is about ASYNC operations, and this is one
insert with nothing queued behind it, so `job_id` is served null rather
than pointing at a poll that would answer nothing. `billRunIdOf()` reads
`id ?? run_id` and refuses to guess when neither arrives; `id` is the one
served. **11b §2.8b records exactly this**, so the next lane reads what was
served rather than re-deriving it.

`bill_date` IS ACCEPTED AND STORED (BR-BIL-070 — PO ruling 2026-08-11
closing OQ-122, option A: *"A Store what they type and use it"*). It lands
on `bill_runs.bill_date` and becomes the run's SERVICE date, so a run whose
clerk typed 3 Aug over a cycle dated 1 Aug prices at 3 Aug. Omitting it, or
sending null or "", records that nobody typed one and the cycle's date is
used — the behaviour every run had before the ruling.

This docstring previously read *"`bill_date` IS ACCEPTED AND NOT STORED …
OQ-122 carries the divergence to the PO"*. The OQ is closed and the claim
is now false, so it is rewritten rather than left standing (hard-won law 1).

`due_days` IS ACCEPTED AND STORED TOO (CR-029 D9, PO 2026-08-23: *"when we
configure Cycle we are provideing default values; mostly it wil remain as it
is but user can over ride them during billing"*). Worked, and it is the
figure the ruling was confirmed on: cycle 06-A bills 1 July with 21
due-days, so an ordinary run falls due **22 July**; a run created with
`due_days: 14` falls due **15 July**, and the cycle still says 21 for the
next run. `0` is lawful and means due on the bill date.

get.description:
`GET /billing/runs/scope-list?cycle_id=&list=nobody|missing_meter` —
the rows behind Scope's *Nobody to bill* and *Missing meter* counts, PAGED
(`page`, `per` — NFR-3), in the product's page envelope. READ ONLY
(DEF-BIL-8221).

Refusals: no cycle → `billing.runScope.refusal.cycleMissing`; an unknown
`list` → VAL-005 on `list`; a cycle this tenant cannot see → 404; a module
that does not answer → SYS-PROVIDER with the preview's own key for it.

`GET /billing/runs/scope-preview` — everything the Scope step shows. READ ONLY.

Takes the same fields the POST takes (`cycle_id`, `period_start`,
`period_end`, `bill_date`, `due_days`, `template_id`, `label`) and answers
the refusals and warnings the POST would give, all at once, each on its
field; the cycle's counts and the previous run's three account counts;
the cycle's details; continuity; and the cycle's previous runs, PAGED
(`page`, `per` — NFR-3), newest first, through the one run-list read
(`selectors.bill_runs_page`) so this panel and screen 27 cannot describe a
run differently.

⚠ **IT WRITES NOTHING** — no run, no number allocated, no audit row. An
Executive may call it and is told `not_allowed` among the refusals, which is
the truthful answer to *could I start this*.

`GET /billing/runs/scope-templates` — the bill templates a run may be
started on (a published version each), PAGED (`page`, `per` — NFR-3).
READ ONLY (DEF-BIL-8222). *Must be published* stays the POST's refusal.

`GET /billing/runs/{id}` — ONE run: its phase, scope, decisions, counts.

CR-051 task 1, and the block above the run views records why it was absent
and why that reason expired. READ ONLY: five grouped queries over rows that
already exist, and no prepare pass — which is exactly what `GET .../findings`
cannot claim, because that one re-runs the whole of phase 1 on every refresh.

**`phase` IS DERIVED FROM EVIDENCE AND `status` IS THE STORED COLUMN.** Both
are served, and they answer different questions: `phase` is how far this run
got through the WIZARD (draft · calculated · authorised · issued), `status`
is the word screen 27's STATUS column shows a clerk (`BR-BIL-1045`).

⚠ **THIS PARAGRAPH SAID `status` IS WRITTEN `"draft"` AT CREATION AND NEVER
MOVES, AND UNTIL 2026-09-15 IT WAS TRUE (`DEF-BIL-5352`).** It moves now —
`runs.record_run_outcome` advances it the instant the issue pass returns, so
the reason `phase` had to exist at all is half gone. `phase` STAYS: a run may
be authorised with nothing issued, and no status word says that. The stored
column is served beside the derived one rather than hidden, which is what
made the defect findable in the first place.

No money of any kind (BR-MET-078 as hardened by CR-029).

`GET /billing/runs/{id}/breaks` — BR-BIL-053's list, and it SURVIVES now.

CR-051 tasks 5/6. Until migration 0026 the breaks lived only in
`runs.CalculatedRun.breaks`, so this endpoint could not exist without
calculating inside a read. It now reads `bill_run_breaks` and writes
nothing: a refresh, a logout and a shift change all leave the list intact,
and two clerks working it see the same rows and the same resolutions because
the list is the server's rather than each browser's.

OUTSTANDING BY DEFAULT — that is the work list, and BR-BIL-053's own word.
`?f.resolved=all` adds the ones a later pass drafted, for the supervisor's
question rather than the clerk's.

post.description:
BR-BIL-053's SECOND way out — *"or mark for later"*.

The account joins the Pending-billing queue and waits for a catch-up
sub-run; the rest of the run issues (BR-BIL-055 — *"a break never blocks the
run"*). It writes the `bill_run_exclusions` row that IS that queue, and it
goes through `pending.mark_break_for_later` rather than
`runs.mark_for_later` for the reason that wrapper exists: the reason code
has to carry the STAGE (BR-BIL-040), so the queue can tell *"we never
calculated this"* from *"we calculated it and it broke"*, and a call site
that composed its own code would produce a row whose origin is `unknown`.

**THE STAGE COMES FROM THE STORED BREAK ROW, NEVER FROM THE CALLER.** A
client-supplied stage would be a fact about the failure invented by
something that did not witness it. A request naming an account with no
outstanding break is refused rather than queued on a guess.

**IDEMPOTENT (hard rule 6)** on (run, account) through the table's own
unique constraint, so a double-click marks once and answers success — a
replay is not an error.

BR-BIL-053's FIRST way out — *"retry immediately by fixing the issue"*.

⚠ **`runs.retry_account` HAS EXISTED, COMPLETE AND TESTED, SINCE 2026-08-11
AND HAD NO HTTP CALLER** (DEF-2856, and `DEF-2557` filed the frontend half
of the same absence). So the break panel drew its Retry control DISABLED
carrying *"Trying one customer again is not something this screen can do
yet"* — accurate, and it left a clerk one option for a single missing read:
re-run the whole cycle. Hard-won law 2, and neither suite could see it,
because the backend tests call the function directly and the frontend test
asserts the disabled control.

**ONE ACCOUNT, STAGES 1–6, AND NOTHING ELSE IS TOUCHED.** The other drafts
are not recomputed and no other break is closed. On success the account
joins the draft set and its break row closes as `drafted` — the same value a
whole-run pass writes, because it is the same fact.

**A RETRY THAT STILL FAILS IS A REFUSAL, NOT A 201.** Nothing was fixed, the
account still cannot be billed, and the break row is left exactly as it was:
`retry_account` closes it only after the draft commits. Answering success
over an account that still has no read would move the discovery to the gate.

**IT IS NOT A RE-PRICE.** BR-BIL-023 is unchanged and unchangeable here: a
computed amount is never typed over, and this route accepts no amount, no
quantity and no line. What it accepts is the request to try again after a
human fixed what the reason named.

**THE CLERK'S RECORDED DECISIONS ARE FOLDED IN FIRST**, exactly as
`run_calculate` does it — an account whose missing read was answered on
S31.3 must retry on that answer, or the retry fails for the reason the
clerk has already dealt with. It is a POST, which is where a write belongs;
`selectors.py` records why a GET must never reach `apply_decisions`.

S31 step 4's "Work out the bills" — PHASE 2 (US-BIL-004 · BR-BIL-051/052).

⚠ **THIS ROUTE WAS THE THIRD BRICK IN DEF-116's WALL, AND IT WAS THE ONE
NOBODY HAD NAMED.** The defect reported *"the wizard drives to a 201 draft
run and then reports READY TO BILL 0, Draft bills 0"* and its prevention
column asked for the release and issue routes. Both were mounted on
2026-08-15 — and the run STILL could not issue, because **nothing in the
product ever called `runs.calculate_run`.** Measured on a booted stack the
day after: `POST .../release` answered *"run … has no bills to release, so
there is no amount and no currency to record … an authorisation of nothing
would be a signature against a blank page"*, which is the correct refusal
over an empty run. The engine was built on 2026-08-11, tested, listed in
`pipeline.PUBLIC_ENTRY_POINTS`, and had **no caller outside its own tests**
— hard-won law 2 again, one phase earlier than anybody was looking.

**WHAT ONE CALL DOES:** phase 1's prepare pass (which writes nothing), then
one DRAFT per ready account, each in its own transaction. **A break never
stops the run** (BR-BIL-055): the account that failed comes back named, with
the STAGE it stopped at, and every other draft is untouched.

**NOTHING MONEY-BEARING EXISTS WHEN IT RETURNS** (J24 step 4, BR-BIL-004): a
draft carries no `issued_at`, no stamped GL account, no journal line and no
delivery row. That is why this is a route a clerk may click twice: it is the
last phase before the gate, and the gate is where money starts.

**IDEMPOTENT (hard rule 6) BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY A FLAG.** Stage 6
REPLACES an account's draft for this run rather than adding a second
(BR-BIL-023), and stages 1–5 are pure — so a re-run converges on the same
drafts and a killed pass resumes without recomputing what it already wrote
(BR-BIL-052). The guarantee lives in the WRITE, which is the only place it
cannot rot.

NO EVENT TIME IS TAKEN, and that is not an oversight: the service date is
the bill date the clerk typed on step 1 (BR-BIL-070) and comes off the run
row through `runs.effective_bill_date`. There is no clock in this file (G6).

**`background: true` HANDS THE PASS TO A WORKER AND ANSWERS 202** (CR-051
task 8 · BR-BIL-051, whose background half has been unsatisfied since
2026-08-11). The body is the job id and the poll address `/api/jobs/{id}`
the framework already serves; the clerk may close the tab. Absent, this runs
inline exactly as it always has — see `_wants_background` for why the choice
is the caller's rather than a row threshold, and `CALCULATE_UNAVAILABLE` for
what is served about it on every response.

A SECOND CLICK IS ONE JOB, NOT TWO PASSES. The enqueue carries the scope key
`billing:calculate:<run id>`, so a re-enqueue while that job is still active
returns THE EXISTING RECORD (NFR-16). That decides what a second CLICK does;
BR-BIL-023's draft replacement decides what a second PASS does, and neither
substitutes for the other.

Start a catch-up SUB-RUN over held accounts (US-BIL-006 TC-2/5/6).

The queue's bulk action, server-side. It writes ONE `bill_runs` row — a
child of the run named in the path, over that run's period, scoped to a
subset of its unresolved holds and keyed on the parent's key plus that
scope (BR-BIL-005/015). It bills nothing: preparing, calculating and
issuing a sub-run are the same five phases as any other run, reached
through the same endpoints, which is US-BIL-006's own *"flowing
drafts→issue like any run"*.

**A duplicate is a 409 carrying who/when/link**, not a 422 — the same shape
`POST /billing/runs` gives a repeated cycle run, because it is the same
rule at sub-run granularity and a screen should not have to tell the two
refusals apart.

get.description:
`POST` starts the Check (or re-checks `account_ids` — A6); `GET` is its

Answer ONE tag: for all its accounts (`scope: "all"` — the standing
answer), or for named accounts (`scope: "accounts"`, `account_ids`, and
`service_code` where the case is per service). An account's own answer
always beats its tag's. Accepting a suggestion is `choice:
"accept_suggestion"`.

get.description:
Categories → tags with counts (no `tag`), ONE tag's accounts (`tag=`),
the Ready list (`list=ready`), or ONE account's every problem
(`account=`). A staleness sweep runs first (OQ-843 option C).

post.description:
Write ONE fact the clerk supplies on a blocked row through the module
that owns it (`check_fixes.FIXES`), then re-check that account. Body:
`{account_id, fix, …the fix's values}`. Answers the account after it.

BR-BIL-1054 — leave READY accounts out of this run (`account_ids`). They
join Not in this run and, at Send, Pending billing as *left out by clerk*.
All or nothing: one account that is not ready refuses the request.
BR-BIL-1054 — put left-out accounts back into this run.

Re-check NAMED accounts only (B15). Up to `INLINE_RECHECK` inline; more
go to the billing queue. `categories` (optional, DEF-BIL-8286) re-runs only
those categories of the Check and what is downstream of them.

get.description:
The run's read-only Check report — tiles, tags, and each account's
problems, paged; for a sent run, exactly as at Send.

post.description:
A3 — resume a Check job that stopped (a worker lost, a utility-wide
stop cleared). It carries on after the last account it saved.

`POST /billing/runs/{id}/discard` — throw a DRAFT run away (`DEF-BIL-9255`).

The run keeps its row as `abandoned` (BR-BIL-1045) and its draft bills go;
an issued, signed-off or catch-up-parent run is refused by name. The whole
rule and its reasoning are `runs.discard_run`'s docstring. Audited
`bill_run.discarded` (hard rule 7).

get.description:
S31.3's case tables (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-003) — phase 1, READ ONLY.

Same prepare pass as the findings, asked a different question: which
accounts are waiting on a human, what may be chosen for each, and what has
been chosen already.

post.description:
One recorded staff decision, or one bulk action (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-003).

*"All the decisions are made on screen and recorded"* — recorded is the
operative word, and the row carries who made it. `case_ids` in the body is
BR-BIL-060's bulk: N rows sharing ONE `bulk_action_id`, minted by the
SERVER because only the server can share an id across rows.

`amount` + `unit` are accepted because BR-BIL-015's *estimate* disposition
is a QUANTITY a clerk supplies and `record_decision` refuses one without
its unit (CLAUDE.md rule 3). **No screen sends them yet** — the shipped
`BillRunResolveBody` carries `choice`, `reason` and `case_ids` only — so
choosing *estimate* over HTTP refuses today with that rule's own sentence.
REPORTED to the S31 lane rather than worked around here.

get.description:
S31.2 "Check what we found" (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-002) — phase 1, READ ONLY.

`runs.prepare_run` writes NOTHING — not a draft, not an exclusion, not a
status change — which is what makes this safe to serve on a GET a clerk may
refresh. The body is `runs.PreparedRun` field for field; see
`selectors.findings_dict` for why it is not paginated.

── THE POST (CR-051 task 9), AND WHY THE VERB CHANGED ────────────────────
The GET *"re-runs the whole prepare pass over every account in the cycle, on
a GET a clerk can refresh"* — measured and named by CR-051. `POST` with
`background: true` hands that pass to a worker and answers 202 with the poll
address, so the clerk is not held. **It is a POST rather than a GET with a
parameter because it CREATES A JOB RECORD**, which is a write, and a GET
that writes is the thing `selectors.py` is careful never to do.

**WHAT IT LEAVES BEHIND IS COUNTS, NOT A CACHE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS
STATED ON EVERY RESPONSE** (`FINDINGS_UNAVAILABLE`). The GET is unchanged
and still recomputes. Snapshotting the case lists is `OQ-843`.

A POST with no `background: true` runs the pass inline and answers the same
body the GET does — the honest shape when nothing would run a job.
