get.description:
Screen 17's band strip and KPI strip — THE NUMBERS, WITHOUT THE ROWS.

⚠ **WHY IT IS ITS OWN ADDRESS.** Every chip on the Check screen is `.length`
of an array the browser was sent, over a findings read that is unpaginated
BY DECLARED DESIGN — because its lists are the denominator the chips count.
That is one argument holding up both halves, and this endpoint is what takes
it apart: once the counts arrive as counts, the rows are free to page. At
10,000 accounts the old shape put ten thousand account rows on the wire on
every refresh to draw twenty-six numbers.

⛔ **IT IS NOT A CACHE AND MAY NOT BECOME ONE.** `OQ-843` is CLOSED on the
PO's ruling that the pass is dynamic — a clerk who fixes a plan and comes
back must see the fix. This recomputes, like the findings read beside it.
What it saves is the wire and the browser's arithmetic.

**`as_of` IS REQUIRED.** The waiting-time bands are measured against a day,
and *today* belongs to the tenant rather than to this process (BR-TEN-043 /
gate G6). A queue whose ages came from the server's clock ages by a day the
moment somebody opens it from another timezone.

**`age_bands_from` IS AN UNANSWERED QUESTION WEARING A PARAMETER.** An
account held across cycles has two candidate cycles whose bands could
govern it — the one it was held from, and the one being run now — and which
is right has not been ruled. Sending neither is the honest default: those
accounts are counted on their own and kept out of the three age tags rather
than banded on a guess.

post.description:
S31 step 6's "Send them out" — PHASE 5 (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-005 · BR-BIL-051).

🔒 HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING — this is the transition INTO financial
immutability. After this call an issued bill cannot be un-issued, only
corrected by a new row (hard rule 4); row in
12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md.

⚠ **THIS ROUTE WAS ABSENT FOR FOUR DAYS AND THE PARAGRAPH THAT EXPLAINED WHY
IS NOW WRONG IN ALL THREE OF ITS CLAUSES** (DEF-116 — *"the bill-run wizard
cannot issue"*). It said issue needed three things this layer could not
honestly supply. (a) The **template pin** — BR-BIL-025's table now exists
and `_template_pin_for` asks for it. (b) The **event time** — `issued_at` is
a required body field, which is what BR-TEN-043 asks for: the CALLER names
the moment, and refusing to invent one was never a reason not to accept one.
(c) The **authorised release row** — `POST .../release` writes it, and this
route refuses without it. Each is corrected here rather than left standing
(hard-won law 1).

IT CALLS `release.release_run`, which is phase 5 whole: the issue pass, and
then `released_at` stamped on the authorisation row IF the pass returns.
The order is the design — stamping first would turn a crash mid-issue into a
run that claims to have gone out.

**WHAT ONE CALL DOES, per bill and in one transaction each** (issue's own
docstring is the long form): the number the DRAFT already carries is
verified, the due date is derived, BR-BIL-035's arrears are stamped, the
document is rendered as the BR-BIL-033 precondition, every line's GL account
is stamped and frozen, the status moves, `audit_log` is written, the
balanced posting handoff is emitted to the ledger's sole writer, and the
delivery rows are queued. **Queueing is not sending** and `ran: true` on a
handoff never means a customer received a bill.

**A BREAK NEVER BLOCKS THE RUN** (BR-BIL-055). 499 issue and one comes back
named in `issued.broken`; there is no batch rollback and there never will be.

**IDEMPOTENT (hard rule 6), at two levels and both of them matter.** The
inner one is structural: `issue_run` selects the run's REMAINING DRAFTS, so
a second pass finds nothing and issues nothing (US-BIL-005 TC-6) — the
guarantee lives in the SELECTION, which cannot rot, rather than in a flag.
The outer one is this route: a run whose release is already stamped
`released_at` answers **200 `created: false`** with that release rather than
a refusal, because a double-clicked Send is a replay and not an error — the
shape `POST /accounts/{id}/payments` already gives a replayed payment
(11b §2.9b).

`issued_at` is REQUIRED and is the caller's. `released_at` may be sent
separately and DEFAULTS to `issued_at`, because they are one business
moment: the clerk pressed Send once, the bills carry that instant, and the
release completed at it. The default is a stated reading of one event, never
a clock read — there is no clock in this file (G6).

get.description:
`GET …/issue/progress?job=<id>` — the Send's *n of N*, the read the Send
step polls (DEF-BIL-8710).

The Check's own read (`GET …/check`) has handed a worker-less Check back to
the billing worker since DEF-BIL-8511; the Send polled `GET /jobs/{id}`,
which is the jobs kernel's and decides nothing, so a Send whose worker died
froze for good. This read answers the same record AND, when the workers say
nobody is on it, hands it back through `run_jobs.resume_job` — the Check's
path, its locks and its refusal with no worker. `job` names the Send the
screen started; without it the run's active Send is read. A job that is not
this run's Send answers `job: null`, never another run's record.

Every account the run does not bill and every unit it cannot, paged;
`group=` presses a filter (Sign off's *See* opens it this way).

post.description:
Mark accounts this run left in Pending billing for the NEXT cycle
(`account_ids`, and `at` — the clerk's event time, BR-TEN-043).

The screen's heartbeat: *I have this run open* — answered with who else
has (`others`, names only). A courtesy, never a lock (`run_presence`).

get.description:
S31.2's PRICING-SHADOW panel — step 3 of the R1–R7 cutover. READ ONLY.

Runs the ruled pricing chain beside the live path over this run's ready
accounts and reports every place the two answer differently. **It prices
nothing and writes nothing**: the decision log's own table gives step 3
"nothing" under *what changes on a bill*, and this route is not on any path
a bill travels.

⚠ **IT IS A SECOND REQUEST, NOT A MEMBER OF `findings`, ON PURPOSE.** The
findings body is the stage a clerk cannot bill without; the comparison is
advisory and is allowed to be empty, slow or unhappy without taking the
billable stage down with it. `shadow_report` says why at length.

The body always carries `attempted` beside `disagreed` — *"read the third
and fourth numbers together or they lie: 0 disagreed is also what perfect
agreement looks like"* — and always carries `not_attempted` with
`blocked_by_reason`, so an operator can tell agreement from a question
nobody could ask.

`GET /billing/runs/{id}/read-lock` — the Sent card's *"Meter reads:
Locked"* (DEF-BIL-8685), on its own read since `DEF-BIL-8809`.

It rode `GET /billing/runs/{id}` and was ~1.1 s of that read's 1.2 s on a
sent 40,008-bill run, so every screen of the bulk run page waited for a
row only the Sent card draws. Null until the run is released with nothing
left to send. No money.

post.description:
S31 step 5's sign-off — the RELEASE GATE (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-005, phase 4).

🔒 HUMAN-REVIEW-PENDING — this is the door money goes through. It writes the
`bill_run_releases` row that `issue_run` requires and nothing else can
forge; row in 12-governance/09-human-review-ledger.md.

BR-BIL-058, the PO's own words: *"take final confirm from user, compliance
confirmation, emails, text mandates, auto pay mandates and then release the
bills"*. FIVE separately recorded facts, not one tick, because *"a release
that went out without the compliance check is a different event from one
that did"*. The service refuses while any is untaken and NAMES every one of
them (US-BIL-005 TC-10).

**IT ISSUES NOTHING.** This is the last moment at which nothing has been
billed, and that is the point of separating it from `POST .../issue`: the
gate is the record of authorisation, and the release is the act. A crash
between the two leaves exactly the state TC-13 describes — a row with
`released_at` NULL, authorised but not released — which is a resumable
position rather than a re-authorisation.

**IDEMPOTENT (hard rule 6).** A run that already has an AUTHORISED BUT
UNRELEASED row answers **200 `created: false`** with that row instead of
writing a second: TC-13 requires that a resume *"does NOT ask for
authorisation a second time"*, and a double-clicked Confirm is the same
shape at one second's distance. A run whose release is already RELEASED is
a different case entirely and gets a new row — `release_run`'s own docstring
says a second authorised release (a catch-up sub-run, a resumed batch) is a
SECOND row with its own confirmations.

`confirmed_at` is REQUIRED and is the caller's (BR-TEN-043 / G6). There is
no clock in this path.

get.description:
Who is billed (accounts and units, each adding back to Scope's figure),
usage and charges per service with the other categories, payments and
balances with how the amount due will be paid, by customer type, waived.

`GET /billing/runs/{id}/summary` — PHASE 4's panel (US-BIL-005 · DEF-2853).

⚠ **`release.summary_for` HAS COMPUTED EVERY FIGURE ON THIS PANEL SINCE
2026-08-11 AND HAD NO CALLER BUT `POST .../release`, WHICH STORES IT AND
NEVER SERVES IT BACK.** So S31 steps 4 and 5 drew *"Customers in this run —
Not worked out"*, *"Usage, per service — Not worked out"* and *"Amount — Not
worked out"* over a complete, tested implementation, and a clerk was asked to
sign a release against figures the product would not show them. Hard-won law
2, one function over from DEF-116's own two routes. `EP-BIL-01`'s field map
had written the gap down in prose — *"still no endpoint and no screen"* — and
nothing reads prose for truth.

**THE FOUR FIGURES ARE THE PO's OWN WORDS** (2026-08-11): *"show the billing
summary in how many accounts, how many bills generated, how much consumption
and how much bill amount and various categories"*. Consumption carries its
explicit unit and is never summed across units (rule 3); the amount carries
its currency (rule 2).

**IT RECALCULATES ON EVERY CALL AND THAT IS THE RULING, NOT AN OVERSIGHT.**
PO 2026-08-11, option B, put in plain English with its worked figure: approve
480 bills at $52,847.19, void two next week, and the screen must read 478.
So this route reads the run's CURRENT bills and reads `bill_run_releases`
never. `POST .../release` answers the other question — what was authorised —
and after that ruling the stored row is the ONLY answer to it.

**READ ONLY, AND MONEY-BEARING, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT A FIELD ON
`GET /billing/runs/{id}`.** That route is five grouped counts with no money
at all (BR-MET-078 as hardened by CR-029) and it is POLLED while a batch
runs. This one sums bills, walks every correction chain (BR-BIL-064) and
reaches the customers seam for mandate coverage; it is read once, at the
gate. Folding it in would put a money aggregation on a poll.

A refusal from the summary is a REFUSAL, not an empty panel: a run holding a
`corrected` bill that nothing replaces cannot say what the customer owes now,
and both figures it could reach are wrong (`current_position_bills` argues
it at length). It surfaces under BR-BIL-056 rather than being flattened to
zero.

`GET /billing/runs/{id}/totals` — `/summary`'s headline alone: bills,
amount net of credit notes, currency (`DEF-BIL-8809`).

The bulk run page draws exactly these from the panel (the Sent card's
total, the Send step's bill count) and was asking for the whole of it —
consumption, three category axes, coverage, the waived list — ~1.1 s at
40,008 bills, on the read the Sent card waits for. Same functions as
`/summary` (`release.totals_for`), live on every call, the same refusals
under the same rule.

S30's Budget Bills tab — every account on the programme.

Serves the accounts, not a summary: a "312 enrolled" chip with no rows is
the shape a clerk cannot work from, and every figure here is per-account.

`parameters` carries the tenant's own S69 settings (BR-BIL-021) so the
screen can say *"we average 12 months and true up in month 12"* in the
tenant's numbers rather than in a hardcoded sentence. When those settings
have not been published the block is served as null WITH the reason — never
as the ratified defaults, which would print figures no tenant chose.

⚠ **THE REASON IS `BUDGET_PARAMETERS_UNREADABLE`, A GAP IN THE SAME SHAPE
AS `unavailable[]`, AND NOT THE SEAM'S SENTENCE (`DEF-BIL-5339`).** Until
2026-09-15 this served `str(BillingConfigError)` — *"apps.tenancy.selectors
.settings_family is not published … (BR-BIL-017) …"* — and the tab printed
it at a clerk. The seam's sentence is the engineer's and goes to the log.

§05 entry 25.3 — every customer waiting for a person to put them on a level.

⚠ **PAGED AT THE SEAM, NOT AFTER IT** (`NFR-3`, and `DEF-PAY-4221` is what
the alternative costs). `limit`/`offset` travel to the owning module so this
can never become the fifth unpaginated list in the product. Nothing here
caps a tenant and nothing declares a maximum (`NFR-5`, B6).

⚠ **`count` IS `null` WHILE THE ROWS ARE UNREADABLE, NOT `0`.** DRF's
envelope wants a number and this one refuses to invent it, for the reason
`customers_seam` gives for every other unreachable read: a zero is a claim
about customers and a null is a claim about the product.

post.description:
US-BIL-018 — put ONE account on budget billing.

ONE account, deliberately. The prototype offers "All eligible residential
(312)" and a CSV import; neither is served (see `BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE`).
Enrolment fixes what a customer pays every month for a year, and a bulk
action over accounts whose plan flag nothing can read would enrol people at
a level nobody looked at.

❄️ Worked on WE-8/GT-24: trailing-12 $2,904 → level **$242**, variance opens
at 0.00, the settle-up month is copied from the tenant setting and one audit
row is written. Nothing in this file computes any of that.

get.description:
§05 entry **25.2 `Settle-up forecast`** — READ ONLY, and it posts nothing.

The clerk's sentence the drawing opens with: *"Who is going to be trued up,
when, and for how much — so I can answer them before they ring?"*

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠ THERE IS NO BUTTON HERE ON PURPOSE, AND THIS IS WHERE THE REASON LIVES
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
An earlier version of the drawing offered a bulk **"Settle these 2"**. The
blueprint withdrew it and recorded why, which is the half worth keeping:
*"The cycle run already posts the settle-up, on the account's own bill,
inside the same write that creates it, idempotently per invoice. A bulk
button would have been a second writer for the same money."*
`budget_service.record_bill` is that writer and
`uq_budget_event_once_per_invoice` is the constraint that makes a re-draft
return the same facts rather than moving the variance twice. So this route
is a **GET and nothing else**, and there is no sibling POST to add later.

B14 rule 33 keeps that paragraph OFF the screen — *"RATIONALE … is ZERO
WORDS ON SCREEN, it belongs in the code and the register"* — which is why it
is here, at length, rather than in the catalogue.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT IT SERVES, AND WHY THE THREE MONEY COLUMNS TIE OUT
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
`PAID ON THE LEVEL` and `ACTUAL SO FAR` are the two sums
`selectors.budget_settle_up_windows` takes over the account's CURRENT
settle-up period, and `BALANCE` is the same account's `variance_balance` put
through `budget.settle_up`. Those are not two answers to one question: a
`billed` event's movement IS `level − actual`, so over that window
`Σlevel − Σactual` is the balance by construction. **The browser therefore
adds nothing** — every figure on the screen is a decimal string this route
computed, which is the rule screen 25.1's lane applied when it refused to
sum twelve monthly figures client-side.

⚠ **THE DRAWN SIGN IS `budget.SettleUp.signed`, NOT A FLIPPED CONVENTION.**
The drawing prints `+$212.80 Collect` and `−$61.40 Credit`, and the engine's
`variance_balance` runs the other way (❄️ WE-8: −50.87 is the month the
customer UNDER-paid). Those are the same fact and the reconciliation was
already written: `SettleUp.amount` is always positive, `direction` carries
the sign, and `SettleUp.signed`'s own docstring reads *"+ collects, −
credits"* — exactly the drawn column. So `balance_signed` is served from the
frozen dataclass rather than negated here, and **no frozen figure moves**.

⚠ **AN ACCOUNT WITH NO SETTLE-UP MONTH IS NOT A ROW WITH A BLANK CELL.**
`settle_up_month` is nullable — a tenant that has never published one
enrols accounts without it (BR-BIL-021, never defaulted) — and such an
account NEVER trues up. It is excluded from the rows and the tiles and
COUNTED in `no_settle_month`, so the screen can say so in one line instead
of printing a forecast that silently omits people.

⚠ **ONE CURRENCY OR NONE ON THE TILES** (CLAUDE.md rule 2), which is
`_summary`'s rule on the neighbouring screen and it carries over unchanged:
a tenant whose settling accounts carry two currencies gets the COUNTS and no
totals. Adding 100 USD to 100 CAD is not 200 of anything.

`as_of` is the forecast's horizon and is a QUERY ARGUMENT defaulting to
today. It decides one thing only — which occurrence of each account's month
comes next — and having it on the request is what lets a test stand at a
fixed date instead of freezing a clock (BR-TEN-043's posture for a read).

One enrolled account: its level, its position and its whole event trail.

The trail is the append-only `account_budget_events` ledger (US-BIL-019
TC-6), and it is served WITH the derived balance beside the cached one so
the screen can show them agreeing. A cache nobody checks is a second source
of truth waiting to disagree — the service keeps `recompute_balance` for
exactly this, and hiding it here would waste it.

*"What would this customer's flat monthly amount be?"* — READ ONLY.

The prototype's step 2 shows the clerk the number before they commit
("Last 12mo total → New flat monthly"), and this is that read. It writes
nothing: no status row, no event, no audit row. A clerk who opens it and
walks away has enrolled nobody.

⚠ **IT DOES NOT ANSWER THE PLAN QUESTION AND SAYS SO.** `eligible` is null
when `plan_offers_budget` is not supplied on the query, because BR-RAT-043
puts that flag on the rate plan and nothing publishes it (OQ-237). A `true`
here would be this route deciding a rule it does not own; a `false` would
refuse customers who qualify. So the two halves it CAN answer — the history
length and the computed level — are answered, and the third is named.

post.description:
US-BIL-020 — the per-account override, bounded ±30% WITH a reason.

❄️ Worked (TC-3): computed 242, staff set **200** with "customer hardship
request" → accepted, because the bound is **169.40 – 314.60**. TC-4's 150
and 320 are both refused, and so is any override with no reason.

The bound is measured against the COMPUTED level and never against a
previous override — chaining them would let three 30% steps walk a level to
twice what the trailing twelve months say, one audited row at a time. That
is `budget.validate_override`'s guarantee and this route does not repeat it.

US-BIL-020 — the S30 "Re-level" row action (`manual=True`).

Manual skips the CADENCE gate and NOT the arithmetic: the level is
recomputed from the trailing actuals exactly as the periodic job computes
it. BR-BIL-017 allows a staff re-level with an audit row, and the row says
`manual: true` so a later reader can tell it from a cadence run.

A re-level that does not MOVE the level answers 200 with `changed: false`
and the unchanged row. That is not a failure — *"we looked and it was fine"*
is the fact J09 step 5 asks for (US-BIL-020 TC-1) — and reporting it as an
error would train a clerk to ignore the one that matters.

The ONLY way off the programme — a STAFF decision with a name on it.

PO ruling 2026-08-11, verbatim *"nodrop we chase for payments until write
off"*: BR-BIL-017's automatic drop-off is SUPERSEDED, so nothing here can be
triggered by arrears. The variance balance is CARRIED, never dropped
(US-BIL-020 §5), and the response says so with the figure — a customer
coming off budget billing still owes (or is owed) that money, and a screen
that reported "removed" with no number would let it disappear from view.

get.description:
`CR-156-BRC10` · CHG-02 step 1's *Code* — the Settings codes NOT IN USE
(PO 2026-10-01: *"when user select code from list show what are not in use
only"*), of the asked kind or of no kind yet, for a base of the asked
service or of none. `?kind=base|plan|other&service=<code>`.

Unpaginated deliberately and on its own facts, not by reference to any
other list: its rows are bounded by the codes a utility has MINTED on
Settings and not yet configured (tens, never thousands), and a type-ahead
over a page would hide a free code past the page edge.

`CR-087` · `CHG-01`'s Plans tab — WHICH plans this charge code reaches.

The tab rendered one sentence saying it could not answer: *"The tile above
counts the plans that carry this definition. Naming them one by one needs a
read that does not exist yet."* This is that read. **PO ruling 2026-09-10,
verbatim, asked whether the empty tab bodies should exist at all:
*"build"*.**

⚠ **AND THE TILE IT SAT UNDER WAS UNDERCOUNTING.** `charge_used_by` counts
`plan_charge_rules` only, so a code that is every water size's BASE — reached
through `BR-RAT-088` rather than through an attachment — reads `0` while it
prices every connection on the service. `selectors.charge_reach_plan_ids`
returns both routes and this endpoint serves both, each row naming which one
it is on (`DEF-RAT-4832`).

⚠ **THE PAGINATION IS THE POINT, NOT THE PLUMBING (`NFR-3`).** The paginator
is handed the QUERYSET, so `count` is a SQL `COUNT` over the whole set and
the page is a SQL `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`; only the page's plans are then enriched.
A code carried by every plan of a 40,000-account tenant is exactly the list
`NFR-3` exists for, and nothing here caps anything (`NFR-5`).

⚠ **NO FILTERS, NO SORT, DELIBERATELY** — the same posture `plan_units`
takes one screen across. The frame draws one table with no toolbar;
`BR-SHL-011`'s grammar admits `page` and `per`, which the paginator reads,
and an undeclared param is ignored rather than erroring.

`GET /cheques?as_of=` — the three lists CS-30 asks for (S33 · S37).

    uncleared          structured cheques still `processing` — the money
                       has not arrived. *"the thing a bookkeeper actually
                       asks for"*, in CS-30's own words.
    bankable_today     post-dated cheques whose day has come and that are
                       not yet in a batch. **This is the half that makes the
                       hold safe**: without it a post-dated cheque sits in
                       the drawer and nothing ever says it is ready.
    held               post-dated cheques not yet bankable on `as_of`.

`as_of` is REQUIRED and this module reads NO clock (BR-TEN-043, gate G6) —
the same requirement `GET /outstandings` and `GET /payments/summary` already
impose, and for the same reason: a server clock decides a business day in
the SERVER's timezone.

Unpaginated, matching `/outstandings`: a utility under 3,000 connections has
a drawer, not a database, and the three counts must foot to the three lists
exactly. A paginated body would make a count describe a page.

The ladder board — a PREVIEW that steps nothing (US-PAY-014/015).

`POST /collections/run` already existed and it SENDS: it writes the notice,
advances the tier and records a skip row on every path. There was no way to
look first, so a clerk drove a five-stop-condition engine over a selection
they could not inspect. This is the look.

`as_of` is the caller's business day (BR-TEN-043 — this layer reads no
clock). `balance_floor` and `partial_pause_percent` may be stated; when they
are not, the board answers `next_step_available: false` with the reason
rather than inventing either figure (OQ-136 · OQ-137 · OQ-157).

post.description:
`POST /collections/notices` — send ONE rung, by hand, over a selection.

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  THE ROUTE TWO LIVE BUTTONS HAVE BEEN POINTING AT AND NOT REACHING.  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
`OutstandingsTab.tsx` renders *Send a reminder* and *Send a disconnection
notice* DISABLED with their reason, and the reason names this address. The
services behind them — `notices.send_reminders`, `send_disconnect_notices`
and `ladder.step_one` — have been complete and tested since 2026-08-11 and
2026-09-07; **only the door was missing**, which is the `G25` shape this
repo has now met four times.

THE BODY::

    account_ids       the S34 selection — REQUIRED, non-empty
    tone              friendly | firm | final     ─┐ exactly one
    rung              one of BR-PAY-017's four    ─┘ of these two
    as_of             the clerk's business day — REQUIRED, never a clock
    cut_date          optional; defaults inside `step_one` to as_of + 10d
    channels          optional; defaults to ("pdf_print",) — DISCONNECT
                      rungs only. The friendly reminder's channels are
                      the Settings rule's and the customer's
                      (`DEF-PAY-10651`, PO 2026-10-29 ruling 1A)
    balance_floor     optional; the tenant's, passed as `collections/run`
    partial_pause_percent   optional, same
    medical_hold_account_ids  optional — a clinical fact customers owns
    idempotency_key   the form's submit token — REQUIRED (hard rule 6)

**IT SHARES ONE VOCABULARY WITH THE AUTOMATIC LADDER**, which is the whole
point and is `BR-PAY-017` in one sentence: *"manual sends use the same tier
ladder, channels and exclusions as the sequence engine, and advance the same
state."* The stop conditions are `ladder.decide`'s, the send is
`ladder.step_one`, the state row is the one shared row, and every skip is
written to `notice_history`. See `notices_by_hand`'s docstring for why each
of those is borrowed rather than minted.

**A PER-ACCOUNT REFUSAL IS NOT A REQUEST FAILURE.** 200 with `sent` and
`skipped` beside each other: a selection of twelve where one is on a medical
hold sends eleven and says why the twelfth did not. A 4xx would make one
hold cancel a morning's chase.

**NOTHING IS SENT HERE OR ANYWHERE** (`BR-NOT-005`). Every notice is a write
to `outbound_messages`; the dispatcher sends. There is no SMTP call on this
path and there must not be one.

Advance the collection ladder over an S34 selection (US-PAY-014).

⚠ THIS IS NOT THE NIGHTLY JOB. BR-PAY-017's ladder is evaluated on a
schedule and BE-07 registers no collections job; every response carries
`no_scheduled_caller` saying so. This route lets a clerk drive the same
engine over the rows they have selected, which is the S34 bulk action.

get.description:
`GET /connections` — B18 §5.4.6's list row, and S86's only endpoint.
**`POST /connections` — `create_connection`, CR-070 wave B (`US-WRK-002`).**

⚠ **THE POST IS SERVED FROM THIS FUNCTION AND NOT FROM ITS OWN VIEW, AND
THAT IS A ROUTING FACT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.** Django reaches only the
FIRST view registered on a path, so a sibling `path("connections", …)` for
the write would be dead code that looked mounted — the exact bug `G52`
found in the lane that built the refunds doors. One path, one view, and the
role split lives in the permission class where it can be cited.

⚠ **THE POST IS NOT THE WIZARD'S COMMIT DOOR AND MUST NOT BECOME ONE.**
`NewConnectWizard.tsx` posts to `POST /connections/commit` with NO id,
because `BR-MET-112` means no connection row exists before step 9. That door
is still unserved and is REPORTED where it always was
(`newConnectEndpoints.ts` exception E3). This mounts the finished writer so
that no writer in `connections.py` is behind a Python shell (`US-WRK-002`
TC-7), and so a draft can be raised against an existing premises.

The read half was read-only until CR-070 wave B, when the twelve other write
paths this module holds got their doors; the reason given here for the
absence — *"they belong to the wizard's lane"* — outlived the absence by
nine days, which is hard-won law 1 in one comment.

⛔ **`?segment=` accepts `all` and nothing else** — `NotImplementedError(
"OQ-371")` otherwise, the posture `finance/cost-reconciliation/download`
already takes for OQ-204: a named refusal rather than a 404, because a 404
reads as a typo and this is a decision nobody has taken. The screen is told
the same thing in words it can render, on `unavailable`, so it never has to
call the route to find out.

`q`/`page`/`per` are parsed by the ONE house parser (BR-SHL-011); `sort` and
`dir` are declared empty because B18 §5.4.2 fixes the order — *"Sorted by
target date, soonest first"* — and an undeclared param is ignored, never
refused.

post.description:

**`POST /connections` — `create_connection`, CR-070 wave B (`US-WRK-002`).**

THAT IS A ROUTING FACT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE.** Django reaches only the

`POST /connections/commit` — **the New Connect wizard's one press.**

⚠ **THIS ADDRESS ANSWERED 404 UNTIL 2026-09-16 AND THE BUTTON HAS BEEN
PRESSING IT SINCE THE WIZARD SHIPPED (`DEF-MET-5441`).** `NewConnectWizard`
posts here with NO id in the path, because `BR-MET-112` means no connection
row exists before the last step. Wave B mounted the thirteen connection
writers and deliberately did not mount this one — `create_connection` needs
a premises and `commit_connection` needs an existing draft — and the
orchestration behind one door was left unwritten, recorded in two comments
and on no register. **No build made through that screen had ever reached the
database.**

⚠ **THE LITERAL IS REGISTERED ABOVE `connections/<uuid:connection_id>/…`,
AND THAT IS THE HOUSE HABIT RATHER THAN A FIX.** `<uuid:…>` would not match
`commit` today, so nothing is currently at risk; the ordering is what stops
the next literal being swallowed the day somebody registers a looser
converter beside it.

**THIN, like every other view here.** The whole payload IS the plan — the
id-bearing commit below reads `request.data["plan"]` because a lane wrapped
it, and this screen sends the plan itself — and `commit_new_connect`
sequences the two services inside one transaction. This view computes no
figure and defaults no absence.

get.description:
`GET /connections/message-templates` — **step 7's drawn picker rows.**

⚠ **BOTH HALVES WERE BUILT AND NEITHER WAS REACHABLE (hard-won law 2).**
`connection_messages.template_choices` and
`notifications.connection_events.connection_templates` landed on 2026-09-16
with thirteen green cases between them, and `connection_events.py`'s own
lifecycle block records the gap in as many words — *"D=deferred(reached
through metering's seam, no HTTP surface of its own)"*. The step-7 screen is
the wave that needs it, so the address is mounted here rather than the
picker shipping over an empty table.

⚠ **NO CONNECTION ID, AND THAT IS `BR-MET-112` RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT.**
Step 7 runs seven steps before anything is written, so there is no build to
hang this read on. It lists the three classes for the TENANT; which of them
a given build can actually queue is `queue_on_commit`'s answer and is not
knowable here.

⚠ **THE LITERAL IS REGISTERED ABOVE `connections/<uuid:connection_id>`** —
the same house habit as `connections/commit` below it, for the same reason.

**THIN.** The search term is passed through untouched: `template_choices`
matches *the name a human gave it* (B14 rule 31) and this view neither
filters nor sorts, so a clerk and a test see one behaviour.

`GET /connections/proposed-work-orders?services=electric,water` —
`US-WRK-017`, and the sentence that comes off `Work-004`.

Step 6 of the New Connect wizard has been called *Plans & work orders*
since the wizard shipped and has proposed no work orders at all: the screen
says, in its own copy, *"Those templates are not built yet, so no orders
are proposed here."* Wave D built the templates. This is what the step
reads instead.

⚠ **`AnyTenantRole`, NOT THE SETTINGS CLASS THE REST OF THIS FILE'S
TEMPLATE ROUTES USE.** Authoring a template is a system admin's act, which
is why `/work/templates` is `SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin`; READING which
jobs a new build needs is what a clerk running the wizard does all day, and
`OQ-WRK-1492` was closed on 2026-09-04 with exactly that reasoning in the
PO's own words — *"clark can do it sicne it s a day to day work"*.

⚠ **THIS PATH BEGINS WITH METERING'S NOUN AND IS SERVED HERE ON PURPOSE.**
Wave O set the pattern (`premises/{id}/work-orders`, `accounts/{id}/build`):
the noun belongs to another module, the CONTENT is Work's, so Work serves
it. It is also what keeps `apps/customers` honest — the wizard reads this
over HTTP and never touches `work_order_templates` with an ORM query, which
is `A7`'s boundary and the mirror of what `G78` enforces from Work's side.

⚠ **NOTHING IS WRITTEN, HERE OR ANYWHERE, UNTIL STEP 9** (`BR-MET-112`).

post.description:
`POST /connections/quote-preview` — **what this build will cost, before it exists.**

⚠ **THIS ADDRESS EXISTS BECAUSE A MONEY SCREEN SHOWED NO MONEY
(`DEF-CUS-6115`).** New Connect step 6 counted its quantities, named the
charge code a clerk picked, and printed no unit price, no line total and no
total — so the acceptance walk committed six builds without the clerk ever
seeing a figure, and the commit then raised `7 x $45.00 = $315.00`. The
pricing engine could always answer; this is the door that asks it.

⚠ **A POST THAT WRITES NOTHING, AND THE PRECEDENT IS BILLING'S OWN.**
`POST /billing/one-time/preview` is the same shape for the same reason: the
question is a LIST of coded lines and a list does not fit in a query string.
Nothing here creates a run, a document or a number.

⚠ **NO CONNECTION ID, AND THAT IS `BR-MET-112` RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT** —
the same sentence `connection_message_templates` above it carries. Step 6
runs two steps before anything is written, so there is no build to hang this
on. The whole payload is the question.

⚠ **THE LITERAL IS REGISTERED ABOVE `connections/<uuid:connection_id>`**,
the house habit this file already keeps for `connections/commit`.

**THIN.** `connection_reads.preview_quote` reads the lines through the
commit's own shape check and prices them through the commit's own engine;
this view computes no figure and defaults no absence.

get.description:
`GET /connections/{id}` — S88 `NCT-02`, the connection detail.

⚠ **THE SCREEN HAS BEEN LIVE AND BROKEN, WHICH IS WHY THIS VIEW IS ONE
LINE.** `ConnectionDetailPage.tsx` is built, is routed at
`/connections/:connectionId`, and rendered the server's own 404 because the
read behind it did not exist — hard-won law 2 with the halves the other way
round: wired, and not built.

**It computes nothing.** No figure is derived here, no absence is defaulted
and no null is filled: the read model's payload is returned verbatim,
`unavailable` included, so the four fields the product cannot produce reach
the screen as nulls beside the reasons the service wrote for them. A view
that helpfully turned one of them into `0` would be DEF-127 again.

`AnyTenantRole`, matching `connections` above and NOT the `AdminOrClerk` the
write doors beside it carry. The asymmetry is deliberate: A4 gives Executive
VIEW on this family, and reading a build is not committing one.

post.description:
`POST /connections/{id}/activate` — `{service_ids, acknowledge_open_orders}`.

One transaction per press: the service rows activate through
`transition_service`, their assets install, the premises and the owner's
master account become Active on the first one, and the messages go
(`connection_activation.activate`). Refusals name the unit and the order.

get.description:
`GET /connections/{id}/activation` — every unit × service row of the
build, what stands on it, its orders, whether it is ready, and what the
Approve warning will list (`connection_activation.activation_readiness`).

post.description:
`POST /connections/{id}/cancel` — `cancel_connection`, with the reason.

The destructive one, and the only door on this screen wearing B14 rule 6's
danger tier. Nothing here is irreversible in the database — the stamp is a
timestamp — but the derived state becomes `cancelled` and every other door
on this build then refuses (`_refuse_if_cancelled`).

`POST /connections/{id}/charges/tag` — `tag_charges_to_account` (BR-MET-113).

It refuses to RE-tag: a quote that moved debtor after being stated is the
hazard hard rule 4 exists for, and a correction is a new charge on the right
account rather than a quiet re-pointing of the old one.

`POST /connections/{id}/commit` — S87 step 9's ONE commit (task 6.10).

⚠ **THIS IS THE ONLY DOOR THE WIZARD POSTS TO, AND THAT IS THE POINT.**
`BR-MET-112` says *"nothing is written until step 9"*, so the whole wizard
is a draft. Three sequential POSTs from a browser would invent exactly the
half-committed state the rule forbids — a premises created, then the tab
closed, and a unit that belongs to nothing. The orchestration therefore
lives in `connections.commit_connection`, which sequences five modules'
own services rather than writing across them (CLAUDE.md's cross-module
ban), and this view sequences nothing at all.

It computes no figure and defaults no absence: the seven-count manifest it
returns is the service's, verbatim.

`POST /connections/{id}/fees` — a fee added after submission (`CR-163-BRC10`
item 2). A NEW issued bill against the build's payer, never an edit of the
quote (hard rule 4); `connection_fees.add_connection_fee` holds the rule.
`AdminOrClerk`: raising a receivable is a write.

`POST /connections/{id}/hold` — `hold_connection`, with the REASON.

The reason is required by the service, not defaulted here: *"Left off,
because the permit has not come back"* is the thing the hold exists to
carry, and an unattributed hold is half a hold.

get.description:
`GET /connections/{id}/messages/{code}/preview` — what the letter would
say for THIS build. A READ: nothing is queued and no number is spent.

post.description:
`POST /connections/{id}/messages/{code}/send` — *Send now* / *Resend*.

`CR-163-BRC10` item 26. Body `{channel, recipient}`; `channel` is one of
email · pdf_print · sms and `recipient` is `owner` or `co_applicant`. One
letter, one channel, the next copy — `connection_messages.send_now` holds
the whole rule, and `notifications.queue_document` is the only write.
`AdminOrClerk`: sending is a write a read-only role may not make.

`POST /connections/{id}/outstanding-work` — `mark_outstanding` (BR-MET-114).

⚠ **THE SERVICE IS `mark_outstanding`, NOT `mark_outstanding_work`.**
`07-endpoints.md` §1 rows 9–10 and the wave plan both name the longer
spelling; the code has carried the shorter one since CR-030 W6. Recorded
here rather than renamed, because renaming a signed, tested service to match
a table cell is the tail wagging the dog (the docs are corrected instead).

`POST /connections/{id}/outstanding-work/{tid}/close` — `close_outstanding`.

**Only a PERSON closes one** — the service refuses without a resolvable
`identity.User` behind the actor, by name (`BR-MET-114`), and this view does
not soften that into a default.

`POST /connections/{id}/outstanding-work/{tid}/edit` — the author edits
their own note (`connections.update_note`).

`POST /connections/{id}/outstanding-work/{tid}/reopen` — a to-do marked
Done by mistake comes back (`connections.reopen_outstanding`).

`POST /connections/{id}/owner-account` — `create_owner_account` (BR-MET-116).

A CROSS-MODULE write that goes through customers' own `create_master_account`
seam; a build with no common-area unit is refused by name rather than given
an invented anchor.

get.description:
`GET /connections/{id}/record` — **the whole build record, in one call.**

Everything blueprint pages 98–107 draw: the header, the five tiles, the six
`Overview` blocks and the first page of every list the six drawn tabs carry.

⚠ **THIS SERVES THE PROPERTY'S BUILD TAB AND DOES NOT REVIVE A BUILD
SCREEN.** `OQ-MET-12520` closed 2026-09-21 on the PO's option C — *"The
drawing isn't asking for a duplicate; it's asking for completeness we don't
have"* — which re-confirms the 2026-09-04 ruling that deleted
`ConnectionDetailPage.tsx` and adds what the blueprint was really asking
for: the drawn tabs land on the Build tab AS SECTIONS. Pages 100–107 stay
the CONTENT contract; their address and tab strip are superseded.
`/connections/:id` still REDIRECTS on the client and nothing here changes
that.

⚠ **ONE CALL, BECAUSE THE POINT OF THE RULING IS THAT THE CLERK STOPS
HOPPING BETWEEN THREE PLACES.** Three round trips to fill one tab would be
that problem wearing a different hat, so every list comes back on page one
and `?section=` pages one of them deeper. `?page` / `?per` follow
`BR-SHL-011` — clamp, never error — and every list carries its own
`count`/`page`/`per` (`NFR-3`: no unpaginated list anywhere).

**It computes nothing.** The read model's payload is returned verbatim,
`unavailable` included, so every figure the product cannot produce reaches
the screen as a null beside the reason the service wrote for it. A view that
helpfully turned one into `0` would be `DEF-127` again — and on the
`OUTSTANDING` tile a zero says *settled* about a debt.

`AnyTenantRole`, matching the detail read above and NOT the `AdminOrClerk`
the write doors carry: A4 gives Executive VIEW on this family, and reading a
build is not committing one.

post.description:
`POST /connections/{id}/release` — `release_connection`.

`waiting_on` is PASSED, never assumed: a build can come off hold and still
be waiting for materials, which is exactly what `CON-26-0121` draws. The
caller says; neither the service nor this view guesses.

`POST /connections/{id}/services` — `add_connection_service`, step 4.

One service, at one unit or at the premise. The service refuses a service
the tenant does not run through metering's own seam, so the refusal is the
same sentence the unit wizard gives.

`POST /connections/{id}/services/{sid}/transition` — `transition_service`.

The connection id is in the path for the shape of the resource and is NOT
re-checked here: the service filters the row by the tenant in context and
answers a stranger's id with the same 404 an absent row gets (`BR-TEN-003`).
Re-deriving the parent link in the view would be a second copy of a check
the service already makes correctly.
`POST /connections/{id}/submit` — `submit_connection`: Draft → Requested.

get.description:
`GET /connections/{id}/todos` — the To-do tab: to-dos and notes, newest
first (`connections.todo_list`).

post.description:
`POST /connections/{id}/units` — *Add unit* with its services
(`connections.add_unit_to_build`).

put.description:
`PUT /connections/{id}/units/{uid}/characteristics/{key}` — `set_characteristic`.

`PUT` and not `POST` because the key is in the path and the write is
idempotent on it: the same key set twice is one row with the second value.

⚠ **`unit_of_measure` IS REQUIRED AND IS NOT DEFAULTED HERE** — hard rule 3,
and the reason `BR-MET-108` refused a column per service. A view that
supplied a unit when the caller left it out would be inventing the one fact
the rule exists to make explicit.

post.description:
`POST /connections/{id}/waiting-on` — `set_waiting_on`, on a build that is
NOT held. Waiting on something and being on hold are two independent axes
(`NCT-01` fact 1a), which is why this is its own door and not a flag on the
hold.

get.description:
GET: the case list. POST: open a case — **which writes no money**.

BR-BIL-014 is explicit that nothing money-bearing exists before approval,
and `open_case` writes exactly three kinds of row: the case, its pinned
bills and their impacts. The 201 this returns therefore means *"here is what
it would cost"*, never *"it is done"* — which is why the response carries the
preview and the standing statement rather than a success message.

THE WRITE IS `AdminOrClerk` AND THE READ IS `AnyTenantRole`, checked in the
body rather than at the decorator, because DRF gates a view and this route
is two verbs. A4 gives Executive VIEW on Reads & Billing runs and
BR-SHL-025 is server-enforced, so an Executive may look at a case and may
not open one.

post.description:
GET: the case list. POST: open a case — **which writes no money**.

BR-BIL-014 is explicit that nothing money-bearing exists before approval,
and `open_case` writes exactly three kinds of row: the case, its pinned
bills and their impacts. The 201 this returns therefore means *"here is what
it would cost"*, never *"it is done"* — which is why the response carries the
preview and the standing statement rather than a success message.

THE WRITE IS `AdminOrClerk` AND THE READ IS `AnyTenantRole`, checked in the
body rather than at the decorator, because DRF gates a view and this route
is two verbs. A4 gives Executive VIEW on Reads & Billing runs and
BR-SHL-025 is server-enforced, so an Executive may look at a case and may
not open one.

get.description:
`GET /corrections/jobs/{job_id}` — a bulk act's state and answer
(`DEF-BIL-10091`). Reads only.

`status` / `progress` are the job record's (the same `/jobs/{id}` serves);
`refusal` is the act's refusal by `message_key`; `preview` is a stored
preview, ONE PAGE of its bills (`page`, `per` — NFR-3), its totals over
all of them; `case` is the case a Send opened or an approval issued, with
`result` once the bills have run.

`GET /corrections/options` — contract A2. **Writes nothing.**

What the "What was wrong" row selects offer: the plans and their versions,
the rate schedules and theirs, the taxes, the charge codes (base charges
excluded — they come with the plan version, decision log item 7), the
discount programmes and the price-mistake targets. With a scope (the same
params as `/resolve`), also the meters the bills were priced from, the
bills' charge lines and what the first bill was billed on — the defaults
a row shows before the clerk changes them (decision log item 6).

post.description:
`POST /corrections/preview` — `CR-180-BRC10` §2. **WRITES NOTHING.**

The scope and the "What was wrong" rows in; the corrected bills out: the
class derived across the rows (R > C > D), per bill the nine sections, the
old and new bill laid out by service and rate type, the posting month and
the new due date; for bulk the aggregate with up and down apart; the page
changes; the bills not offered; and the `preview_hash` Send must quote.

No case, no row, no saved reading — BR-BIL-014, and the decision log's own
measurement of the old flow, where step 1's Continue opened a case that then
blocked the bill. A read: `AnyTenantRole` may look, as `/resolve` allows.

get.description:
US-BIL-017's reference data — every reason, its class, and what it DOES.

The class travels as a WORD as well as a code (BR-BIL-041 / TC-1a: *"the
class is shown in the operator's words … never as an enum value"*), so the
screen can put "issues a corrected bill: the original is credited in full…"
beside the reason a clerk is about to pick rather than the string
`restatement`.

`routed_elsewhere` is served too, and it is the half that stops work landing
in the wrong workflow: an estimate replaced by an actual read, a bill that
should never have existed, a period never billed, a payment on the wrong
bill and a master-data-only fix are the five things people bring to a
correction screen that are NOT corrections. EP-BIL-04 §1a asks the screen to
*"say so by name rather than accepting the work"* — it cannot do that
without the sentences.

`GET /corrections/resolve` — the bills a scope resolves to, PAGED, with totals.

`CR-101-BRC03` §06, screen 26 (p133): step 1 shows *"the bills it resolves
to, with what each asked and what has been paid"* BEFORE a reason is
picked and before any case exists — `BILL · PERIOD · AMOUNT · PAID ·
STATE` and a totals row over the whole scope. This is that read. It writes
nothing (not even a case row), takes the same selector vocabulary as the
POST (`scope_kind` + `bill_run_id` / `cycle_id` / `plan_id` /
`service_code` / `period_start` + `period_end` / `invoice_id(s)`), and
resolves through the ONE filter `open_case` will pin from, so what the
clerk saw in step 1 is what the case holds in step 2.

Paginated by the standard envelope (`page` / `per`, `NFR-3`): a run at T5
is 40,000 bills, the page is fifty, and `totals` is computed in SQL over
all of them rather than summed from the page. `AnyTenantRole`: it is a
read, and an Executive may look (BR-SHL-025's split, as `correction_cases`
states it).
The case an approver is about to sign, or the record of one that ran.

post.description:
Close a case over unresolved failures — with a reason (BR-BIL-047).

A blank reason is refused by the service and the refusal is the point:
those bills are still wrong, and the record has to say why nobody is going
to fix them. "Closed" with no explanation is indistinguishable from
"finished".

The gate. **Server-side, and that is the whole point** (US-BIL-017 TC-4).

`SystemAdminOnly` is not a convenience over a disabled button: the preview
is an artifact, not a permission, and a client that POSTs straight to
`/execute` without this must be refused by the SERVER. BR-BIL-014 v1
(OQ-072 closed) puts every correction behind a System Admin.

`preview_hash` is what the approver's screen was rendered from and is
REQUIRED here rather than optional. `bulk_corrections.approve` treats a null
as "no claim" and lets it through, which is right for a service used by a
resumed job — but a browser always knows which figures it drew, and an
approval that did not say which artifact it covered would be exactly the
signature BR-BIL-044 exists to prevent.

`POST /corrections/{id}/approve-and-issue` — `CR-180-BRC10` §4 (B10).

The approver opens Send and presses *Approve and issue* (decision log
2026-10-12, step 4): the gate and the job as ONE act, server-side. The
approval binds `preview_hash` (a mismatch refuses, `figuresMoved`), then
every bill runs on its own — credit note + new bill, two balanced entries,
payments' re-allocation, delivery rows, audit — and a bill that fails
leaves nothing and does not undo the others (BR-BIL-047). The answer is
`/execute`'s: per bill `succeeded` / `failed` / `skipped_already_done`.

`on_date` and `issued_at` are the caller's (BR-TEN-043 — never a clock on
a money path), exactly as `/approve` and `/execute` take them.

Run the approved case. Idempotent, resumable, no rollback (rule 6).

A repeat is not an error and does not answer 409: `bulk_corrections.execute`
skips a row already `done` and REPORTS it as skipped, so a double-clicked
button, a retry storm and a resumed worker all leave exactly one credit note
and one rebill per bill. The response carries the skipped list by name, so
the screen can say *"3 already done"* instead of showing a silent success
over work it did not do.

THE REBILL'S TEMPLATE PIN IS RESOLVED HERE, not defaulted from the original.
BR-BIL-026 pins the CURRENT published version at rebill issue, and
`templates_service.resolve_for` is the one implementation of that resolution
order. Silently reprinting on the superseded version the original carried is
the unsafe option, so it is the one nobody can take (hard-won law 3).

get.description:
`GET /counter-receipts` — **money taken at a counter, in payments.**

CR-094-BRC01 lane H, the PO ruling of 2026-09-15: *"payemnt should show in
payments, in ledge and in fiannce books"*. The ledger half is automatic —
the collection posts a balanced pair, so the money is on the journal, the
trial balance and the GL detail for its two accounts the minute it is
taken. **This is the payments half**, and it exists because a row nobody can
open does not satisfy that ruling.

Why these rows are not on `GET /payments`: a `Payment` in this product is a
payment BY AN ACCOUNT, and the whole reason this table exists is that there
is no account yet. Mixing the two into one paginated queryset would give
`totals` two kinds of money to add up and every column an *if*.

Pagination is mandatory on every list (`NFR-3`) and the page is taken in the
DATABASE, ordered by the moment the money was taken.

`f.state` filters to `held`, `applied` or `earned`. `held` is the one a
finance clerk actually opens: it is everything `2400 Customer credit
balances` is carrying for applications nobody has decided yet.

Two members ride alongside the DRF envelope, exactly as `GET /payments`
carries its roll-up:

  `totals`          `taken` and `held` for the CURRENT filter, four-decimal
                    strings with the tenant's `CHAR(3)` beside them. `held`
                    is what is still a liability — the sum of every row's
                    `amount − earned_amount` — which is the figure that
                    should agree with 2400 and is the point of the screen.
                    `by_method` splits the same figures by tender.
  `states`          the three, so a filter control needs no hardcoded list.

⚠ **`f.taken_on` IS HOW A CLERK BALANCES A TILL, AND WITHOUT IT THEY CANNOT.**
`YYYY-MM-DD`, optional, and ABSENT MEANS ABSENT rather than today — this
layer reads no clock (`BR-TEN-043`), so a day is always one the caller
named. **The counter money is never in a deposit batch**: `BR-PAY-025`
groups a batch by day and method and writes membership onto a `payments`
row, and a counter receipt is deliberately not one, because there is no
account yet. A clerk reconciling against batches alone therefore finds the
counter cash missing every single day, and this is the figure that answers
it — `f.taken_on=2026-05-12` with `totals.by_method`'s cash line is what
gets counted against the notes and coin in the drawer.

⚠ **AND NOTHING MOUNTS THIS ENDPOINT — `DEF-PAY-5875`, filed rather than
left in this trailer.** A `grep` of `07-frontend/src/` for it returns
nothing: the screen was deferred when lane H shipped on 2026-09-15 and is
deferred still, so **a clerk cannot balance a till from the product today**
even though the figure above is correct. That is hard-won law 2's mirror —
a live endpoint behind no control — and it is a register row now because a
deferral written only into a docstring is one nobody can count.

`/counters` — ONE route, two verbs, and they are not two views.

⚠ **DJANGO RESOLVES THE PATH FIRST AND THE METHOD SECOND**, so two `path()`
entries with the same pattern would leave the second unreachable: the POST
view would answer 405 for ever and every test of it would have to call the
wrong URL to pass. One view, dispatched on the verb.

⚠ **THE TWO VERBS NEED DIFFERENT ROLES AND `permission_classes` IS PER
VIEW, SO THE WRITE ROLE IS ON THE SERVICE** — which is where `BR-SHL-025`
puts it anyway. `AnyTenantRole` lets an Executive READ the supervisor's
list (A4: payments is VIEW for them), and
`counters.open_counter` carries `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN,
BILLING_CLERK)`, so an Executive pressing *Start counter* is refused by the
service with AUTH-002 no matter what any endpoint allows.

get.description:
`GET /counters/service-centres` — the places a till can be opened at.

⚠ **`DEF-PAY-10768` (L1-11, 2026-10-30) — WHY THIS IS NOT THE SETTINGS
READ.** *Start counter* read `GET /settings/reference-data/service-centres`,
which A4's `settings_lookups` row closes to a Billing Clerk (403, and that
matrix is signed — `SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin`). The clerk is the
person who runs a till, so the list came back empty and *Main office*
could never be chosen. This is the payments-owned read of the same rows:
each centre's `slug` (what `counters._service_centre` resolves) and its
`name`, and nothing else — no hours, actions or portal settings, which
remain Settings' to show.

Every centre, hidden ones too: hidden is a PORTAL state, and a depot a
customer cannot see is still a window a clerk sits at.

`GET /counters/{id}` — 3·2 My counter, with the running split by method.

The split is a `GROUP BY` in the database. The reference the task names,
`counter_receipts.list_totals`, materialises its rows and sums in Python —
right for a screen that lists what it sums, wrong here, where a shift holds
any number of payments and `NFR-5` forbids a cap on it.

post.description:
`POST /counters/{id}/close` — 3·3b, *"does the drawer match?"*

    counted_totals   REQUIRED — {"cash": "510.00", "check": "1284.60"}
    closed_at        REQUIRED — the moment, from the caller
    note             required ONLY when the difference is not zero

**200, not 201.** Nothing is created; the till the screen already had is
sealed. The body is the sealed row, so the screen can show the difference
it just recorded without a second read.

`POST /counters/{id}/declare` — 3·3d, the count, late.

    counted_totals   REQUIRED
    declared_at      REQUIRED — the moment, from the caller
    note             required ONLY when the difference is not zero

⚠ **THE FORCED CLOSE STANDS.** `close_kind` does not move — PO ruling
2026-09-23 §3.2, *"Nothing is erased"*. The row then says both: force-closed
Monday by the supervisor, declared Tuesday by Dana, $12 short.

`POST /counters/{id}/force-close` — 3·3c, supervisor only.

    reason      REQUIRED — a forced close with no reason is a mistake
    closed_at   REQUIRED — the moment, from the caller

⚠ **`SystemAdminOnly` HERE IS NOT THE GUARANTEE.**
`counters.force_close_counter` carries `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)` and is
what actually enforces it (BR-SHL-025). Deleting this decorator would leave
the rule standing; deleting the service's would not.

get.description:
THE registry every placed screen reads (US-TEN-017, BR-TEN-053).

`?entity=assets&screen=S51&mode=input` — one cached read per screen, not a
query per field. Any tenant role, because a meter tech filling in S51 is not
a System Admin; the definitions are tenant configuration, not tenant
secrets, and RLS FORCE plus the explicit tenant filter keep another
utility's field set invisible either way (US-TEN-014 TC-6).

`GET /customers` — CR-056 W5 task 25. THE LIST THAT DID NOT EXIST.

This file's own header recorded the absence, verbatim: *"no story owns a
customer LIST or DETAIL endpoint yet"*. Until today a person could be
reached only BACKWARDS, through an account, so a landlord whose account
numbers nobody remembers was unreachable.

One search box, four legs: the customer number, the legacy reference, the
name, and the phone through its blind index. A READ — no audit row.

⚠ **PAGED IN SQL, NOT IN PYTHON, SINCE 2026-09-18 (`NFR-3`,
`DEF-CUS-5753`).** This route was built on `_paginated`, which slices a
BUILT list — so a landlord-heavy utility built every customer it holds in
order to draw fifty, and each row then asked for that person's accounts on
its own. `selectors.customer_page` takes the page and its `COUNT(*)` in the
database and batches the page's links into one query; `_prepaged` serves
the same envelope `GET /accounts` does, re-clamping `page` per
`BR-SHL-011`.

post.description:
`POST /customers/match` — New Connection step 1's owner lookup
(`CR-164-BRC10` item 11, PO ruling Q5 of 2026-10-02).

A READ carried on POST because its body is a Social Security number, a
licence or a Tax ID, and a query string is logged by every proxy between
the browser and here. Nothing is written, so no audit row. The verdict and
its reasoning are `owner_lookup`'s; this view only scopes the tenant.

get.description:
`GET /customers/{id}` — one person and the accounts linked to them.
**`PATCH /customers/{id}` — BR-CUS-1054, and it did not exist until
2026-09-13.** PO, verbatim: *"Start the customer edit one also - we will
need this"*. A misspelt name, a wrong telephone number and a wrong email
could not be corrected anywhere in the product: this route is read-only no
longer, and the account edit surfaces never reached these fields because
they are not `accounts` columns.

404-never-403 for an id another tenant holds (HR-1/G4): from outside the
tenant, an id that exists elsewhere and an id that does not exist are the
same fact, and telling them apart is a membership oracle.

⚠ **THE WRITE IS GUARDED IN THE SERVICE, NOT HERE.** `AnyTenantRole` reads;
`customer_edit.update_customer` carries `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN,
BILLING_CLERK)` and refuses whichever door forgets — `BR-SHL-025`: the
server-side guard is THE guard. Mounting a narrower permission class on the
whole view would take the READ away from an Executive who has it today.

get.description:
`GET /customers/{id}/deposit-carry-forward` — TC-MVI-2/3 (task 5.5).

**AN OFFER, AND ONLY AN OFFER.** BR-CUS-024's mechanics are PROPOSED and
`deposit_on_file` is a refused field on every non-import door, so there is
no accept path and the payload names the missing rule
(`carry_forward_has_no_accept_path`).

**BR-CUS-089: money moves only on a `strong` match.** The service READS a
stored tier and can neither compute nor accept one — `tier` is not a
parameter of the callable, which a test pins against the signature. Every
other tier is refused carrying `identity_match_strength_has_no_rule`, and
**the refusal shows no figure at all**: a number on a refused offer is an
invitation to type it in by hand. What earns `strong` is **OQ-364**, open.

`GET /customers/{id}/deposit-position` — B18 §5.5.5 (task 5.5).

⚠ **TWO GAPS ARE SERVED HERE AND THEY POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS.**
`deposit_interest_not_readable` — BR-CUS-057's accrual is unbuilt, so
interest and the refundable total are `null` rather than 0.00; a zero would
carry $150.00 where $153.50 is owed. And
`deposit_not_net_of_settlement` — BR-CUS-025 settles the deposit at close
and **nothing writes that back** (`move_out_settlement` returns
`persisted: false`), so a closed account's column is the deposit AS
RECEIVED. Carrying it silently would pay a customer twice.

Both travel to the client verbatim. A READ — no audit row.

CS-12 — every account this customer holds, and every bill still open.

The list a clerk aims one cheque at. Read-only; nothing here writes.

post.description:
CS-12 — ONE cheque from one customer, settling several of their accounts.

    amount           the cheque total, a decimal STRING > 0
    posted_at        the USER's posting date — required (BR-PAY-033)
    cleared_at       the clearing date, or absent = still processing
    method           a tenant method CODE (BR-PAY-026) — optional
    reference        the cheque number — optional, copied onto every part
    memo             optional, and a part may carry its own
    currency         optional; must equal the accounts' (BR-TEN-042)
    idempotency_key  the form's client token — REQUIRED (see the module
                     docstring; it also derives a DISTINCT key per account)
    parts[]          {account_id, amount, apply_to?, targets[]?, memo?}

**The parts must sum to `amount` EXACTLY or nothing at all is recorded** —
no payment, no allocation, no journal entry, no receipt (BR-PAY-1127). The
refusal states both figures and their difference, because *"the amounts do
not add up"* is not something a clerk can act on.

201 on a new tender with every payment it made inline — a clerk who has just
taken $520.00 across three properties has to be shown what each part paid,
and the allocator worked all three out in the same transaction. 200 with
`created: false` on a replay.

get.description:
`GET · POST /cutover-plans` — the go-live plans and their items.

**GET** pages server-side (`NFR-3`, and this module has no unpaginated list
anywhere). **POST** creates a plan with its items in one transaction; a
NULL `runbook_key` on an item is a human task the engine never performs
(`03-field-map.md` D-7), which is why the field is optional here rather than
validated into existence.

Staff read, Admin writes — `07-endpoints.md` §1's standing sentence, applied
by `ReadAnyRoleWriteSystemAdmin` rather than by an `if` inside the view.
`DEF-196` is what an `if` costs.

patch.description:
`PATCH /cutover-plans/{id}/items/{seq}` — tick, un-tick or re-own ONE item.

⚠ **THE ITEM IS ADDRESSED BY `seq` AND NOT BY ITS ID** (B14 rule 31). `seq`
is UNIQUE per plan and is the number an implementer says out loud — *"item 4
is still open"* — so the address a person can read is the address the route
takes.

post.description:
`POST /cutover-plans/{id}/items/{seq}/evidence` — **Attach to plan ✓**.

The run's result becomes the item's evidence, and a run whose verdict
carries no blocker turns the item green on its own (`US-RBS-008` §7). Four
refusals guard it and `cutover.attach_evidence` states each one — the run
must be finished, it must be the runbook the item names, a human task
refuses evidence entirely, and the figures come from the FROZEN report
rather than being recomputed here.

SET-07 step 3 — BR-MET-080's *"47 accounts unscheduled"*, computed
INCLUDING the routes step 2 has just selected.
BR-MET-077 — the same, for SET-07 step 1.
