get.description:
CR-038 W1 — BR-MET-057's chase list (US-MET-018): the cycle's meters
still missing plan-required registers, each named channel by channel, with
unit · premises · meter · route · service · days left — ordered days-left
asc then unit label, shaped for the CSV export a later lane wires (IS-9).

`?period=YYYY-MM-DD` (or `YYYY-MM`) names the reading month; without it
the CURRENT window answers. Before window open the list is EMPTY with
`window_opens` saying when — US-MET-018 TC-6's *"window opens Aug 12"*,
never pending pressure ahead of the window. Bounded by the cycle's own
membership (BR-MET-055 — this can never exceed the cycle's meters).

House URL grammar (resource, then verb-as-subpath); the A11 row for this
route is OWED — see the exceptions trailer.

**CR-054 W1 task 4/5 — `reading_sheet_<cycle>_<month>.csv`.**

One row per expected meter per required register, with the previous reading
and its date already in it. This is the file the PO asked for on 2026-08-30:
*"on step 2 we have ready csv file - with all meters and existing data that
is availale - only details clark has to fill is readings"*.

`?period=YYYY-MM` names the reading month; without it, the tenant's current
month. `?read_method=<code>` writes the stage-1 collection method onto every
row — omitted, the column is blank and BR-MET-014's batch tag inherits.

A cycle with no schedule has no window to expect reads in, so there is no
sheet to serve: it refuses 409, and the refusal REUSES
`metering.read.reason.cycle_window_not_set` — *"The cycle has no read window,
so there is nothing to be outside of"* — the catalogue's own sentence for
exactly this fact, rather than minting an eleventh-catalogue key for it
(G32's ratchet; `cycle_chase_list`'s reuse precedent). REPORTED: the
sentence's trailing clause was written for the out-of-window rule and reads
oddly here; the summary route below states the same absence with no refusal
at all, and that is the one the download button reads.

**CR-054 W1 — what the download button needs to name its own number.**

RDS-03 stage 2 draws *"↓ Reading sheet for CY-001 · 1,180 rows"* (CR-054
task 6), and a button that has to download the file to learn its size is a
button that downloads it twice. Same builder, counted — never a second count
(hard-won law 5).

Answers 200 with `window_absent_reason` set when the cycle has no schedule,
so the button can state the absence without a failed request.

BR-MET-162 (DEF-898) — **the same sheet, asked for by CYCLE.**

PO 2026-08-27: *"allow route of Cycle - both"*. The route sheet already
printed its cycle in its own header, so the cycle was a first-class fact of
the artefact with **no way to ask for one** — and a monthly walk is
organised by cycle as often as by route.

⚠ **A MISSING ENTRY POINT IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY TEST THAT ONLY EXERCISES
THE ENTRY POINT THAT EXISTS**, which is why this shipped half-built and
green: every test asked for a route sheet by route and got one.

Same content, same print-ready HTML, same `AnyTenantRole` read, same HR-1
single 404 for an unknown, malformed or cross-tenant id. The body is
SECTIONED by route because a walk order belongs to a route (D11) and no
ruled ordering exists across routes.

`GET /dashboard/summary` (A11 S7 row · 11b §1) — US-REP-019.

**This route existed in the contract and nowhere else until 2026-08-16**,
which is one half of DEF-129: the first screen after every sign-in had no
story, no screen and no endpoint, and `/{tenant}/dashboard` fell through the
router's catch-all to render the literal string "SMARTBillHub — W0 scaffold".

⚠ **CR-015 (2026-08-19) ADDS `f.period`.** The PO: *"we will ahve to allow
period filter on dashbaord - so user can select the filter."* It is spelled
`f.period` because BR-SHL-011's URL grammar spells a filter `f.<name>`, and
the point of putting it in the URL rather than in component state is that a
period a person is looking at is then SHAREABLE: they can paste the link and
the other person sees the same window. An unknown, misspelled or
no-longer-available value FALLS BACK to the ruled default rather than
refusing — a landing page that 500s on a stale bookmark is a locked front
door, and `f.period=last_cycle` on a tenant that has since retired its only
cycle is exactly that bookmark.

⚠ **CR-012 (2026-08-18) ADDED `asOf` AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT RENAME THIS
ROUTE.** The PO's build spec names `GET /api/dashboard?tenantId&asOf`. Two
halves of that, and they are answered differently:

  `asOf`      ADDED. It picks WHICH accounting period, and it is an argument
              rather than a clock (BR-TEN-043) for the same reason
              `payments.summary` takes one: a dashboard that cannot be asked
              for last month cannot be reconciled against last month's
              day-end. Absent ⇒ the tenant's own today.
  `tenantId`  **REFUSED, and it is not a preference.** The tenant comes from
              the request context (hard rule 1, RLS FORCE). A tenant id in a
              query string is a tenant id a caller can edit.
  the path    UNCHANGED. `GET /dashboard/summary` is A11's own S7 row and a
              SIGNED interface; renaming it is a contract decision, so it is
              REPORTED rather than silently taken.

The window is otherwise the tenant's own computed period (BR-TEN-022) — the
same one S36, S59 and S60 head their pages with, so four screens cannot
disagree about which month a figure belongs to. Everything else the answer
contains is described in `apps/reports/dashboard.py`, whose one law is
BR-REP-024: a tile renders the OWNER's figure or reports that it cannot
answer, never a zero.

Always 200. There is no 404 and no 422: a malformed `asOf` FALLS BACK to the
tenant's today (BR-SHL-011 — an undeclared or impossible parameter falls
back rather than refusing), because a landing page that 500s on a
hand-edited URL is a locked front door. An absent figure is a `null` with a
reason beside it, which is a state of this deployment rather than an error
the caller caused.

`GET /debtors/{id}` — bills, ladder state and history, in ONE call.

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  "Why does this account owe $1,284.60, and what have we already      ║
║   tried?" — 7·2's own question, which nothing answers today.         ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
The blueprint's TODAY line for this screen is four words: *"No such
screen."* The debtor list is a report a clerk cannot drill into, so the
person with the customer on the telephone opens four screens and assembles
the answer themselves.

⚠ **THE SCREEN IS `P4.8` AND IS HELD TO WAVE 2.** This read is built ahead
of it so the screen lane has one call instead of four — and that is said
here, in `debtor_read`'s docstring and on the CR board's `P4.8` row,
because **a read nothing calls is hard-won law 2's dead UI facing
backwards**: it serves nothing, every test passes, and the feature does not
exist. Its consumer is named so the absence is visible rather than assumed.

QUERY PARAMETERS::

    as_of            the clerk's business day — REQUIRED, never a clock
    history_page     which page of the notice trail (default 1)
    history_per      how many rows (clamped to the platform's page sizes)

**ONLY THE HISTORY PAGES, AND `NFR-3` IS WHY.** The position is one row, the
ladder state is one row and the open bills are bounded by the account; the
notice trail grows for ever, because every send AND every skip appends
(J4 step 2) and the ladder runs nightly. It is paged with `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`
**in the database**, and `history_count` is a real `COUNT(*)` — so there is
no number here any row can be beyond (`NFR-5`).

**A cross-tenant or unknown account id reads as ABSENT, never as
forbidden** (`BR-TEN-003`, HR-1): a 403 would confirm the row exists.

A READ. No clock, no money arithmetic, no write, no audit row.

post.description:
A piece of post came back — single or bulk (US-NOT-014 TC-1/TC-2).

Body: `{"message_ids": [...], "returned_on": "2026-08-16"}`. The date is
REQUIRED and is the CALLER's business date (BR-TEN-043) — Tuesday's stack is
marked as Tuesday even when it is worked on Wednesday.

TWO THINGS HAPPEN AND BOTH ARE REPORTED:
  1. the queue row is stamped returned and audited (`delivery.returned`).
     The status does NOT move — a returned letter WAS sent, and overwriting
     that would destroy the fact an auditor needs;
  2. the r12 #8 delivery-return event is handed to **payments' own writer**,
     which sets the bad-address flag, the needs-attention row and the S21
     banner (BR-PAY-018 / US-PAY-016). Notifications writes none of that:
     `payments_seam.flag_returned_addresses` calls payments and payments
     writes payments' table (B1).

**Balances are unaffected** (BR-PAY-018) and nothing here can reach an
invoice, a payment or a journal line.

Paper rows only (TC-6): an email that did not arrive comes back as a
provider BOUNCE on a webhook, which is a fact from an ESP and not something
a clerk can observe about an envelope. Refused rows come back named.

Marking the same envelope twice is a no-op on both sides — the queue row
already carries `returned_at`, and payments' event table is keyed
`UNIQUE (tenant, outbound_message_id)`.

get.description:
S37 / screen 3·1 — one PAGE of the TILL × tender batches, the KPI strip
over the whole filtered set, the chip vocabularies and the named gaps.

`f.status` and `f.method` are the capability matrix's two filters and `q` is
`P1.7`. An unrecognised status REFUSES (422) rather than returning an empty
list: an empty reconciliation queue and an unanswerable one look identical
on screen, and only one of them means "nothing to do".

⚠ **THE PAGE IS TAKEN IN SQL SINCE 2026-09-24 (`DEF-PAY-6554` · `NFR-3` ·
`P1.2`).** This handler used to hand DRF a built dict, so the WIRE was a
full list and the QUERY was unbounded — `StandardPagination` is registered
as the DRF default and an endpoint returning a plain dict never reaches it.
`core.pagination.prepaged` builds byte-for-byte the four keys every other
list serves, with the extras after them.

⚠ **`count` IS THE FILTERED SET AND SO ARE THE TILES, WHICH IS WHY THEY
COME OUT OF THE SAME CALL.** A second `batch_list` for the tiles would be a
second query able to disagree with the first — `batch_kpis`' own recorded
warning. `captured` holds the one body the fetch produced.

⚠ **`statement_imports` STAYS ON THIS BODY.** `ReconciliationStatementPage`
reads the statements to reconcile off the S37 list rather than adding a
route of its own, and that was checked before the envelope moved.

post.description:
Cut ONE drawer day's cleared money into TILL × tender batches (US-PAY-020).

`day` is REQUIRED and is the POSTING day — the physical drawer day, PO
ruling RQ-5 / BR-PAY-025 — and `occurred_at` is the moment the caller names
(BR-TEN-043). Neither is defaulted: a batch cut on the server's idea of
"today" would bank a day the clerk did not choose.

Idempotent by construction — membership is write-once (migration 0005) and
the batch is keyed on (tenant, day, method) — so a double-click cuts nothing
the second time and no total moves (hard rule 6).

get.description:
S39 — one batch: members, the bank side, the trail and the resolutions.

A batch id belonging to another tenant answers 404 and not 403 (BR-TEN-003 /
HR-1): a cross-tenant read must read as ABSENT, because a 403 confirms the
row exists somewhere.

post.description:
A HUMAN names a pairing the exact rule could not make (S38 step 2 → S40).

This is how the card day gets tied at all: the amounts differ by the
processor's fee, so `auto_match` leaves both sides alone and a person says
*"that credit is this deposit"*. **It is not a force-match** — nothing
reconciles here and BR-PAY-035's superseded button still does not exist. The
difference it returns is what S40 must then explain to zero.

S40 — explain every difference with a reason AND a GL, then reconcile.

The tie-out this cannot skip (US-PAY-022 §7, verbatim): *"Σ reason-coded
explanations + Σ member corrections = difference, then difference = 0 at
reconcile."* A residual has NO path through this route, because
BR-PAY-035 made *"Force match anyway"* permanently superseded and there is
no flag here that would carry it.

`resolutions[]` each carry `reason_code`, `gl_account_id` and a SIGNED
`amount` string — the card day's processor fee is `-147.50`. The service
checks every account is live in this tenant's own chart and refuses a
resolution that names none.

BR-PAY-004's ONLY way back — confirm + REASON, audited (US-PAY-023 TC-4).

The reason is required by the service and named here so the form can say so
before the round trip: Unreconcile re-opens a signed-off day and the trail is
the only record of why. Every prior trail entry survives it, forever.

get.description:
`GET /disconnect-notices/awaiting-proof` — the work queue for `BR-CUS-100`.

The certified letters that went out and whose signed receipt has not come
back. Without this the proof door below is reachable only by a clerk who
already knows a notice id, which nothing on any screen shows them —
hard-won law 2 one level down: a door with no handle.

Declared BEFORE `disconnect-notices/<notice_id>/proof` so the literal
segment `awaiting-proof` cannot be read as a notice id.

post.description:
`POST /disconnect-notices/{id}/proof` — the signed receipt came back.

`BR-CUS-100`, and **this is the door that makes a lawful cut possible at
all**: `schedule_cut` calls `assert_service_proved` and refuses without it.
Before this route existed, the ladder could reach tier 3 and stop there
forever, because the only way to record a green card was a Python shell.

Keyed by NOTICE id, not by account: the proof is a fact about one letter.
`served_on` is required and `signed_for_on` is optional — a receipt can be
returned unsigned, and pretending otherwise would put a signature in the
record that nobody wrote.

get.description:
`GET|PATCH /disconnect-rights-footer` — the five rights clauses.

**The whole card in one round trip**: the five clauses in printing order,
each with its heading, its purpose, its current text, whether it is switched
on, whether the text is still ours, and what ours says — plus the two
sentences that mark a default AS a default (BR-NOT-015 (a)).

⚠ **THE ROLE GATE IS THE SERVICE's** (`@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)` on
`rights_footer.update_clauses`) and this layer does not re-implement it, for
US-NOT-004's reason: a permission class here that happened to disagree with
the service would be two gates for one rule, and the one that mattered would
be whichever a caller reached first.

PATCH body: `{"clauses": {"weather_suppression": {"enabled": false},
"dispute_rights": {"text": "…"}}}`. `"text": null` restores the platform
default for that clause. Only what is named is changed.

get.description:
`GET /disconnects` — S90's Disconnects tab (CR-030 W7 task 7.11, B18 §5.8.2).

⛔ **ONLY `?segment=all` IS SERVED, AND THE REFUSAL IS A SENTENCE, NOT A
500.** B18 §5.8.2's six segments are not mutually exclusive — `On hold` is
computed from the account's protections while `At notice`, `Due to cut`,
`Cut` and `Reconnecting` are the stored `disconnect_cases.state`, and no
rule ranks them (see `disconnect_reads` §3; AN OPEN QUESTION IS OWED). The
selector raises `NotImplementedError` because that is the prime directive's
shape for an unruled path; a clerk must not meet it as a stack trace, so it
is translated here into the catalogue refusal with its message key.

TC-DSC-9: tenant B's `GET /disconnects` returns none of tenant A's — the
selector filters on `app.tenant_id` and `require_tenant` is what sets it.

post.description:
`POST /disconnects/schedule` — `DSC-02.5`'s `Schedule the disconnection ✓`.

**THE DISCONNECT WIZARD'S ONE COMMIT**, and `BR-SHL-019` is satisfied by
this single call: one payload, one address, one transaction. The ten other
ladder routes in this file are not steps of it.

⚠ **IT SCHEDULES; IT NEVER CUTS.** `DSC-02`'s footer is on all five steps —
*"nothing is cut until the scheduled date"* — and the button says
`Schedule the disconnection ✓` and not *Cut* for that reason. `commit_cut`
below is a separate act on the day.

⚠ **`cut_on` IS THE CALLER'S AND IS NOT COMPUTED HERE.** The earliest lawful
cut is the notice date plus the statutory period **rolled forward past
weekends and public holidays**, and nothing in this product computes that
roll. A layer that added 48 hours would be implementing *"+2 days"* — a
different rule that agrees with B18's fixture by luck, because Aug 22 2026 is
a Saturday and Aug 24 the Monday, so the drawn case needs no roll at all.

⚠ **`services` IS `{service_code: treatment}`**, never a bare list, *"so a
caller cannot pass a bare list of services and leave the treatment
implied"*. A `restrictor` value is refused BY NAME — `OQ-385` is open and
what a restricted service is CHARGED is unsigned, so building one would
invent a price.

⚠ **`reason` is recorded and NOTHING BRANCHES ON IT** — `OQ-382` asks which
of the five drawn reasons may lawfully cut and on whose authority, and it is
open. Four of the five have no path to a cut today because none reaches
tier 3. This route does not widen that and does not pretend it has.

get.description:
`GET /disconnects/{ref}` — the DISCONNECT CASE RECORD (blueprint p143).

The assembly is `record_detail` and this view adds nothing to it: no figure
is computed here, no absence is defaulted, and **nothing is written.** The
record's three actions post to endpoints that already exist on
`transfer_disconnect_api` — this module mounts no write of its own.

⚠ **`ref` IS THE CASE NUMBER, NEVER A UUID** (B14 rule 31). `DSC-26-0003` is
what a clerk reads back to a customer holding a disconnection notice, and
it is the address the blueprint itself draws.

⚠ **`AdminOrClerk`, NOT `AnyTenantRole`.** Every write this page can reach
is gated to those two roles by `transfer_disconnect_api`, and a page that
hands an Executive the whole cut preview and then refuses every button is
the mismatch that rule exists to prevent.

`GET /disconnects/{ref}/reconnect` — `S148`, both steps, one read.

⚠ **`ref` IS THE CASE NUMBER, NEVER A UUID** (B14 rule 31), and the address
is the case record's own plus one segment — `/disconnects/dsc-26-0005` is
where a clerk comes FROM, so `/disconnects/dsc-26-0005/reconnect` is where
they go, and the back link writes itself.

⚠ **`AdminOrClerk`, NOT `AnyTenantRole`** — the same reasoning
`disconnect_record` states: every write this screen can reach is gated to
those two roles, and a page that shows an Executive the whole restoration
and then refuses every button is the mismatch that rule prevents.

post.description:
`POST /disconnects/{ref}/reconnect/complete` — the request is done; service is back.

⚠ **A STAFF ACT, NEVER A FIELD SIDE-EFFECT** (`BR-PAY-036`). The reconnect
job's state is SHOWN on the screen and on the case; closing it in the field
restores nothing by itself. Refused by name before the request
(`not_reconnecting`) and after the restoration (`no_open_case`), so the
*Service restored* message is queued exactly once.

`POST /disconnects/{ref}/reconnect/request` — S148's Confirm on a CUT case.

Body: `{"on_date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "services": ["water", …]}` — `services`
are the rows still to be raised on *Work order*; rows on *Remote* or *No
visit*, and rows the clerk already raised from the row, are not sent. An
unpaid balance never refuses (`BR-CUS-1097`); the request is recorded with
what was owed, who and when (`mark_reconnecting`'s audit row).

`POST /disconnects/{ref}/reconnect/work-orders` — raise ONE row's visit.

⚠ **THE CLERK RAISES IT FROM THE ROW, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF 4.5.**
Before this, a work order was IMPLIED: `mark_reconnecting` raised whatever
templates a clerk had ticked, at commit, and the row showed a word. A word
is not a job — hard-won law 2 read from the screen end — so the row now
carries the act, and a raised one shows its reference and who it is with.

⚠ **IT GOES THROUGH `services._raise_flow_work` AND NOWHERE ELSE.** That is
the named door customers already uses to ask Work for a job, and `G78` fails
a foreign write from Work's first commit. This endpoint adds an address; it
adds no new way into Work's tables.

⚠ **IT NEVER FAILS THE SCREEN** (`BR-WRK-055`). `_raise_flow_work` returns
the sentence rather than raising, so a deactivated template or an absent
seam comes back as a warning on a row and the clerk carries on. A field
module able to stop a restoration because a template was retired would be
this product refusing to put somebody's water back on over a catalogue row.
`{ended_on, reason}` — end ONE enrollment (the Accounts tab's row act).

`{}` — the proof is on file: ONE *Proof pending* enrollment becomes
*Receiving* (the Accounts tab's row act).

DEF-RAT-9325 (CR-166 task 9 web walk): `discount_services.verify_enrolment`
was built and never routed, so an enrollment whose version needs proof
before the first reduction stayed pending for ever and its bill never
carried the discount — Senior 15% on a $60.00 bill read $0.00, not −$9.00.
The service decides everything (the recertification clock, the audit row);
this view only opens the door.

`GET /discount-programmes` — B18 §5.5.5, and it is a SECOND NAME.

⚠ `GET /discounts` already serves these rows (`apps/rating/api.discounts`
over `rating.selectors.discount_list`); CR-013 part 3 built the whole
catalogue on 2026-08-19. This route exists because B18 names it and the
move-in panel asks for it, and it reads THROUGH THE SEAM to that same
table rather than growing a parallel catalogue — which would be
BR-RAT-069's *"available is not granted"* failure under a different name.
Programmes are tenant-authored, not a shipped list. REPORTED against B18.

Every list the New discount form renders — the utility's own program
owners, exclusivity groups and who-qualifies values (Settings › Reference
data) and the fixed vocabularies — plus the utility's currency.

ONE discount — the read behind `CHG-01.discount` (BR-RAT-084, §18 row 11).

⚠ It serves **counts, never people**: no enrolment row, no account id and no
document reaches this payload, so BR-RAT-079's restricted income and medical
proof cannot leak through a list that forgot to filter.

The Accounts tab — who receives it, paged, searched and filtered in SQL
(`f.status`, `f.plan`, `q`). BR-RAT-079: a proof document is served to a
System Admin only, as the account document's id (`DEF-CUS-9780`).

Approve — the LAST act: the version goes live by itself on its start

Every change to the discount, its versions, its plan links and its
enrollments, newest first, paged: `{at, actor, action, before, after,

`?format=csv` (`DEF-1005`) streams every row, 500 a read (NFR-3, no cap).

`{code, name}` — `DEF-RAT-9310`: a NEW DRAFT discount copied from the
version in force (`discount_services.duplicate_discount`).

patch.description:
CR-066 B3 — where this discount posts. `{"gl_account_id": uuid | null}`.

⚠ **THE OBJECT ROUTE STAYS READ-ONLY AND THIS IS NOT A CRACK IN THAT.** The
block above says an edit to a discount is a NEW DATED VERSION and never a
PATCH, because BR-RAT-078 makes enrolments survive versioning. **A GL
account is not part of the priced agreement**: it moves no money, changes no
customer's reduction, and is the same kind of fact as
`charges.gl_account_id` two screens over — a mapping a bookkeeper re-points
on Settings → Accounting. So it gets its own narrow door, named for exactly
the one field it writes, and the versioned door remains the only way to
change what a discount is WORTH.

The refusals and the audit row belong to `services.set_discount_gl_account`;
this is `require_tenant` + delegate, the shape every other write here has.

⚠ **THE `GET` IS `DEF-RAT-5817` AND IT IS HALF THE FIX.** The POST below
refuses a second draft in words; a refusal that says *finish it or discard
it* is only actionable if the clerk can SEE the draft, and until this read
they could not — DIS-02's Audit tab rendered the stated absence *"no

patch.description:
`BR-RAT-1016` verb 1 — edit a DRAFT version that has never been submitted.

A draft has priced nothing, so there is nothing to preserve and nothing to
explain: no reason, no version bump, no approval. The service refuses on any
other status and NAMES the correction route in its refusal, so the road does
not end where a clerk is standing.

post.description:
Make an approved version the one in force, superseding its predecessor —
and lift the DISCOUNT itself out of `draft` (BR-RAT-072's four statuses).

The service refuses a type no engine can price here rather than at bill time
(BR-RAT-068), which is why this is the act that can fail on a version that
saved cleanly.

Approve a pending version. The gate is unchanged — activation still needs
an approval ACT — and a self-approval is recorded rather than refused.

`BR-RAT-1016` verb 2 — correct a LIVE version over the SAME window.

⚠ **IT IS A POST TO A COLLECTION AND NOT A PATCH, AND THE SHAPE IS THE
RULE.** A correction MINTS a row; the corrected version is never rewritten.
The same spelling `POST /taxes/{id}/corrections` already uses, because two
objects answering the same question must not answer it two ways.

`DEF-RAT-5817` — throw a parked DRAFT away, so the edit door reopens.

A `POST` to a named act and not a `DELETE` on the version, which is the
shape `discard_rate_schedule_draft` already uses for the identical index on
`tariff_versions`: what is being asked for is *discard this draft*, an act
the service audits, rather than *remove this row*. The nesting is CHECKED —
`discount_version_or_404` resolves the pair, so a version id belonging to
another discount refuses instead of discarding it.

Submit a DRAFT version for approval — and submitting FREEZES it (§A7.2).

This is the call BR-RAT-077 hangs off: the requirement and the threshold that
decided it are written onto the row HERE and read unchanged at approval.

get.description:
Every document this utility sealed between two dates — the regulator's list.

`CR-048`'s E9 example is the case: *a regulator asking to see the exact
disconnection letter a customer was sent last July*. This answers the first
half — WHICH letters exist and what each one is — and `stored_document`
opens one.

**System Admin only** (step 5f: *"the MOST SENSITIVE OPERATION IN THE
PRODUCT — every document a utility ever sent"*), and **audited**, because
"who asked to see the whole file, and when" is exactly the question that
follows a regulator request.

⚠ **A LIST, NOT A DOWNLOAD.** No bytes are read and no hash is verified here
— verifying 500 documents to draw a table would fetch every object in the
range. The verification happens when a document is OPENED, which is where a
corrupted one has to be caught. The `content_hash` is reported so a caller
holding an archive can check it against ours without asking us to.

⚠ **THE ENUMERATION IS A DATABASE QUERY** over `(tenant, stored_at)`. The bucket
is never listed: it is slow at half a million objects and it is scoped by a
string prefix, which one mistake turns into a cross-tenant read (step 5d
decision 4). The table also returns what a listing never could — *the March
bill for account ACC-1042* rather than a UUID.

One document the register named, opened.

The id came from a row this tenant could already see (`document_register`, or
a reprint), and it is re-resolved under the caller's own tenant context here
— a link is never issued for a document the caller could not have found.

A document that does not exist and a document belonging to somebody else are
**the same 404 with the same body** (HR-1). `document_store` raises the same
`DocumentStoreError` for both and this converts it without inspecting it,
because a handler that could tell them apart would eventually report the
difference.

post.description: Withdraw a claim now. Revoked, never deleted — see the service.

get.description: C2's preview. Params: `from` + `to`, both REQUIRED. Writes nothing.

post.description:
C2's post. Body: `from`, `to`, `posted_at` — all REQUIRED.

The service is the enforcement: the role gate, the closed-period refusal and
the replay guard are all in `apps/ledger/unbilled_accrual.py`, where a
caller that is not this endpoint meets them too.

get.description:
BR-LED-006's five items, computed live, plus every period ever closed.

Params: `from` + `to`, both REQUIRED.

The five items are the rule's own — runs issued · batches reconciled · bank
rec current · accruals posted · remittance recorded — and **three of them
answer `unknown`**, because billing and payments publish no count of
unissued runs, unreconciled batches or unmatched bank lines. Each names the
callable it wants. That is served as it is computed; an API layer that
flattened `unknown` into `incomplete` would erase the distinction between
*"we looked and it is not done"* and *"nobody can look"*, which is the whole
reason the third state exists.

The closed-period history rides along because the S42 banner needs it in the
same paint (*"closed through July"*), and a second request for one date would
be a second round trip for a card.

The captured-cost register (US-LED-019) and a capture (US-LED-018).

**GET** serves ONE PAGE of the filtered set, with a footer and counts that
are still the WHOLE filtered set. `?page` and `?page_size` are the grammar
every other list in the product uses.

⚠ **THIS ENDPOINT WAS UNPAGINATED UNTIL 2026-09-25 (`DEF-LED-6710`)** and
said so in this docstring, on the old 3,000-connection ceiling's reasoning.
`NFR-3` makes server pagination universal and load-bearing; the Finance

get.description:
S74 — the reconciliation the accounting package cannot produce.

Per service, per period: the volume BOUGHT beside the volume BILLED, and the
unaccounted-for percentage between them — leak, meter under-registration or
theft, in one number, computable only here because only this product holds
the billed volumes.

**A ZERO IS NEVER AN ANSWER ON THIS SCREEN.** Every row either carries a
percentage or carries the REASON it cannot, with its count: *"no volume
captured for 1 of 5 water purchases this period"*, *"MMBtu vs ccf"*, *"the
billed volume could not be read"*. The suppressed case is the whole point of
BR-LED-031: against a partial denominator July reads **−13.75%**, a utility
that delivered more than it bought, and that number never reaches a screen,
a CSV, a PDF or this payload.

`basis` defaults to the RULED service period (OQ-202, PO 2026-08-16). The
issued basis is still served — an accountant asking a REVENUE question wants
it — and it labels itself as not the ruled one.

**NOT BUILT — OQ-204 is OPEN.** Served as a named refusal rather than a
404, because a 404 reads as a typo and this is a decision nobody has taken.

See the module header. The screen never calls this: its Download control is
disabled with the same reason, carried on the reconciliation payload. The
route exists so that a client which calls it anyway is told WHY.

patch.description:
US-LED-019's edit — OQ-203's after-close correction — and, since
2026-09-02, **the route that records a settlement and moves the books**.

⚠ **A BODY CARRYING `paid_on` GOES TO `_record_settlement` AND NOWHERE
ELSE** (CR-060 C1 / task T6, PO ruling 2026-09-02: *"why cant to add the
check that whether this is paid or unpaid and allow clark to udpaet it"*).
Setting the date posts `DR cost / CR cash` through the one posting service;
clearing it is lawful while nothing has posted and refused once it has.
Everything below this line is the ordinary edit of a captured fact, which
posts nothing and never has.

While the period is OPEN this is BR-LED-034's ordinary edit. After it has
CLOSED the edit is still lawful (PO 2026-08-16: *"Yes it can be
corrected"*) and `correction_reason` becomes REQUIRED; the response then
carries `after_close`, naming every export batch whose window contains this
purchase. Those batches no longer match the register and the difference has
to be posted by hand at the accounting system's end, because the export is
idempotent and cannot be re-run (BR-LED-004).

**Re-dating a closed-period purchase is refused by name** — moving it is not
correcting it. ⚠ **OQ-227 CLOSED 2026-08-16** and this sentence used to end
*"the two available behaviours each move a different month's
reconciliation"*, i.e. it described an OPEN question. The PO ruled, on the
option as put to them: *"Stay in July (what ships now) — a correction is a
correction. July's register keeps its $310.00; both months' totals are
unchanged. Re-dating is refused by name as a move, not a correction. - this
is correct"*. The behaviour is unchanged; it is now LAW rather than a
placeholder, and the refusal says so to the clerk who hits it.

get.description:
The supplier's own invoice, attached to the purchase it settles.

The Finance blueprint draws this on 5·3a — *"Attach the invoice · drag or
choose the supplier's PDF"* — and the product had nowhere to put it: the PO
reported it on 2026-09-25 as *"in capture invoice User cannot attach invoice
copy digital copy pdf"*.

⚠ **IT IS A LIST AND NOT ONE FIELD.** A purchase can carry several — the
invoice, the delivery note, the credit — which is exactly why
`tenancy/0051` put the link on `stored_documents.source_type`/`source_id`
and gave `supplier_invoices` no column.

⚠ **RETENTION IS RULED AND IS NOT THIS ENDPOINT'S TO RESTATE.** PO
2026-09-25, *"Seven years, same as tax receipts"* (`BR-LED-799`). The store
holds that schedule; nothing here writes one. And B14 rule 33 keeps it off
the screen: rationale is zero words, so the form says nothing about how long
a document is kept.

⚠ **NO SECOND STORE AND NO SECOND UPLOADER.** `apps.tenancy.document_store`
is the one door in, with six calling modules before this one; the screen
mounts the shared `DocumentCapture` (B14 rule 43).

*"Void, never delete"* — BR-LED-035, and **there is no DELETE route at
all**, at any layer. The reason is REQUIRED and is the point of the feature:
the row stays visible in the register precisely so a clerk reconciling
against a supplier statement can see WHY a line was withdrawn.

`voided_at` is a body input (BR-TEN-043) so a retried void stamps one moment.

get.description: C20's charge before it posts. Params: `from` + `to`. Writes nothing.

post.description:
C20's *"period trigger"*. Body: `from`, `to`, `posted_at` — all REQUIRED.

C20 names no endpoint at all — *"a posting path and a period trigger, not a
calculation"* — and this is the trigger. The amount is not in the body and
could not be: it comes from the asset register's own figures, and a typed
figure here would be a second implementation of BR-AST-047 wearing a form.

get.description:
GET — S42's export history. POST — LE-5's recorded, idempotent handover.

GET params: `target` (optional filter). POST body: `from`, `to`, `target`,
`granularity` (default `summary`) and `created_at` (REQUIRED — BR-TEN-043; a
retried send must stamp ONE moment).

**THE FOUR REFUSALS ARE THE FEATURE, and each carries a different catalog
code so a screen can act on them differently:**

    period still open        409 BIZ-LOCKED       BR-LED-017
    already handed over      409 BIZ-IDEMPOTENT   BR-LED-004 (+ the batch)
    the books do not foot    500 SYS-DRIFT        BR-LED-007
    an account has no ref    422 BIZ-COMPLETENESS BR-LED-014

The idempotency refusal carries the EXISTING batch on `params`, because
T5-07's whole recovery path is *re-DOWNLOAD, never re-export* and a refusal
that did not carry the link would send a clerk hunting for it.

**The drift refusal is a 500 on purpose.** SYS-DRIFT's law in the B12 §3
catalog is BR-LED-007, and unbalanced books are not a thing the user did
wrong: they mean a posting-service bypass happened. A 422 would invite the
screen to render it as a field error a clerk could fix.

Two clerks clicking send at once do not race past this: the SELECT above is
checked first, and `uq_export_batches_period_target` catches what a SELECT
cannot — the residual `ExportError` is re-classified through the same table.

post.description:
GET — S42's export history. POST — LE-5's recorded, idempotent handover.

GET params: `target` (optional filter). POST body: `from`, `to`, `target`,
`granularity` (default `summary`) and `created_at` (REQUIRED — BR-TEN-043; a
retried send must stamp ONE moment).

**THE FOUR REFUSALS ARE THE FEATURE, and each carries a different catalog
code so a screen can act on them differently:**

    period still open        409 BIZ-LOCKED       BR-LED-017
    already handed over      409 BIZ-IDEMPOTENT   BR-LED-004 (+ the batch)
    the books do not foot    500 SYS-DRIFT        BR-LED-007
    an account has no ref    422 BIZ-COMPLETENESS BR-LED-014

The idempotency refusal carries the EXISTING batch on `params`, because
T5-07's whole recovery path is *re-DOWNLOAD, never re-export* and a refusal
that did not carry the link would send a clerk hunting for it.

**The drift refusal is a 500 on purpose.** SYS-DRIFT's law in the B12 §3
catalog is BR-LED-007, and unbalanced books are not a thing the user did
wrong: they mean a posting-service bypass happened. A 422 would invite the

Two clerks clicking send at once do not race past this: the SELECT above is
checked first, and `uq_export_batches_period_target` catches what a SELECT
cannot — the residual `ExportError` is re-classified through the same table.

`P5.4` — record what the accounting package's operator said.

Body: `state` (one of `accepted` · `rejected` · `partial`),
`acknowledged_at` (REQUIRED — `BR-TEN-043`; the import happened when it
happened and this file reads no clock), and optionally `reference` — their
id for it in their system — and `note`, which is what they said when the
answer is `rejected` or `partial`.

⚠ **THE BLUEPRINT'S OWN SENTENCE IS THE TASK:** *"Nothing reports back
whether the accounting package accepted it."* A handover recorded who sent
what and when, and then ended; a finance officer asking *"did QuickBooks
take July?"* got `finance.export.noAckStatus`, a stated absence the screen
has rendered since it shipped.

⚠ **A RECORDED ANSWER, NOT A LIVE ONE.** `BR-LED-020` makes v1 a FILE/batch
handover and direct connect v2, so there is nothing to poll. The person who
closes the loop is the clerk the accountant replied to. A live status would
be `DEF-007`'s three green *Connected* chips over nothing.

⚠ **THERE IS NO `pending`, AND AN UNANSWERED BATCH IS NOT IN A STATE.** It
carries `ack_state: null`, which means NOBODY HAS SAID — a different fact
from *the import is running* and from *it was refused*. `DEF-127` is what
it costs to spell those the same way, and the CHECK constraint admits NULL
for exactly that reason.

A batch id from another tenant answers **404**, never 403: HR-1 makes
existence itself non-leaking, and the service refuses it as an unknown batch
under RLS — byte-identical to a batch that never existed.

get.description:
US-LED-016 TC-3 — *"what is the 506.31?"* answered in dimensioned lines.

Param: `code`, the GL account code of the exported figure.

The figure is looked up in the STORED payload and the lines are read for the
BATCH'S OWN window, so a drill-back proves what was HANDED OVER rather than
what the books say now — which is exactly the question an auditor holding the
ERP's copy is asking.

A batch id from another tenant answers **404**, never 403: HR-1 makes
existence itself non-leaking, and `exports.drill_back` refuses it as an
unknown batch under RLS.

`P4.2` — the FILE of a recorded hand-over. The re-download door.

`BR-LED-004`'s refusal of a second export says so in as many words: *"The
ratified door is to RE-DOWNLOAD the recorded batch"*, and until today that
door opened onto nothing — `apps/ledger/exports.py` said *"No file is
written and nothing is sent"* and the hand-over history drew **Not
written** in the File column.

**The bytes are re-derived from the batch's FROZEN payload on every
request** (`apps/ledger/export_files.render`), which is what makes `J19`
step 7's hash-stability true by construction: there is one thing in the
world the file comes from, so two downloads cannot differ, and
`US-LED-006` TC-4's later ref edit cannot reach a batch already sent
(`BR-TEN-020`, CLAUDE.md rule 4).

**A batch id from another tenant answers 404**, never 403 — the lookup is
an ordinary RLS-scoped query, so the row is not hidden from the answer, it
is not in the set the answer is computed from (HR-1).

⚠ **`X-Cost-Rows-Omitted` IS NOT A DETAIL.** The three vendor targets carry
the journal rows only, because an import file must foot and `BR-LED-039`'s
cost section deliberately does not (`US-LED-021` TC-7). The header states
how many rows were left out so *"seven rows"* and *"seven of nine rows"*
can never read the same; it is `0` on CSV, which carries everything.

⚠ **IT HONOURS THE TENANT'S RETENTION WINDOW SINCE `P4.9`** — the *Keep
files for* setting on the accounting connection. Past the window the file is
refused with the tenant's own number in the sentence. **The payload is NOT
purged**; see `_retention_months` for why that half is a question rather
than a feature.

The batches whose cost section no longer matches the register.

**This route is the CONDITION the Product Owner attached to OQ-203.** They
permitted the after-close correction — *"Yes it can be corrected"* — on the
stated basis that the utility is told **which exported batch no longer
matches**, so a human can fix it at the ERP end. The registry row is blunt
about the alternative: *"Building the edit without that warning would be
worse than freezing it."*

Every figure carries its currency and both sides are quoted — *"carried
51,902.50 USD, the register now totals 51,747.50 USD"* — because the person
receiving this warning has to go and post the difference by hand.

BR-LED-004's dimension extracts — by service · premises · authority.

Params: `from` + `to` (REQUIRED).

⚠ **THIS SAID THE BY-PREMISES EXTRACT ANSWERS `available: false` UNTIL
2026-09-03, AND IT HAS ANSWERED WITH REAL ROWS SINCE 2026-08-16
(`DEF-2345`, completing `DEF-3382`).** It read: *"the by-premises extract
answers `available: false` and says what it cannot attribute, because
`journal_lines.premises_id` is NULL on every line in the product
(US-LED-002 unbuilt) … an empty table would read as 'no activity this
period' over 553.69 of billed money."* **US-LED-002 landed on 2026-08-16**:
`posting._stamped` resolves account → unit → premises at posting time, and
the extract now carries LE-6's three rows — **500 Main St 247.87 · Oak Grove
16.42 · Marina Bay 289.40**, footing to the same **553.69** that used to be
the refusal's measurement. The money did not move; it acquired an address.

**WHAT IS STILL PASSED THROUGH UNCHANGED, because it is still right:** this
endpoint derives nothing. `reporting.by_premises_summary` remains the single
read, refusals and all — a tenant whose chart designates no AR account still
gets `available: false`, and money that lawfully carries no premises is still
reported beside the table as `unattributed_*` rather than dropped from the
footer.

S43's balanced preview, and the four gates said out loud BEFORE a send.

Params: `from` + `to` (REQUIRED), `target` (REQUIRED — one of
`models.EXPORT_TARGETS`), `granularity` (default `summary`).

Writes NOTHING. It runs the same gates `create_export_batch` runs and reports
which ones would refuse, so the modal can say *"July is still open"* or
*"6900 · Bad debt has no QBO ref"* before a clerk clicks send rather than
after. That is the whole reason the preview exists as a separate read: a
refusal a human meets on the confirm button is a refusal they meet with the
modal already dismissed.

Every period this tenant has ever closed, newest first (US-LED-015 §5's
*closed-through* card). No window: the question is "what is shut".

Not paginated, and that is not an oversight of 11b G5. The row count is one
per CLOSED period — twelve a year for a monthly tenant — not one per
transaction, and the S42 banner reads the newest row of the whole set.

post.description:
BR-LED-018 — WARN + CONFIRM. Never a silent close, never a hard lockout.

Body: `from`, `to`, `closed_at` (REQUIRED — BR-TEN-043) and `reason`
(required only when the checklist is not complete).

**The 422 over an incomplete checklist is the WARN, not a lockout.** It names
every incomplete item in `params.incomplete`, and the same request with a
reason succeeds — that is what BR-LED-018 means by *close-anyway with an
audited reason*. The items are SNAPSHOTTED beside the reason on the close row
by `apps.ledger.close`, because recomputing them later answers a different
question (J19 step 1's *"reason + incomplete-item snapshot recorded on the
close"*).

⚠ **THE ROLE GATE IS RULED, NOT READ — AMENDED 2026-09-24. THIS PARAGRAPH
SAID THE OPPOSITE.** PO ruling 2026-09-24, verbatim: *"system admin and
clark"*. **So System Admin + Billing Clerk close a month by signed law
(BR-LED-006, amended), and `POST /finance/periods/reopen` stays System Admin
only — confirmed the same day, verbatim: *"yes correct - Reopening a month
System Admin only"*.** The gate did NOT move; what moved is that it stopped
describing itself as a guess. `close.ROLE_GATE_IS_A_READING` and its
`unavailable` sentence are RETIRED, so this response's `unavailable` is now
EMPTY where it used to carry one entry.

Until that day the two roles were carried from OQ-175 (2026-08-12, *"System
Admin, Billing Clerk"* — **about REVERSING a posted entry**) and EP-LED-05 §8
flagged the carry. ⚠ **§8 FLAGS TWO CARRIES AND THIS RULING COVERS ONE: the
REMITTANCE record below was never put to the PO and stays flagged.**

The permission class here matches the service gate deliberately: a mismatch
would answer 403 in one layer and 200 in the other.

BR-LED-006 / BR-TEN-038 — *"SysAdmin reopens"*, with a reason, audited.

Body: `from`, `to`, `reopened_at` (REQUIRED) and `reason` (REQUIRED).

This is the one role gate in the close family that IS separately ruled rather
than read across from OQ-175: both rules name the System Admin explicitly, so
a Billing Clerk who may close a month may not reopen one (US-LED-015 TC-4).
The permission class says so at the door and `close.reopen_period` says so
again at the service, which BR-SHL-025 makes the enforcement either way.

The reason is required BEFORE the door opens, not after: a reopened month can
receive entries that change totals an ERP has already been handed
(BR-LED-017), so the record of why has to exist first.

get.description:
S36's whole tab, out of journal-line dimensions and nothing else.

Params: `from` + `to` (both REQUIRED — a KPI strip with no period states a
money figure over an unstated window, which is BR-REP-001's whole subject),
and `ytd_start`, the first day of the tenant's fiscal year for the
*Written off YTD* KPI.

**`ytd_start` IS NOT DEFAULTED AND IS NOT DERIVED HERE.** BR-TEN-022 makes
periods COMPUTED from fiscal settings and never stored, so no row holds it;
`reporting.revenue_and_ar` takes it as an input for exactly that reason and
says so. Omitting it makes the read model sum write-offs from the beginning
of the books — a real number that is not a year-to-date one — so this
endpoint serves `written_off_ytd: null` with the reason attached rather
than mislabelling it (`wire.WRITTEN_OFF_YTD_WINDOW_UNSTATED`). The screen
passes the day it reads off S8's Regional tab and the KPI fills in.

NOT PAGINATED, and that is not an oversight of 11b G5. This is a DASHBOARD
resource, not a list: its `revenue_by_service` table is bounded by the
tenant's enabled service set (six, BR-REP-006) and its KPI strip is the
DENOMINATOR those rows foot to. A page of it would make the footer a page
total — the same reasoning `GET /billing/runs/{id}/findings` records.

S41 Taxes & Remittance — BOTH bases, always (BR-LED-002 / BR-LED-013).

11b §1 marks this row **OK** with one amendment: *"dual-basis always —
billed AND collected per authority + basis indicator + remitted/outstanding
columns"*, superseding the prototype's collected-only table. The amendment
is honoured in the only way the books allow it to be: the billed basis is
real (LE-3's **47.38** across the three July bills, split State 13.87 ·
County 2.22 · City 4.44 · PUC 0.44), `remitted` is real (Σ debits from
remittance-sourced entries — the JE that drains the liability), and the
COLLECTED column is served **null with its reason** rather than filled with
the billed figure.

That null is BR-LED-002's own definition refusing to be guessed: *"tax
inside cleared payments via allocation"*, and an `allocations` row carries
no line class (OQ-129). LE-3's signed **20.97** works only because that
allocation covered its tax lines IN FULL; what a PARTIAL payment meets —
tax pro-rata, first, or last — is a money rule nobody has signed, and one
invented here would decide permanently and invisibly how much tax a utility
remits.

`remitting_basis` is null per authority for the same class of reason: r13
#3 puts the setting on `tax_remittances`, that table does not exist, and
LE-3 has State on COLLECTED while County is on BILLED — so `outstanding` is
given PER BASIS and never as one number, because a default would be wrong
for one of them in the first month it ran.

Params `from` + `to` are REQUIRED: a remittance table is always *for a
period* (an authority is filed with quarterly or monthly), and an unstated
window would make "outstanding" mean something different to every reader.

POST — record a filing. GET — `P4.11`'s filing history.

US-LED-014 TC-3 — DR the authority's tax payable / CR cash, balanced.

Body: `tax_account_id` (the authority's own 2200-nn account — BR-BIL-069
makes the account the authority's identity in the books), `from`, `to`,
`amount` (a decimal STRING), `basis` (`billed` or `collected`),
`confirmation_ref` (REQUIRED — BR-LED-019), `entry_date` and `posted_at`.

**The amount is the caller's and is never derived here.** It is the figure a
human read off S41 and actually paid. Deriving it would make the payment
agree with the report by construction, which is exactly the property that
hides a wrong report.

⚠ **A `receipt` FILE IS ACCEPTED AND KEPT SINCE 2026-09-24 (`P4.3`).** This
paragraph read *"a receipt file is refused BY NAME … `tax_remittances` is
not in the schema, so accepting a file and dropping it would leave a clerk
believing it was kept"* — which was true and is not now. `ledger/0020`
builds the register and `tenancy/0052` makes `tax_remittance` a document
source, so the file goes to `stored_documents` against the filing it proves.
Send it as **multipart**, under the field name `receipt`; a JSON body with
no file still works exactly as before.

⚠ **THE ROLE GATE HERE IS STILL A READING, AND THIS SENTENCE NO LONGER
LEANS ON THE CLOSE (amended 2026-09-24).** It read *"same flagged role
reading as the close"*, and the close's reading became a RULING that day
(PO, *"system admin and clark"*, BR-LED-006 amended) — so a pointer saying
*same as the close* would now read as *ratified*, which is exactly backwards.

**Recording a remittance was never put to the PO.** OQ-175 (2026-08-12) was
about REVERSING a posted entry; 2026-09-24 was about CLOSING A MONTH. Neither
was about handing money to a tax authority, so `AdminOrClerk` is carried here
as the reading EP-LED-05 §8 flags, and it **RETURNS TO THE AGENDA**. A
signature covers only what was shown. `journal.ROLE_GATE_IS_THE_API_HALF` and
this docstring carry it rather than treating it as ratified.

post.description:
POST — record a filing. GET — `P4.11`'s filing history.

US-LED-014 TC-3 — DR the authority's tax payable / CR cash, balanced.

Body: `tax_account_id` (the authority's own 2200-nn account — BR-BIL-069
makes the account the authority's identity in the books), `from`, `to`,
`amount` (a decimal STRING), `basis` (`billed` or `collected`),
`confirmation_ref` (REQUIRED — BR-LED-019), `entry_date` and `posted_at`.

**The amount is the caller's and is never derived here.** It is the figure a
human read off S41 and actually paid. Deriving it would make the payment
agree with the report by construction, which is exactly the property that
hides a wrong report.

⚠ **A `receipt` FILE IS ACCEPTED AND KEPT SINCE 2026-09-24 (`P4.3`).** This
paragraph read *"a receipt file is refused BY NAME … `tax_remittances` is
not in the schema, so accepting a file and dropping it would leave a clerk
believing it was kept"* — which was true and is not now. `ledger/0020`
builds the register and `tenancy/0052` makes `tax_remittance` a document
source, so the file goes to `stored_documents` against the filing it proves.
Send it as **multipart**, under the field name `receipt`; a JSON body with
no file still works exactly as before.

⚠ **THE ROLE GATE HERE IS STILL A READING, AND THIS SENTENCE NO LONGER
LEANS ON THE CLOSE (amended 2026-09-24).** It read *"same flagged role
reading as the close"*, and the close's reading became a RULING that day
(PO, *"system admin and clark"*, BR-LED-006 amended) — so a pointer saying
*same as the close* would now read as *ratified*, which is exactly backwards.

**Recording a remittance was never put to the PO.** OQ-175 (2026-08-12) was
about REVERSING a posted entry; 2026-09-24 was about CLOSING A MONTH. Neither
was about handing money to a tax authority, so `AdminOrClerk` is carried here
as the reading EP-LED-05 §8 flags, and it **RETURNS TO THE AGENDA**. A
signature covers only what was shown. `journal.ROLE_GATE_IS_THE_API_HALF` and
this docstring carry it rather than treating it as ratified.

get.description:
`P4.3` — the filing receipt, followed as an ordinary link.

⚠ **IT REDIRECTS RATHER THAN RETURNING A URL IN A BODY, AND THAT IS THE
WHOLE REASON THIS VIEW EXISTS.** `GET /accounts/{id}/documents/{docId}`
answers `{url: …}` and has **no caller anywhere in the front end** — because
a screen that fetches a link and then opens it is fighting the browser's
popup blocker: the window has to be opened synchronously in the click, and
the URL only arrives after an await. So this one answers **302** and the
cell is a plain `<a download>`: the session cookie authorises the redirect,
the browser saves the file, and no JavaScript is involved at all.

⚠ **THE ROW IS RESOLVED UNDER THIS TENANT FIRST AND THE URL IS MINTED
SECOND.** The same order `account_documents.document_link` uses, for the
same reason: a link is never issued for a document the caller could not have
found. Another utility asking for this filing gets a 404 — the same answer
as for one that never existed (HR-1, BR-TEN-003).

⚠ **THE LINK IT REDIRECTS TO IS A BEARER TOKEN**, minted at
`document_storage.url_ttl_seconds()` and capped at four hours by the PO
ruling of 2026-08-30. Whoever holds it reads this one file with no session
until it expires; it cannot be used to find another.

BR-LED-007's three control-vs-register comparisons — the release blocker.

Params: `from` + `to`, both REQUIRED (they scope the TAX row; AR and
deposits are cumulative control balances — see `tie_out.tie_outs`).

**THE DRIFT AUDIT IS WRITTEN HERE AND ONLY ON DRIFT** (US-LED-004 §5's
`audit_log tieout.drift_detected`; BR-LED-015). It is in the endpoint rather
than in `apps/ledger/tie_out.py` for two reasons that both matter: that
module has NO writes by design (a module that could write could also be made
to store an acknowledgement, and TC-5 forbids one), and an actor only exists
at the request. The row carries both figures and the delta, so a month-end
reviewer can grep `tieout.drift_detected` and read what disagreed without
re-running anything.

⚠ **THIS IS A GET THAT AUDITS, WHICH IS UNUSUAL AND IS DELIBERATE.** The
volume objection — a clerk leaving S36 open writes a row per refresh — is
real and is accepted: drift is a RELEASE BLOCKER, so on a correct book this
writes nothing at all, and on a drifting one a repeated record of *how long
the books disagreed and by how much* is exactly what an auditor asks for
afterwards. A first-observation-only row would need state, and state here is
one small step from the dismiss path TC-5 forbids.

`POST` — stage 1 · EXTRACT: file received, hashed SERVER-SIDE, every row
staged. NOTHING is written to `premises` (BR-MET-085 · B15 §4.1).

`GET` — PRM-04's run table, newest first. A READ; it writes nothing, not
even an audit row, because looking at a list is not an event.

post.description:
`POST` — stage 1 · EXTRACT: file received, hashed SERVER-SIDE, every row
staged. NOTHING is written to `premises` (BR-MET-085 · B15 §4.1).

`GET` — PRM-04's run table, newest first. A READ; it writes nothing, not
even an audit row, because looking at a list is not an event.

get.description:
`CR-025` — the sample CSV stage 1 offers for download. A READ that
writes nothing: header row derived from `target_columns` (BR-MET-088),
one example row (the `reads_template.csv` precedent, BR-MET-032).

⛔ **AND, ON THE SAME URL, WHAT ITS COLUMNS TAKE (`DEF-1077`).** Ask for
`application/json` and this answers the template's NOTES instead of the
file: the columns that declare a `help` sentence, plus any `blank_reason`
this tenant's own data makes true. One resource, two representations —
the notes are ABOUT the sample, so they live at the sample's own address
rather than at a second endpoint that could drift from it.

⚠ **CSV IS STILL THE DEFAULT FOR ANYTHING BROWSER-SHAPED**, which is what
`DEF-553` fixed: a browser sends `Accept: */*` and negotiation lands on
`CsvRenderer`, first in the list. Only an explicit JSON `Accept` — which is
what `ApiClient` sends unless a caller names another type — takes the notes
branch, so the download button is untouched (it asks for `text/csv`).

**THE POLL SURFACE (CR-026).** One run, its counts, its rules and its
live `progress` — *"Validating… 62,000 of 100,000"*.

A READ. It writes nothing, not even an audit row, because a screen asking
*"how far?"* every two seconds is not an event; that is also why it must
stay cheap enough to be asked that often.

⚠ **`?reject_offset=` / `?reject_limit=` — THE REJECT WINDOW (DEF-766).**
"Cheap enough to be asked that often" was a claim this route did not keep:
the reject list rode along unbounded and each reject carries its full source
cells, so the PO's 9,881-reject run answered 4.28 MB every two seconds. The
window defaults to the screen's own first page and is clamped in
`import_runs.reject_window`; the payload states the TOTAL beside it, so the
operator still reads *"9,881"* and the pager still reaches every one of
them — one page per request instead of all of them per poll.

Stage 2's `MAPS TO` list — **the REAL target columns** (BR-MET-088) plus
this tenant's own custom fields, plus `— ignore —`, plus the transforms we
cannot offer and why.

post.description:
**POST the opening balances a run is HOLDING, under the operator's real
changeover date** (PO ruling 2026-08-27).

An accounts import that ran without a changeover date loaded every account
and posted **no journal entry at all** — which is the only state in which
the date is still changeable, because hard rule 4 makes a posted entry
permanent. This is the door that ends that state, and it is the only one.

`{"changeover_on": "2026-07-31"}` — *the last day your old system was in
charge of the money*. That sentence is the label the screen must use: the
Product Owner met the word *cutover* on a screen that blocks people and
could not tell what it was for, and nobody at a two-person utility will do
better.

Stage 4's REHEARSAL — what a commit in this write mode would do. **NO
WRITE**, not even an audit row.

Serves `will_create` / `will_update` / `rejected` / `unplanned_units`, the
`approval` block (BR-MET-098's two bars beside the run's own numbers) and,
for `replace` only, BR-MET-099's three numbers — `not_in_file`,
`skipped_occupied`, `will_deactivate`. The write mode is a BODY field
rather than a query param because it is the operator's choice about a
write, and re-running it is how the screen answers *"what changes if I pick
a different mode"*.

Stage 4 · LOAD — **THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS WORKFLOW THAT WRITES.**

Creates and updates rows of the run's target, retires what a `replace` run
no longer carries (BR-MET-099 — DEACTIVATE, never DELETE), records a
rollback point, and answers with stage 5's receipt. A second commit of the
same run returns that same receipt rather than loading twice (hard rule 6).

⚠ **CR-026 — OVER `ASYNC_ROW_BAR` ROWS THIS ANSWERS 202 AND THE COMMIT RUNS
IN A WORKER** (101.5s measured at 50,000 rows, in ONE transaction: the load
is all-or-nothing and the decision log of 2026-08-22 records why). Three
answers are still given on THIS call and never by poll, because each is a
refusal or a receipt the caller asked for: an already-loaded run returns its
receipt (hard rule 6), a run that never validated is refused, and BR-MET-098's
approval bar is checked before anything is enqueued.

⚠ **BR-MET-098's APPROVER IS CHECKED HERE — AND, SINCE `DEF-545`, IN THE
ENGINE TOO.** The rule reads *"THE APPROVER IS AN OWNER OR AN ADMIN … the
same pair of roles as the rate-change second approval (BR-RAT-091's 10%
bar)"*, and this product's answer to that pair is `SystemAdminOnly` — which
is exactly what `/discounts/{id}/versions/{vid}/approve` already carries.
The clerk keeps the LOAD (that is `AdminOrClerk` above and
`@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN, BILLING_CLERK)` in the service); what they may
not do is be the second pair of eyes.

⚠ **THIS SENTENCE SAID "HERE, AND HERE ONLY" UNTIL 2026-08-27, AND IT ENDED
"REPORTED rather than fixed at source".** Both halves are now false and
that is the point: `import_runs._load_locked` carries its own `BR-MET-098`
refusal, so a service-layer caller — a management command, a worker, the
next module — no longer walks past the only check there was (`BR-SHL-025`,
defence in depth). **The two layers are deliberately not identical.** This
one refuses `approved` from a non-admin ALWAYS, because at the edge a flag
a caller may not set is worth refusing on sight. The engine's fires only
where the bar is actually crossed, because that is where the rule speaks.
Do not "align" them by loosening this one.

get.description:
Stage 5 · RESULT — the receipt, READ from what the run recorded.

⚠ Nothing on this path counts a row again (BR-MET-090's posture applied
past the commit): a receipt reading *"245 loaded"* in August must still
read it in December, whatever anyone has deactivated since.

⚠ **`import_runs._run` IS REACHED FOR DELIBERATELY AND IT IS REPORTED.**
`receipt()` takes the run MODEL and the module publishes no
`read_receipt(run_id)`. The alternative was an ORM query in this file,
which B8/LAW 0 forbids outright; `_run` is a tenant-scoped read inside the
SAME app that raises `NotFoundError` for a run of another tenant, so the
module boundary is intact and only the underscore is wrong. A public
`read_receipt` belongs in `import_runs.py`, which this lane does not own,
and is REPORTED in the build report rather than reached into twice.

⚠ **AND TODAY THIS ROUTE REFUSES EVERY RUN THAT HAS A RECEIPT (`DEF-541`).**
`_run()` rejects the statuses `loaded` and `rolled_back` before `receipt()`
is reached — one guard that also kills the load's idempotency branch and
the rollback entirely. The route is mounted rather than withheld because it
is CORRECT: when that guard learns to take its allowed statuses from its
caller, this answers without a line changing here. The screen does not
depend on it — stage 5 draws the receipt `/load` already answered with.

`GET /imports/{run_id}/results.csv?kind=successes|failures` — **the two
files a migration comes out as (CR-047 task 13).**

PO ruling 2026-08-29, verbatim: *"at the end we need 2 CsV file 1 for
success record and other for failed records"*.

⚠ **THE FAILURES FILE IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN FILE PLUS TWO COLUMNS**
(`why_it_failed`, `how_to_fix_it`) — same headers, same order, same cells.
They fix two things in the spreadsheet they already know and upload it
again; a file under OUR column names would have to be re-mapped first.

⚠ **IT STREAMS.** `StreamingHttpResponse` over a generator that reads the
run's rows from the database in chunks, because the file sizes the PO named
for this runner are *"50,000 or 100,000 … at a time"* and a 100,000-row CSV
built in memory is DEF-766's 4.28 MB payload twenty times over. Nothing
larger than one row exists at once.

⚠ **`CsvRenderer` FIRST, FOR `DEF-553`'S REASON.** `@api_view`'s default
renderers satisfy only JSON, so DRF's content negotiation refused a
browser's `Accept` with 400 *before the view ran* and the S28 template
button had never downloaded anything. This view returns an
`HttpResponse` subclass and never calls `render`; the renderer exists so
negotiation has a media type that matches.

A READ: it writes nothing, not even an audit row — downloading the receipt
of a run is not an event (`imports`' own GET takes the same posture).

post.description:
Reverse what a run created — and it **DEACTIVATES; IT DOES NOT DELETE**
(hard rule 4), skipping anything now occupied and reporting how many.

Answers the same receipt shape stage 5 draws, with the run now
`rolled_back` and its rollback point spent, so one screen renders both.

patch.description:
r10's inline correction — *"Fix the rejects here — no need to
re-upload"* — patch ONE staged row's raw cells by source-column name
(CR-028: *"Load into inventory instead"* is this route clearing
`UNIT_REF`). Writes RUN ROWS ONLY, never a target row, and sends the run
back to stage 1 so stages 2–3 re-judge before anything can commit. The
`read_batch_row` PATCH is the shape's precedent.

post.description:
Stage 2's "Save mapping as template" (BR-AST-048 — COPY-ON-WRITE: a new
tenant row in tenancy's `import_mappings`, never an update of a system
default). Writes ONE tenancy row through the seam; no run row moves.

Stage 2 · TRANSFORM — in / duplicates dropped / forward. NO WRITE.

**202 over `ASYNC_ROW_BAR` rows** — measured at 77.9s for 50,000, which no
browser waits for; poll `GET /imports/{id}` (or the job's own URL) for the
gauge. Under the bar, unchanged: 200, with the answer.

Stage 3 · VALIDATE — checked / clean / errors / warnings, the rules AS
THEY WERE (BR-MET-090) and the reject list. NO WRITE.

**202 over `ASYNC_ROW_BAR` rows** (50.8s measured at 50,000), as transform.

get.description:
`GET /in-app-messages` — the bell's badge and its popover, in one read.

One request rather than two, because the badge and the list are drawn
together and a count fetched separately from the list it counts is a count
that can disagree with what is on screen.

post.description: `POST /in-app-messages/read-all` — the popover's "Mark all read".

`POST /in-app-messages/{id}/read` — opening a message in the bell.

Idempotent: a second click on an already-read message returns the same
message rather than an error, because clicking twice is not a mistake worth
reporting to anybody.

get.description:
`GET /integrations` — seventeen cards from the registry, this tenant's state.

Under the request's tenant context (BE-01) RLS FORCE already hides every
other tenant's rows; the selector's own `tenant_id` filter is the second
guard. The payload carries `credential.hint` (`••••3F9A`) and never a
payload — the credential table's encrypted column is not even read.

`POST /api/{utility}/integrations/inbound/{key}/{operation}` — the
per-utility address. An operation a manifest PUBLISHES on the partner
surface (`served_path`) is not answered here; see `_serve`.

post.description:
`POST /api/{utility}/integrations/inbound/{key}/{operation}` — the
per-utility address. An operation a manifest PUBLISHES on the partner
surface (`served_path`) is not answered here; see `_serve`.

`POST /integrations/meter-reading/fetch` → 200 `{result, reading,
message_key}` — DEF-CUS-10050, ONE request per press of *Fetch reading*.
Body `{meter_no, as_of?}` (`as_of` = `YYYY-MM-DD`: the reading on or last
before that day; absent = the latest). See `meter_reading.fetch` for the
four results. Nothing is written.

get.description:
`GET /integrations/page-policy` — the generated Content-Security-Policy.

⚠ **`AllowAny`, AND `page_policy.py`'s DOCSTRING CARRIES THE REASONING.**
In one sentence: a document is served before anybody signs in, an SPA does
not reload after sign-in, so a policy computed from a session would be
computed once on the login page with no hosts in it and the map would be
blocked for the rest of the session by a policy that was correct when it
was made. What this discloses is the set of hosts the browser is about to
be told to fetch from — a fact any viewer reads out of their own developer
tools a second later — and no credential, count, name or row.

Read by `07-frontend/server.mjs`, which puts the value on the DOCUMENT
response. A header on this JSON governs nothing a browser enforces; the
document's does.

post.description: `POST /api/{utility}/integrations/platform/sms_twilio/status` — signed.

get.description: `GET /integrations/subprocessors` — the register, derived (TC-8).

delete.description: `PATCH /integrations/{key}` (non-secret settings) · `DELETE` (disconnect).

patch.description: `PATCH /integrations/{key}` (non-secret settings) · `DELETE` (disconnect).

get.description:
`GET /integrations/{key}/access-log` — *Who has been reading* (S142).

One row per page a partner took: when, what they took, how many, and the
key's HINT. Never the key — `IntegrationRun` never held one, because
`PartnerCaller` never carried one out of `resolve_caller()`.

⚠ **THIS IS NOT A SECOND RECORD.** Wave C's `IntegrationRun` is the record,
filtered to `direction = inbound_read`; the plan says so and inventing an
`AccessLog` table would have put the same fact in two places and let them
disagree. The screen's name is *Who has been reading*; the storage is runs.

`GET /integrations/gis_esri/address-search?q=&session=` → 200, INLINE.

⚠ **200 AND NOT 202.** Every other provider call in this API answers `202`
with a job id and a poll url; this one answers the candidates themselves,
because `C15` says an inline operation is *a latency budget, not a job*.
There is no `core.jobs` row to poll and no progress for a screen to draw.

**Nothing is written** (`C16`, disposition `offer`). The reply carries
`reachable: false` and a `message_key` when the City is not answering, so
the screen draws frame 66.2's amber box rather than a red error — the City
being slow is not the clerk doing something wrong.

post.description:
`POST /integrations/{key}/apis` — add one custom API (§7.3's form).

Answers the CARD, which is what the screen re-renders: the new row is in
`operations[]` and the Kind has left `custom_api_kinds`, both from the one
read the page already knows how to draw. Answering the ROW would make the
screen splice it in by hand and then disagree with the next fetch about
whether the dropdown still offers that Kind.

patch.description:
`PATCH /integrations/{key}/apis/standard/{operation}` — the switch on an
API that ships with the connector.

⚠ **A SEPARATE ROUTE BECAUSE A STANDARD API HAS NO ROW UNTIL NOW.** Absence
means ON (`custom_apis.is_enabled`), so there is no id to address until
somebody first disagrees with that default — and inventing one so the two
switches could share a URL would mean writing a row per operation per
connection at migration time, for the sake of a tidier route.

⚠ **THE OPERATION NAME IS NOT A DATABASE ID AND IS NEVER RENDERED** (B14
rule 31). It is the manifest's own name — the same string `…/runs` and the
catalogue stem already use in a URL.

delete.description:
`PATCH /integrations/{key}/apis/{id}` — rename, re-point, or switch ·
`DELETE` — remove a custom API.

⚠ **ONE PATCH FOR BOTH THE EDIT AND THE SWITCH, AND THE SERVICE KEEPS THEM
APART.** `enabled` is legal on a STANDARD row and `name`/`url` are not
(R36 — *"standard APis those will be availabel for enable diable but those
will not be editable"*), so `custom_apis.edit` refuses a standard row by
name while `custom_apis.switch` accepts one. Splitting the route instead
would put that rule in the URL, where nothing enforces it.

patch.description:
`PATCH /integrations/{key}/apis/{id}` — rename, re-point, or switch ·
`DELETE` — remove a custom API.

⚠ **ONE PATCH FOR BOTH THE EDIT AND THE SWITCH, AND THE SERVICE KEEPS THEM
APART.** `enabled` is legal on a STANDARD row and `name`/`url` are not
(R36 — *"standard APis those will be availabel for enable diable but those
will not be editable"*), so `custom_apis.edit` refuses a standard row by
name while `custom_apis.switch` accepts one. Splitting the route instead
would put that rule in the URL, where nothing enforces it.

post.description:
`POST /integrations/{key}/arrival` — a file landed on this connection.

Multipart with a `file` part, or a raw body; `operation` names which of the
provider's file operations it arrived for. Answers **201** when the file is
new and **409** when these exact bytes have arrived on this connection
before, with the sentence that names the first arrival by day and time.

⚠ 409 AND NOT 200. A duplicate is a REFUSAL a clerk has to see and act on —
*did Wednesday's upload go in twice?* — and answering 200 with a quiet flag
is how a second application of a bank file becomes invisible. The run row
is written either way, so the arrival itself is never lost.

⚠ THE RESPONSE CARRIES NO FILE CONTENT AND NO CREDENTIAL. It carries the
run's trace id, the content hash, and the refusal sentence — which is what
S142 draws and what a clerk reads down the phone.

`POST /integrations/gis_esri/check-address` → 200 `{result, match,
session, message_key}` — `CR-177-BRC10` task 2, ONE request per press of
*Check address*. Body `{address_line, city, state, postal_code}`. See
`gis.check_address` for the four results. Nothing is written.

`POST /integrations/{key}/connect` → 201 and the card.

Body: `{environment, cadence, label?, fields: {name: value}}` — the
modal's one mapping. The service splits it by the manifest's field kinds,
validates BOTH halves before any write, and stores nothing on a refusal.

`POST /integrations/{key}/credential` — rotate. 202 when a test was
queued behind it, 200 with the card otherwise.

`POST /integrations/{key}/credential/rollback` — the previous version
active again in one row, and nobody re-authorises (US-INT-024).

Answers the CARD, not the credential: the screen wants the connection's
new word (*Not tested yet*) and the refreshed history, and a credential
row is not a thing this API ever serves.

`POST /integrations/{key}/export` — a period was asked for on this connection.

Body: `{operation, period_start, period_end, target}`. Answers **201** when
the window has not gone out on this connection before and **409** when it
has, with the sentence naming the first handover by date. An unregistered
format is refused **422** by name with the list of what this connection
offers, before a run row exists at all.

⚠ THE MIRROR OF `arrival` BELOW, AND THE 409 IS THE SAME ARGUMENT. A second
handover of July is a REFUSAL a clerk has to see and act on — *did I export
July twice?* — and answering 200 with a quiet flag is how an ERP books a
month's revenue twice with nothing going red. The run row is written either
way, so the second request is never invisible.

⚠ AND 422 RATHER THAN 409 FOR THE FORMAT, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL. A
duplicate is a state of the world; an unregistered format is a bad request,
and it leaves no row because nothing was ever a handover (`BR-INT-031` —
inbound degrades, outbound refuses). ⚠ **422 and not 400**: `core/errors.py`
maps the whole VAL class to 422 (IS-7, `OQ-004`'s closure), so every
validation refusal in this product answers 422 and this endpoint is not an
exception. This docstring said 400 until it was read against the running
server.

⚠ THE RESPONSE CARRIES NO FIGURE AND NO FILE. It carries the run's trace
id, the export key, and the refusal sentence — because what is IN the file
is Runbooks' (`BR-INT-054`, `CR-069` §20.4) and this door does not know it.

`POST /integrations/{key}/grant` — the audited grant (S5).

`OQ-INT-1481` was ruled on 2026-09-04 to option (a): **the System Admin**
authorises an outside system to read this utility's payments and bills, and
the authorisation is *"an audited grant on the connection, plus a
subprocessor-register row pointing inward"*. Both halves are here: the
grant is written to the connection's non-secret config and to `audit_log`,
and the register row is DERIVED from it on the next read — so the two can
never disagree, because there is only one of them.

⚠ **NOT (c).** A signed data-processing-agreement reference is NOT a
precondition. The PO did not require one and gating on a document reference
would refuse a lawful connection. Nothing here asks for one.

The permission class is the gate: `SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin` writes
only for a System Admin, which is the ruling expressed as a class rather
than as an `if` somebody could delete.

get.description: `GET` the section (settings, password HINT, recent files) · `PUT` save it.

put.description: `GET` the section (settings, password HINT, recent files) · `PUT` save it.

post.description: A person sends one day again: `{day: "2026-10-05", reason: "…"}`.

**Test connection** — 200 with `{ok, sentence, server_key, …}`, ok or not.

A refusal from the far end is an ANSWER, not an error: it comes back 200
with `ok: false` and its one sentence, the way the card's own test does.

delete.description:
`POST /integrations/{key}/key` — issue or replace · `DELETE` — revoke.

⚠ **THE `POST` BODY IS THE ONLY TIME THE KEY IS EVER RENDERED, ANYWHERE.**
It is not in `GET /integrations`, not on the card, not in the audit row,
not in a run row and not in any error message; `selectors` serves the
four-character hint and nothing else, and no route re-reads it, because
there is nothing stored to re-read (`machine_auth`'s module docstring).
If the person who pressed the button loses this response, the answer is to

the connection's new state and the refreshed key list.

post.description:
`POST /integrations/{key}/key` — issue or replace · `DELETE` — revoke.

It is not in `GET /integrations`, not on the card, not in the audit row,
not in a run row and not in any error message; `selectors` serves the
four-character hint and nothing else, and no route re-reads it, because
there is nothing stored to re-read (`machine_auth`'s module docstring).
If the person who pressed the button loses this response, the answer is to
issue another key — which is what pressing the button again does.
