the connection's new state and the refreshed key list.

get.description: Their words for our things, for one provider — read or set.

put.description: Their words for our things, for one provider — read or set.

get.description:
`GET /integrations/{key}/oauth/return?code=…&state=…` — the trip back.

Answers the CARD, exactly as `credential_rollback` does and for the same
reason: the screen wants the connection's new word and its refreshed
history, and a credential row is not a thing this API ever serves.

⚠ **GET, because a provider redirects a BROWSER here** — it is not our
form post. The `state` nonce minted at `start` is what makes that safe, and
`oauth.complete` refuses before exchanging the code when it does not match.

post.description:
`POST /integrations/{key}/oauth/start` → `{authorize_url, state}`.

⚠ THIS ROUTE REFUSED EVERY CALL UNTIL 2026-09-06 and its docstring said so.
Wave H built the round trip, so the refusal went in the same commit — a
control still refusing over a screen that has landed is the mirror of
hard-won law 2 and costs more than dead UI, because every check passes over
it (DEF-CWP-3925).

The body carries `redirect_uri`: the address the provider brings the person
back to. It is the CALLER's because the front end knows its own origin and
the server does not — a hardcoded one here would work on the demo host and
silently send every production sign-in to the wrong place.

get.description:
The card: provided by the platform, configured or not, sender kind and a
masked tail, callbacks on or off, when a text last left, the last failure.

post.description:
One real text to a number the admin types. Refused by name when the
platform is not set up; audited either way (hard rule 7).

`POST /integrations/gis_esri/premises` → 201 and the premises.

Body: `{parcel?, session?, premises: {...}}`. With a `parcel` the City is
asked again at this moment (`C16`); without one the address is taken as
typed and the row is marked unchecked (`OQ-INT-1471`, ruled option (b)).

⚠ **THE WRITE IS INTEGRATIONS' AND THAT IS A DATED RULING**, not an
oversight: `OQ-INT-1728` was ruled option (a) on 2026-09-06 — a record
update a person makes synchronously on a screen stays with the module that
owns the screen.

`POST /integrations/gis_esri/reconcile` → 200 and the report itself.

Body: `{mode: "preview" | "apply"}`. **`preview` is what a missing mode
means** — hard-won law 3, the unsafe option is the one somebody types.

⚠ **THE ROUTE DID NOT EXIST AND THE RUN HAD NO CALLER (`DEF-INT-5601`).**
`CR-112` reported the sync as *"callable and tested, not yet exposed"*; this
is the exposure. PO ruling R31 of 2026-09-17, verbatim: *"i dont have Run
button here"*.

⚠ **200 AND NOT 202, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF `POST /integrations/{key}/run`
ON THIS SAME FILE, AND THE REASON IS THE REPORT.** That route enqueues and
hands back a job id and a poll url; a `core.jobs` record carries a
`result_link` and no payload, so a clerk pressing *Preview* to find out what
a reconciliation WOULD do would be handed a link to nothing. The thing being
asked for here is the answer, so the answer is what comes back. The
scheduled, unattended form of the same run is Runbooks' (`BR-INT-054`) and
is not this route.

⚠ **`started_by` IS TAKEN FROM THE REQUEST AND NEVER FROM THE BODY.** A
client that could name the person could name somebody else; the name is the
signed-in user's, and a run with no user on the request is refused rather
than recorded as anonymous.

⚠ **`pages` — `?pages=3` or `{"pages": 3}` (`DEF-INT-9849`, PO GIS review
gap 3).** A PREVIEW stops after that many of the City's pages and says so;
with none given a preview reads `gis.MANUAL_PREVIEW_PAGES` (3), because the
whole register at Ann Arbor's size outlasts this worker's 60 seconds and the
clerk got nothing at all. An APPLY with `pages` is refused (all or nothing);
an APPLY without it reads the whole register, exactly as before. The query
string wins over the body, so a hand-typed test URL means what it says.

`POST /integrations/{key}/run` → 202.

Body: `{operation, work?: [...], parameters?: {...}, window?: {from, to},
request_key?}`. The last three are wave K's (`CR-069`): what the request
states, the span a walk covers, and the key a partner-state write may only
be made once under. All three are OPTIONAL and an operation that needs none
is unchanged — which is what let the water meter cloud arrive without a
single edit to this view's contract for the six providers before it.

get.description: The connection's recent activity, and the trace-id search behind it.
One run: its items, its artifact, and the provider's own sentence.

`GET|POST /integrations/{key}/sending-domain` — the DNS records, and who is waiting.

**`GET` never dials and always answers.** It serves what we last stored,
plus the one record we can always give (DMARC, which no ESP issues), so a
panel opens on a connector nobody has checked yet — which is the state every
utility is in on the day the clock starts.

**`POST` is the press that asks the provider**, through the guard like every
other dial in this module, and answers the same shape.

⚠ **200 AND NOT 202, LIKE `reconcile` AND UNLIKE `run`.** A person is
looking at a panel and the thing they asked for IS the answer; a `core.jobs`
record carries a `result_link` and no payload, so a clerk pressing *Check*
would be handed a link to nothing. The operation declares a latency budget
for exactly this (`C15`).

⚠ **THE LONG POLE IS THEIRS, NOT OURS** — PO 2026-09-17: the utility's IT
team takes *"one to three weeks"* and Production waits on them. Which is why
`GET` gives away everything it can before anybody presses anything.

get.description:
`GET /integrations/gis_esri/state` → `{state, message_key}` (PO GIS review
gaps 9 and 12, 2026-10-07).

`none` hides the City's fields; `broken` keeps them and says why in one
sentence; `working` says nothing. Reads the connection row, dials nothing.

post.description:
`POST /integrations/{key}/test` → 202 + `{job_id, status_url}`.

Body: `{recipient?}` — the typed address a mail test sends to. The `jobs`
row exists before the broker message and before this reply.

get.description:
S30 All bills (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-025), and the S21 Bills tab scoped by
`f.account_id` — one endpoint, because a per-tab read model would be a
second place for BR-BIL-063's draft rule and the past-due posture to drift.

Pagination is mandatory on every list (11b G5) and its sizes are ratified
at 50/100/200/500/1000, default 50 (A11 Addendum r2). The page is taken in
the DATABASE: only the rows on screen are serialized.

The header roll-up rides alongside the DRF envelope exactly as
`GET /accounts` answers, and its money members are null — see
`selectors.invoices_rollup`.

S30 bill detail (11b §2.8 · US-BIL-026) — READ ONLY, by law.

An unknown id, a malformed id and another tenant's id are ONE answer
(HR-1 / 11b G4): the response body is byte-identical, so existence cannot
be probed. US-BIL-026 TC-6 requires exactly that, and the screen's own
message names all three possibilities rather than picking one.

US-BIL-015 TC-3 — *"the chain original ↔ credit note ↔ rebill, navigable
both ways"*, served for S30's bill detail.

BOTH DIRECTIONS COME OFF ONE COLUMN (`invoices.corrects_invoice_id`, PO
2026-08-12 closing OQ-120), which is why the chain cannot fork or disagree
with itself. `is_latest` is what BR-BIL-048 lets a new case be opened on —
so a screen can disable "Fix this bill" on a superseded original AND name
its replacement, instead of letting a clerk find out at preview time.

The bill as it was sent — structure, HTML and the link to its page.

READ ONLY, like every other route on an invoice path (BR-BIL-004 / HR-4).
Neither half writes anything: the kept bytes are read and hashed, and the
structure is opened from the frozen payload and the pinned version, so a
clerk refreshing this screen cannot change a customer's record.

⚠ **THE ORIGINAL IS RESOLVED FIRST, BEFORE ANYTHING IS RENDERED.** A bill
with a kept copy has that copy served; the render only fills the structured
bands beside it. Doing it the other way round — render, then decide — is how
a route ends up quietly serving the rebuild when the fetch is slow or
refuses, which is `DEF-2553` again with a stored document in the room.

The printable page (BR-BIL-036's floor), as `application/pdf`.

INLINE, not an attachment: a clerk answering a phone call wants the page on
screen beside the account, and the browser's own viewer offers the download
and the print. The filename is still declared so a save keeps the bill
number rather than a uuid.

⚠ **THE KEPT PAGE, WHEN THERE IS ONE (CR-049 task 4).** This docstring used
to end: *"There is no cached artifact to stream, and pretending otherwise
would claim a durable document exists."* There is one now, it is streamed,
and it is hash-verified on the way out. A bill issued before `v2.88.0` has
none and falls back to the re-render — **which the response SAYS**, in
`X-Document-Provenance`, because a PDF has nowhere to carry a caption and a
rebuild handed over as `application/pdf` with nothing marking it is exactly
what `BR-NOT-027` forbids.

EP-LED-02's capability row, served — and US-LED-005 TC-2's Add.

**NOT PAGINATED.** The row count is the tenant's CHART — the twenty-four
seeded rows plus its own additions plus one per tax authority — and it does
not grow with transaction volume. The Type filter and the designation
picker on the screen are both derived from the whole list, so a page would
make each of them a claim about a page.

`with_references=1` adds the per-kind reference counts every row's Delete
control needs. It is OPT-IN because it is N queries over the journal, and a
screen that only draws the table does not pay for them.

Validate a mapped chart file, and load it only when asked to.

    {"rows": [{"code": "1150", "name": "Trade debtors", "type": "asset"}],
     "commit": false}

**The CSV never reaches this endpoint as a file, and that is deliberate.**
r10's flow is *upload → map columns → validate → load*: the mapping step is
the screen's — a person looking at their own spreadsheet's headers and
saying which column is the code — so the server takes ROWS that have
already been mapped. Parsing a file here would mean this endpoint guessing
which column was which, which is the step the CR gives to a human.

`commit: false` (the default) writes NOTHING and returns the full per-row
report the preview table draws. `commit: true` refuses outright if any row
is invalid or duplicated in the file — see `services.import_accounts` for
why an all-or-nothing load is the usable one.

**System Admin, per CR-008 #4** — the PO's ruling for the whole Accounting
screen. `SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin` allows any tenant role to READ
and only a System Admin to write, and this route is a write.

delete.description:
One chart row: read it, edit it, or remove it if nothing points at it.

⚠ **PATCH ACCEPTS FIVE FIELDS SINCE 2026-10-29 — `code` JOINED THE FOUR
(`CR-196-BRC10`).** It read *"PATCH accepts FOUR fields and refuses every
other, including `code` and `type`"*. The PO ruled, verbatim: *"in many
cases utilities are giving there own GL codes; which means we have to
ability to change existing GL code as per the given utility for that
specific tenant; even if they are used"*. So `code` is accepted — for a
**System Admin only** (Q4 A; a clerk is refused BY NAME by
`services.change_account_code`, and nothing else in the same request lands)
— and applies everywhere at once because everything holds the account's id.
**`type` is still refused** with `field_not_editable` (Q3 A).

⚠ **ONE TRANSACTION FOR THE WHOLE PATCH.** A code change and a rename in one
request either both land or neither does: a refusal raised inside the block
rolls it back and is NOT caught, so hard-won law 14's aborted-transaction
trap cannot arise here.

**GET carries `usage`** — `services.account_code_usage`, the counts and the
closed/exported month the code-change confirmation shows (PO (2) and Q2).

**DELETE is IS-1's hard delete and refuses unless the row is unreferenced
AND every reference kind was readable.** Two of the four kinds are other
modules' reads that publish no reverse lookup, so the answer is *"I cannot
tell"* rather than zero, and this route refuses on that alone. Deactivate is
always available and loses nothing.

post.description: IS-1 deactivate-first. `at` is REQUIRED (BR-TEN-043 — see `_moment`).

The other direction. `at` is read and ignored for the value — the row is
cleared, not stamped — but is still REQUIRED, so both controls send the same
body and neither is the one that "does not need a date".

get.description:
Which accruals owe a day-1 mirror as of `as_of`, and when each is due.

**`as_of` IS REQUIRED AND IS THE CALLER'S** (BR-TEN-043 / gate G6). A read
that took "today" from the server clock could not be asked about a day the
host was down, and a catch-up run is the normal case after one was.

This is the same question `close._accruals_item` asks the month-close
checklist, through the same function, so the checklist and this panel can
never disagree about whether October is safe to bill.

post.description:
BR-LED-005's sweep, run because a human asked. Idempotent by construction.

A replay writes nothing: the posting key is
`journal_entry|<accrual id>|auto_reversed`, one string per accrual forever,
so pressing the button twice produces the same books. Every accrual it
CONSIDERED comes back, including the ones it skipped — an accrual a human
already reversed by hand cannot take a second mirror, and reporting that is
more useful than silently doing nothing (US-LED-012's own posture).

Both `as_of` and `posted_at` are the caller's (BR-TEN-043).

get.description:
BR-LED-014's page — and, since **CR-060 C10 / T11**, the ONE SAVE behind it.

⚠ **`PUT` IS SERVED HERE, ON THE PATH 11b §2.10 NAMES, AND IT USED TO BE
DECLINED.** The reason published on this read said so in terms: *"Half of
what it would write is tenancy's `tenant_services.revenue_account` (a
cross-module write, forbidden by B1)."* **That was right about the
constraint and wrong about the conclusion.** The write goes through the
module that OWNS each column — the ledger writes `ledger_accounts.
designation`, tenancy writes its own row through a published callable — so
there is no cross-module write anywhere on the path. `UNSERVED_MAPPING_WRITE`
is RETIRED with this change rather than reworded, because it describes a
limit that no longer holds (hard-won law 1).

⚠ **ONE VIEW AND NOT TWO, because Django dispatches on the PATH.** A second
`path("ledger/gl-mappings", …)` entry would never be reached: the first
match wins and the read view would answer the PUT with a 405, which is a
route that looks served and is not.

**THE PERMISSION IS PER METHOD AND THE CLASS IS THE ONE THAT DOES THAT.**
`SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin` — any tenant role may READ this map, only
a System Admin may change it, which is the posture the whole Accounting tab
already has. It was `AnyTenantRole` while this was read-only; widening the
method without narrowing the write is DEF-196's shape in reverse.

── THE READ ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Four sections, and every one of them is the LIVE pointer rather than the
seed's default (BR-LED-038 / PO 2026-08-11: *"you create an account, but
allow tenant user to override it"*):

  * **designations** — the twelve of `chart.GL_DESIGNATIONS`, each resolved
    through `apps.ledger.selectors.designation_map()`. A `null` account is a
    REAL and reportable state: `budget_variance` has no seeded home at all
    (its account is an addition to ❄️ frozen B5 line 74 awaiting a finance
    re-sign), and a designation whose account was deactivated resolves to
    nothing until another row claims it.
  * **services** — the tenant's enabled services with their revenue and base
    pointers, read through the seam. When the seam is unwired the section is
    served ABSENT WITH ITS REASON, never as an empty list: "this tenant sells
    nothing" and "the ledger cannot see tenancy" have the same shape, and an
    empty list would render a mapping page that looks complete.
  * **tax_authorities** — every live 2200-series account. B5 line 74 seeds
    none of them (*"tenant authorities mint their own"*), so an empty
    section here means this tenant has entered no authority, which is a
    different fact from a gap and is labelled as one.
  * **export_codes** — US-LED-006's QBO/Xero refs with their gaps, straight
    from `services.export_code_map()`.

get.description:
The S56 list, with drafts, posted entries, reversals and links all
first-class visible (BR-LED-012 / US-LED-013 §1).

The capability row's filters, under BR-SHL-011's `f.<name>` grammar and the
period params the other reads use:

    f.type          standard | accrual | reversing
    f.status        draft | posted
    f.source_type   the raw journal source (invoice, payment, manual_je, …)
    f.premises      entries with a LINE carrying this property   (C24)
    f.ledger_account  entries with a LINE on this chart account  (C23)
    q               searches the JE #, the MEMO and — since `DEF-LED-10071`
                    J1 (PO 2026-10-12) — what any LINE belongs to: account
                    number, customer number, customer name, premises
                    address, unit label. Still one SQL query, still paged;
                    the row is the whole entry.
    from / to       the entry-date window (the matrix's "period" filter)

**THE TWO NEWEST FILTERS SELECT AN ENTRY BY WHAT ITS LINES CARRY, AND THE
ROW REMAINS THE WHOLE ENTRY (CR-060 C24 · C23).** Debit and credit are still
totalled over ALL of an entry's lines, so a filtered row still balances and
`balanced` keeps meaning what it means everywhere else on this screen. Half
an entry is not an entry: totalling only the matching lines would show
`balanced: false` on entries that are perfectly balanced, which is a false
alarm of exactly the kind the trial balance refuses to raise one endpoint
over. See `reporting.journal_entry_list` for why this differs, correctly,
from `trial_balance`'s choice to narrow its sums.

**`f.ledger_account` IS HOW C23's *"open a trial-balance line to its
entries"* IS SERVED**, and it is the cheaper of the two shapes that were on
the table: the row a clerk clicks IS a chart account and this list already
sits on the same screen, so it needs no new read model, no new route and no
new serializer. The alternative was `journal_entry_detail(entry_id)`, a
second read model for one entry — a larger surface for a smaller question.
⚠ **WHAT IT ANSWERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT:** it says WHICH ENTRIES TOUCHED
the account; it does not say what each entry contributed TO it. That figure
is the dimension expansion and is still unbuilt — stated here so a screen
does not present an entry's full debit as its contribution to one account.

**`q` SEARCHES BOTH FIELDS THE MATRIX NAMES — "JE #, memo" — SINCE
BR-LED-021.** OQ-176 is CLOSED (PO 2026-08-12, *"Approve a JE- series"*):
`journal_entries.number` carries a `JE-` number allocated per tenant under
BR-TEN-035 and stamped AT POST, so the clerk told to *"look at JE-105"* can
now type exactly that. Every row carries `je_number`, and it is **null on a
draft by ruling** (*"a draft has NO number"*). A POSTED row with a null
number means this tenant has no `journal_entry` series row — reported in
`unavailable` as `posted_entries_without_a_je_number`, never faked.

**`f.status=reversed` IS NOT ACCEPTED**, though the matrix lists it beside
draft and posted. "Reversed" is not a status a row carries — it is the
presence of a `reversed_by_entry_id` link, and `journal_entries.status`
holds exactly two values (B2 r13 #2). The LINK is served on every row in
both directions, so the screen can render the state; inventing a third
status here would put a value in a filter that no column can ever equal.
REPORTED.

**DRAFTS APPEAR HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE.** Every money figure in this module
filters `status='posted'`, because a draft is not in the books; this one
list exists to show that a draft EXISTS so somebody can finish or delete
it. `status` keeps the two facts apart and `balanced` says whether the
draft may post at all (BR-LED-003).

⚠ **THE PAGE IS TAKEN IN THE DATABASE SINCE 2026-09-24 (`DEF-LED-6493` ·
`NFR-3` · `P1.8`), AND THIS PARAGRAPH RECORDED THE OPPOSITE.** It read *"THE
PAGE IS TAKEN IN MEMORY, NOT IN THE DATABASE — a stated deviation … the
QUERY is not [bounded], which is a performance note the next lane should
have rather than a correctness one."* At T7 that note was fair; at the top
of T5 it is **40,000 entries built to draw fifty**, which is `NFR-3`
breached rather than noted. Measured on the old code: **67 statements over
60 entries and 307 over 300**, one per entry.

`reporting.journal_entry_list` now takes `offset`/`limit`/`sort`/`direction`
and returns `total` from a `COUNT(*)`, so the LIMIT and the OFFSET are in
SQL and the cost of this screen no longer follows the book. The envelope is
unchanged — `core.pagination.prepaged` builds byte-for-byte the four keys
`StandardPagination` served, with the three extra keys after them exactly
where they were.

**`sort` ACCEPTS TWO NAMES AND `number` IS NOT ONE OF THEM IN SQL.** The
drawing puts a `⇅` on ENTRY NO. and DATE; `JE-{MM}{DD}{YY}-{0000}` does not
sort chronologically as text, so `?sort=number` orders by `entry_date`
(`P1.18`, `reporting.JOURNAL_SORT_COLUMNS`).

post.description:
S57's *Save draft* — create, or update the one named by `entry_id`.

ONE route for both because BR-LED-003 makes them one act: a draft is
editable until it posts, so "save" is what the modal does every time, and
two routes would mean a screen deciding which verb its own state deserves.

BR-LED-798 — post a whole batch, in full or not at all (`P1.22`).

PO ruling 2026-09-24 closing `OQ-LED-12630`, option (c): all-or-nothing,
**and** the batch is checked in full before the first entry is attempted.

⚠ **THIS ROUTE EXISTS BECAUSE A CLIENT LOOP CANNOT BE A TRANSACTION, AND
THAT IS WHAT THE QUESTION DECIDED.** `POST /ledger/journal-entries/{id}/post`
posts exactly one entry; five of those from a browser are five transactions,
and the fifth failing leaves the first four irreversibly in the books (hard
rule 4). The register row said *"doing nothing is choosing (b)"* for exactly
this reason, and (b) is the option the PO rejected.

**THE REFUSAL NAMES THE ENTRY.** A batch refused with *"something was
wrong"* leaves a finance officer opening five drafts to find out which; the
pre-check reports EVERY problem in one answer, each with its entry id and
its reason, which is what makes the round trip worth taking.

⚠ **A REFUSAL IS A 409 AND NOT A 422**, the same classification
`journal_entry_post` already makes through `_refused`: the request is
well-formed and the BOOKS' STATE refuses it.

`posted_at` is REQUIRED and is the caller's (BR-TEN-043) — one moment for
the whole batch, so five entries posted together carry one timestamp rather
than five moments a re-read would have to reconcile.

delete.description:
One entry: OPEN it (GET) or delete a draft (DELETE). Two verbs, one path.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHY THE GET IS HERE AND NOT IN `apps/ledger/api.py` WITH THE OTHER READS
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
**Django resolves by URL and NOT by method.** `ledger/journal-entries/
<uuid:entry_id>` is registered in this file, so a second registration of
the same path in `api.py` would shadow one of the two views entirely —
the identical constraint that put the draft WRITE at `…/drafts` rather
than at `11b` §2.10's `POST /ledger/journal-entries`, recorded in this
module's docstring. The read therefore joins the verb that already owns
the path, and the ROLE split moves onto a permission class
(`JournalEntryReadAnyDeleteAdminOrClerk`) so neither verb's gate is
changed by the other's arrival. `ConnectionsReadAnyWriteAdminOrClerk` is
the precedent and says so in its own docstring.

⚠ **`apps/ledger/api.py`'S "NO WRITE VERB ON ANY PATH IN THIS FILE"
GUARANTEE IS UNTOUCHED.** It is a statement about THAT file and this is
not that file; `api.py` already carries writes' neighbours the same way.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
GET — `DEF-LED-6723`, the eye on Finance blueprint p020 item 7
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
`11b` §2.10 / A1 S56 name this route and call the screen *"Journal list +
detail"* with *"lines expand to dimensions"*. It was never served, so the
Journal's `👁` shipped VISIBLE AND DISABLED with its reason (BR-SHL-025),
which was the honest build of a true refusal and is no longer true. The
Product Owner reported it on **v2.351.84**: *"on this screen user is
unable to see detail screen of Journal entry - we cannot click on eye."*

**READ-ONLY, AND THE ABSENCE OF AN EDIT IS THE RULE RATHER THAN A GAP.**
Hard rule 4 makes a posted entry immutable for ever; BR-LED-003 makes the
one correction a reverse + repost, which writes two NEW entries through the
posting service. There is no PATCH on this path and there must never be
one — this file's exception (2) already records why.

**THE LINES PAGE (`NFR-3`).** `?page` / `?per` slice in SQL and the
envelope is the one every other list in the product serves. The entry's
own `debit`, `credit` and `balanced` are over ALL its lines and not over
the page — computed in the read model, before the slice, for the reason
stated there.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
DELETE — US-LED-011 TC-6, unchanged
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
*"gone without trace in the books"*, audit row kept.

**A POSTED ENTRY IS NOT DELETABLE AND THIS ROUTE DOES NOT TRY.** The refusal
comes from `posting.delete_draft`, which checks the status, and from
`ledger/0007`'s trigger underneath it. Hard rule 4 has no exception for a
posted entry and needs none for a draft: BR-LED-003 calls a draft
*worthless* — it sums into no report — so deleting one leaves the books
byte-identical.

post.description:
BR-LED-003's *Post entry ✓* — balanced, memo'd, role-gated, immutable after.

All three demands are enforced BELOW this line whatever the modal did, and
the balance is enforced a third time by the database at COMMIT. `posted_at`
is REQUIRED and is the caller's (BR-TEN-043).

The response carries the `JE-` number BR-LED-021 stamps at post — **or a
named reason there is none**. No tenant has the `journal_entry` number
series seeded yet (`apps.tenancy.services.SERIES_DEFAULTS` has five and this
is not among them), so an entry posts unnumbered and says
`JOURNAL_NUMBER_SERIES_NOT_SEEDED` rather than composing a number a second
allocator would collide with. It is never faked and never blank.

LE-8's one click: post the linked mirror, hand back the prefilled draft.

**THE PREFILLED CORRECTION IS RETURNED, NOT WRITTEN**, and the response says
so by name (`repost_draft_is_not_persisted`). The screen loads it into S57,
the clerk corrects the figure, and *Save draft* is what makes it a row —
which keeps the draft lifecycle in exactly one place.

A second click returns the FIRST mirror with `mirror_created: false`. That
is the correct outcome of a double-submitted form, not an error: the
posting key is one string per original, forever.

get.description:
LE-1's table and its footer — *"Totals 598.69 | 598.69 ✔"*.

Params: `from` + `to`, both OPTIONAL and deliberately so. A trial balance
with no `from` is the cumulative position — which is what makes the AR row
equal the Still-owed KPI on S36 (one derivation, two presentations) — and
an open end is a legitimate request a required bound would refuse.

**NOT PAGINATED, and the footer is why.** US-LED-008 TC-1 requires the
table to foot to 598.69 = 598.69 over ALL rows; a page would make
`total_debit` a page total and the word *Balanced* a claim about a page.
The row count is bounded by the tenant's CHART OF ACCOUNTS — the eleven
designations plus their tax authorities and whatever the tenant added — not
by transaction volume, so it does not grow with the books. `GET /payments`
pages because it lists transactions; this lists accounts.

**THE PREMISES FILTER OF BR-LED-009 IS NOW SERVED — `?f.premises=<id>`
(CR-060 C24, 2026-09-03; renamed by `P0.14`, 2026-09-24).** ⚠ **IT WAS A
BARE `?premises=` UNTIL 2026-09-24 AND THE JOURNAL LIST ON THE SAME TAB
TOOK `?f.premises=`** — one filter, two spellings, so a clerk carrying a
property from one screen to the other got an unfiltered, footing report.
**Both are accepted and `f.premises` wins**; the bare one is deprecated
rather than removed, so no saved link breaks. See `_premises_filter`.
This paragraph has been corrected twice before and the
chain is kept, because each correction was true when it was written and the
pair is the record of how the blocker shrank. It first read *"`journal_lines.
premises_id` is NULL on every row in the product (US-LED-002 unbuilt), so a
`premises` param would accept a value and change nothing"* — hard-won law 1
in a served docstring, corrected 2026-09-02 by `DEF-3382` when US-LED-002
turned out to have landed on **2026-08-16**. It then read that the filter was
*"not served because nothing calls it (LAW 0)"*, which was also true: no
screen asked. **The finance-screens lane then verified the dimension, removed
the General Ledger's own false sentence, and could not ship the dropdown
because this endpoint took no property.** So the param exists now for the
reason LAW 0 wants — a caller is waiting for it.

⚠ **AND THE FILTERED TABLE DOES NOT FOOT, WHICH THE BODY SAYS RATHER THAN
THE SCREEN GUESSING.** `balanced` comes back **`null`** — never `false` —
with `a_trial_balance_narrowed_to_one_premises_does_not_foot` on
`unavailable`. Balance is a property of an ENTRY: a receipt's cash leg
carries no property at all, so narrowing removes it and leaves the AR leg.
See `reporting.GAP_FILTERED_BALANCE_IS_NOT_A_VERDICT` for the argument.

**An unbalanced UNFILTERED period is still served unbalanced.**
`balanced: false` with the `difference` on it is the BR-LED-007 red flag
reaching a human; there is no branch here that hides, rounds or "corrects"
it (US-LED-008 TC-5). That is exactly why the filtered case may not borrow
the same word for a different fact.

`GET /lookups/{list}/fixture-gap` — BR-TEN-161 / DEF-902.

Which entries the platform fixture ships for this list that this tenant
does not hold. A READ: it delivers nothing and changes nothing (BR-TEN-160
keeps delivery in the sweep, and OQ-550 asks the PO whether the sweep
should re-offer a list a tenant already holds).

⚠ **ITS ROUTE SITS ABOVE `lookups/<list>/<entry_id>`**, which would
otherwise match `fixture-gap` as an entry id and answer 404 for a list
that has one — the DEF-520 route-ordering shape, and the same reason
`assets/stock` sits above `assets/<uuid>`.

Same A4 gate as the list it describes: a role that cannot read the list
cannot read what is missing from it.

GET /me/permissions — the caller's OWN effective permission set.

Why it exists (PO directive 2026-08-09, "create endpoints for all and
integrate"): `/roles` serves the whole grid and is System-Admin-only, so a
Billing Clerk or Executive had no way to discover what they may reach — the
Settings UI had to probe each tab and read the 403. This route answers the
caller's own A4 row and nothing else: no other role's cells, no catalog
enumeration, no cross-tenant data (the role comes from the membership of
the path-resolved tenant, server-attached, never client input).

It is UI-gating CONVENIENCE (BR-SHL-025 / 11b G13): every endpoint still
enforces its own gate, and a client that lies about this payload gains
nothing. ETag/304 like the other reference reads (11b G6).

`GET /move-ins` — the Accounts page's Move-ins tab (CR-030 W5, B18 §5.5.2).

The list is `move_reads.move_ins_list` and this view adds nothing to it: no
figure is computed here, no absence is defaulted, and nothing is written.

⚠ **`AdminOrClerk`, NOT `AnyTenantRole`, FOR THE REASON `transfers_list`
GIVES.** Each row carries a DEPOSIT cell, and the deposit statement the
layer below builds is gated `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN, BILLING_CLERK)`.
`AnyTenantRole` here would hand an Executive figures the service refuses
them. Matching the narrower gate is the precedent set by `transfers_list`
and `account_close_impact`.

**A move-in is not a table — it is the life of a BR-CUS-018 draft account**,
from `services.create_account` writing a `pending_activation` row to
`services.activate_account` making it occupy. The window is the terminal
CLASS, never the label (BR-CUS-055).

§5.7.3's counting contract is applied inside the read model, not here: a
committed transfer's incoming half goes through `create_account` and would
otherwise appear on this list, so `transfers.exclude_transfer_halves` is
load-bearing rather than tidy.

The staged file itself — the account document content view's headers,
taken from that view rather than restated.

post.description:
`POST /move-ins/handover` `{unit_id, opened_at, move_in_park_id?}`
(`DEF-CUS-10190`) — the move-in found somebody still on the unit, so it
raises the old occupant's MOVE-OUT as a draft (prefilled; the day before
the move-in) and answers where to go. Writes one draft and nothing else;
the account is settled by the normal move-out. A disconnected unit answers
`close_out_first` and writes nothing. See `move_in_units.start_handover`.

get.description:
`GET /move-ins/message-templates?search=` — the Messaging table's
*+ Add message* picker (P2.33, image 46). `{served, results: [{code,
name}]}`; the two defaults are never offered. Writes nothing.

⚠ **REGISTERED IN THIS FILE, NOT `api.py`,** for this module's own reason
above: `customers/api.py` is shared surface, and a literal two-segment
`move-ins/…` path cannot collide with `move-ins/<…>` reads there.

`GET /move-ins/messages?category=&deposit_taken=&deposit_cleared=` (`DEF-CUS-6365`) —
what the move-in's save will queue for the customer, for its review step.

Readable by every role, like the move-in itself: the notification RULES are
a Settings door a Billing Clerk may not open (`SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin`),
and this serves only the answer those rules give for this one flow — which
channels, which template — never the rules. A READ: nothing is written.

`GET /move-ins/units?q=&page=&per=` (`DEF-CUS-10190`, PO 2026-10-17) —
EVERY live unit of this utility a move-in may be for, VACANT FIRST, each
row with its `state`, `occupant`, `selectable`, the `path` a move-in takes
(`move_in` · `move_out_first` · `close_out_first`) and, when blocked, a
`reason_key`. A removed unit is not listed. Paged in SQL (`NFR-3`), the
standard envelope. See `move_in_units.search`.

`GET /move-outs` — the Accounts page's Move-outs tab (CR-030 W5, B18 §5.6.2).

Same envelope as `GET /move-ins`, so one screen component reads both.

⚠⚠ **THIS DOCSTRING SAID *"ONLY A MOVE-OUT THAT HAS ALREADY HAPPENED IS
SERVABLE"* UNTIL 2026-09-19, AND IT IS NOT TRUE ANY MORE.** PO ruling of
that day, verbatim **`yes`**, asked whether the Move-outs list should show
move-outs that have not finished yet. The envelope now carries TWO kinds of
row — closed accounts, and the `wizard_parks` drafts a clerk started and put
down — each naming itself in `row_kind`. It was never a missing column: the
draft store has carried `flow`, `step` and `waiting_on` for all five flows
since `CR-035`, and what was missing was this list's WINDOW.

⚠ **WHAT IS STILL TRUE:** a move-out nobody has STARTED leaves no trace at
all — `accounts` carries no `scheduled_move_out_on` — so B18 §5.6.7's
`Scheduled` row is the one state this product still cannot hold, and
`MOVE_OUT_STATES` marks it unsupported with its reason.

The read model states an absence on every cell a draft cannot answer rather
than inventing a value, and the tiles it cannot compute come back `null`
with their reason attached. **Do not "fix" those nulls by defaulting them to
0 here: an unknown and a zero are different answers, and only one of them is
true.**

`GET /moves/{ref}` — the MOVE RECORD screen (blueprint p074).

The assembly is `move_record_reads.record_detail` and this view adds
nothing to it: no figure is computed here, no absence is defaulted, and
**nothing is written — this endpoint has no sibling that writes.** That is
the blueprint's own ruling rather than an omission (see that module's §1).

⚠ **`ref` IS THE MOVE NUMBER, NEVER A UUID** (B14 rule 31). `MVI-26-0114`
is what the list links to and what a clerk quotes on the phone, and it
keeps resolving across the commit because a draft and the finished record
carry the same string (`CR-122-BRC06`).

⚠ **`AdminOrClerk`, NOT `AnyTenantRole`,** for the reason `move_ins_list`
gives one screen over: this page carries a deposit box, and the deposit
statement the layer below builds is gated to the same two roles. Handing an
Executive a figure the service refuses them is the defect that rule exists
to prevent.

post.description:
`POST /moves/{ref}/cancel` — *Cancel move-in* (🔒, images 10, 14).
Body `{"note"?, "refund_method"? ("check" | "ach")}`.

get.description:
`GET /moves/{ref}/cancel-preview` — J6's confirm modal: what a cancel
would reverse, and whether it may. Writes nothing.

post.description:
`POST /moves/{ref}/move-in-date` — *Change move-in date* (image 13, J7).
Body `{"opened_at": "YYYY-MM-DD"}`.

`POST /moves/{ref}/opening-reads` — *Enter opening read* (image 13).
Body `{"reads": [{"meter_no", "value" | "estimate", "channel"?, "read_at"?}]}`.

`POST /moves/{ref}/work-orders` — *Add a work order* (images 14, 27).
Body = the wizard's *Field visit* answer `{"template_ids"?, "orders"?}`.

get.description:
`GET /notice-tones` — BR-PAY-035's mapping, made visible.

`notices.TONE_TO_STEP` is the whole of it and there is no other copy. Until
this route landed **no surface anywhere showed a clerk which letter a tone
selects**, and the consequence is not cosmetic: BR-NOT-008 says *"regulated
ladder steps ALWAYS render the disconnect-notice template class regardless
of the tone picked in the reminder modal"*, so choosing **Firm** in a
reminder modal does not send a firmer reminder — it sends the REGULATED
10-day disconnect notice, with its cut date and its statutory footer.
Choosing **Final** sends the 48-hour certified letter, at real postage.

The day numbers come from the TENANT's ladder configuration (BR-REP-016 —
*"always tenant config, never constants"*) and this route REFUSES to invent
them: when the settings family cannot be read, `stage_days` is reported as
unavailable with its reason and the tones still render, because which CLASS
a tone selects is a rule and does not depend on any day number.

What this utility has told its customers — sends AND skips.

`notice_history` (r12 #7) is PAYMENTS' table; this reads it through
`payments_seam.notice_history_window`, which resolves payments' published
functions BY NAME (B1). It had no reader at all until DEF-128: every
disconnect letter, every medical-hold skip and every certified 48-hour final
was recorded where no surface could open it.

⚠ **THE PAGE IS TAKEN IN THE DATABASE AND THERE IS NO CEILING
(`NFR-3` · `NFR-5`, `DEF-NOT-5750`, 2026-09-19).** Until today this read
asked payments for 2,000 rows, built 2,000 dicts and let DRF slice fifty —
so **the 2,001st notice was unreachable on every page**, `count` was a floor
rather than a total, and a `notice_history_truncated` problem row said so.
All three are gone: one `COUNT(*)` and one `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`, whatever the
record holds. **The copy went with the cap.** A sentence telling a clerk
where the record stopped is a lie once it stops anywhere, and an honest
absence outliving the thing it was honest about is the shape hard-won law 2
warns about.

Filters: `f.account_id` · `f.notice_type` · `f.tier` · `f.outcome` ·
**`f.certified=true`**, which is the CERTIFIED-MAIL REGISTER — the 48-hour
final tier BR-CUS-039 makes certified mail mandatory for. Each row states
`certified_mail`, and its `certified_number` is NULL with the reason beside
it: the number arrives on a provider response at dispatch and no provider
adapter exists on any channel (PO ruling 2026-08-15). A tracking number is
never fabricated onto a legal record.

SKIPS ARE INCLUDED BY DEFAULT and that is deliberate (J4 step 2): an account
excluded for a medical hold must never be indistinguishable from one nobody
ever chased.

Money members carry the tenant's currency — see the module docstring.

`GET /notification-rules` — the SET-12 matrix.

Every event, in the PO's own order, with its audience, its channels, its
timing and its On state. Rows are created from the catalogue on first read,
so a tenant that has never opened this screen still has a complete, stated
configuration rather than an empty table (the same discipline
`NotificationSettings` records).

`GET|PUT /notification-rules/{event}` — the SET-12D page.

The PUT carries a PARTIAL change set and the response is always the whole
page again (BR-TEN-024's atomic per-tab save, the shape every rule page in
this product already uses). One transaction, one audit row, and the matrix
the screen returns to is re-read from the server rather than patched
client-side.

put.description:
`GET|PUT /notification-rules/{event}` — the SET-12D page.

The PUT carries a PARTIAL change set and the response is always the whole
page again (BR-TEN-024's atomic per-tab save, the shape every rule page in
this product already uses). One transaction, one audit row, and the matrix
the screen returns to is re-read from the server rather than patched
client-side.

post.description:
`POST /notification-rules/{event}/queue-test` — ENQUEUE a test to yourself.

⚠ **THE NAME IS THE CONTRACT.** This route writes a queue row and returns;
it makes no provider call, and no route in this module may. BR-NOT-005's
*"queue only, no synchronous send endpoint"* is intact and asserted by name.

The response carries the provider seam's own verdict unchanged, plus the
channel's own line from the Channel status card (`channel_line`,
`DEF-NOT-10537`), so a System Admin who clicks the button is told what
actually happened: *on its way* where the dispatcher will send it, and
*queued*, with the channel's reason, where it will not. ⚠ AMENDED
2026-10-22: this read *"it will not leave the building until an adapter is
plugged in"* — false once the Custom SMTP adapter went live.

get.description:
`GET|PATCH /notification-sender` — the mail server, READ from Connectors.

PO 2026-10-22 (`DEF-NOT-10534`): *"We have to move everything in connector
not any other place"*. The Notifications *Email sender (SMTP)* form is gone
and this route is now a read of the Custom SMTP connector — host, sender,
state — which Configure → Notifications shows with a link to Connectors.

⚠ PATCH STAYS MOUNTED SO IT CAN REFUSE. A write naming a mail-server field
is refused BY NAME (*"Set this on Connectors."*); any other field is
unknown and refused as before. Nothing on this route writes.

patch.description:
`GET|PATCH /notification-sender` — the mail server, READ from Connectors.

PO 2026-10-22 (`DEF-NOT-10534`): *"We have to move everything in connector
not any other place"*. The Notifications *Email sender (SMTP)* form is gone
and this route is now a read of the Custom SMTP connector — host, sender,
state — which Configure → Notifications shows with a link to Connectors.

⚠ PATCH STAYS MOUNTED SO IT CAN REFUSE. A write naming a mail-server field
is refused BY NAME (*"Set this on Connectors."*); any other field is
unknown and refused as before. Nothing on this route writes.

get.description:
`GET|PATCH /notification-settings` — S8's dispatch config card.

The service has been complete, role-gated and audited since 2026-08-15 and
had no route, so the four values the dispatcher obeys could not be seen or
changed by anybody. The S8 tab's own header said so in as many words.

**The role gate is the SERVICE's** (`@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)`), and this
layer does not re-implement it: US-NOT-004 TC-5 is a Billing Clerk's
batch-size edit being SERVER-rejected, and a permission class here that
happened to disagree with the service would be two gates for one rule.

patch.description:
`GET|PATCH /notification-settings` — S8's dispatch config card.

The service has been complete, role-gated and audited since 2026-08-15 and
had no route, so the four values the dispatcher obeys could not be seen or
changed by anybody. The S8 tab's own header said so in as many words.

**The role gate is the SERVICE's** (`@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN)`), and this

get.description:
`GET /notification-templates` — the letters this utility can produce.

One row per template class this module owns, each answering the only
question that matters before a notice is generated: **is there a published
body, and if not, what happens instead?**

Four things travel per class and each is a rule rather than a display
choice:

* `published` — the version `template_service.resolve` would pin, resolved
  through BR-BIL-025's own order for the tenant-default variant. `null`
  means nothing renders and the notice HOLDS (field map N-1: *"dispatch
  holds safely on missing published template; content never invented"*).
* `variables` — US-NOT-005's merge-variable catalogue, which is a WHITELIST:
  a token outside it is refused at save rather than rendered empty. Serving
  it is what lets a person see what a letter of this kind may say.
* `custom_field_variables` — US-NOT-016's half. Custom fields resolve as
  `{{entity.custom.key}}` from the STAMPED SNAPSHOT and never from live
  master data (BR-NOT-012), which is why the shape is served rather than a
  list of this tenant's current fields: a list read live here would be the
  very lookup that rule forbids.
* `catalog_unavailable` — for the seventeen classes A19 ratifies and gives
  no tokens (OQ-206, OQ-207), the REASON, verbatim. An empty catalogue and
  an unspecified one are different facts and are spelled differently.
* `body_unavailable` — **DEF-163's half.** Why this PLATFORM has no body for
  the class, naming the open question that would settle it. Null for the
  classes provisioning plants. See the module docstring: this is a different
  question from `published`, and a screen that shows one cell for both sends
  a person to the wrong fix.

⚠ **`writable` IS FALSE ON EVERY ROW AND THAT IS THE PO's RULING, NOT A
GAP.** S91–S96 were CUT from R2 on 2026-08-16; there is no designer and this
endpoint is a READ. Bodies are platform-authored and seeded.

S8's platform queue list, and the S30/S35 delivery panels (US-NOT-013).

The S8 capability row's vocabulary, served: search on recipient/account/ref,
filters on type · channel · status · date range (plus `f.held` and
`f.account_id`), the five sortable columns, and the ratified default —
*"failed+bounced first, then queued_at"*, so the six failures are not buried
under nine hundred rows that are fine.

Pagination is mandatory on every list (11b G5) at the ratified sizes
50/100/200/500/1000, default 50 (A11 Addendum r2). The page is taken in the
DATABASE: only the rows on screen are serialized.

post.description:
*"Re-queue selected"* — the S8 capability row's bulk action (US-NOT-013).

Contracted here rather than in 11b §2.13, which lists the single-row form
only; US-NOT-013 §1 ratifies both (*"a re-queue action (row + bulk)"*) and
EP-NOT-04's capability matrix names the bulk one by name. A11 Addendum r4
records it as a build-time addition under the r2 CONFIRMED-DIRECTIONAL
clause.

Per-row results, never one boolean: a selection containing one held row is
a normal Tuesday and must not kill the other ten.

get.description:
*"Select all N matching"* — DEF-NOT-10650 (PO 2026-10-29, 2A).

The SAME list params as `GET /outbound` (search and `f.*`), resolved to
every matching id rather than to a page, so the selection is the view the
clerk is looking at. ⚠ **ABOVE `attention.SELECTION_CAP` IT REFUSES AND
RETURNS NO IDS** — a selection the clerk cannot see the size of is never
handed back to be re-queued. A view matching nothing returns an empty list,
which the bulk re-queue then refuses: *empty* never becomes *all*.

The dispatch home's counts — US-NOT-013 TC-1, US-NOT-015 TC-1.

ONE function answers both (`delivery_ops.queue_health`), because two
counters over one table is how a dashboard and a canned report come to
disagree about the same day.

⚠ **`delivered` AND `bounced` ARE SERVED AS NOT REPORTED, NEVER AS ZERO.**
Both are provider facts — a delivery confirmation and an ESP bounce webhook
— and no provider adapter exists on any channel, print included: delivery is
out of this release by PO ruling (2026-08-15). "0 delivered of 142 sent"
reads as a delivery failure when the truth is that nobody is reporting, so
the two statuses travel on `unpopulated_statuses` and the reason travels in
`problems` (`apps/billing/release.py`'s rule: *"'0 of 1,122 hold an address'
and 'we could not count' must never render the same"*).

Show me what we actually sent this customer.

Answers ONE of two states, and a screen must branch on `provenance`:

  * `original` — this IS the document the customer received, byte for byte,
    with `document` carrying it and its hash verified on this read.
  * `re_rendered_from_data_not_the_original` — no sealed copy exists, so
    **`document` is null** and `message_key` names the sentence that has to
    appear beside anything the screen shows instead.

`exempt` separates the two innocent reasons for the second state — an in-app
staff alert and a send test, both ruled out of the freeze by the PO — from
the one that is a real gap. They are not the same fact and a screen should
not say "we did not keep this" about a rehearsal.

⚠ A row still `queued` genuinely has no original. That is not a failure; it
is the honest answer, and it is why this state cannot be deleted even once
the dispatcher's precondition makes it unreachable for a `sent` row.

post.description:
Put ONE failed message back in the pool (11b §2.13 · US-NOT-013 TC-3).

Resolved through the tenant's own rows first, so a forged id from another
tenant is a 404 that cannot be told from any other 404 (HR-1; TC-5).

⚠ This CLEARS `batch_id` — see `delivery_ops.requeue`'s box. A re-queue that
reset only the status would look correct on every screen and would leave a
crashed hand-off's rows permanently invisible to the dispatcher.

Send the customer ANOTHER COPY — a new row, never an edit (US-NOT-011).

Body: `{"copy_no": 1}` — **REQUIRED**. Read the module docstring's resend
section before changing that: the copy number IS the idempotency key
(CLAUDE.md rule 6), the database is the arbiter, and an endpoint that
allocated the number itself would post a second letter on every double
click while looking perfectly correct.

What is copied: the source document, the channel, the template PIN and the
recipient snapshot — the same pinned version renders forever (BR-BIL-026,
US-NOT-011 TC-3) and the recipient is the one snapshotted at queue time
(BR-TEN-017).

⚠ **OQ-223 — whether a staff resend should RE-RESOLVE the recipient after
an address change is not ruled anywhere**, and the response says so on every
call rather than leaving a clerk to discover it. BR-TEN-017 is what IS
signed, so the snapshot is reused; the question is raised, not answered.

Refuses a HELD row (BR-PAY-018): that letter's address is already known to
be wrong, and posting it again is the one outcome the hold exists to
prevent.

*Fix address and retry* — DEF-NOT-10650 (PO 2026-10-29, ruling 3B).

Body: `{"address": "jo.prather@example.com"}`. Queues a NEW message — the
same document, template version and figures — to the corrected address,
and changes NOTHING else: the failed message stays as the record and the
customer's contact is not written. The audit row carries old → new.

Refused on sent/delivered, queued, complained/unsubscribed and held rows,
and on channels with no typed address (print, in-app, portal). A replay of
the same correction finds the earlier click's row (rule 6).

get.description:
Show me the message nobody could have sent — or say why it is not shown.

⚠ **THIS IS NOT `outbound/{id}/document` AND THE TWO MUST NEVER MERGE.**
That route answers *what did we SEND this customer* and serves the sealed
copy, never a render (`BR-NOT-027`). This one answers *what is WAITING to
go, on a channel with nothing behind it* — a different fact about a
different state, and the reason it exists is that a beta tenant with no
provider otherwise cannot finish a portal enrolment at all.

Always 200. A closed gate is `disclosable: false` with no content, because
*a provider is connected* is a correct state a screen must be able to
explain rather than an error.

`AdminOrClerk` rather than the list's `AnyTenantRole`: the queue LIST is a
settings read an Executive may hold, and a one-time code is a credential
they have no reason to. This narrows what is already on screen; it widens
nothing.

S34 Outstandings (US-PAY-013) — AR high→low with its ageing strip.

⚠ **THIS CAN NOW PAGE AND SORT IN SQL, AND IT DOES SO ONLY WHEN ASKED —
READ THE SECOND WARNING BELOW BEFORE QUOTING THE FIRST.** The docstring
that stood here said "Unpaginated ON PURPOSE" and `CLAUDE.md` QUOTED IT AS
THE `NFR-3` BREACH IT NAMES BY NAME (`DEF-PAY-4221`). The argument it made
was that the KPI tiles must foot to the rows exactly (US-PAY-013 TC-1) and
that a paginated body would make the tiles describe a page instead of the
debt. **The premise was wrong rather than the conclusion:** the tiles are
a SQL aggregate over the whole filtered set whether a page is cut or not,
so the strip ties to the debt either way.

Measured on real PostgreSQL 16 (`10-scripts/cr138_p4_debtor_cost.py`,
median of 3 after a discarded warm-up, 2026-09-23):

    2,046 debtors    3.089 s ·  2,041 statements  →  0.232 s · 13
    40,046 debtors  61.539 s · 40,041 statements  →  3.746 s · 12

⚠ **A WEB WORKER IS GIVEN SIXTY SECONDS** (`docker-entrypoint.sh`,
`GUNICORN_TIMEOUT:-60`), so at 40,046 debtors — the top of the ICP — the
old read did not merely run slowly: **it was killed by the worker before
it answered.** The 2,046-debtor figure is two thirds of the OLD 3,000
ceiling, so the sentence justifying it was already 3 seconds of server
time inside the tier it claimed to be correct in.

⚠⚠ **AND THOSE FIGURES ARE FOR A CALLER THAT ASKS FOR A PAGE. NOTHING
ASKS YET — `DEF-PAY-4221` STAYS OPEN.** See the comment at the call
below: the screen declares ten sorts, a search and four filters, this
query honours three sorts and two filters, and cutting a page underneath
the rest would be a live screen behind a broken control. The engine is
built, measured and tested; the wiring is `DEF-PAY-6271`.

`q`/`sort`/`dir`/`page`/`per`/`f.<name>` is BR-SHL-011's grammar and an
invalid value CLAMPS rather than erroring. `NFR-5`: `per` is a page size
from `PAGE_SIZES`, never a cap on the list.

`problems` travels on the body: the DSO tile is null with its reason, the
medical-hold column is unavailable, and any unpaid bill with no due date is
named rather than aged on a date nobody has.

post.description:
`POST /payment-plans/{id}/activate` — the customer signed (BR-CUS-044).

`signed_on` is REQUIRED and is the day the CUSTOMER signed, not the day a
clerk keys it: BR-TEN-043 makes the event date an input, and a plan whose
signature date is the keying date misstates when dunning stopped.

No countersignature is taken and none exists — BR-CUS-044 supersedes A19
§3's countersign block in those words.

get.description:
S33 Record payments (11b §1 · US-PAY-004), and the S21 Payments tab
scoped by `f.account_id` — one endpoint, because a per-tab read model would
be a second place for the "Applied to" join and the BR-PAY-021 date columns
to drift.

Pagination is mandatory on every list (11b G5) and its sizes are ratified at
50/100/200/500/1000, default 50. The page is taken in the DATABASE.

Two members ride alongside the DRF envelope, exactly as `GET /invoices`
carries its roll-up:

  `totals`  US-PAY-004 TC-1's "totals row per current filter" — and it
            states no money figure when the filter matched nothing or when
            the rows could not honestly be summed (`selectors`).
  `methods` the tenant's LIVE method list (BR-PAY-026 / BR-REP-006). The
            S33 method FILTER and the S22 Record form's picker read this one
            list, so the two can never offer different vocabularies. It is
            served here rather than at `GET /lookups/payment_methods`
            because payments has registered no handler for that list, so
            that route 404s on this deployment — REPORTED.

`GET /payments/reason-codes` — this utility's own credit/adjustment reasons.

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  THE LIST A LIVE CONTROL HAS NEEDED SINCE 2026-09-02 AND NEVER HAD.  ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
**DEF-PAY-5128.** CR-059 CS-35 taught `record_payment` the type AND the
reason and built the type select; nothing ever published the reasons. So
S33's select has offered *Credit* and *Adjustment* since 2026-09-02 and
`services._reason_code` refuses either with no reason BY NAME — two options
of a live control that could only fail, and every test of that form drives
the default `payment`, for which a reason is REFUSED. It is also what
`DEF-CUS-5126`'s `Adjust` control on the account needs.

**WHY IT IS NOT `GET /lookups/reason_codes`.** That route is gated on
`SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin` and A4 gives the Billing Clerk **no
`settings_lookups` cell** — so the one role A4 lets *Request* an adjustment
cannot read the reasons through Settings. Same rows, clerk-facing surface.

**UNPAGINATED, AND THAT IS NOT `NFR-3` BEING BROKEN.** This is a tenant's
own reference list — five seeded rows, tenant-extensible — and it is a
`<select>`'s whole contents, not a record list: a picker that pages cannot
be used. The rule NFR-3 exists for is a list that grows with ACCOUNTS, and
this one does not; `GET /lookups/payment_methods`'s stand-in on the same
form takes the same shape for the same reason.

Read-only. No clock, no money, no write.

post.description:
`POST /payments/selection-total` — CR-059 CS-43 (S33's selection bar).

The acceptance line, verbatim from the change register: *"four rows selected
on page one and two on page two show `6 selected · 3,918.44` — not a
blank."*

**A POST that writes nothing, and the verb is the considered half.** The body
is a list of payment ids and a clerk may tick five hundred of them; a query
string carrying five hundred uuids is 18,000 characters and meets a proxy's
URL limit long before it meets the server. So the selection travels in a
body. Nothing is created, nothing is stored, and the same request may be sent
twice with no consequence — which is why it needs no idempotency token and
has none.

**200 always, including for an empty selection**, which answers
`count: 0, amount: null, amount_unavailable: "no_rows"`. A `0.00` there would
read as *"these rows are worth nothing"* rather than *"nothing is selected"*,
and the two are different sentences on a screen a clerk is about to press
Refund on.

**`AnyTenantRole`, matching `GET /payments`.** This is a total over rows the
caller can already list one page at a time; a narrower gate here would mean a
role could read six payments and not their sum.

Money comes back twice, both as STRINGS (CLAUDE.md rule 2): `amount` is the
exact stored decimal and `amount_display` is the two-place figure the bar
renders. The client formats neither — `rating.selectors._display_money`
records why (DEF-364: a percent shipped as `0.015000` and a customer read
`0.015000`).

get.description:
S32 Summary (US-PAY-005) — five panels, no stored aggregate anywhere.

Carries `currency` for the same reason `/outstandings` does (DEF-099): a
money figure without its code is half of CLAUDE.md rule 2.

`GET /payments/{id}` — one payment, at its own address (P3.1).

**This is what a payment had no address for.** `paymentDetail.tsx` says so
in its own words and lists the three things a page would need; this is the
first, and `P3.9` is the other two.

The body is `PaymentRow` — the same builder `GET /payments` uses, so the
page and the list can never print different figures — plus the header strip
(`source`, `reconciled`), the four controls' own preconditions (`actions`),
the receipt rows the Resend modal draws its ① from, and `unavailable[]`.

**The history is NOT in this body.** It is the one member that has to be
paginated, and a paginated member inside an unpaginated body is exactly how
an unbounded read hides (`NFR-3`). `GET /payments/{id}/history` serves it.

post.description: One payment's held credit onto its account's open bills, oldest first.
One payment's email receipt, unless one is still waiting to go out.

`POST /payments/{id}/cancel` — undo a payment taken by mistake (P3.2).

The body is 2·3d's modal:

    reason         REQUIRED — the *Why* field, one of `cancel.CANCEL_REASONS`
    note           optional — *"What happened, in your words"*
    cancelled_on   REQUIRED — the caller's moment, never a clock (G6)

**201 on a new cancel, 200 on a replay**, both carrying the reversing row's
own `PMT-` number and `created`. A second click is the same act, not a new
one: `cancel_payment` finds the payment already `cancelled` and answers with
the first cancel rather than a 409 — *"a 409 toast for a button that worked
is a wrong answer a clerk would act on"*.

⚠ **A CLEARED PAYMENT IS REFUSED AND THE REFUSAL NAMES REVERSE.** That is
`P3.13`'s assertion and it is the point of the whole phase: Cancel and
Reverse are one word to a clerk and two acts to the ledger. A bare *"cannot
cancel"* leaves somebody holding a returned cheque with nowhere to go.

`problems[]` travels verbatim and is not decoration here: it is where the
cancel reports that **nothing was unposted and no bill re-opened**, because
a `processing` payment reached neither. A screen that implied a bill moved
would be describing a different act.

`POST /payments/{id}/cheque/void` — torn up before the deposit (S33 · S35).

The body:

    reason    REQUIRED — a payment that vanishes from the drawer with no
              explanation is the one thing a bookkeeper cannot reconcile
    on_date   the caller's business day — REQUIRED, never a clock

**200, not 201.** Nothing is created: the payment moves from `processing` to
`failed` and an audit row records why. The thing a screen re-reads afterwards
is the payment it already had.

⚠ **THIS IS NOT A REVERSAL AND THE SCREEN MUST NOT PRESENT IT AS ONE.** No
reversing row, no journal entry, no NSF count, no cash-only flag. The cheque
never cleared, so nothing reached the books — which is exactly why a counter
void is expressible at all. A cheque that HAS cleared is refused here by
name and goes to `POST /payments/{id}/reverse`, which is Admin-only and
writes both.

⚠ **THE REASON LIVES ONLY IN `audit_log`, WHICH IS PRUNED** — the same cost
the PO accepted for a corrected cheque number on 2026-09-02, and the same
open question (`OQ-1340`). `problems[]` says so on every response, and no
screen may describe this as a permanent record of why until that is answered.

`POST /payments/{id}/correct-reference` — S35's Correct-reference modal.

The body is the whole of what may be corrected, and nothing else:

    reference   the cheque or confirmation number — optional
    memo        the clerk's note on the payment itself — optional
    tender_id   the instrument, where the payment has not been banked yet
    note        WHY — REQUIRED (see `amendments.amend_reference`)

**A body carrying `amount`, `account_id`, `posted_at`, `cleared_at` or
`allocations` is refused with that field NAMED**, which is CS-34's first
proof and is live today. So is an unknown field: the route accepts four
things, and *"a route that accepts a partial body invites the next field to
be added to it"* is the spec's own reason for that.

⚠ **A REQUEST THAT PASSES EVERY REFUSAL MEETS THE STUB** and raises, because
the write is blocked on an open question. That is deliberate and is stated
in this module's docstring; it refuses nothing that works today, because
nothing corrects a reference today.

get.description:
`GET /payments/{id}/history` — WHEN · WHAT · WHO · NOTE (P3.4).

**This is what makes Cancel honest: a cancelled payment does not vanish.**
The original keeps its row, its number and its amount, its status reads
`cancelled`, and this says who did it and when.

⚠ **PAGINATED IN THE DATABASE** (`NFR-3`). `payment_detail.history_queryset`
hands back a QuerySet that audit ordered on `ix_audit_entity`, and
`StandardPagination` puts the `LIMIT/OFFSET` in the SQL. A busy payment's
trail is unbounded — a recording, an allocation, a batch seal, a
reconciliation, a correction, a resend, a cancel — and
`apps/metering/connection_reads._history` materialising its whole trail is
the shape this deliberately does not copy.

⚠ **IT NEVER CLAIMS PERMANENCE, AND IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHY.**
`audit_log` is pruned and no row type is exempt (PO ruling 2026-09-23,
`OQ-1340` CLOSED). B14 rule 33 puts rationale at ZERO words on screen, so
the fact travels as the `unavailable[]` CODE on the detail read and the
panel explains no retention policy — a screen that explained it in order to
be honest would break rule 33 while trying to obey the ruling.

post.description:
`POST /payments/{id}/mark-returned` — the bank sent an ACH payment back.

PO, 2026-10-07: *"(a) Let billing clerks mark an ACH payment returned, any
day, with a reason and the bank code. The same effect follows: balance
restored, fee and notice."* The body:

    returned_on      the BANK's return date — REQUIRED, never a clock
    reason           `nsf` or `bank_chargeback` — REQUIRED
    return_code      the Nacha code, e.g. `R01` — REQUIRED
    memo             optional
    idempotency_key  the dialog's submit token — REQUIRED

**A SEPARATE DOOR, NOT A WIDER `/reverse`.** `/reverse` stays
`SystemAdminOnly` with every reason, a partial amount, targets and the
bank-fee field; this one carries only what an ACH return needs, and the
service it calls refuses every other tender by name. Widening `/reverse`
would promise a clerk a reach the service then denies (`BR-PAY-1070`'s own
reason for mirroring the gate).

`reason` and `return_code` are refused HERE when absent, by field, so the
dialog can put the sentence under the box; their VALUES are the service's
to judge, so a clerk meets one rule and not two copies of it.

`POST /payments/{id}/move` — this money was never that account's (S35 · S21).

The body is the *"Move to another account"* modal:

    to_account_id    the account that should have had it — REQUIRED
    reason           REQUIRED (CS-32 asks for it in terms)
    moved_on         the day the correction is made — REQUIRED, never a clock
    approval         BR-PAY-011's acknowledgement, when the SERVICE asks for
                     one. Not required by this layer: only the service knows
                     whether a bill re-opens or a closed month is touched,
                     and a second copy of that rule here is a second place
                     for it to drift.
    idempotency_key  the modal's submit token — REQUIRED

**201 on a new move**, carrying the reversing row on the source, the new
payment on the destination, what re-opened, what the money met and both
accounts' credit positions afterwards.

⚠ **A MOVE IS REFUSED WHILE THE DEPOSIT BATCH IS RECONCILED** (BR-PAY-867)
and the refusal is a 422 the screen renders as a sentence, not an error
toast. It is the OPPOSITE of the bounce rule and both are right: a returned
cheque inside a reconciled batch IS recorded (PO 2026-08-12, OQ-134) because
the bank returned it, while a move is our own choice about money the bank has
already agreed a total for.

get.description:
`GET /payments/{id}/move-preview?to=` — what re-opens and what it meets.

`SystemAdminOnly` for the same reason `reversal_api.payment_reversal_plan`
is: the preview names every bill on both accounts and what each balance
becomes, and a role that may not take the action has no business being shown
its consequences.

`GET /payments/{id}/nsf-fee?on=` — "+$30.00 NSF fee" before Confirm.

BILLING's own quote (`apps/billing/nsf_fee.quote_nsf_fee`): the account →
its unit → that unit's plan → the plan's NSF charge code, priced on `on`
(the bank's return date the dialog holds). It is the SAME computation the
write runs, so the figure the clerk is shown is the figure the fee bill
carries. Writes nothing.

    {"status": "charged", "code": "NSF", "amount": "30.0000", "currency": "USD"}
    {"status": "nsf_fee_not_set_on_plan", "amount": null, ...}

`amount` is null whenever no fee would be charged — never 0.00.

post.description:
`POST /payments/{id}/reapply` — BR-PAY-031, at last (S33 · S35).

The body is the Reapply modal:

    targets   `[{"invoice_id": …, "amount": "292.87"}, …]` — where the money
              goes. EXPLICIT: a reapply exists because the automatic order
              was wrong, so re-running that order would undo the correction.
    release   which bills to take it OFF. Optional; absent means every bill
              this payment currently meets, which is the ordinary case.
    reason    REQUIRED — the audit row is the only record of why.
    on_date   the caller's business day — REQUIRED, never a clock.

**200, not 201.** Nothing is created that a caller could go and fetch: a
reapply moves an existing payment's money between existing bills, and the
thing the screen re-reads afterwards is the payment it already had.

⚠ **NOTHING IS POSTED TO THE LEDGER AND `problems[]` SAYS SO ON EVERY
RESPONSE.** It is the one write path in this module that posts nothing, and
the row is there so a reviewer reading the payload does not have to know that
already (CR-059 CS-11: *"a reapply that posted would double-count the
money"*).

⚠ **NO IDEMPOTENCY TOKEN, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN MISSING.** A
double-clicked reapply is refused by the service on its own terms: the second
call finds the money already off the named bills and answers *"payment … has
nothing on bill …"*, because `_net_by_invoice` reads the CURRENT net position
rather than the original rows. A token would add a second guard over a state
check that is already exact — and unlike a payment, a reapply moves no money
in or out, so a lost race costs a refusal rather than a duplicate receipt.

get.description:
`GET /payments/{id}/reapply-plan` — the left-hand side of S35's modal.

What this payment currently meets, bill by bill, NET of every mirror row —
so a payment that has already been reapplied once, or partly released by a
restatement, shows its true position rather than its original one.

A GET: it writes nothing and may be taken twice with no consequence.

post.description:
`POST /payments/{id}/receipt` — send the receipt again (P3.3).

The body is 2·3h's modal:

    channels   REQUIRED — `pdf_print` · `email` · `sms`, the three a receipt
               goes out on. The drawing's *Send by* chips.
    copy_no    REQUIRED — and it is the whole idempotency guarantee
               (hard rule 6). `GET /payments/{id}` serves `next_copy_no`, so
               the number the clerk submits is the number the server just
               showed them; a double-click resubmits it, collides with its
               own row in the DATABASE and comes back `created: false`.
               An endpoint that allocated the number itself would post a
               second receipt on every double-click while looking perfectly
               correct — `apps/notifications/api.py` records that argument
               in full and this door obeys the same rule.

**Nothing about the payment changes** (p050's act table: *Resend · a queue
row · the ledger: Nothing*), and `problems[]` says so on every call.

This RE-QUEUES AN EXISTING DOCUMENT. A channel this payment has no receipt
on is refused by name rather than composed here — templates, channels and
queue all exist, and building a second receipt path is what the PO ruled out
on 2026-09-22.

get.description:
`GET /payments/{id}/receipt/document` — paper at the window (P3.19).

*"The queue is asynchronous; a counter needs a receipt in hand now."*

⚠ **IT IS A READ AND IT MINTS NO SEND ENDPOINT.** A11 Addendum r2 §4 —
*"no synchronous send endpoint anywhere (queue only, BR-NOT-005)"* — and
`apps/notifications/api.py` states that minting one is a gate failure. This
renders a row that is ALREADY QUEUED, through notifications' own
`render_for_dispatch` and its PINNED version (BR-BIL-026), and dispatches
nothing: the queued row keeps its place and the print job will still take
it. A customer standing at the counter has no address to resolve and no
provider to hand off to; the delivery is a person taking a piece of paper.

`receipt_resend`'s module docstring holds the whole argument and
`12-governance/02-decision-log.md` holds the ruling, because the drawing
does not settle it.

The body is TEXT, not a PDF — `rendering.py`'s own exception (2), `OQ-149`
CLOSED 2026-08-12: no page-rendering library is in the image and printable
classes render their text body. The browser's print dialog does the rest.

`GET /payments/{id}/receipt/print` — the one-page counter receipt's facts.

PO 2026-10-30, Q3 = A: *Print receipt* opens a one-page receipt in the
browser to print now. A READ: nothing is queued, sent or changed —
`receipt_print`'s docstring says where each field comes from. `DEF-PAY-10743`.

`GET /payments/{id}/reversal-plan?reason=&on=` — BR-PAY-011's fourth clause.

Answers, for the reason the clerk has picked and the business day they are
working on:

  * **the window** — the tender, how many days ago the money moved, the limit
    BR-PAY-011 gives that tender, and whether this is inside it. Returned as
    those parts rather than as a boolean, so S35 can say *"this ACH cleared
    74 days ago — outside the 60-day window"* instead of *"not allowed"*.
  * **whether an approval is needed and WHY** — the payment is applied to an
    issued bill, or the day falls in a closed accounting period.
  * **the consequences** — every bill that re-opens and by how much, and what
    the account's credit balance becomes. A credit that goes below zero is
    flagged: that is money the customer never paid and is a real debt
    (PO 2026-08-11, `OQ-132`).

`reason` defaults to the bounce, which is the only reason that needs no
window and no approval, so a caller that omits it gets the LEAST restrictive
preview and can never be misled into thinking a staff correction is allowed.

`on` is the caller's business day and is REQUIRED for a staff reason
(BR-TEN-043, gate G6): a window that expired at midnight in the server's
timezone would refuse a correction a clerk started before closing time.

post.description:
`POST /payments/{id}/reverse` — a cheque came back (US-PAY-009 · CS-5).

The body is S35's Reverse modal:

    returned_on      the BANK's return date — REQUIRED, never a clock
    reason           `nsf` (the default and, today, the only one served)
    memo             optional
    bank_memo        LBX-04 — the bank's own words, ≤ 60 characters, saved
                     on the REVERSING row (PO 2026-10-30)
    charge_nsf_fee   DEF-PAY-10698 — default TRUE: an `nsf` bounce charges
                     the NSF code the account's plan lists; FALSE is the
                     clerk unticking it and needs …
    nsf_fee_waive_reason   … the reason, REQUIRED when unticked
    bank_fee         OUR bank's charge for the returned item — optional,
                     and absent is not 0.00
    resume_collections   the clerk's choice; default False
    idempotency_key  the modal's submit token — REQUIRED (see the module
                     docstring)

**201 on a new reversal, 200 on a replay**, both carrying the reversing row
and `created`. A clerk who has just reversed **292.87** is shown what
re-opened, because `reverse_payment` worked it out in the same transaction
and making the screen ask again would be perverse — the same argument
`account_payments` makes for showing an allocation.

**`problems[]` travels verbatim**, and on this path it is not decoration: it
is where the bounce reports the customer's NSF fee it cannot add, the
account-balance cache it may not write, the notice-history row it will not
invent — and, per bounce, whether the collection ladder was restarted or
left paused. The screen groups on the code and renders the sentence.

⚠ **THE LOCKED-BATCH CASE IS NOT AN ERROR HERE AND THE SCREEN LANE MUST NOT
RENDER ONE.** CS-5's screen note asks for *"the locked-batch refusal shown
BEFORE the button, not as an error after it"* — but the PO closed `OQ-134`
on 2026-08-12 and **a bounce inside a reconciled batch no longer refuses**:
the batch total stands and the bounce is new rows. What this path still
refuses is a payment naming a batch it cannot READ or that does not exist,
which is a broken reference and not a state a screen can pre-empt.

get.description:
`CR-167-BRC10` §7.3 — what the New/Edit form offers on `?on=` (the date
the version starts), each item a `ref` with its version and from-date.

`CR-167-BRC10` §7.3 — the plan's Audit in WORDS, paged in SQL: the plan's
own changes and what moved underneath it (schedules, charge codes, taxes,
discounts). `f.kind=plan|underneath`, `f.from`, `f.to`, `format=csv`.

PO ruling 2026-09-18 — **A PLAN IS TOLD WHEN WHAT IT BINDS CHANGES.**

Verbatim: *"yes we should build this. It measn every time Rate, taxes,
Charge code, Discounts are changed, at apporval we need to take action to
inform Plan about it - Fix this"*.

It follows from the PO's own correction of the same day — *"plan will not do
any edits to Rates … plan only binds it"*, which is `BR-RAT-088` restated.
Once money lives entirely on the bound objects, **the plan's whole job is to
show what it is bound to, and it was showing only half of that**: which
schedule it binds, and never that the bound schedule's price moved.

⚠ **READ-ONLY, AND NOT ADMIN-ONLY.** Every write in this module is
`SystemAdminOnly`; this reads a log a clerk needs in order to understand a
bill they are being asked about, and gating it would put the answer behind
the one person who is not on the phone. Tenant scoping is the guard that
matters here (hard rule 1) and `require_tenant` is it.

⚠ **PAGINATED FROM THE SERVER, AND THE PAGINATION IS THE POINT (`NFR-3`).**
The paginator is handed the QUERYSET, so `count` is a SQL `COUNT` over the
whole set and the page is a SQL `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`. One tax or one charge code
reaches EVERY plan that binds it, so this set grows with the ESTATE rather
than with the plan — and `NFR-5` forbids a cap anywhere.

⚠ **IT IS NOT A PLAN VERSION AND MUST NEVER BECOME ONE.** A bound object
changing is not a change to the PLAN — that is the whole point of the PO's
ruling — so nothing here writes `plan_versions` and `rate_plans.version`
does not move. A lane that "fixes" this by minting a version has inverted it.

⚠ **THE ANSWER CARRIES WHAT IT COULD NOT SEE (`DEF-RAT-5738`).** Only
`schedule` and `charge` rows are ever written to `rate_change_log`; no tax
and no discount path writes one. `coverage` names both lists so the screen
can say so, rather than drawing an empty tax section that reads as good news
— hard-won law 7, *reporting zero over a scope it silently excludes*.

post.description:
`OQ-RAT-12409` option A — `BR-RAT-1016` verb 2 for the PLAN.

The route spelling is the other four objects' spelling on purpose
