get.description:
`GET .../approval-preview?outcome=…` — `WHAT APPROVING WILL DO`.

**This is what the Approve modal prints, and the modal computes none of it.**
Drawn p083–p084 of the Accounts blueprint (read as images, scale 2): five
`THEN` / `WHAT` rows, of which two change with the chosen radio. The payload
carries those rows as KEYS, what will be created, the queue it lands on, and
the outstanding money that travels with it.

`outcome` is optional and defaults to the request's own committed pick, so
the same route answers *what did this become* and *what would it become*.
The whole set also rides on the detail's decision tab
(`what_approving_will_do`), keyed by outcome, so the modal can redraw the
table as a radio moves without a round trip.

⚠ **A PREVIEW IS NOT A PROMISE THE APPROVAL KEEPS BY ITSELF.** `blockers`
lists what would stop the job being raised — no resolved premises, no live
account, a job already linked — and **none of them blocks the approval**:
the drawn callout is *"the money does not gate approval and the documents
do"*, and a request whose job cannot be raised is still approved with the
reason named.

post.description:
`POST .../approve` — gated by the outcome AND every blocking condition.

A blocked approval answers a `BIZ-COMPLETENESS` refusal naming the condition,
**not a move to `Refused`**: *"Nothing is refused — it simply cannot be
approved yet."* Conflating the two would put a reason on a customer's record
that nobody gave.

⚠ **IT TAKES AN OPTIONAL `outcome` SINCE 2026-09-16 (`DEF-CUS-5427`).** The
Approve dialog sends the radio the clerk picked, and the outcome and the
approval then commit or roll back together. `POST .../decision` is untouched
and is still the Decision tab's own door.

⚠ **SINCE `CR-094-BRC01` IT ALSO RAISES THE JOB** — PO 2026-09-15, *"pass all
information to create the new connect requets or move -in request based on
selction"*, drawn on p083–p084 as `Approve and raise the build`. The response
carries `job`, which holds EITHER `raised` (what was created, its reference
and the queue it is on) OR `not_raised` (why nothing was, by name). Never
both and never neither, so a screen cannot render a job that does not exist.

BR-CUS-080 — one SR produces ONE live child per decision, and the SR alone

`customer_id: null` records **"searched, and there is no prior

`GET .../customer-search` — the Approve dialog's *Search customer*
(`DEF-CUS-10043`): the move-in's *Search customer ID* asked with the

post.description:
`POST .../decision` — `WHAT SHOULD THIS BECOME?`

✅ **`disconnect` IS ONE OF THE FIVE — BR-CUS-091**, *"Yes customer can
request it"*. ⚠ And it is NOT a move-out: a move-out closes the account and
settles the deposit (BR-CUS-030), a disconnect leaves it open and accruing
(BR-MET-105). This route stores exactly what the clerk sent and maps
nothing.

get.description:
**GATE ONE: attaching never blocks CREATION** — REQ-03.4's `NOT BLOCKING`
callout. The POST lands `not_checked`, always.

⚠ **TWO POSTS, ONE ADDRESS, TOLD APART BY WHETHER A FILE CAME WITH IT.**

  * **With a `file` part** — the bytes go to the document store and the row
    gets `name`, `size`, `storage_ref`, `uploaded_by` and `uploaded_at`.
    This is what the PO ruled in with *"you will have to reduce the size and
    save them on cloud container etc"*; the capture screen's step 4 said
    *"We cannot take a file yet — there is nowhere to store it"* until it
    landed, and that sentence was true.
  * **Without one** — the JSON path that has always been here: a clerk TICKS
    what the applicant is expected to bring, and the request records it. It
    is untouched, and it is deliberately still reachable. ⚠ **THIS SAID
    the beta's six rows were ticks of exactly this kind; they are SEEDED
    PLACEHOLDERS pointing at nothing (`DEF-CUS-5872`)**, which is a
    different fact and was never measured before it was written.

They are one endpoint rather than two because they produce the same row on
the same tab, and a second address would make *"attach a document"* two
things a screen has to choose between.

⚠ **413 AND 415 ARE CAUGHT HERE AND NOT RAISED AS CATALOG REFUSALS.**
`HTTP_STATUS_BY_CODE` maps a B12 §3 code to a status and neither transport
row has one, so a `ValidationError` would answer 422 to a file over the cap
(B12 r1's HTTP-series rows; 11b G11). The body is the SHARED envelope
`core.errors.http_series_refusal_body`, exactly as the account-documents
door already answers.

⚠ **THE FILE PART IS NEVER READ AS A FORM FIELD.** `request.data` on a
multipart request carries the upload too; `file` is stripped out of the
payload dict so a clerk cannot smuggle a value into a column by naming a
part after it.

get.description:
`GET /service-requests/{id}/documents/{docId}/content?as=view|download`
— the file itself, for a clerk to open or save (`CR-158-BRC10`).

⚠ **THE HEADERS ARE THE SAFETY, AND EACH ONE IS THERE FOR A REASON:**
  * `Content-Disposition` — `inline` only for a PDF, PNG or JPEG asked for
    with `as=view`; everything else is `attachment`, so a browser saves it
    rather than rendering it;
  * `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` — the browser draws the type we
    declare and never guesses a more dangerous one from the bytes;
  * `Content-Security-Policy` — no script runs inside a served file
    (`DOCUMENT_CSP`);
  * `Cache-Control: private, no-store` — a stranger's licence is not kept
    in a shared cache or on the clerk's disk by the browser.

Resolved under this tenant first; another utility gets 404. Audited, one row
per open or download (`document_content`).

`GET /service-requests/{id}/documents/{docId}/download` — a link that dies.

⚠ **THE ROW IS RESOLVED UNDER THIS TENANT FIRST, AND THE URL IS MINTED
SECOND.** A link is never issued for a document the caller could not have
found; another utility asking for this file gets a **404**, the same answer
as for one that never existed (`BR-TEN-003`, HR-1 — existence must not
leak). The order is `account_documents.document_link`'s and `work.evidence`'s.

⚠ **FOUR HOURS, AND IT IS A BEARER TOKEN** (PO ruling 2026-08-30). Whoever
holds this URL reads this one document with no session until it expires. Do
not put one in an email that outlives it — issue a new link instead.

⚠ **`AnyTenantRole`, NOT `AdminOrClerk`** — this is a READ. An Executive who
may see the request may see what was filed on it; the split `POST` makes is
about who may FILE (`BR-SHL-031`, *"v1 uploads staff-mediated"*).

not the same as verifying it."* A document with no file cannot be verified —

post.description:
`POST .../fee-collection` — **BR-CUS-090, the counter takes the WHOLE
application fee, or the fee is waived (`OQ-CUS-12624`, 2026-09-24).**

PO verbatim: *"all or waived"*. `amount` must equal the fee still owing;
anything else is refused before a row is written (422, `BIZ-COMPLETENESS`,
`customers.serviceRequest.feeTakeInFull`, params `amount` and `currency`).
The way out of a fee not paid in full is BR-CUS-073's waiver, with a
reason, on a line.

**Worked:** quoted $130.00, `{"amount": "25.00", "method": "cash",
"receipt_no": "RCP-26-4471"}` → refused, *"Take the full $130.00. Or waive
it."*; `{"amount": "130.00", …}` → *$130.00 collected · $0.00
outstanding*.

⛔ SUPERSEDED 2026-09-24: *"A shortfall is never refused here"* (BR-CUS-090's
2026-08-24 desk clause, *"we acept it and in finance we will reconcile"*).

⚠ `amount` must be a STRING. A JSON float is refused, not coerced (rule 2).
⚠ Idempotent on the receipt number (rule 6) — the desk is exactly where a
double-click happens. A repeat with the same receipt is a no-op; a second
collection with a different receipt is refused rather than summed.

⚠ **AND SINCE 2026-09-15 IT POSTS (PO ruling).** *"payemnt should show in
payments, in ledge and in fiannce books"*. One `counter_receipts` row in
payments and one balanced journal entry — DR the tender's clearing account,
else `1010 Undeposited funds` · CR `2400 Customer credit balances` — in the
same transaction as the columns above. Still no invoice and still no
customer account: there is neither at capture, and a balanced pair needs
neither.

⚠ **THE TENDER DETAIL IS OPTIONAL AND TYPED, AND THE CARD NUMBER IS NOT IN
IT.** PO: *"we need to allow to take payment detials, card detial scheck
details here curerntly is is not taking inputs"*. Two optional objects, and
a body that sends neither behaves exactly as it did yesterday:

    "card":   {"last4": "4242", "brand": "visa", "auth_code": "A19422"}
    "check":  {"number": "10241", "bank": "First National",
               "date": "2026-05-12"}

The full card number is **never** accepted. Last four, brand and the
terminal's authorisation code are what match our line to the bank's; the
number itself is read by nothing in this product and would put the whole
database under card-industry rules.

**Worked, the drawn case:** `{"amount": "25.00", "method": "cash",
"receipt_no": "RCP-26-4471"}` → $25.00 recorded, `DR 1010 25.0000 · CR 2400
25.0000`, and the request reads *$25.00 collected · $0.00 outstanding*.

get.description:
`GET/POST/PATCH .../interruption` — open one, move it, set the stretch.

**`GET`** answers the section. A request that is neither a report nor
attached to an interruption answers **404**, not an empty object — a section
that rendered for every request would be an empty frame on every move-in in
the product (`BR-CWP-093` in the staff app's dialect).

**`POST`** is `BR-CWP-101`: a clerk judges the reports real and opens the
operational record. With `interruption_id` in the body it ATTACHES to one
already open — that is how twelve reports of one burst main become twelve
requests pointing at one interruption. With no body it OPENS a new one from
the report's own kind and its own words.

**`PATCH`** may carry `status`, `affected_area` or `expected_back_on`, in
any combination; each reaches its own service door and each writes its own
audit row. It refuses with 404 while nothing is attached, because there is
nothing to move.

post.description:
`Add a note`, badged **`Internal · never shown to the customer`**. There
is no customer-visible path and there must not be one — the portal is out of
v1 scope, so a visibility flag would be a permission with nothing to permit.

`POST .../refuse` — the register's reason, the utility's code, and the
one sentence the APPLICANT reads.

⚠ **`message_to_applicant` IS THE BLUEPRINT'S `What to tell them`**, whose
helper line reads *"Goes into the refusal letter."* It is the letter's body.
`reason` stays internal and `reason_code` is what the refusal is FILED
under, now one of five (`DEF-CUS-5389`). None of the three is the same
audience, and the response carries `applicant_message` so the screen can say
whether the letter was queued rather than assume it.

`POST .../reopen` — *Reopen* on a declined move-in request (image 08;
PO 2026-10-05, `OQ-CUS-12789` → (a)). Body `{"reason"}` — REQUIRED
(`BR-CUS-072`); it lands on the timeline row beside the decline. Answers the detail: `header.state` is
`submitted` (*To approve*). A request that is not a declined MOVE-IN is
refused by name (`transitionNotAllowed` / `reopenNotAMoveIn`).

`POST .../resend-ask` — *Resend the ask* (`CR-171-BRC10` P1.06, image 05).

Takes NO body: the words are the stored ask's, never the caller's, so a
resend cannot become a different message wearing the old one's history.
Answers the detail plus `applicant_message` — whether the letter was
queued, by the same shape `refuse` and `transitions` answer with.

`POST .../resolve-address` — the resolver writes EVIDENCE, never a
decision. BR-CUS-070: `address_as_given` is untouched and the resolved ids
land in their own columns beside it.

`POST .../services` — the capture wizard's step 3, replacing the set.

⚠ **STEP 3 SINCE 2026-09-29 AND STEP 2 BEFORE IT.** The six-step wizard put
the services on their own screen; the four-step drawing merges them with
the fees and the payment (PO: *"can we merge this two and create table
array for this"*).

✅ **BR-CUS-1070 — AN ENTRY MAY CARRY ITS OWN START.** `services` is a list
whose members are either a bare code (`"electric"`, the shape every caller
sent until 2026-09-15, meaning *this service, no date given*) or an object
`{"code": "electric", "requested_start": "2026-12-05"}`. A mixed list is
fine; the old shape is not deprecated and nothing was migrated, because the
join table held **0 rows** across the demo tenant's 8 requests when this
landed.

⚠ **THE SHAPE CHECK STAYS HERE AND THE VALUE CHECKS STAY IN THE SERVICE.**
This view answers *is `services` a list of things that could be services*;
an unknown code, a repeated code and an unparseable date are each refused BY
NAME by `set_services`, which is the door every caller goes through —
including the ones that never touch HTTP.

`POST .../submit` — **idempotent, BR-CUS-093 consequence (e)**.

*"`submit` no longer allocates anything, so a repeated submit is a state
transition on a row that already has its identity — the idempotency key is
the request itself."* A second call answers 200 with
`idempotent_replay: true` and sends the customer nothing twice.

Approve a *Temporary stop* or *Restart now* request. Dates may be sent
(the clerk agreed different ones); `field_visit_needed` must be a literal
`true` to count, so a string `"false"` is never read as a yes.

`POST .../transitions` — every lifecycle move except approve and refuse,
which have their own doors because each carries a guard this one does not
(the condition gate; the reason code).

S8 Company → Brand logo upload (BR-TEN-019 as SUPERSEDED 2026-10-27,
`DEF-TEN-10618`): PNG or JPG only → an SVG is 415
`settings.company.logo_svg_not_accepted`, anything else outside the
allowlist 415, ≤2 MB → 413 over the cap (B12 r1 upload rows), and the bytes
must BE what the type says (magic bytes, 422 on a mismatch). Returns the
stored REFERENCE; the bytes never come back out of this endpoint.

The two guards here are transport-level (they render B12 r1 rows that have
no catalog code); the identical law runs again inside the service, so a
job or shell caller cannot bypass it — see services.save_company_logo.

No DELETE: neither US-TEN-005 nor the prototype drop-zone anchors logo
removal, so no removal endpoint is invented (reported).

get.description:
`GET /settings/company/logo/file` — THE one address every drawing of the
logo uses: the app header, Settings › Company › Brand, the Bill layout,
Customer portal settings and the customer portal itself.

⚠ **THE BYTES COME FROM THE COMMON DOCUMENT STORE SINCE 2026-10-05
(`CR-172-BRC10`)** — `selectors.logo_bytes()` → `document_store.fetch()`,
which re-hashes what S3 returns. Until then they were read from
`tenants.logo_bytes`, a column a lane chose because no store existed.

⚠ **READABLE WITHOUT SIGNING IN (`CR-172-BRC10`, judgment (2) in the
decision log of 2026-10-05).** The logo is printed on every bill and drawn
on the PUBLIC portal, so a sign-in on this read protected nothing and left
the portal unable to draw it. `authentication_classes([])` beside
`AllowAny` for the reason `subdomain_check` gives: a public read must not
be refused because the browser also carries some other session.
The UPLOAD (`company_logo` above) is unchanged: System Admin only, and the
sanitiser is still its only way in.

**TENANT SCOPING (CLAUDE.md hard rule 1).** `require_tenant` first — the
tenant is the one the ADDRESS names, set by the middleware — then
`selectors.logo_bytes()`, which accepts no id and no tenant from the caller.
There is no parameter that reaches another utility's logo; `?v=` is the
browser's cache key and is never read.

**CACHING.** The ETag is the logo's REFERENCE (the stored document's id), so
a replacement is a new ETag; the front end also puts the reference in the
address (`?v=`), so a replaced logo is a different URL and is fetched at
once. A matching `If-None-Match` is answered 304 from the row alone, with no
trip to the store. `Cache-Control: private` — never a shared cache entry.

A store that cannot return the logo answers 503
(`settings.company.logo_storage_unavailable`); the front end draws the
generated mark in its place rather than a broken image.

`PUT /settings/read-validation/{service}` — one enabled service's VEE
thresholds (CR-038 A1) **and its per-rule ENABLED switches** (BR-MET-136).
Partial change set in, the saved row out; a service with no row yet
requires every FIGURE (no ratified figure exists to merge with —
BR-MET-020) but never the switch map, whose default IS ratified: all
enabled. Every successful write appends ONE audit row naming field, old,
new and actor, plus a second `settings.read_validation.rule_switched` row
when a switch moved.

`rule_enabled` is `{rule: bool}` and is MERGED over what is stored — naming
one rule never re-enables the others. An attempt to disable an INTEGRITY
rule is REFUSED 422 with the rule NAMED (BR-MET-136 clause 4), never
ignored: a save that silently drops the request would leave an admin
believing they turned off a check that is still running.

get.description:
`GET /settings/sample-data` — the BR-TEN-060 honesty report.

Serves the stored ledger, the removal plan, and `seeded_total`. A tenant
that has never run the job gets `modules: []` and `succeeded: false`, which
is why `has_run` is sent as its own boolean: "never asked" and "asked and
nothing loaded" are different facts and the screen must not merge them into
one zero (the DEF-127 posture — a count nothing wrote is not a count).

post.description:
`POST /settings/sample-data/remove` — BR-TEN-066, partial-and-named.

Returns the plan, which today is "nothing is removable, and here is the
named reason per module". It is a POST rather than a DELETE because the
contracted action is a REMOVAL RUN over a tagged row set, not the deletion
of the resource this path names — and because DELETE on a route that
removes nothing reads as a destructive button that worked.

`POST /settings/sample-data/retry` — CR-039 wave B: re-run ONE block.

Body: `{"module": "billing", "block": "seed_sample_records"}` — the pair
`sample_data_runs.blocks[]` reports, because a module owns up to three
blocks and "retry billing" would be ambiguous the moment it owned two.

`SystemAdminOnly` like the other two writes: BR-TEN-064's *"a human asks"*
does not become *"anyone asks"* because the unit got smaller.

Answers the WHOLE report, not just this block. Fixing the ROOT of a cascade
does not by itself clear the consequences below it — those blocks are still
unseeded until they too are run — and an operator who pressed retry needs
to see which lines are still red, not a green line in isolation.

`POST /settings/sample-data/seed` — BR-TEN-064: a human asks, always.

Synchronous on purpose (see the block comment above). Idempotent per tenant
by BR-TEN-063, so a second press updates the ledger rather than doubling it.

get.description:
`GET settings/security-policy/audit` — the Audit log card under Save.

The approved redesign of 2026-09-29 puts a full-width card below the Save
button showing **the last five changes made on this tab**, not the
platform-wide log (PO: *"keep it here only in this screen"*). `View all →`
on that card opens S61, which is where the whole log and its paging live.

⚠ **SAME ROLE GATE AS THE POLICY READ, ON PURPOSE.** A System Admin edits
and an Executive views (`BR-IDN-019`); a Billing Clerk cannot see the
Security tab at all, and a history of it is the same disclosure as the
values it lists. A gate of its own here would be a second answer to one
question.

⚠ **NO ETag/304.** `_maybe_304` is for reference data that rarely moves
(/roles, the policy itself). This read changes every time anybody saves,
and it carries timestamps, so a cached answer is the one thing a history
card must never give.

⚠ **NO PAGE ENVELOPE, AND THAT IS NOT AN `NFR-3` BREACH.** The read is a
fixed five rows over a bounded scan (`audit_seam.SCAN_LIMIT`), so it does
not grow with the tenant; the unbounded view of the same data is S61,
which pages.

`GET/PUT settings/security-policy/field-app-pins` — the field app's
certificate pins, the "Field app certificates" card on Settings › Security
(`OQ-FLD-12797`, PO 2026-10-24: *"use settings - security values set in
staff portal"*).

A PUT carries the WHOLE list (`{"pins": [...]}`) — add and deactivate are
both "the list as it should be", so one validator sees the result the
phones will get and can refuse a list that would strand them
(`field_pins.validate_pins`). Same role gate as the policy itself
(`BR-IDN-019`): a System Admin edits, an Executive views.

⚠ **NO ETag/304.** The derived `status` and `days_left` move with the
calendar, so a cached answer would go on calling a key *Valid* the day it
starts to expire.

get.description:
`GET /settlements` — 5·1, *"The bank shows one credit. Which payments is it?"*

    q            the payout's reference, or the provider
    sort         paid_out_at | code | provider | gross | net | payments | status
    dir          asc | desc
    page / per   50 · 100 · 200 · 500 · 1000
    f.state      received | matched
    f.provider   one provider_key
    as_of        the business day PAID OUT TODAY and FEES THIS MONTH mean

⚠ **PAGINATED AND SORTED IN SQL** (`NFR-3`, `NFR-5`). The `count` below is
the database's `COUNT(*)` over the filtered set, not `len()` of a
materialised list.
`GET /settlements/{code}` — 5·2's head and its four figures.

`GET /settlements/{code}/members` — *"Which 46 payments made up this?"*

⚠ **A SEPARATE, PAGED DOOR RATHER THAN A `members[]` ON THE DETAIL.** A
payout holds any number of payments and `NFR-5` forbids a cap on it, so a
detail payload that carried them all would be an unbounded response with a
table's worth of controls that could not reach the server. The drawing puts
a full toolbar and a pagination footer under this table (p071), which only
a list endpoint can answer.

`GET /shell/display` — the branding and the formats every screen draws.

⚠ **A BILLING CLERK COULD NOT USE THIS PRODUCT AT ALL BETWEEN 2026-08-21 AND
2026-09-06 AND THIS ROUTE IS THE FIX (`DEF-SHL-4272`).** The app shell boots
by reading the tenant's branding and its date/number formats; it took both
from `GET /settings/company` and `GET /settings/regional`, which are
`SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin` — `{system_admin, executive}`, because
A4's `settings_lookups` row gives a Billing Clerk **no cell**. A clerk
signed in successfully, reached `/dashboard`, and every screen in the
product rendered the shell's failure state with a Retry that could not
succeed.

**WHY A NEW ROUTE RATHER THAN WIDENING THE GATE ON THE TWO EXISTING ONES.**
Two reasons, and the second is the one that decided it.

*One:* widening `SettingsReadAnyWriteSystemAdmin` re-opens `DEF-196`, whose
docstring records the first cut of that fix doing exactly this, passing
every test written for it, and being caught by `US-TEN-009 TC-5`. A4 is
signed; no cell means no access.

*Two, and this stands on its own even if A4 said otherwise:*
`GET /settings/regional` also serves `accounting_method`, `close_cadence`,
`close_day` and `lock_closed_periods`. Those are a utility's finance policy.
Nobody should receive a close-period lock in order to render `03/04/2026`.

**AND IT CARRIES THE CURRENT ACCOUNTING PERIOD (`DEF-SHL-4283`,
2026-09-06).** `{fy_label, period, start, end, status}` — the label a screen
puts on a figure and the window it runs a report over, computed by
`selectors.current_period()` and never stored (`BR-TEN-022`). It was left
off the first cut of this route, and two screens A4 gives a Billing Clerk
broke on the omission: `Reports → By premises` never ran its report, and
`Payments → Refunds` headed itself *"Set the fiscal year start to see the
current period."* at a tenant whose fiscal year start is set. The card's
sixth field, `close_by`, stays on `GET /settings/regional` — it is
`close_day` in another shape, a finance-close deadline rather than a
drawing fact.

**ONE ROUTE AND NOT TWO** (branding and formats could have been separate).
The shell cannot draw a screen with half of this, so splitting it would give
one indivisible fact two loading states, two failure states and two Retry
buttons — and a boot read failing with a dead Retry is the defect being
fixed. Halving the number of things that can fail at boot is part of the
fix, not a convenience.

**READ ONLY, FOR EVERY ROLE INCLUDING THE SYSTEM ADMIN.** `ShellDisplayRead`
refuses every mutating verb, so this cannot become a second write path
around `PUT /settings/regional`'s validation and audit trail. Settings is
still the one door in.

Tenant-scoped like every other read here: `require_tenant` first, and
`selectors.shell_display()` takes no tenant argument — it resolves the row
from `app.tenant_id`, so there is no id a caller could supply to reach
another utility's branding.

What this tenant buys from Bynry — the read S107 renders.

**THE PATH IS 11b §2.16's OWN**, `GET /subscription`, ratified 2026-08-09
and unserved until today. It is not `settings/subscription`: the audit row
names this resource without the Settings prefix, and a screen living on a
Settings tab does not make its resource a setting.

**GET ONLY, and that is a decision rather than a stage.** Nothing on this
surface writes. A utility cannot change what it pays Bynry from inside its
own product — a plan change is `S107`'s *Change plan* action, which has no
endpoint, no rule and no ruling — and the implementation order is a record
of what Bynry SOLD, whose editability is the open half of `OQ-610`. A PUT
here would be a door onto a decision nobody has made.

**The role gate is A4's `settings_lookups` cell**, the same class every
other Settings read on this module uses: System Admin *Full*, Executive
*View*, Billing Clerk no cell at all. A clerk at a 1–2 staff utility has no
business reading the subscription price, and `DEF-196`'s class already
encodes exactly that split (it refuses a clerk on the READ, which is the
half that was wrong for a day).

The blocked-addresses list — every address this utility must not send to.

⚠ **PAGINATED, LIKE EVERY LIST IN THIS PRODUCT (`NFR-3`, 11b G5).** The page
is taken in the DATABASE at the ratified sizes 50/100/200/500/1000, default
50. There is no shape of tenant for which an unpaginated version of this
would be correct: the list grows for ever — a released row is KEPT as
history — and `DEF-PAY-4221` is what an unpaginated list costs when the
ceiling moves.

**Active first, newest first.** A released address is history and belongs
below the thing a clerk came here to act on; `?f.state=released` asks for
the history on its own and `?f.state=all` for both. Served from
`suppression.active()` so that *active* means one thing in this module.

**Three filters, all taken in SQL: `f.state`, `f.channel`, `f.reason`.**
`f.reason` is one of `vocabulary.reasons` and narrows to nothing when it is
a word this product does not have — see `suppression.listing` for why that
is not a fall-back to *all reasons*.

⚠ **NO DATABASE ID IS THE VISIBLE VALUE OF A FIELD** (B14 rule 31). `id`
travels because the Release call needs it, and the screen shows the ADDRESS.

post.description:
**Release** — let this address through again (the PO asked for it by name).

Body: `{"note": "typo, corrected on the account", "released_on":
"2026-09-17"}`. The date is the CALLER's business date (`BR-TEN-043`), like
`POST /deliveries/returned` one screen over; the note is optional and is the
one field in this table that is a person's own words.

TWO THINGS HAPPEN AND BOTH ARE REPORTED:
  1. the suppression is stamped released and **KEPT** — this is not a
     delete, because *why did this customer stop getting email in March* has
     to stay answerable after `audit_log` is pruned;
  2. every queue row held BY THIS RULE for that address becomes selectable
     again. Nothing is re-rendered and nothing is re-created — the same
     rows, the same pins, the same recipient snapshots
     (`delivery_ops.release_held_for_accounts`' ratified shape).

Releasing twice is refused rather than silently accepted: a clerk pressing
Release a second time should be told the second press did nothing.

⚠ **THIS IS THE ONLY DOOR OUT, AND IT IS A PERSON'S DOOR.** Nothing
automatic releases an address — an automatic un-suppression is a policy
nobody has ruled, and `RB-122`'s own *Re-enable when the contact is updated*
parameter is recorded as having nothing to watch. A clerk deciding that an
address is good again is the whole mechanism.

get.description:
BR-TEN-037: this tenant's own jurisdictions — there is no global registry.

⚠ **THIS SERVED A BARE ARRAY UNTIL 2026-09-19 (`DEF-RAT-5754`, `NFR-3`).**
It was the SEVENTH list read in this module and the one `DEF-RAT-5742`
could not find: that lane grepped for `_paginated`, which by construction
cannot see a read that never reached the paginator at all. `core.pagination`
says an endpoint *"has to go out of its way to be unbounded, and none may"*
— this one did, by returning the selector's list straight to `Response`.

⚠ **IT DOES NOT LOOK LIKE A LIST, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED SIX WEEKS.** It
feeds the S13 wizard's step-1 PICKER, so it reads as a lookup vocabulary
rather than as a catalogue — and a vocabulary is the one shape a reader
forgives for being whole.

⚠ **AND THE HONEST SIZE OF IT, BECAUSE OVERSTATING THIS WOULD BE ITS OWN
DEFECT.** A real tenant holds about **53** jurisdictions (`CR-077` seeds
`TX`, `ALL` and every US state code), and that number does NOT follow the
account count — T5's 40,000 is accounts, not jurisdictions. So nothing a
clerk can see changed today. What changed is that the shape was unbounded:
no rule, index or code path stopped a utility entering five thousand, and
nothing would have refused to serve all five thousand in one reply. This is
`NFR-3` conformance and `NFR-5` read forwards, not a performance rescue.

⚠ **THE WIRE SHAPE CHANGED, SO THE CLIENT CHANGED IN THE SAME COMMIT.**
`TaxJurisdiction[]` became the four-key envelope; `getTaxJurisdictions`
now follows `count` and the S13 picker still receives every row
(`BR-SHL-033` — a picker that can only see page 1 would have been a new
defect, not a fix). Shipping the backend half alone was the whole reason
`DEF-RAT-5742` left this one open.

Every list the New tax form renders — boundaries (only those that bill
today), the six due-date rules, the four computation forms and the filing
frequencies — so no screen hard-codes a choice the engine cannot honour.

DEF-380 — *"the matched premise count so a wrong boundary is visible
before rates are entered"*.

A GET taking the SCOPE itself, not a tax id, because the moment the
safeguard has to work is TAX-02 step 1: nothing is saved yet and no rate has
been typed. That is the whole point of the sentence — *before rates are
entered*. Reading a saved tax's scope is the same call with its two stored
values, which is what the tax's own page reads.

── ⚠ IT TOOK THE BOUNDARY AND NOTHING ELSE UNTIL CR-087 (`PRB-05`) ────────
A tax states three restrictions and this read honoured one, so a levy
restricted to Commercial customers on Water reported EVERY premises in the
utility. That is the one way this safeguard can mislead rather than fail:
the number is larger than the truth, on the control whose entire job is to
be smaller than the total when something is wrong. Both other restrictions
are passed through now, and the count runs the engine's own predicate over
all three (BR-RAT-107).

⚠ **NFR-3 — THIS READ RETURNS A COUNT AND A THREE-LINE SAMPLE.** It must
never grow into a list of the premises it counted; a list of a T5 tenant's
40,000 addresses is exactly the unpaginated read that rule forbids.

post.description:
DEF-387 — put a DRAFT into force, optionally on a future statutory date.

Part 4 step 4's *Activate* and *Save & schedule*. The date is the only
difference between them, so there is one route and one service.

get.description:
Every change to this tax and every version of it, newest first, paged
(NFR-3): `{at, actor, action, before, after, reason}`. A window onto
`audit_log` (pruned on retention — hard rule 4), read through rating's
seam onto the audit module's one query.

post.description:
DEF-384 — *"a documented correction version with a reason"*, at last.

The door `PATCH /taxes/{id}` now names when it refuses a rate-history edit
on a live tax. It was refused on the client and nowhere else, and there was
nothing to send the operator to; both halves are here.

201, not 200: a correction CREATES a row (the corrected one is superseded,
never rewritten), and the Location header points at the new rate so a client
can read what is now in force.

patch.description:
Settings › Accounting's door to a tax's liability account — the only
one after creation (PO 2026-10-03 on CR-008). `{"liability_gl_account_id":
uuid | null}`. `PATCH /taxes/{id}` refuses the field on a live tax.

post.description:
*New rate from a date* (`DEF-RAT-9283`): ends the live version the day
before `effective_from` and creates the next one, in ONE transaction. 201
with the new version, like a correction.

get.description:
WHICH plans carry this tax, and HOW each one gets it.

The tile above it has always counted them (`used_by_plans`); this names
them and says, per plan, whether the tax arrives through the authority the
plan binds or through an attachment somebody made on the plan — the two
mechanisms `BR-RAT-113` gives, which behave differently when the authority
changes.

post.description: *Retire* — ends the window on `effective_to`; never `deleted_at`.

get.description:
THIS TAX'S OWN DATED ROWS, newest first — what the rate has been.

⚠ **IT IS THE OBJECT'S OWN CHAIN AND NEVER A FILTERED `audit_log` QUERY.**
The two are both append-only histories of the same object and they answer
different questions: a version row is a priced state bills still resolve
to, an audit row is an actor + action + timestamp the engine never reads —
and `audit_log` is PRUNED on a retention schedule (hard rule 4's
2026-09-02 narrowing), so a rate history sourced from it loses its authors
with nothing raising.

`GET /template-catalog` — every document and message this platform sends.

CR-007's own statement of purpose is drawn on the screen and is worth
repeating where the data is produced: *"Notifications decide WHEN, Templates
define WHAT."* Nothing on this route schedules, triggers or sends anything.

BR-SHL-011 throughout: `q` searches name, category and used-by;
`f.category` takes the chips; `sort`/`dir`/`page`/`per` are the standard
grammar and an unknown value FALLS BACK rather than erroring.

`GET /template-catalog/{code}` — the detail screen's whole payload.

Header, variant switcher, merge-field palette, version history and a
rendered preview, in one round trip, because they are one screen and four
requests for one screen is four ways for it to be half-loaded.

`?variant=<id>` selects which variant the preview and the version list are
for; without it the `(default, default)` variant is chosen — BR-NOT-001's
mandatory fallback, which is also what resolution would pick.

`GET /template-catalog/{code}/changes/{version_id}` — `BR-NOT-027` part 3.

**The two halves are served together on purpose.** The PO asked them as one
question — *"any changes to tempalte or any items hsould be noted as
changed; that way it will keep the santity of the legal documents"* — and a
caller able to fetch *"what changed"* without *"who is holding the old
wording"* will, which is the version history that already exists.

  * `changed_fields` / `fields` — WHICH wording fields moved and by how many
    lines. Never a sentence, and never an author's account of WHY: that is
    `OQ-255`(b), open with the Product Owner, and a derived diff dressed as
    a note would be this product putting words in a person's mouth.
  * `superseded` — the version this one replaced, HOW MANY already-sent
    documents still stand on it, and a page of them. Each row carries the id
    of the KEPT COPY where one exists, which opens the existing
    `GET /documents/{id}`. **A storage key is never served** — the caller
    gets a document id it can re-resolve under its own tenant, exactly as
    `CR-049` task 3's routes do.

⚠ **`superseded.documents` IS THE TOTAL AND `superseded.sample` IS A PAGE OF
IT.** They are the same query, so the panel can say *"20 of 3,412"* without
the two numbers being about different sets — which on this screen would be a
false statement to a regulator rather than an off-by-one.

⚠ **SYSTEM ADMIN, like every other door on this screen.** The endpoint gate
is narrower than `BR-BIL-027`'s service gate, and deliberately: the PO ruled
this SETTINGS SURFACE System-Admin-only (exception 4 below), and this route
lists customers who received a particular letter, which is the most
sensitive read on it.

post.description:
`POST /template-catalog/{code}/deactivate` — CR-007's *"a variant in use
can't be deleted — deactivate only, with usage warning listing consumers"*.

Archives the variant's live version. The response names the consumers
BEFORE and AFTER, because the warning the CR asks for is only useful if it
is the server's count and not the screen's guess.

`POST /template-catalog/{code}/draft` — an edit is a NEW version.

BR-BIL-026: the published version is untouched and keeps rendering until
somebody publishes this one. **Unknown merge token BLOCKS the save with an
inline error** (CR-007's own rule, US-NOT-005 TC-5) — the refusal comes from
`rendering.validate_body` and names the token and the class, and it is
returned as a field error so the editor can put it under the body box.

`POST /template-catalog/{code}/from-default` — *Create from our default*.

`CR-190-BRC10`, PO 2026-10-22, verbatim: *"A: keep your rule (each utility
publishes its own) but make it one click ('Create from our default')"*.
DEF-NOT-10442: on a contract class with no variant the platform's wording was
SHOWN and never usable — *Duplicate as variant* opened a blank editor and the
admin had to retype the agreement.

One action, System Admin only, and BR-NOT-002 stands in full: it creates the
`(default, default)` variant (idempotent, `template_service.register`) and
saves ONE DRAFT whose subject and body are the platform's offered wording,
dated with the `effective_from` the admin chose — a contract still needs a
human's date, and nothing here is PUBLISHED. The admin reads it, edits it if
they wish, and publishes it with the existing Publish action. A class the
platform offers no wording for is refused by name; so is a class that
already has a variant (that variant is the place to edit).

`POST /template-catalog/{code}/make-live-again` — History's action on an
earlier published version (drawing 07–09, 15).

Body: `version_id`. Writes a NEW version holding that version's own stored
wording and publishes it (`outcome: "live"`); the version it replaces stays
in history and every message already pinned renders what it always did. For
a legal notice the copy is left as a DRAFT for a System Admin's approval
(`outcome: "sent_for_approval"`, A1 C) and the live version keeps going out.

`POST /template-catalog/{code}/new-variant` — *+ New variant* and
*Duplicate as variant* (A3 A: channel × language × customer category).

Body: `language` (`default` = the utility's language), `category`
(`default` = all customers), optional `channel` (must be this class's),
`start_from` (`published` | `variant` | `blank`), `source_variant` (the
variant to copy for `variant`), `effective_from` (contracts only), `name`.

The new variant is a DRAFT — nothing is published. Refused by name: a
combination that exists, a language the utility has not switched on (A4 B),
a category it does not have, a channel this class is not.

`POST /template-catalog/{code}/preview` — the LIVE half of the preview.

A READ despite being a POST: it writes nothing, and it is a POST because a
candidate body is a document that does not fit in a query string. **Any
tenant role may call it** — CR-007's *"others read-only + preview"*, and the
PO's Settings ruling makes reading and previewing the clerk's half.

It renders the body the editor CURRENTLY HOLDS, not the saved one, which is
what makes the pane live — and it refuses exactly what the save refuses,
because both go through `rendering.validate_body`. An editor whose preview
accepts what its save rejects teaches the wrong lesson.

`POST /template-catalog/{code}/publish` — BR-BIL-027's narrow right.

Publishing affects FUTURE renders only. The previous published version is
auto-archived and is retained forever; every document already pinned to it
still renders from it (J22 step 4: *"Nothing re-renders"*).

`POST /template-catalog/{code}/queue-test` — CR-048 B7, from SET-10.

⚠ **THE NAME IS THE CONTRACT: IT QUEUES.** BR-NOT-005 and A11 Addendum r2 §4
make a synchronous send endpoint a gate failure rather than a choice, so
there is no `send`, no `send-test` and no `test-send` beside this and a test
asserts those absences as hard as it asserts this presence. What the button
does is write ONE real row on the outgoing queue, addressed to the person
who pressed it, and then say plainly whether the dispatcher will send it —
with the channel's own line (`channel_line`, `DEF-NOT-10537`; this read
*"say plainly that nothing will leave the building"* until 2026-10-22).
⚠ **AND THE SPELLING DIVERGES FROM A11 §11b ON PURPOSE.** The API audit
lists this as `POST /templates/{id}/send-test`; it is `queue-test` here
because that is what the notification-rules surface already shipped and one
product should not name the same act two ways. The divergence is recorded in
the decision log rather than settled silently.

⚠ **THIS IS WHERE THE ROLE IS CHECKED, AND IT IS CHECKED ONCE (DEF-2515).**
A4 gives Settings & lookup tables to a System Admin in full and to an
Executive as a view; queueing a row is not viewing. The service behind this
carries no decorator of its own, because a second check behind the door can
only ever produce a false refusal.

`POST /template-catalog/{code}/restore` — history is never rewritten.

Restoring v2 saves v2's body as a NEW draft. The old row is untouched
(migration 0006's trigger would refuse anyway) and every document pinned to
it renders exactly what it always rendered. The audit trail records which
version the body came from — "v4 was typed" and "v4 is v2 restored" are
different facts about a customer-facing document.

get.description:
`GET /template-catalog/{code}/variant-options` — what the *New variant*
and *Duplicate as variant* dialogs offer (drawing 06, 10, 18).

Served rather than typed by the screen: the categories are the utility's own
customer classes and the languages are A4 B's switched-on set, both of which
change with the utility's data. `taken` lists the combinations that already
exist so the dialog can say so before the server refuses.

post.description:
`POST /template-catalog/{code}/variants` — CR-007's *"add variant (name
+ language + audience note)"*.

The "audience note" IS the consumer category: BR-NOT-001's four values are
the audiences this platform has (residential / commercial / industrial /
government) plus the mandatory `default` fallback, and a free-text note
beside them would be a second, unenforced way of saying who a letter is for.

get.description:
`{default_language, languages: [{language, accounts, is_default,
no_preference}], total}` for the tenant in context.

**THE ONE TEMPLATES LIST — CR-048 task E9, `BR-NOT-026`.**

S8 → Configure → Templates used to draw TWO lists on one tab: the catalogue
of everything this utility sends, and, underneath it, billing's bill-layout
chooser. A person looking for *"the template we print bills on"* had to know
which of the two panels owned it.

This serves both as ONE list. Each row says what it stores
(`content_model`) and which editor it opens (`editor`), because the two
kinds keep their own editors — the PO's ruling of 2026-08-30 asked for one
list and one lifecycle and did not ask for one editor, and a text box over a
layout key would be the wrong screen for both.

⚠ **`kind` IS A FILTER, NOT A ROUTE.** Both stores answer the same call and
neither is the default: omitting it is the whole list, which is the state
the screen opens in.

⛔ **NOTHING HERE READS OR WRITES BILLING'S TABLES.** `unified_templates`
delegates to `apps.billing.templates_service`, which is the only writer of
`bill_templates` (B2 §2). This route knows about HTTP and nothing else.

`GET /transfers` — S89's Transfers tab (CR-030 W7 task 7.4, B18 §5.7.2).

B18 §6.2 lists this row as `❌`. The list is `transfer_reads.list_transfers`
and this view adds nothing to it: no figure is computed, no absence is
defaulted and no money is moved anywhere in this layer.

⚠ **`AdminOrClerk`, NOT `AnyTenantRole`, AND THE REASON IS THE PAYLOAD.**
A4 gives Executive VIEW on Accounts and every other read on this file is
`AnyTenantRole`. But the MONEY cell this list serves is the same statement
`transfers.money_statement` gates with `@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN,
BILLING_CLERK)`, so `AnyTenantRole` here would hand an Executive figures the
layer below refuses them. The narrower gate is mounted to match rather than
promising a view the service denies — the precedent is
`account_close_impact`, mounted the same way for the same reason.

post.description:
`POST /transfers/account-preview` — **step 1's answer, the moment the
account is picked.** Writes nothing.

⊕ 2026-09-23 (`DEF-CUS-6395`, `DEF-CUS-5182`). It serves the refusal the
commit WOULD raise (`transfers.sale_refusal`, one function for both doors),
the seller as the account names them, whether the account is the premises'
master account, and the billing cycle, current period, next bill and ledger
start the wizard used to hard-code as *"Not available yet"*.

A POST for `buyer-preview`'s reason and for consistency with it: it is a
question put to the sale about to happen, not a resource read.

`POST /transfers/buyer-preview` — **`TRF-02.2`'s missing feedback line.**

⛔ **NEW 2026-09-20.** The conformance walk of that day, on step 2:
*"feedback `Matched an existing customer. C-00902 · Vasquez, M., on the
phone number.` — NOT BUILT: the match happens server-side at commit and the
clerk is never told."* It is drawn on p126 and it is the step's whole
premise — *"Matched first, created only on no match"* — stated back about
the buyer actually being typed.

⚠ **A POST THAT WRITES NOTHING, WHICH IS UNUSUAL AND IS DELIBERATE.** It is
a POST because a government identifier may not travel in a query string:
a URL is logged by every proxy, appears in a browser's history and lands in
the referer header of the next request. `BR-CUS-092`(c) — *"the full value
is never in a list response, an export, a log line or an audit `details`
blob"* — is about exactly that class of leak, and a `GET` would put an SSN
in three of them at once. The idempotency this gives up is worth nothing
here, because there is nothing to be idempotent about.

⚠ **IT CREATES NO TRANSFER ROW, AND THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS.**
`uq_transfers_open_from` allows ONE open transfer per account and no screen
lists a transfer in flight (`US-CUS-027 §8`), so a preview that started a
job would leave an account that can never be sold again and that nobody can
find to cancel. This takes no `from_account_id` at all.

**200 always, or a refusal.** A buyer nobody has seen before is a real
answer and not an error — `verdict: "none"` — which is the reading
`identity_match.recognise` already takes of a search that found nothing.

`POST /transfers/commit` — `TRF-02.5`'s `Complete the sale ✓`.

⛔ **REWRITTEN 2026-09-01 — `BR-CUS-1030`. THIS DOOR NOW REASSIGNS AN
ACCOUNT; IT USED TO CREATE ONE.** PO ruling, verbatim: *"dont create new
account - we reassing that account - bascailly I have sold my property - so
account get transfer to new person or business"*.

The wizard sends ONE `TransferCommitPlan` and this view runs the five staged
writes inside ONE `transaction.atomic()`:

    start_transfer      from_account_id
    set_new_customer    customer{display_name · kind · identity}
    set_sale_date       sold_on
    acknowledge_money   (nothing to elect — the debt follows the property)
    reassign_account    customer{...}

**Django nests `atomic()` as savepoints**, so each service keeping its own
`transaction.atomic()` is correct and untouched — the outer block is what
makes the run all-or-nothing.

⚠ **THE BUYER'S BLOCK IS SENT TWICE AND VALIDATED TWICE, ON PURPOSE.** Step
2 validates it so the clerk is refused in front of the form they are typing
into (`BR-CUS-1023`: name the missing thing at the door), and
`reassign_account` validates it again because a service-layer caller — a
management command, another module, the next lane — does not have to pass
through step 2. `transfers` stores no identifier between the two, and that
is deliberate: a government identifier belongs in customers' encrypted
column and nowhere else (`BR-CUS-1020`).

⚠ **THE ROLLBACK IS THE FEATURE, NOT THE TIDINESS.** `uq_transfers_open_from`
allows ONE open transfer per account and no screen shows a transfer in
flight (`US-CUS-027 §8`). Without the outer block, a refusal at stage 5
would strand an `in_progress` row that blocks that account from ever being
sold again and that nobody can find to cancel. Here, zero rows survive and
the clerk simply goes again.

⚖️ **NO MONEY MOVES, AND THAT IS NOW THE RULING RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE.** PO
2026-09-01: *"money follow property - new owner boutght everything property
+ debt also"*. The account carries its own ledger, so **the balance never
moves because the thing it sits on never moves** — and the response carries
`reassignment.balance_at_sale` and `.deposit_at_sale`, the figures as they
stood at the moment of sale, so what the buyer took on is on the record.

⛔ **AND NOTHING ALREADY ISSUED TO THE SELLER IS TOUCHED** — hard rule 4.
Their invoices, payments and journal entries stay exactly as issued, in
their name, for ever.

⚠ **`reads` IS GONE FROM THIS PAYLOAD.** It carried ONE meter read serving a
closing account and an opening one (`BR-MET-128`'s transfer event). **A sale
closes no account and opens none**, so there is no final read and no opening
read: the meter keeps running on one unbroken account and the next ordinary
read serves it. A lane that puts `reads` back is re-creating the second
account this ruling removed.

**200, not 201.** The old door created an account and answered `Created`.
This one changes who an existing account belongs to; nothing was created.

get.description:
`GET /transfers/{ref}` — the TRANSFER RECORD screen (blueprint p133).

The assembly is `transfer_reads.record_detail` and this view adds nothing
to it: no figure is computed here, no absence is defaulted, and nothing is
written.

⚠ **`AdminOrClerk`, NOT `AnyTenantRole`, and it is the same reasoning
`move_record_detail` and `transfers_list` both carry.** This page draws a
MONEY section, and the deposit statement the layer below builds is gated
`@require_role(SYSTEM_ADMIN, BILLING_CLERK)`. Handing an Executive a figure
the service beneath refuses them is the defect that rule exists to prevent,
and matching the narrower gate is the precedent the transfers LIST already
set on this same resource.

post.description:
`POST /transfers/{id}/cancel` — abandon an open transfer.

NOT a stage, which is why it has a route while the five stages do not.
`uq_transfers_open_from` allows ONE open transfer per outgoing account, so
without this an account carrying an open row can never be transferred again
— and open rows exist in this tree today, because the **demo seeder** calls
`start_transfer`. The one-door commit above creates none of them and cannot
clear them.

A committed transfer cannot be cancelled: the accounts have already moved
and hard rule 4's posture applies — a correction is a new job, never an edit
of this one. The service refuses it.

get.description:
`GET /transfers/{id}/money` — `transfers.money_statement`, a pure read.

No audit row: it moves nothing and decides nothing, exactly as
`discounts.deposit_position` does.

⚠ **`deposit_carried` IS NULL WHENEVER `BR-CUS-057`'s INTEREST CANNOT BE
READ, AND THAT IS THE FEATURE** — see the endpoint file's own block. The
figure travels absent with its reason in `unavailable[]`; nothing here
substitutes the principal.

⚠ **Keyed by a TRANSFER id, and under the one-door commit above there is no
transfer row until the commit succeeds.** So this serves a transfer the
seeder left behind or one already committed — `TRF-02.4`'s figures cannot be
read before the thing they describe exists, and the step says so rather than
printing a fixture.

CR-089 wave E (`E6`/`PUJ-26`) — the numbers the review shows.

`BR-MET-1165`: **the number is taken on the press, never reserved by the
preview.** This endpoint therefore allocates nothing, advances nothing and
locks nothing — two clerks reviewing at the same moment are both shown the
same next number, and the second one to press gets the one after it. The
rule and its reasoning are in `services.preview_unit_numbers`.

`GET /units/unit-types` — the tenant's unit-type vocabulary.

`BR-MET-084` (CR-010 A-4) made unit types a seeded, tenant-extensible
reference list. **A clerk adds units, so a clerk must be able to read the
list** — and `/lookups/unit_types` is System-Admin-only, so the Add-units
wizard could not read it through Settings and fell back to a hardcoded
five-string array in the bundle instead (`DEF-MET-5656`). This is the same
door `read_methods` above opened for `DEF-196`, for the same reason.

READ-ONLY, and the tenant-scoped role gate is the whole authorisation:
this lists names a clerk must choose between. Writing to the list stays
where `BR-TEN-036` put it — Settings, System Admin only.

`GET /units/{id}/account` — CR-089 wave I, the S15 Account tab.

`DEF-CUS-4691`: the tab rendered FIVE facts — number, status, start, balance,
autopay — and every one of them was correct. What it could not show was that
the account carries a medical certificate, so **a supervisor standing on the
unit arranging a shut-off could not see the one row that forbids it.**

NOT PAGED, for `unit_assets`' reason one route up: this is everything about
ONE account at ONE unit, the tab draws all of it at once, and a `{count,
next}` envelope would describe navigation no control offers. The one list
inside it — the account's notes — is the account's whole set, ordered pinned-
first by the index customers built for it.

An unknown or foreign unit is a 404 through `selectors.unit_row`, before any
account is read.

`GET /units/{id}/assets` — B18 W5 task 5.2, move-in step 3's asset panel.

*"Every meter, sub-meter and behind-the-meter device at the unit"*, grouped
on `asset_types.category` **post-CR-028** (BR-AST-004: exactly one tab per
asset) and NOT on the `(sub)/(master)` qualifier — a behind-the-meter
inverter hangs off its meter by `parent_asset`, so the qualifier would file
it as a sub-meter. See `selectors.unit_assets` for the whole disposition.

NOT PAGED, and deliberately: this is everything installed at ONE unit, the
panel draws all of it at once, and a `{count, next}` envelope would describe
navigation no control offers (the `route_read_windows` reasoning, same
grammar). An unknown or foreign unit id is 404 through `unit_row`, before
any asset is read — never an empty panel that would read as *"nothing is
installed here"*.

NO 11b ROW TO FOLLOW — B18 §5.5.5 marks this endpoint **NEW**. House
grammar (resource, then subpath), REPORTED for the A11 addendum with the
`/reads` and `/imports` routes that are in the same position.

post.description:
BR-MET-095 (CR-024): move a unit to another premise, as a dated event.

A correction, not a deactivation — so it takes the create/edit role pair
BR-MET-035 names rather than `SystemAdminOnly`. Every refusal (no reason, no
date, a FUTURE date, the same premise, a colliding label, an un-acknowledged
unit that has had accounts) is the SERVICE's; this view decides nothing.

POST /units/{unit_id}/move-in (`DEF-CUS-6353`) — the move-in that names
the UNIT, for a unit nobody has lived in. Same body, same guards and same
201 + Location as `POST /accounts/{id}/move-in`: both run
`services._move_in`, and the only difference is where the unit comes from.
That includes `BR-CUS-1101`'s optional `services` list — same field, same
refusals, validated against THIS unit's points.
See `services.move_in_to_unit`.

get.description: `GET /units/{id}/move-in-facts` — step 1's unit card (P1.17, image 30).
`GET /units/{id}/move-in-meters` — *Services and meters* (P1.18, image 30).

post.description:
`POST /units/{id}/move-in-meters/check` — *Below the last read.* per
row (image 32). Body `{"reads": [{meter_no, value}]}`. Writes nothing.

get.description:
`GET /units/{id}/move-out-services?as_of=YYYY-MM-DD` — move-out step 2's
services, grouped by billing basis (`DEF-CUS-10051`, BR-TEN-1180).
`as_of` is the move-out date; absent = the tenant's today; a malformed
date is refused, never read as absent. Writes nothing; one unit's list.

`GET /units/{id}/move-preview?premises_id=` — CR-089 wave J (`PUJ-46`).

**WHAT MOVING THIS UNIT WILL DO, ITEMISED, BEFORE ANYBODY PRESSES ANYTHING.**
The screen used to describe the consequence in two sentences and neither of
them mentioned the two that travel furthest: every asset tagged to the unit
changes address with it (an address is stored on `premises` and nowhere
else), and the route and cycle change, so a different person reads the meter
on a different day.

`?premises_id=` is OPTIONAL. Without it the answer is the *from* side only —
what the unit carries today — which is what the screen draws before a
destination has been chosen. Unknown or foreign ids on either side are a 404
through the selectors, never a preview of absences.

⛔ **IT DECIDES NOTHING AND APPROVES NOTHING.** `POST /units/{id}/move` still
owns every refusal, this endpoint duplicates none of them, and a preview and
a refusal that disagree are the refusal being right.

`GET /units/{id}/pricing` — B18 W5 task 5.3 + **CR-034 (b)**, the unit's
Plan tab: what this unit is priced on FOR A STATED PERIOD.

🔒 Serves rating's figures; computes none of them. The period and its
`as_of` · plan (and the plan CHANGES inside the period, reported never
collapsed) · services and their base charges · one rate-schedule card per
service WITH its blocks, resolved on the service date · minimum charges ·
charge codes WITH the code's own amount · discounts the plan OFFERS ·
taxes · the penalty rule.

`?period_start=&period_end=` are optional and are BOTH-or-NEITHER. **With
neither, the answer is byte-identical to what this endpoint served before
CR-034 (b)** — `period: null`, `as_of` = the tenant's today. No default
month is invented; `selectors.unit_pricing` carries the calendar worked
example for why that would show a customer next month's rates.

**The worked month B18 asks for is still NOT served and the payload states
its own absence** (OQ-363) — nothing in this product prices a plan outside a
bill run, and no signed rule says what consumption a worked month would be
priced at. Inventing either would be billing math this repo has frozen
(B4/B5, GT-1..61) or an open question resolved by picking a value.

Four further absences are STATED rather than filled, each with its own
reason so no screen renders one sentence for several facts: a unit with no
plan · a plan this tenant cannot read · rating not publishing at all · the
discount GRANT and the CONTRACT, neither of which a unit can answer.

post.description: `{status, effective_date, reason}` — BR-MET-1164 one level down.

get.description: The unit's live dependency counts, for the status dialog (`PUJ-48`).

The caller's OWN preference for `key`, read and written.

A4/BR-SHL-025: every signed-in role may manage their own UI preferences —
a Billing Clerk choosing which columns they see grants them nothing, and
gating this on System Admin would make the product's column chooser work
for one person per tenant.

post.description:
`POST users/{id}/activation-code` — a NEW code for the native app
(`CR-187-BRC10`, `R105`): the one the office gave was lost, or seven days
passed. Every earlier unused code of the login is void at once. The code is
shown once, never retrievable — the temporary password's rule (BR-IDN-022).
System Admin only, like every other user-management act (BR-IDN-009).

`POST users/{id}/resend-invitation` — `CR-188-BRC10`, PO answer 5:
*"A: 'Resend invitation' on the row: a new password and a new email."*

INVITED rows only (the person has never signed in). A new on-screen
temporary password (`issue_temp_password`, which voids every earlier link
and password) and a new invitation email whose link voids the old one.

get.description: `GET /api/{utility}/v1/billing` — RETIRED, see `/partner/v1/bills`.

The published specification, *"rather than a bespoke document"* (§1).

⚠ **AUTHENTICATED LIKE THE OTHER TWO.** A specification is not a secret,
but an unauthenticated one at a tenant's own address answers *does this
utility exist* to anybody who asks, which is the enumeration oracle
`BR-INT-044` exists to close, arriving through the one door nobody thinks
to lock. It refuses with the same five words as everything else.

It is DERIVED FROM THE MANIFEST, so it cannot describe an operation this
product does not serve, and a field added to a seam without being added
here shows up as a difference rather than as a silent extra.
`GET /api/{utility}/v1/payments` — RETIRED, see `/partner/v1/payments`.

The "Waiting on" list, and parking a new draft onto it.

**The list is newest first and every row carries `age_days`.** That is not
decoration: BR-SHL-048 accepts, in as many words, that a parked move-out is
invisible to the rest of the product and *"the remind-on date and the
visible age … are the only thing stopping a draft sitting forever"*. The
server computes the age with the same arithmetic `parkAgeDays` uses in
`WizardFrame.tsx`, so the number beside the control inside a wizard and the
number in the list's AGE column cannot drift apart by a day.

⚠ **THE LIST IS PAGINATED** (11b G5 — pagination is mandatory on every
list), so the body is the DRF envelope `{count, next, previous, results}`
and the rows are under `results`. `?page=` and `?per=` behave as on every
other list in the product.

delete.description:
One draft: read it to resume, patch it to save more, delete to discard.

**GET is the resume read, and it writes an audit row** (`wizard_park.
resumed`) — reasoned in `wizard_parks.resume`: opening a parked move-in is
an access to a person's name, email and phone before any customer row
exists, and rule 7 wants the who and the when. One row per open is the
stated cost.

**DELETE really deletes, and that is lawful.** CLAUDE.md rule 4's
immutability governs issued invoices, invoice lines, payments and journal
lines; a half-typed form has moved no money and posted nothing. 204 with no
body — there is nothing left to return.

A draft belonging to another tenant is a **404, never a 403** (HR-1), on all
three verbs, and RLS FORCE refuses it at the database as well.

get.description:
`GET /work-items` — row 17: the work list, **paged on the server**.

Filters are `BR-SHL-011`'s `f.<name>` grammar: `f.source`, `f.status`,
`f.owner`. An unknown filter name is IGNORED and an unknown value falls back
to unfiltered — a list URL never 4xx's over its own params.

⚠ **`f.status` DEFAULTS TO `open` AND THAT IS A CHOICE, NOT AN OMISSION.**
The screen is *everything waiting on a person*; a default that included
resolved rows would put last month's closed items on top of this morning's
work. `f.status=resolved` and `f.status=all` are both reachable.

patch.description:
`PATCH /work-items/{id}` — row 17: **assign, resolve, reopen**.

Three verbs on one route because they are three values of one field plus an
owner, and `US-RBS-006` §5 states each: *resolving stamps `resolved_at`;
reopening clears it and keeps the row.*

⚠ **WHAT A PERSON MAY NOT DO IS HAVE A RESOLVED ITEM SILENTLY RE-RAISED AS
A NEW ROW**, and that is the engine's guarantee rather than this route's:
the fingerprint finds the row again and reopens it with its history
(`TC-RBS-006.2`).

An item of another tenant and one that never existed are the same 404.

get.description:
`GET /work-orders` — Work-007's table: every open order, every anchor.
**`POST /work-orders` — THE ONE RAISE EVERY DOOR USES** (CR-070 wave B).

`sort`/`dir` are declared empty because the order is fixed until the
dispatcher's columns exist (wave G), and an undeclared param is ignored,
never refused (BR-SHL-011).

⚠ **THE POST SHARES THIS VIEW BECAUSE DJANGO REACHES ONLY THE FIRST VIEW ON
A PATH.** A sibling `path("work-orders", …)` for the write would be dead
code that read as mounted — the bug `G52` found in the refunds lane. The
role split lives in the permission class, one rule in one place.

⚠ **`07-endpoints.md` §1 row 14 — one raise, every caller.** The connection
detail's *Raise order* (wave B), the Assets door, the move-out door and the
rules engine (all wave M) arrive HERE. `apps.work.services.raise_work_order`
hands straight to metering's `create_work_order` through the seam, which
allocates the `WO-` number, writes the audit row naming the anchor, and
refuses an order standing on nothing with a sentence a clerk can read
(`work.order.anchor_required`) before the database's CHECK ever sees it.

Wave A shipped this raise with the terminal as its only door, deliberately —
*"a route with no screen and a screen with no route are the two halves of
hard-won law 2"*. Wave B lands the screen and the route together.

get.description:
`GET /work-orders/awaiting-approval` — `Work-009`, `BR-WRK-007`.

Every order the field has finished and nobody has accepted, across every
connection and every anchor, oldest first. **The queue is a null, not a
table:** no migration lands in this wave.

The envelope carries one figure the standard one does not — `oldest_waiting`
— because `Work-009`'s footer is *"3 orders · oldest waiting 6 days"* and
the second half is a fact about the WHOLE queue that the page in hand cannot
supply. It is `null` on an empty queue rather than `0`, because zero there
would read as *"something has been waiting no time at all"*.

⚠ **A CROSS-TENANT ID IS A 404 IDENTICAL TO AN ABSENT ONE**, which needs no
code here and is the point: the seam filters by the tenant in context and
RLS `FORCE` sits under it, so Lone Star Ridge's queue simply has no Brazos
Bend rows in it (`US-WRK-003` TC-5, hard rule 1).

post.description: `POST /work-orders/bulk` — per-order results, never a boolean.

`POST /work-orders/bulk-raise` — one job per ticked unit (ruling 19), or
per ticked asset when an asset type was chosen (ruling 20); one savepoint
per job (law 14); an answer per job; a repeated `idempotency_key` returns
the first answer (`CR-168-BRC10` P2.12).

get.description:
`GET /work-orders/by-number/{order_no}` — the ONE door that takes the
reference a person can read, and the only new route `DEF-WRK-4518` needed.

⚠ **WHY A LOOKUP AND NOT A BY-NUMBER TWIN OF ALL FOURTEEN ROUTES.** The
order-detail screen makes fourteen calls and every route on this family is
`<uuid:order_id>`, so an address carrying `WO-0016` 404'd fourteen times and
drew a dash for each. Two shapes of fix were on the table: give the whole
family a by-number door, or let the screen RESOLVE the number once and use
the id for the other thirteen. This is the second, and the reasons are
recorded in `02-decision-log.md` (2026-09-07): one new endpoint against
fourteen changed ones, and a by-number vocabulary spread over fourteen
routes would make every future route on this family choose a door.

⚠ **IT RETURNS THE WHOLE ROW, NOT JUST THE ID, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF
RESOLVING ONCE.** The screen's first call is the detail read either way, so
answering with the id alone would cost a second round trip to fetch what
this query already has in hand.

Read permission is `AnyTenantRole`, the same as `GET /work-orders/{id}` —
this door answers exactly what that one answers and must not become a way
to read a row a role could not otherwise reach (`BR-SHL-025`).

`GET /work-orders/map` — the day's work on the ground (`US-WRK-029`).

⚠ **THE SAME SIX FILTERS, CHECKED BY THE SAME FUNCTION.** `check_filters`
runs here exactly as it does on the list, so a seventh parameter is a `400`
on the map too (`BR-WRK-026`). A map that quietly ignored a filter the list
refuses would let a dispatcher believe they were looking at North when they
were looking at everything — the same argument `BR-WRK-026` makes for the
list, and stronger here, because you cannot count pins.

`GET /work-orders/{id}` — one order's dispatch row.
`PATCH /work-orders/{id}` — **everything a dispatcher changes after the
order exists** (`CR-070` wave I, `US-WRK-031`, `Work-021`).

Wave H builds `Work-008` on the GET; it was served by `G2` because a screen
with no route is the other half of hard-won law 2.

⚠ **TWO VERBS ON ONE VIEW, BECAUSE DJANGO REACHES ONLY THE FIRST VIEW
REGISTERED ON A PATH.** A sibling `path("work-orders/<uuid:order_id>", …)`
for the write would be dead code that never runs — the mistake this file
already records twice, for `work-orders` itself and in the `G52` shape.

as before, and restricts only the PATCH to a System Admin or a Billing
Clerk — the same pair holding every other write in this file. `BR-SHL-025`:
the server enforces it independently of whatever the screen has disabled.

safety lock holds** (`BR-WRK-037`).

⚠ **THE REFUSAL IS HERE AND NOT ONLY ON THE SCREEN.** `Work-008` greys the
task list and `Work-011` locks it, and both of those are courtesies: this
route refuses on its own, so the rule survives a replayed request, a sync
batch that arrived out of order, and anything the phone attempts while
offline. Hard-won law 1 — a disabled control claiming a guarantee is not
the guarantee.

`POST /work-orders/{id}/accept` — BR-MET-110 step two, THE HUMAN ACT.

⚠ **THIS ROUTE IS WHY THE COMMIT ABOVE IT MATTERS: BR-MET-110 AND
BR-MET-115 WERE RULED, BUILT, TESTED AND AUDITED WITH NO WAY FOR A HUMAN
TO PERFORM THE ACT.** `connections.dispatch_communication`'s own docstring
read *"NO SUCH BUTTON IS DRAWN ANYWHERE"* — a signed trigger reachable only
from a Python shell. S88's work-order drawer now carries the control and
this is the door behind it.

One human act, one auditable moment, three consequences (PO 2026-08-25):
data accepted, service activated, customer told. **The third is guarded,
not defaulted — `OQ-372`**: the PO fixed the TRIGGER and did not say which
job's completion sends the letter, so the service refuses rather than
picking one, and this view passes that refusal through unchanged.

PO 2026-08-25: *"Work order will send the data and confirm from field;
utility staff will review these work order, accept them and use data from
them to activate these services."*

**Nothing activates here.** This deliberately does the least: it records
what the field sent. The act that matters is `/accept` below, and keeping
them two doors is what makes the review a real review rather than a
formality the transport performs on staff's behalf.

`GET /work/areas` — the Area chip's options, from `tenancy.Area` (US-WRK-011).

⚠ **NOT A SEVENTH FILTER.** `BR-WRK-026` counts the filters ON THE LIST; this
serves the options for one of the six, the way every other chip in the

`GET /work/builds/{id}/home` — where an old `/connections/…` link lands.

⚠ **A BOOKMARK IS A WORKING LINK AND STAYS ONE** (execution plan judgment
5). The New Connect wizard's completion, the *New connects* tab and every
bookmark point at `/connections/<uuid>` today. Answering 404 would break a
working link in order to punish a screen, so the front end reads this and
redirects: to the owner account where there is one, to the premises
otherwise.

A cross-tenant or unknown id is a **404 identical to an absent one** — the
seam filters by the tenant in context and RLS refuses underneath it, so
*"not yours"* and *"not there"* are the same sentence (hard rule 1).

`GET /work/candidates?template_id=&premises_id=&unit_ids=&on=&q=&page=&per=`
— the same advice BEFORE the job exists (`CR-168-BRC10` P2.5, ruling 25:
*"user can either assign or can leave blank"*). The raise's step 2 has no
order to ask about, so it names what the order WILL be: the template (its
skill), the premises (its area — ruling 24, never asked) and the day.

`GET /work/certification-watch` — expiries within 30 and 60 days.

⚠ **IT REFUSES NOTHING AND IT NEVER DID.** What changed on 2026-09-04 is
that `OQ-WRK-1493` was RULED — option (c), a per-tenant setting defaulting
to *warn* — so the answer now carries `policy` and `blocks`, and the screen
renders *blocked from N template types* only where the utility has switched
blocking on. A screen may not claim a guarantee the setting has switched
off (hard-won law 1).

`GET /work/crew-directory` — who works here, as a NAME and an EMAIL.

`BR-AST-533`, PO ruling 2026-09-12: ***"a) Let a clerk read the crew list
(name + email only)"***. It exists so that a Billing Clerk logging a repair
(`BR-AST-038`) picks the technician from a list instead of typing a uuid
into a text box, which is B14 rule 31 broken for the one role that screen
was written for.

⚠ **READ-ONLY, AND GET-ONLY.** There is no POST here and there must not be:
inviting a login is `identity`'s (`BR-IDN-011`) and making one a technician
is `POST /work/technicians` one function up. This route answers a picker and
nothing else.

⚠ **IT DOES NOT WIDEN `GET /users`, WHICH STAYS `SystemAdminOnly`.**
Measured with a real Billing Clerk session on `pine-hill`, 2026-09-12:
`GET /users` → **403 `BR-IDN-009`**, this route → **200 · 7 rows**.

⚠ **AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT `GET /work/technicians`.** A clerk can
already read that one, and it carries `role_code`, `status` and
`has_profile` — the three things the ruling names as not-served. They
cannot be dropped from it (`Work-023` marks who already has a profile), so
the narrow contract gets its own address rather than the wide one getting
quietly narrowed under a screen that needs it.

The permission class is the workforce set's own: **any of the three office
roles reads**, a system admin or a billing clerk writes — and there is
nothing here to write. A `field_technician` still meets 403, because
`core.permissions.ROLES` is the three office roles and `_role_of` answers
None for the fourth (`US-WRK-023` TC-4, unchanged by this route).

The envelope carries `counts`, which is `Work-023`'s footer sentence — *6
rows · 4 people, 1 crew, 1 contractor* — computed over the whole list and
not over the page, because it is a fact about the utility.

post.description:
`POST /work/flows/meter-read/raise` — send somebody out to these meters.

**THE SIXTH CALLER OF `from_flows.raise_for`** (PO ruling 2026-09-14,
verbatim ***"please build this"***, reversing that morning's deferral of the
Reads→Work door). Body:

    {"meters": ["<asset id>", …], "template_ids": ["<template id>", …]}

⚠ **WHY THE RAISE IS HTTP HERE WHEN THE OTHER FIVE DO IT AS A SERVICE
CALL.** Those five raise INSIDE the flow's own transaction, because the job
has to exist in the same commit that finishes the move-out or not at all. A
shortfall has no such commit: pressing *Send someone out* IS the whole act.
So the raise is a ROUTE, on the Work side, for the reason
`flow_proposed_work_orders` directly above already gives — the noun belongs
to metering, the CONTENT is Work's, so Work serves it. Metering therefore
writes nothing to `work_orders` and needs no seam of its own for this.

⚠ **THE RAISE IS OFFERED AND NEVER AUTOMATIC** (`from_flows` rule 1). This
route is reached only by a person pressing a control and ticking templates;
**no flag, no validation rule and no import commit calls it.** Empty
`template_ids` raises nothing and is not an error — a clerk who ticked
nothing has answered the question.

⚠ **PARTIAL SUCCESS IS AN ANSWER, NOT AN ERROR — `BR-WRK-055`.** One meter
whose premises cannot be resolved must not cost the other eleven their
visits, and must not cost the clerk their reading work either. Each meter is
raised inside `raise_for`'s own `atomic()`, which is the OUTERMOST block here
(`ATOMIC_REQUESTS` is set nowhere in `config/settings`), so a refusal rolls
back that meter alone and the next iteration opens a fresh transaction. ⚠
**That is hard-won law 14 and it is a claim about PostgreSQL the default
suite cannot test** — the suite is in-memory SQLite, which has no
aborted-transaction state and passes the broken version too. It is proved on
a real database in `06-backend/tests/test_reads_field_work_pg.py`.

⚠ **AND NO SECOND SIGNATURE.** PO, the same day: *"we do not need
confirmation or sign off from another person."* Nothing here waits for an
approval, and nothing is left pending for one.

get.description:
`GET /work/flows/{kind}/{id}/proposed` — what this flow could raise.

`kind` is one of `service_request` · `move_out` · `move_in` · `transfer` ·
`reconnect`. The answer is the utility's own PUBLISHED templates for the
services the flow touches, the flow's own reference, and — when judgment 8
bites — a `refusal` the panel draws instead of the list.

⚠ **THIS IS THE DOOR `apps/customers` USES TO DRAW THE PANEL, AND IT IS
HTTP ON PURPOSE.** `A7`'s boundary and `G78`'s mirror: the wizard reads what
Work has to offer over the API and never touches `work_order_templates`
with an ORM query. The RAISE is a different door — a service call inside the
flow's own transaction (`apps/customers/seams.py`), because the job has to
be created in the same commit that finishes the flow or not at all.

⚠ **`AnyTenantRole`, for `proposed_work_orders`' reason directly above:**
`OQ-WRK-1492` was closed on 2026-09-04 in the PO's own words — *"clark can
do it sicne it s a day to day work"*. Reading which jobs a move-out needs is
exactly that.

**NOTHING IS WRITTEN.** `propose` is a read end to end.

`POST /work/mobile/devices` — register this handset's push token (#91).

Idempotent on the token: re-registering the same one refreshes the row
rather than adding a second, because a service worker re-subscribes on every
install and browser update, and two rows for one phone would push the same
job twice.

The answer carries the device id and the token's last four characters. **It
never carries the token** — see `models.TechnicianDevice`.

⚠ **`CR-187-BRC10`, ADDITIVE:** with a handset id — the native app's bearer
credential, or `device_id` in the body — `POST {name, push_token?,
platform?}` registers the HANDSET by name, push token optional
(`mobile._register_handset`). `GET` lists the signed-in technician's own
registrations, paged.

`GET /work/mobile/jobs/{id}` — one job, whole, in one response (#89).

The order's six copies, the customer's contact and the help documents as
pre-signed links. ONE response by design: `BR-WRK-042` says the bundle is
fetched at sync and never on tap, and a route that answered half a job would
make that rule unimplementable however careful the client was.

Another technician's job — or another tenant's — is a **404**, byte-identical
to one that does not exist (HR-1).
